# Pack documentation

What each pack in this repo does, how to use it, and how to configure it.

> **Keep this file up to date.** Any change to a pack's behavior, commands or `config.js` must update this file in the same commit. `npm run check` fails if a pack, command, config option or `### How to use` section is missing from this file (see [Keeping this file current](#keeping-this-file-current)).
>
> **This file is also the players' documentation.** The [Our realm](https://mc.nish.software/realm/) page on mc.nish.software is generated from it (in the `nishant/hosting` repo: `cd minecraft && node tools/pack-docs.mjs`). Every pack section is published, plus the sections marked `<!-- on the site -->`. Write in plain American English, and quote in-game text and ids exactly as the code has them (in backticks). See [Publishing to mc.nish.software](#publishing-to-mcnishsoftware).

## Common to all packs

### Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| Minecraft | Bedrock **1.21.100+** (`min_engine_version`) |
| Script API | `@minecraft/server` **2.1.0**, `@minecraft/server-ui` **2.0.0** (stable) |
| Experiments | **None.** Only stable APIs are used, so no experimental toggles are needed on the Realm |
| Cheats | **Not required** for any command (`cheatsRequired: false`) |
| Achievements | Any non-Marketplace behavior pack turns off achievements for the world (that's how Bedrock works) |

### Installing from mc.nish.software
<!-- on the site -->

The realm runs everything as two packs: **Realm Bundle**, a behavior pack with every feature, and **Realm Resources**, a resource pack with every texture, particle, fog and sound. A pack can't be both kinds, so two is the fewest possible. To install or update them:

1. **Download** the latest Realm Bundle and Realm Resources `.mcpack` files from [mc.nish.software/realm](https://mc.nish.software/realm/) on the device you play on (Windows, phone or tablet) and open each. Minecraft starts and imports them as "Realm Bundle" and "Realm Resources".
2. **Open the realm's settings** (the pencil next to the realm). Under **Behavior Packs**, find Realm Bundle under **Available** and activate it. Under **Resource Packs**, activate Realm Resources and move it to the **top** of the active list, so its rain, sky and tools win over other resource packs. Minecraft uploads both to the realm.
3. **Join** once the realm restarts, and accept the resource pack download if asked. The welcome popup and the `/realm:` commands mean it's running.

**Updating:** download and open the newer version, then check that the realm's active Realm Bundle (or Realm Resources) shows the new version. If it still shows the old one, deactivate it and activate it again so the new version uploads. Nothing is lost: in-game settings and stats are stored in the world. Version numbers are the build date and time in UTC (`YYYY.MMDD.HHMM`, without leading zeros, so 5 January at 09:05 is `2026.105.905`), so every build is higher than the last, which Minecraft needs to treat it as an update.

**What's in each:** the Realm Bundle holds every behavior pack in this repo, Rain Extras included. Realm Resources holds the seven resource packs: [Realistic Rain](#realistic-rain--rain_rp), [Realm Skies](#realm-skies--sky_rp), [Translucent Tools](#translucent-tools--translucent_rp), [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp), [Platypus Models](#platypus-models--platypus_rp), [Easy Building Guides](#easy-building-guides--build_rp) and [Silly Enchants Sounds](#silly-enchants-sounds--silly_rp). Players get both packs automatically when they join. Realm Skies draws the tornadoes, rainbows, aurora, shooting stars, meteors, sandstorms, blizzards, moon fogs and trails of the bundle's sky packs: without it those still happen, but you can't see them.

**Only some features?** Every feature is also its own pack, downloaded from its card or the "one at a time" list under the Realm Bundle download, and activated the same way. Use **either** the Realm Bundle **or** single packs, never both: the same commands would be registered twice and fail to load. The same goes for Realm Resources and the single resource packs. If you had Realistic Rain, Realm Skies, Translucent Tools or Rain Extras active on their own before, remove them when you add the bundles. Switching between them starts the features' in-game settings over (welcome and news text, tips, settings from `/realm:config`, per-player choices, remembered chests, zones and farms); stats on the scoreboard are kept. Single packs use ordinary version numbers (`1.0.0`) that go up whenever that pack changes.

### Installing on a Realm

For whoever builds the packs from this repo:

1. Build the packs with `npm run build` (one `dist/<folder>.mcpack` per pack), or `npm run bundle -- --all` and `npm run bundle -- --resources` for the two bundles (`dist/realm_bundle.mcpack`, `dist/realm_resources.mcpack`).
2. Open the `.mcpack` on a device with Minecraft. It imports automatically.
3. Go to **Play → Realms → ✏️ Edit Realm → Behavior Packs** and move the pack from **Available** to **Active**. A resource pack (Realm Resources, or `rain_rp`, `sky_rp`, `translucent_rp`, `hud_rp`, `platypus_rp`, `build_rp` on their own) goes under **Resource Packs** instead, at the top of the active list.
   *Another way:* download the Realm world, activate the pack under the world's **Behavior Packs**, and upload the world again.
4. Rejoin. Commands are registered when the world loads.

> ⚠️ Activate **either** the individual packs **or** a bundle that contains them, never both. Otherwise every command is registered twice, and the duplicate commands fail to load. Packs listed in `tools/standalone.json` (none today) are never in a bundle: activate them next to it.

### Commands

- **Every command starts with `/realm:`**, e.g. `/realm:welcome`, `/realm:stats`. Type `/realm` to see all of them in autocomplete, or run `/realm:help` for a page that explains each one, with usage.
- All packs share the `realm` namespace because Bedrock requires **one command namespace per add-on**. A bundle is one add-on, so if packs used different namespaces, only the first pack's commands would register and the rest would show as "unknown command". `npm run check` and the bundler both enforce this.
- **Everyone** commands work for all players. **Ops** commands (permission level `GameDirectors`) only work for, and are only shown to, operators. Every pack counts a player as an operator by that same permission level, and operators' menus and forms check it again when a button is picked or a form is sent, so a player de-opped while one is open gets `Only operators can do that.` (or a line naming the action) and nothing changes.

### Two ways to configure

| | Where | Who | Takes effect | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **In-game, every pack** | `/realm:config` ([Realm Settings](#realm-settings--settings_bp)), or an item named `Realm Settings` | Operators | Immediately | The options that make sense to change live, in every installed pack: switches, numbers and choices. Saved in the world, and overrides `config.js`. **Reset a pack to defaults** goes back to `config.js` |
| **In-game, per player** | `/realm:prefs`, and toggles such as `/realm:durability`, `/realm:phantoms`, `/realm:rain` | Every player, for themselves | Immediately | Overrides the realm's value for that player only |
| **In-game editors** | `/realm:welcome_edit`, `/realm:news_edit`, `/realm:news_tips`, `/realm:stats_sidebar` | Operators | Immediately | Texts, tips and the sidebar. Saved in the world, and overrides `config.js` |
| **`config.js`** | `packs/<folder>/scripts/config.js` | Whoever builds the pack | After rebuilding and re-applying the pack | Defaults for all of the above, and the options that have no in-game editor: lists, texts, tick intervals and command permissions |

### Setting up a new world or a big server
<!-- on the site -->

- **Set up this world** (`/realm:admin_setup`, or the first button of the [Realm Configuration](#realm-configuration--admin_bp) item's **Operator Tools**) walks an operator through every one-time job, one page each: place the townsfolk, add a town, a safe zone at spawn, the caravan spot, the bounty board, a waystone at spawn, the expedition site and the rest. Operators are players with permission level 1 or more (Realm operators, `/op` or `permissions.json` on a dedicated server); tags never make anyone an operator.
- **Server size** (Operator Tools) switches the settings that depend on the number of players between **Small Realm** (the defaults, up to about 10 players) and **Large server** (30 to 100+), showing each change before anything changes.
- **Pack diagnostics** (`/realm:diag`) shows how much script time and saved data each pack uses, and can make one pack forget its saved data before you remove it.

### Updating a pack

1. Edit the pack.
2. **Increase `header.version`** in its `manifest.json`, e.g. `[1, 0, 0]` → `[1, 0, 1]`. If you don't, devices keep using their cached copy. (Bundles do this automatically.)
3. `npm run build`, then re-import and re-apply the pack.

### Formatting codes
<!-- on the site -->

Text that operators edit in game (the welcome popup, news, tips) supports these codes:

| Code | Effect |
|---|---|
| `\n` | New line, in the welcome and news **body** only (not in titles, the button or tips). The in-game text boxes are one line, so type a literal `\n` |
| `\|` | New line in text pasted with `/realm:news_body` or `/realm:news_add` (chat commands drop the backslash of `\n`, which then shows as a plain `n`) |
| `%` | Doesn't show: Minecraft takes it for a formatting code. Write `percent` instead |
| `§0`–`§9`, `§a`–`§f` | Colors: `§a` green, `§b` aqua, `§c` red, `§e` yellow, `§6` gold, `§7` gray |
| `§l` `§o` `§r` | Bold, italic, reset |

## Realm Help — `help_bp`

One help page for every realm command: how each feature works, and each command with its usage.

### How to use

1. Run `/realm:help`. A **Realm help** menu lists every feature installed on this realm, with its commands under its name.
2. Tap **All commands** to see every command with its usage on one page, or tap a feature for its how-to steps and its commands. **Back** returns to the menu.
3. Jump straight to a page with `/realm:help <feature>`, for example `/realm:help stash` or `/realm:help find`, or `/realm:help all` for every command. Chat autocompletes the feature names.
4. **Operators** also see the operator-only commands and steps, marked `(operators)`.

### What players see

- Only features that are installed show up: each pack answers when the help asks, so a realm running a few single packs gets help for just those.
- Usages follow the usual notation: `<name>` must be typed, `[name]` is optional.
- The text is the same as on mc.nish.software/realm: it's generated from this file.
- Running `/realm:help` again while the help is already open does nothing, so menus don't stack. If chat or another screen stays open for about 20 seconds, chat says `Couldn't open the help. Close chat or your inventory and try again.`

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:help [feature]` | Everyone | Opens the help menu, or the page for `feature` (a pack's folder name without `_bp`, such as `stash`, `crowns` or `quests`; chat autocompletes them) or `all` |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `answerTicks` | `10` | Ticks to wait for the installed packs to answer before the help opens (20 = 1 s) |
| `showOpsToEveryone` | `false` | Show operator-only commands and steps to everyone. Operators can change it in game with `/realm:config` |

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `help:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` (`showOpsToEveryone`) |

### How it works

- `scripts/catalog.js` holds every pack's summary, `### How to use` steps and Commands table from this file, converted to Minecraft formatting. `node tools/help-catalog.mjs` writes it (and bumps this pack's patch version once per commit); `npm run check` fails when it's out of date.
- `/realm:help` sends the script event `realm:help_ping`. Every other pack answers `realm:help_pong` with its folder name, and the help lists the packs that answered within `answerTicks`. Realm Help answers other packs' pings too (`help_bp`), so the [Realm Configuration](#realm-configuration--admin_bp) menu lists `/realm:help`. Script events cross pack boundaries without imports, so the packs stay independent, and work the same in the Realm Bundle and as single packs.

## Realm Settings — `settings_bp`

Change the packs' settings in game: operators set them for everyone with `/realm:config`, and every player picks their own preferences with `/realm:prefs`.

### How to use

1. Run `/realm:prefs` to open **My preferences**: one form with your own choices from every installed pack, such as whether you get durability warnings, phantoms or the rain extras, what sneak-tapping a chest does, and whether chat announces you going AFK. Every switch is named for what it does: on means **Enabled**. Change what you like and tap **Save** at the bottom: nothing applies until you do. A preference the operators have overridden for the whole realm shows as gray text instead of a switch, with its value and why, such as `Coordinates HUD: Disabled` / `Locked by the operators: Coordinates HUD is Disabled for the whole realm` (or `Easy Building needs the tag "builder", which operators give`). Close with X and chat says `My preferences: closed with X, so nothing was saved. To change a setting, run /realm:prefs again and press Save at the bottom.` (the game doesn't hand back what was on a form closed with X). A summary pops up with how many changes were saved and each one as before -> after, for example `1 change saved` and `Phantom Opt-out > Phantoms near me: Enabled -> Disabled` (chat gets the same). Tap **Back to my preferences** to change more, or **Done**.
2. Your choices are remembered. `/realm:durability`, `/realm:phantoms` and `/realm:rain` flip the same switches as the form.
3. **Operators:** run `/realm:config`, or use any item renamed `Realm Settings` on an anvil (a stick works). The first button, **All settings**, holds every pack's settings with a heading per pack (see below); the buttons under it open one pack each. Change settings (switches, sliders and lists) and tap **Save**. They apply right away for everyone. A summary pops up with how many changes were saved and each one as before -> after, such as `Storm wind volume: 70% -> 50%`; tap **Back to Realm Settings** for another pack, or **Done**. A setting shown as text with `(change in config.js, then restart the world)` can only be changed there.
4. **Operators: All settings.** With the whole Realm Bundle that is about 370 settings, so they come on a few pages, such as `All settings (page 1 of 5)`, of at most 100 lines each (`allPageSize`); a pack is never split across pages. The list at the top, **After saving, go to**, picks where **Save and go** takes you next: the next page (already chosen), any other page (each named by its first and last pack, `Page 2: <first pack> to <last pack>`) or **Done (show what was saved)**. Each page saves its changes when you tap **Save and go**; closing a page saves nothing on it. At the end one summary lists every change from every page, each as `Pack > Setting: before -> after`. All settings and a pack's own page show the same saved values: change Leaderboard size on one and the other shows the new number the next time it opens.
5. **Operators:** **Reset a pack to defaults**, at the bottom of the menu, puts one pack's settings back to its `config.js` values after asking. Players' own preferences are kept.

### What players see

- Only installed packs are listed: each pack answers when the menu asks, as with `/realm:help`. Rain Extras is listed too, from the bundle or on its own.
- Each setting has a `!` icon: hover over it or tap it for what the setting does, its default and, for a slider, its range.
- Volumes and other 0 to 1 settings are sliders in percent (`Storm wind volume (%)`, 0 to 100 in steps of 5), and settings in fractional steps, such as Chairs' seat reach (1 to 5 blocks in 0.5s), are lists of their exact values: Bedrock's sliders only stop on whole numbers. A setting you don't touch is saved exactly as it was, even a `config.js` value between the steps or outside the in-game range (shown at the nearest place the control can show it).
- Tapping **Save** without changing anything says `No changes`.
- Switches read the same everywhere: the setting is named for what it does, the switch on means **Enabled**, and chat says `Enabled` or `Disabled`. Lists show plain choices, such as `Open the menu` or `Only in protected zones`.
- A preference set to what the realm has follows the realm: if an operator changes that setting later, you get the new value. A preference set to something else stays yours.
- If a pack doesn't confirm a change within half a second, the summary counts it as not saved (`1 change saved, 1 not saved`) and that line says `not saved, the pack didn't answer. Try again`; a value the pack refuses says why.
- Players who aren't operators and use an item named `Realm Settings` are pointed to `/realm:prefs`.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:prefs` | Everyone | Opens **My preferences**: your own choices from every installed pack, in one form |
| `/realm:config` | Ops | Opens **Realm Settings**: **All settings** first (every pack's settings with a heading per pack, about 100 lines per page, `allPageSize`), then each installed pack's own page, then **Reset a pack to defaults**. Using an item named `Realm Settings` opens it too (`itemName`) |

### What each pack offers

Each pack's own section says which of its options are in `/realm:config` and which are preferences in `/realm:prefs` (under its Configuration). With the whole Realm Bundle, `/realm:config` lists every pack that has settings (about 60) and `/realm:prefs` holds about 40 preferences in one form, with a heading per pack, such as **Stats ticker above my hotbar** and its stats, speed, style and colors (`/realm:stats_ticker`), **Welcome popup when I join**, **Low-durability warnings** (`/realm:durability`), **Phantoms near me** (`/realm:phantoms`), **Announce when I go AFK**, Quick Stack & Sort's sneak-tap and hotbar choices, **Unread letters notice on join** and **Rain extras** (`/realm:rain`).

Everything else (lists such as crops, `keepItems` and container types, texts such as name tag prefixes, tick intervals, and command permissions) stays in `config.js`.

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `answerTicks` | `10` | Ticks to wait for the installed packs to answer, and for each change to be confirmed (20 = 1 s) |
| `itemName` | `Realm Settings` | Operators who use an item with exactly this name (renamed on an anvil) open `/realm:config`. `""` turns it off |
| `allPageSize` | `100` | **All settings** puts at most this many lines on a page (a heading per pack plus a line per setting); a pack bigger than that gets a page of its own. `0` puts everything on one page (with the whole bundle about 370 controls, slow to open and to scroll on phones) |

### Saved data

None in this pack. Each pack saves its own settings, so they stay with that pack and still apply when Realm Settings is removed:

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `<prefix>:cfg` (`afk:cfg`, `stash:cfg`, …) | World | JSON of the settings changed in `/realm:config` that differ from `config.js` |
| `<prefix>:pref` (`afk:pref`, `stash:pref`, `welcome:pref`) | Player | JSON of the player's own preferences that differ from the realm's. Stats also keeps an explicit ticker on/off choice when it matches the default, so a later default change does not undo it |
| `durability:off`, `phantom:off`, `rain:off` | Player | The existing switches, kept so nobody's earlier choice is lost |
| `news:tipSettings`, `welcome:settings` | World | Shared with `/realm:news_tips` and `/realm:welcome_edit`, so both menus show the same values |

### How it works

- **Locked preferences:** a player option may list `lock` (`[["enabled", false]]`: the world options and values that make it do nothing) and a `locked(player)` function for other reasons (a tag the player lacks). Each pack's `realm:cfg_schema` answer then gives the option `locked` (the reason, in words, built from the world option's label), and My preferences shows it as text rather than a control. Every player preference whose pack has a realm-wide switch has one, so a preference you can change always does something. Number options may list `choices` (`["1", "2", "5", "10"]`): the menu shows a list, and other values are refused.
- **All settings** and a pack's own page are two views of the same thing: both ask the packs for their current values (`realm:cfg_ping`) each time they open, draw each setting with the same control, and save through the same `realm:cfg_set`, so neither keeps a copy that could go stale. **My preferences** is one form with a heading per pack.
- Every other behavior pack has a `scripts/settings.js` that lists what can change in game. The pack reads those options through it (`get(key)`: the world's saved value over `config.js`; `getFor(player, key)`: the player's own value over the world's), so a change applies on the next use, with no restart.
- The packs never import each other. This pack sends the script event `realm:cfg_ping` (`{id, player}`), and each pack answers `realm:cfg_schema` with its options and their current values (`{id, pack, title, part, parts, options}`), split into parts under the 2048-character limit of a script event message. Saving sends `realm:cfg_set` (`{id, pack, key, value, player?}`) and resetting `realm:cfg_reset` (`{id, pack}`). The pack checks the value (type, range, choices), ignores keys it doesn't have, saves it and answers `realm:cfg_ack` (`{id, pack, key, ok, value, error?}`), which is what the save summary reports.
- An option can carry `invert` (a switch stored as `off` but shown as **Enabled**, so no label is a double negative) and `names` (readable words for a list's choices). Labels name what the setting does, never "Turn off ...".
- In-game text is plain ASCII: Bedrock draws a whole line in a smaller fallback font when it holds a character like `…`, `–`, `•` or an emoji, which is why `/realm:help` once looked different in `/help`. `npm run check` (`tools/check-ascii.mjs`) fails on any other character in pack code, and `tools/help-catalog.mjs` converts the docs' typography when it builds the help.
- The part of `settings.js` that does this is the same in every pack: it's copied from `tools/settings-shared.js` by `node tools/sync-settings.mjs`, and `npm run check` fails if a copy is missing or out of date.
- Operators with cheats on could send the same script events with `/scriptevent`; that does nothing an operator can't do in the menu.

---

## Realm Configuration — `admin_bp`

Every player carries a **Realm Configuration** item (a nether star with a gold name, whose lore starts `Hold it in your hand and use it` / `to open the realm menu:`). Using it opens one menu with **every realm command you can use**: pick what you want to do, pick a command, choose its options from preset lists (townsfolk, weather kinds, relics, online players, sliders with sensible ranges, your position filled in), and it runs as you, with the command's own checks, messages and menus. Players who aren't operators see the same menu without the operator entries; operators see everything, with operator-only entries in **red**. The commands still work as typed; this is for when you'd rather not type them while playing.

### How to use

1. You get the `Realm Configuration` item when you join or respawn without one (`giveToPlayers`). It stays through death and can't be dropped or put in a chest, and you only ever get one. Lost it anyway? Run `/realm:admin_item`. `/realm:admin` opens the same menu. Operators: on a world whose setup isn't finished, chat says once `New world? Set up this world walks you through the one-time setup (townsfolk, a town, safe zones, server size...)`; **Don't remind operators** on its first page stops it for every operator.
2. Use the item (right-click or long press, like eating). The menu starts with **My Preferences** (opens `/realm:prefs`), **Recent** and **Search**, then **What do you want to do?**: **My Screen & Toggles**, **Items & Building**, **Story & Adventure**, **Friends, Crowns & Fun**, **World & Events** and **Towns & Townsfolk** (and **Other** for a pack the menu doesn't know yet; a page with nothing you can use is left out). Each is one page that scrolls, with a heading per section (`On your screen`, `Weather and sky`...). Every button has two lines: what it is (`Find Container`, `Set Weather`...) and, under it, what it does.
3. Pick a command. Without options it runs right away (a menu command such as `/realm:map` opens its own menu). With options, a form asks for them: lists for choices, a list of online players, sliders for amounts, a switch for true or false, and your current position already filled in for coordinates. Leave an optional choice on `(leave out)` or its box empty to skip it. Press **Run**. Afterwards the page you picked it from comes back, so the next command is two taps away (a command that opened its own menu keeps it). Closing the options form, or **Cancel**, goes back too. Chat says `[Realm Configuration] Ran /realm:...` with the exact command, or that it didn't run.
4. **Recent** (with how many it holds, like `Recent (3)`) keeps your last 8 commands with their options (`recentSize`), each with the exact command under it: tap one to run it again right away, with no form. **Search** finds commands by any word of their name, hint, command or description; the results end with **Search again**.
5. **Operators:** you see everything, and the top of each page says `Red = operators only. The rest is for every player.` Red buttons are operator commands; the plain dark ones are what every player sees too. Each pack's own menu (for example `/realm:stats`, `/realm:town` or `/realm:caravan`) marks its operator buttons the same way, in red, and shows them only to operators. The main menu adds **Realm Settings** (right after **My Preferences**; opens `/realm:config`) and, last, **Operator Tools**.
6. **Operators: Operator Tools** is one page (everything on it is for operators). It starts with **Set up this world** (see `/realm:admin_setup`) and **Server size**: **Small Realm** (up to about 10 players: every setting below at its pack's default) or **Large server** (30 to 100+ players). Picking one lists every change first, `Pack: Setting: old -> new` in menu words, plus how many already match and which packs aren't installed; **Yes** changes them all at once (chat: `Server size: Large server. Changed 8 settings.`). Large server sets: [Minimap](#minimap--map_bp) `budgetLevel` normal -> low and `mobRadiusMax` 32 -> 24, [Champions](#champions--elite_bp) `maxAlive` 8 -> 16, [Expeditions](#expeditions--expedition_bp) `slots` 1 -> 3, [Easy Building](#easy-building--build_bp) `maxBlocksCap` 50,000 -> 2,000, `operatorsOnly` Enabled and `allowInfiniteReach` Disabled, [Lag Cleanup](#lag-cleanup--cleanup_bp) `threshold` 500 -> 1,500, [Chest Finder](#chest-finder--find_bp) `liveScanRadius` 16 -> 8, Realm Configuration `checkSeconds` 30 -> 60, [Realm Mail](#realm-mail--mail_bp) `sendCooldownSeconds` 10 -> 30 and [AFK + Smart Sleep](#afk--smart-sleep--afk_bp) `sleep.percent` 100 -> 50; Small Realm puts each back to its default. Then come three headings. **Quick actions** are the vanilla things you'd otherwise type: set the weather (with the [Weather Almanac](#weather-almanac--weather_bp) installed this runs `/realm:weather_set`, because the almanac plans the weather and would undo a plain change), set the time (day, noon, sunset, night, midnight, sunrise), game mode for a player, teleport to a player (nearest first) or a player to you, give an item by id and amount, clear effects, heal, **Show a Title** (1 to 25 seconds, default 5, for everyone online or one player), set the world spawn where you stand, remove hostile mobs nearby (monsters only, named mobs are kept, radius 8 to 128) and game rules (day and night cycle, keep inventory, mob spawning, mob griefing). They work without cheats. **Pack diagnostics**, after the quick actions, measures every pack's script time for 10 seconds and lists the packs, slowest first, with their saved data; a pack's page can forget its saved data (see `/realm:diag`). **Server setup checklist** lists the one-time jobs across the installed packs (place the townsfolk, the relicsmith, story places, towns and their project spots, bounty board, caravan spots, expedition site, waystones, safe zones, Creeper Guard zones, farms, a community goal, welcome message, news, settings); tap one to do it. **Relicsmith** (`/realm:relics_smith`) places Ida, exactly like picking her in **Place the Townsfolk**. The marks are the same as in Set up this world: `[x]` done (its pack says so, or it ran from Set up this world), `[-]` skipped there, a red `[ ]` when its pack says not yet. Under **Realm Configuration**, **Get the Menu Item** gives the item to other players.
7. **Operators:** every `*_remove` and `*_reset` command, anything run for **Everyone online (@a)**, and `/realm:meteor_now`, `/realm:tornado_spawn`, `/realm:caravan_call`, `/realm:crowns_give`, `/realm:domt_draw`, `/realm:weather_set`, `/realm:moon_set`, `/realm:storm_cell`, `/realm:fishing_tournament`, `/realm:wander_clear` and `/realm:calendar_set` ask **Are you sure?** first; so do set the time, set the weather, game rules, and give, heal, clear effects, teleport or a title for everyone online.
8. **Operators: use `/realm:admin_title` (or Show a Title) instead of `/title`.** The [Minimap](#minimap--map_bp)'s compass strip, the story tracker and the other [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) boxes share the title channel with real titles, so they draw over a plain `/title` within a second or two. `/realm:admin_title "Market Day" "In the square" 8` tells every pack with a box first (the title protocol), so the boxes step aside until it has faded and then come back.

### What players see

- **Everyone:** the item in their inventory, a chat line when they're given one (`You have the Realm Configuration item: use it for every realm command you can use, in one menu.`), and the menu. The menu shows only the commands of installed packs that the player's permission level allows: a player who isn't an operator never sees **Realm Settings**, **Operator Tools**, a quick action or a red command, and their search and **Recent** leave those out too.
- **Operators:** everything, with the legend `Red = operators only. The rest is for every player.` at the top of each page, and `(operators only)` next to the command at the top of an operator command's options form.
- Hiding isn't the only check: right before an operator command runs, the menu checks the player's level again, so someone who stopped being an operator with the menu open gets `/realm:... didn't run: it's for operators.` (a quick action: `... didn't run: you aren't an operator any more.`) and nothing changes.
- An item renamed `Realm Settings` on an anvil still opens [Realm Settings](#realm-settings--settings_bp) as before (operators only); the Realm Configuration menu's **Realm Settings** button opens it too.
- With `giveToPlayers` off, only operators get the item (`giveToOperators`), and a player who isn't an operator and uses the real item sees `The Realm Configuration item is for operators here. /realm:admin opens the menu` above the hotbar while it's put away (`removeFromOthers`). `/realm:admin` still opens the menu, with their own commands, for everyone.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:admin` | Everyone | Opens the Realm Configuration menu (the same as using the item): every command you can use; operators see theirs in red |
| `/realm:admin_item [player]` | Everyone | Gives you the Realm Configuration item if you don't carry one. Operators can name other players to check them and give them one. With `giveToPlayers` off it's for operators only |
| `/realm:admin_setup` | Ops | **Set up this world**: walks you through the one-time jobs a new world needs, one page each: what it is, why, whether it's done (the packs say so where they can: townsfolk placed, a town, a safe zone or town over world spawn, a waystone you know near spawn), a button that runs the step's own command, **Mark as done** where no pack can tell, and **Skip**. Steps (only those of installed packs): place the Townsfolk, add a town, a safe zone at spawn, a caravan arrival spot, the bounty board, a first waystone at spawn, the expedition site, Server size, then the rest of the setup checklist. Ends with a summary (`Setup finished: 3 done, 2 skipped.`). A page stops quietly when the operator leaves, dies or respawns; it never reopens forms or changes what a newer page set, and a page waiting for a busy client keeps waiting instead of giving up on the first busy answer. Also the first button of **Operator Tools** |
| `/realm:diag [seconds]` | Ops | **Pack diagnostics**: measures every pack's script time for a few seconds (default 10, 1 to 60), then lists every pack that answered, slowest first, with its version, ms per tick and saved data. Red: over 0.5 ms per tick, or one saved entry over 24 KB (one entry can hold 32 KB). Packs that don't answer (an older version) are listed under **No answer**. A pack's page shows what takes its time (its top two callbacks), its biggest saved entry, and **Forget this pack's saved data**: after you confirm, the pack deletes everything it saved in the world (in a bundle only its own entries), including anything it kept for players there such as stored inventory pages or letters, and saves nothing more until you run `/reload` or restart. If the pack has not answered after 200 ticks, the page says `<pack> hasn't answered yet: it may still have deleted its data` and an answer that arrives later is reported to you in chat (`... forgot N saved entries ..., after taking longer than expected. Run /reload or restart the server now.`, or that it didn't). Up to 16 forgets wait at once, one per pack (a second says it is still waiting), and a forget with no answer after 12,000 ticks (10 minutes) is dropped and a later reply ignored. Scoreboards, tags, structures and data saved on players are kept. Also **Operator Tools > Pack diagnostics** |
| `/realm:admin_title <title> [subtitle] [seconds] [player]` | Ops | Shows a title (quote text with spaces; `""` for no subtitle) for 1 to 25 seconds (default 5) to everyone online, or to the players named. Use it instead of `/title`: the Minimap compass and the other side boxes step aside for it and come back when it fades |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `giveToPlayers` | `true` | Every player without the item gets one when they join or respawn (once: never a second one). Players who aren't operators see only the commands they can use |
| `giveToOperators` | `true` | With `giveToPlayers` off: operators without the item get one when they join or respawn, and within `checkSeconds` of becoming an operator |
| `removeFromOthers` | `true` | With `giveToPlayers` off: take the real item from players who aren't operators (an anvil-renamed item is left alone) |
| `checkSeconds` | `30` | How often to check who carries the item, in seconds (5 to 300). Each round reads the whole inventory of players who became (or stopped being) operators, should get the item and have none, or had a removal fail, one player per tick; every other inventory is read once in 10 rounds (5 minutes by default), for an off hand or cursor changed by a command. Inventory changes are checked at once, not by the round; the cursor is read on a change that involves no real item only after a real item left a slot, was seen in the off hand or on the cursor, or the player spawned |
| `itemType` | `"minecraft:nether_star"` | The vanilla item it's made from. It gets the name, lore, keep on death and an inventory lock |
| `recentSize` | `8` | How many of your last commands **Recent** keeps (1 to 20) |
| `answerTicks` | `10` | Ticks to wait for the installed packs (and the safe zone lists, for the checklist) to answer (20 = 1 second) |

Operators can change `giveToPlayers`, `giveToOperators`, `removeFromOthers`, `checkSeconds` and `recentSize` in game with `/realm:config` when Realm Settings is installed.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `admin:setup` | World | JSON (under 1 KB) for Set up this world: `{ d: {<step>: 1}, s: {<step>: 1}, f?: 1, x?: 1, size?: "small" \| "large" }`: steps done (`d`) and skipped (`s`), finished (`f`), reminders dismissed (`x`) and the Server size picked |
| `admin:setupTold` | Player | `true` once the operator was told about Set up this world. The older `admin:setupHint` is no longer read or written |
| `admin:recent` | Player | JSON list of that player's last commands, newest first: `{ t, l }` (a title and the command line) or `{ t, a, v }` (a quick action's id and its values, with player names rather than list positions) |
| `admin:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- `scripts/catalog.js` lists every `realm:` command of every pack: name, description, permission level, parameters (type, optional, enum values) and the pack. `node tools/admin-catalog.mjs` writes it by loading each pack's `scripts/main.js` in Node with a stand-in for the Minecraft modules and recording what its startup handler registers, so enum values computed from `config.js` (townsfolk ids, relics, story places...) are exact. `npm run check` runs it with `--check` and fails when a command was added or changed and the catalog wasn't rewritten. `scripts/presets.js` (hand-written) adds the groups and their sections (`GROUPS`; `--check` also measures each group's two lines), each command's button name and hint (`NAMES`; `--check` fails when a command has none, or when a name or hint is wider than a button line, 168 pixels of the Minecraft font, because Bedrock cuts longer lines off with `...`), friendlier labels, how enum choices read (townsfolk by name), slider ranges and defaults, the commands that ask first and the setup checklist; a command it doesn't mention still shows in game (under its command name, with plain inputs).
- Which packs are installed: the menu sends `realm:help_ping` like `/realm:help` and keeps the folders that answer (for a minute). If nobody answers, it shows everything.
- Commands run with `player.runCommand`, so a command does exactly what it does when typed by that player. When a command refuses (a bad name, too far from a town...), the game doesn't hand its reason to the script, so chat says `didn't run: the command refused. Check the options, or type it to see its reason` (some packs also explain in chat); a command that doesn't parse shows the game's own error.
- **Titles:** `/realm:admin_title` and **Show a Title** send `realm:title` `{ player, ticks, from: "admin_bp" }` for each player (`ticks`: fade in 10 + the seconds + fade out 20, at most 530) right before `setTitle`; a title without a subtitle sends a one-space subtitle, so the last title's subtitle doesn't show under it. This is the title protocol in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together), so every copy of the side boxes waits until it's over.
- **Set up this world and the checklist** ask the packs only while a page opens (one wait of `answerTicks`; no interval, and a `realm:` listener only while waiting): `realm:npc_places_ping` (townsfolk placed), the safe zones protocol (`realm:zones_ping`: towns, and any safe zone or town covering `world.getDefaultSpawnLocation()` in the Overworld) and `realm:waystones_known_ping` (a waystone this operator knows within 48 blocks of spawn). Steps no pack can answer (caravan spot, bounty board, expedition site and the rest) count as done once their command ran from the wizard, or with **Mark as done**. After a step's command opens its own menu, the step page waits up to 2 minutes for it to close, then says in chat `Setup paused...` if it never could. The reminder chat line goes to an operator once (on join and at each item check) until the setup is finished or dismissed; it needs no item.
- **Server size** asks `realm:cfg_ping` and keeps the `realm:cfg_schema` answers of the packs in the profile, shows the changes, and on **Yes** sends `realm:cfg_set {id, pack, key, value}` per change and waits for `realm:cfg_ack`, like Realm Settings. The operator is checked when the page opens and again right after the confirmation. Only options that change live are in the profile (restart-only ones like the HUDs' `intervalTicks` aren't). Small Realm is each option's default in its pack's `config.js`.
- **Pack diagnostics** sends `realm:diag_ping {id, ticks}` and lists the `realm:diag_pong` answers; packs installed (from the help ping) that don't answer within 40 ticks after the window are **No answer**. Forget sends `realm:diag_forget` (the [diagnostics protocol](#how-the-packs-work-together)) after the confirmation, checking the operator again right before. Each pack declares its world-key prefix (for example `titles`, `welcome`) when its `diag.js` loads, so saved keys no one has touched since the reload are still owned and forgotten by the right pack; an unknown or ambiguous prefix stays unowned and is not forgotten. Times are measured like the test harness's profiler (`Date.now()`, so only totals over many calls mean much; time after an `await` isn't counted) and are approximate.
- The menu opens for everyone and hides commands above the player's level (`commandPermissionLevel`; `GameDirectors` or higher is an operator). Operators are players with permission level 1 (`GameDirectors`) or more: Realm operators, and on a dedicated server players made operator with `/op` or `permissions.json`. Tags never make someone an operator. Right before each command runs it checks that level again against the command's own permission in the catalog, and before each quick action that the player is an operator, so an operator command never runs for someone below its level, whatever the menu showed.
- Items handed out before this change say `Operators only` in their lore; they still count as the real item, and their lore is updated to `Red entries: operators only` the next time the pack checks. So are items that say `Gold entries: operators only` (from when operator entries were gold).
- **One carried item at a time:** when a player joins or respawns, uses the item, runs `/realm:admin_item`, changes their inventory (including switching [Expansive Inventory](#expansive-inventory--stash_bp) pages back to a page that held an older copy) or is checked every `checkSeconds`, the pack keeps a single real `Realm Configuration` item (preferring the selected hotbar slot, then hotbar, then main inventory), normalizes its stack size (`1`), name, lore, `keepOnDeath` and inventory lock in place, and removes any extra real copies across the inventory, offhand and cursor while leaving ordinary items, other locked items and anvil-renamed items without the pack's lore untouched. An item with the pack's lore made of another item than `itemType` (after `itemType` changed) also counts as the real item and is replaced by one made of the current `itemType`, so nobody keeps a locked item they can't drop.

---

## Welcome Message — `welcome_bp`

Shows the same short, spoiler-free default welcome on every world, including this Realm. One scrolling popup introduces the story and the main features that are actually installed, then points to help, personal settings and the story journal. Operators can save their own text in-game.

### How to use

1. Join the realm. The welcome popup appears after about 2 seconds; scroll through it and tap `Close`.
2. Run `/realm:welcome` (or `/realm:welcome_show`) any time to see it again. Don't want the popup when you join? Disable **Welcome popup when I join** in `/realm:prefs`; the chat welcome and the title still come (before 1.5.3 that switch turned them off too).
3. **Operators:** `/realm:welcome` opens the **Welcome Message** menu instead: `Show the welcome message`, `Edit the welcome message`, `Reset to the defaults` and `Settings` (which points to `/realm:config` → Welcome Message). The edit and reset buttons do the same as the commands below. When the one-time migration (below) replaced this world's old saved welcome, the menu also has `Old welcome`: it shows the kept copy, with `Restore it` (puts the old body back, and the old title and button if they were taken out with it and no newer title or button was saved since) and `Delete the copy`. Run `/realm:welcome_edit`, change the title, body or button text and the switches, then submit. The body is split over boxes of 100 characters each (Minecraft's limit), joined in order; type `\n` for a new line. Players see the new text on their next join (with "show once" on, each player sees it one more time, unless you turn off "Show it again to players who've seen it" for a typo fix). `/realm:welcome_reset` asks first, then goes back to the pack's default text.

The default has three normal-size bold gold headings: `The World`, `What You Can Do` (omitted when there are no listed features) and `Where To Go Next`. With Story Questlines installed, it introduces the harbor bell and the strange stars without revealing later events; with Townsfolk too, it names Old Tobin and Mara as the starting point, but only the ones who are placed (`/realm:npc_add`): a new world with nobody placed yet gets no "Tap ..." line, one with only Mara placed says `Tap Mara in town to begin ...`. Townsfolk reports every placement, so the next joiner sees the change. Without Story Questlines it simply welcomes players to explore and build together. Feature and help lines name only installed packs. Installed packs are asked at most once a minute; concurrent joins wait for the same discovery, rather than seeing an incomplete list.

The old saved Realm welcome containing `Tap Old Tobin or Mara in town to begin` is migrated once to this default. Its old built-in title and button are removed only if they still match; other settings and unknown fields stay. Unrelated saved text is not changed. What it takes out is kept in `welcome:legacy`, so house rules or links an operator wrote around the old sentence are not lost: the first operator who joins afterwards is told once in chat (`A copy is kept: /realm:welcome -> Old welcome`), and the copy stays until an operator restores or deletes it. After that migration, later operator edits always win, even if they reuse the old words. `/realm:welcome_reset` returns to the new default, not the retired Realm-specific text.

### What players see

- About 2 seconds after joining (`delayTicks`), one scrolling popup appears with three short sections and one close button. The all-installed default is about 151 words; form labels and content bounds are checked separately from real client rendering, which remains unverified.
- If the player is still loading, or has chat or their inventory open, the game rejects the popup. The pack retries every second for up to 30 seconds.
- Respawning after death does **not** show it. Only joining does.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:welcome` | Everyone | Shows the welcome message to yourself, like `/realm:welcome_show`. Operators get the **Welcome Message** menu instead: show, edit, reset and `Settings` |
| `/realm:welcome_show` | Everyone | Shows the welcome message to yourself (preview). Ignores `showOnce` |
| `/realm:welcome_edit` | Ops | Opens an editor: title, body (Minecraft's text boxes hold only 100 characters each, so the body is split over at least 4 boxes, joined in order with nothing between them; `\n` is a new line; all boxes empty = the default text; a body over 20000 characters isn't saved, and chat says so), button text, and toggles for show once, chat copy, big on-screen title and "Show it again to players who've seen it" (on by default; turn it off for a quiet fix). Saving changes only what you changed: a switch flipped in `/realm:config`, or another operator's edit made while your editor was open, stays. If chat or the inventory stays open, it retries for about 20 s and then says so once |
| `/realm:welcome_reset` | Ops | Asks `Reset the welcome message?` first, then discards in-game edits and goes back to the `config.js` defaults |

Every save from `/realm:welcome_edit` counts as a new revision. With **show once** turned on, everyone sees the edited message one more time.

### Placeholders

| Placeholder | Replaced with |
|---|---|
| `{player}` | The joining player's name |
| `{online}` | Number of players online |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `DEFAULTS`)

These are defaults. Once an op saves with `/realm:welcome_edit`, the saved values win until `/realm:welcome_reset`. The switches `showOnce`, `chat` and `screenTitle` are also in `/realm:config`, saved in the same place, so both menus always show the same values. Each player can disable the popup on join for themselves in `/realm:prefs` (`/realm:welcome` still shows it).

| Option | Default | In-game? | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `§l§6Welcome!` | ✅ | Popup title |
| `body` | `""` | ✅ | Empty means the installed-pack default below. A saved body replaces it with the operator's text, supporting placeholders and formatting |
| `button` | `§lClose` | ✅ | Close button text |
| `showOnce` | `false` | ✅ | `true` = only once per player, shown again after each edit (unless the edit turns that off). `false` = every join |
| `chat` | `false` | ✅ | Also post the title + body in that player's chat |
| `screenTitle` | `false` | ✅ | Also flash the title as big on-screen text |
| `delayTicks` | `40` | ❌ | Ticks after spawn before the first try (20 ticks = 1 s). Not editable in game, so a new value here always applies, edits or not |


### Default text (`scripts/config.js` -> `GENERIC`)

These file defaults apply to every world. They are not extra Realm Settings switches. Saved operator text wins after the one-time legacy migration.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `§l§6Welcome!` | Default popup title |
| `heading.world` | `The World` | First section |
| `heading.features` | `What You Can Do` | Installed-feature section |
| `heading.next` | `Where To Go Next` | Help and settings section |
| `greeting` | `Hey §b{player}§r, glad you're here! §7({online} online)§r` | Supports the player and online placeholders |
| `story` | A sleepy harbor town, its bell lost forty winters ago, ringing again, and strange stars | Exact spoiler-free paragraph in `config.js`; shown only with Story Questlines |
| `storyStart` | `Tap {who} in town to begin §eThe Lantern and the Hollow§r.` | Shown only with Story Questlines and Townsfolk, and only while at least one of `starters` is placed; `{who}` is their names joined with ` or ` |
| `starters.tobin` | `§bOld Tobin§r` | How the start line names Townsfolk `tobin`, the first prologue giver, when he is placed |
| `starters.mara` | `§bMara§r` | How the start line names Townsfolk `mara`, the second prologue giver, when she is placed |
| `noStory` | `A world to explore, build and play in together.` | Used without Story Questlines |
| `lines.quests_bp` | `Daily quests (§b/realm:quests§r)` | Shown only with Daily Quests |
| `lines.expedition_bp` | `Expeditions (§b/realm:expedition§r)` | Shown only with Expeditions |
| `lines.bounty_bp` | `A bounty board (§b/realm:bounty§r)` | Shown only with Bounty Board |
| `lines.town_bp` | `Towns that grow as you help, each with its mayor (§b/realm:town§r)` | Shown only with Town Projects |
| `lines.skills_bp` | `Skills that grow as you play (§b/realm:skills§r)` | Shown only with Skills |
| `lines.crowns_bp` | `Crowns to earn and spend (§b/realm:crowns§r)` | Shown only with Crowns |
| `lines.claims_bp` | `Land claims to keep your builds safe (§b/realm:claim§r)` | Shown only with Land Claims |
| `lines.calendar_bp` | `A calendar of seasons and festivals (§b/realm:calendar§r)` | Shown only with Realm Calendar |
| `lines.party_bp` | `Teams with friends (§b/realm:party§r)` | Shown only with Parties |
| `lines.mail_bp` | `Mail for other players (§b/realm:mail§r)` | Shown only with Realm Mail |
| `lines.map_bp` | `A minimap (§b/realm:map§r)` | Shown only with Minimap |
| `lines.stats_bp` | `Your play stats (§b/realm:stats§r)` | Shown only with Stats |
| `lines.journal_bp` | `A journal of what you have found (§b/realm:journal§r)` | Shown only with Field Journal |
| `next.help_bp` | `/realm:help lists everything this server adds.` | Shown only with Realm Help |
| `next.settings_bp` | `/realm:prefs holds your own settings, this popup included.` | Shown only with My Preferences |
| `next.saga_bp` | `/realm:saga opens your story log: quests, hints and the codex.` | Shown only with Story Questlines |
| `operators` | `Operators: /realm:welcome_edit changes this message.` | Operator directions come last |

### Legacy migration matcher (`scripts/config.js` -> `LEGACY_REALM`)

These identify the retired built-in message, not additional operator settings. They are used only before `welcome:migrated` is set.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sentence` | `Tap Old Tobin or Mara in town to begin` | The saved body must contain this exact phrase after color codes are stripped |
| `title` | `§l§6Welcome to the Realm!` | Only this old title is removed with the matching body |
| `button` | `§lLet's go!` | Only this old button is removed with the matching body |

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `welcome:settings` | World | JSON of in-game edits (only the fields that differ from `config.js`; a field set back to its `config.js` value is removed, so it follows later changes there) |
| `welcome:revision` | World | Increases on every save or reset |
| `welcome:migrated` | World | `1` after the one-time legacy-body migration. Checked on load and before showing or editing; later operator saves are never migrated again |
| `welcome:legacy` | World | JSON `{ body, title?, button?, noted? }`: what the one-time migration took out of the old saved welcome (`noted` once an operator was told). Deleted by `Restore it` or `Delete the copy` |
| `welcome:profile` | World | Retired. Deleted when the world loads |
| `welcome:seen` | Player | Last revision the player saw (used by `showOnce`) |
| `welcome:pref` | Player | JSON `{ popup: false }` when the player turned the popup on join off in `/realm:prefs` |

## Low Durability Warning — `durability_bp`

Warns players before a tool, weapon or armor piece breaks.

### How to use

1. Nothing to set up: hold or wear any tool, weapon or armor piece. At **10%** durability left a yellow warning appears above the hotbar with a soft chime; at **3%** a red "about to break!" warning, an anvil sound and the same line in chat.
2. Repair the item (Mending, an anvil) or swap it before it breaks. A repaired item warns again the next time it runs low.
3. Don't want the warnings? Run `/realm:durability` to turn them off for yourself; run it again to turn them back on. The same switch is in `/realm:prefs`. The choice is remembered.

### What players see

| Level | When | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| **Warning** | ≤ `warnPercent` (10%) left | Yellow message above the hotbar: `! Diamond Pickaxe is low: 141/1561 (9.0%)` + soft "pling" |
| **Critical** | ≤ `criticalPercent` (3%) left | Red message `! Diamond Pickaxe is about to break! 31/1561 (2.0%)` above the hotbar **and in chat** (`chatOnCritical`) + anvil sound |

- Checks the **main hand and offhand** at the next check (every `checkIntervalTicks`, half a second by default) after you mine, hit, use an item (a bow, a hoe, flint and steel...), switch hotbar slots or your inventory changes, and the **helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots** after you get hurt or put armor on from your inventory. A worn **elytra** is checked every fourth check (every 2 seconds), since gliding wears it with no event. A hand holding a **shield** or a **brush** is checked at every check, since a shield wears when it blocks a hit (which hurts no one) and a brush when brushing ends, both with no event. Every slot of every player is also checked once every 10 checks (5 seconds), for armor put on by a dispenser or a command.
- Warns **once per level**. It only warns again when the item drops to the next level.
- A different kind of item in that slot, emptying the slot, or a repair (Mending, an anvil, grindstone) that lifts it at least 2% of its durability above the level resets it, so a Mending tool hovering right at the line doesn't warn again and again. Another item of the same kind that's just as worn doesn't warn again.
- Each **hotbar slot** is tracked separately, so switching to another worn tool warns for that one too.
- Items without durability (blocks, torches, …) are ignored.
- Named items use their custom name (e.g. `Excalibur is low`).
- The [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) steps aside for 3 seconds so the warning stays readable.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:durability` | Everyone | Enables or disables warnings **for yourself**. Remembered between sessions. Chat says `Low-durability warnings: Disabled. Run /realm:durability again to enable them.` |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `warnPercent` | `10` | Warning level, in % of durability left |
| `criticalPercent` | `3` | Critical level, in % left |
| `maxUsesForWarning` | `0` | If > 0, never warn while more than this many uses are left, even under the % (useful for netherite). `0` = off |
| `chatOnCritical` | `true` | Also post critical warnings in chat |
| `checkIntervalTicks` | `10` | How often to check (20 = 1 s) the items players used, hit with or wore down since the last check; every slot of every player is checked once every 10 checks. Read when the world starts, so `/realm:config` only shows it |

Operators can change `warnPercent`, `criticalPercent`, `maxUsesForWarning` and `chatOnCritical` in game with `/realm:config`; they apply at the next check.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `durability:off` | Player | `true` when the player turned warnings off (`/realm:durability` or `/realm:prefs`) |
| `durability:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

## AFK + Smart Sleep — `afk_bp`

Marks idle players as AFK, and skips the night without waiting for them.

### How to use

1. **Going AFK:** just stop playing. After 5 minutes your name shows `[AFK]` and chat says so. To go AFK right away (so the night can be skipped without you), run `/realm:afk`.
2. **Coming back:** move or look around. Chat says you're back and, after 30 seconds or more, how many minutes you were marked AFK. Rather chat didn't announce you? Disable **Announce when I go AFK** in `/realm:prefs`.
3. **Skipping the night:** get in a bed. Players who are AFK, and players in the Nether or the End, aren't waited for. While anyone is in bed, Overworld players see how many are asleep out of how many are needed, above the hotbar, and, when only 1 to 3 counted players are still up, who they are (`Zzz 1/2 sleeping - awake: Sam`). Once everyone needed is in bed, it's morning within about 8 seconds, and rain or thunder stops.

### AFK detection

A player counts as **active** when they do any of these:

| Signal | Notes |
|---|---|
| Movement keys or stick | Checks the actual movement input, so being pushed by water streams, pistons or minecarts **doesn't** count. Tiny stick input (< 10%, controller drift) is ignored |
| Turning the camera | More than 0.5° |
| Breaking, placing, interacting with blocks or entities | |
| Using an item, hitting a block or entity | |
| Jumping or sneaking, changing hotbar slot | |

After `afkMinutes` (5) with none of these:

- The name above the player's head becomes `[AFK] Name` (`nameTagPrefix`). The prefix goes in front of whatever the name tag already shows, so a nickname or title from [Nicknames](#nicknames--nick_bp) stays.
- The player gets the `afk` tag (`tag`). Other packs and commands can use it, e.g. `@a[tag=!afk]`.
- Chat shows `Name is now AFK` (`announce`).

Any activity brings them back, with `Name is back (AFK 12m)` in chat (minutes since being marked AFK; left out under 30 seconds). Sleeping players are never marked AFK. Leftover AFK names or tags are cleared when a player rejoins, and after a script reload.

### Smart sleep (night skip)

Checked every second while at least one player is in bed:

1. **Counted players** = everyone asleep, plus every non-AFK player in the Overworld (also those in the Nether/End if `sleep.countOtherDimensions` is on).
2. **Needed** = `ceil(counted × sleep.percent / 100)`, at least 1.
3. While anyone is in bed, Overworld players see `Zzz 1/2 sleeping - awake: Sam (1 AFK ignored)` above the hotbar. The names show when 1 to 3 counted players are awake. The [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) steps aside for it.
4. **If vanilla's own rule already covers it**, i.e. enough players are asleep to meet the `playerssleepingpercentage` gamerule counting *everyone*, the pack does nothing and lets vanilla skip the night. That's always the case when nobody is AFK and everyone is in bed. Doing both would race, and the second skip would land a full day later.
5. Otherwise, once enough players have been asleep for `sleep.requiredTicks` (about 8 s, and never less than about 7 s, so vanilla's ~5 s skip always comes first):
   - **At night:** moves to the **next morning**. Absolute time moves forward, so the day counter (`showdaysplayed`) stays correct. The weather clears too.
   - **During a daytime thunderstorm:** only clears the weather. The game doesn't let packs read the weather, so the pack remembers the last change it saw (saved, so it survives a restart); a storm that started before the pack was installed isn't cleared.
   - Chat shows `Good morning! (1 AFK player skipped)`.

Lying in bed counts as activity, so a player who waits in bed for a long night isn't marked AFK when they get up.

This works **alongside** the vanilla `playerssleepingpercentage` gamerule: vanilla handles everything it can, and this pack only covers what vanilla wouldn't, such as nights blocked by AFK players or by players in other dimensions.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:afk` | Everyone | Marks you AFK right away. Anything you do in the next 3 seconds (closing chat, the camera settling) is ignored. After that, move to come back. With announcements off (`announce`, or yours in `/realm:prefs`), only you get a confirmation. Run it again while you're AFK and it answers `You're already AFK. Move to come back.` |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `afkMinutes` | `5` | Minutes without input before a player is marked AFK |
| `announce` | `true` | Post AFK / back messages in chat |
| `nameTagPrefix` | `§7[AFK]§r ` | Shown before the name above the player's head |
| `tag` | `afk` | Tag added while AFK. The Stats pack's `afkTag` must match |
| `sleep.enabled` | `true` | Skip the night when enough non-AFK players are in bed |
| `sleep.percent` | `100` | % of counted players that must be asleep |
| `sleep.countOtherDimensions` | `false` | Also count non-AFK players in the Nether/End (who can't sleep), like vanilla |
| `sleep.requiredTicks` | `160` | How long enough players must be asleep before skipping (20 = 1 s). Values below `140` are raised to `140`, so vanilla's ~100-tick skip always comes first |

Operators can change `afkMinutes`, `announce` and every `sleep.` option in game with `/realm:config`; they apply within a second. Each player can stop chat announcing them in `/realm:prefs`. With `announce` off, nobody is announced.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `afk:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `afk:pref` | Player | JSON `{ announce: false }` when the player turned their announcements off in `/realm:prefs` |
| `afk:thunder` | World | `true` while the last Overworld weather change seen was a thunderstorm (for clearing a daytime storm) |

AFK state itself isn't saved: it's kept in memory and resets on rejoin. While a player is AFK, their name tag and the `afk` tag are changed.

### Known limits

- Being fully AFK while in a vehicle with no input still counts as AFK, which is intended.
- Name-tag changes may clash with other packs that also change player name tags. [Nicknames](#nicknames--nick_bp) keeps the prefix in step (its `afkPrefix` must match `nameTagPrefix`).

## Stats & Leaderboards — `stats_bp`

Tracks player stats as scoreboards, with leaderboard menus, a stats ticker above each player's hotbar that each player sets up for themselves, and an optional sidebar for everyone.

With Realm Resources, the native sidebar sits in the vertically centered left-side group after the mob health and Elytra readouts. Its full native height contributes to centering; it is not given a one-row placeholder. Without Realm Resources, vanilla decides its placement. Rotation, scores, colors and the saved sidebar setting are unchanged; this does not enable a previously hidden board.

### How to use

1. Play: stats count on their own (playtime and distance, except while AFK; deaths; mob and player kills; blocks mined and placed; elytra distance; joins).
2. Run `/realm:stats` to open **Realm Stats**. **My stats** shows every stat, with your rank (`#2 of 7`) in each one you've scored in (players with the same score share a place, here, on the leaderboards and on the ticker), and the date you first joined (UTC); **Leaderboards** and a stat shows the top 10.
3. Your own stats show above your hotbar by default, one stat at a time, such as `Mob kills 120 #2 of 7`, changing every 5 seconds. Only you see yours. Tap **Stats ticker** in the same menu (or run `/realm:stats_ticker`) to turn yours off or on; `/realm:prefs` has the same switch.
4. Tap **My ticker settings** (or open `/realm:prefs`, the same settings) to choose which stats it shows (one switch each), how many seconds each stays, **One stat at a time** or **Every chosen stat on one line**, the full style or a compact one (`Kills 120`), and the colors of the names and the numbers. Your choices are remembered.
5. **Operators:** **Sidebar (everyone)** in `/realm:stats` (or `/realm:stats_sidebar <stat>`) picks what the sidebar shows: **Hidden**, one stat, or **Rotate through the stats**, how many seconds each stat stays and which stats the rotation includes. Bedrock shows the same sidebar to everyone, so players can't hide it for themselves; leave it **Hidden** and let players use the ticker if some don't want it. The stat IDs for the command are `playtime`, `deaths`, `mobkills`, `pvpkills`, `mined`, `placed`, `travelled`, `flown` and `joins`, plus `cycle` (rotate) and `off`, for example `/realm:stats_sidebar travelled`.
6. **Operators:** `/realm:config` → **Stats & Leaderboards** has all of that, plus the leaderboard size, **Allow the stats ticker** (`tickerEnabled`), **Stats ticker default** (`tickerDefaultOn`, enabled by default), and what every ticker setting starts as for players who haven't chosen. Disallowing the ticker hides it without erasing anybody's saved choice.

### Stats

| ID (for `/realm:stats_sidebar`) | Label | How it's counted |
|---|---|---|
| `playtime` | Playtime | +1 min per 60 s online. Paused while the player has the `afkTag` tag |
| `deaths` | Deaths | Player deaths |
| `mobkills` | Mob kills | Non-player entities killed by the player (arrows count for the shooter) |
| `pvpkills` | Player kills | Other players killed |
| `mined` | Blocks mined | Blocks broken by the player. Essentials+ tree felling and vein mining only count the first block |
| `placed` | Blocks placed | Blocks placed by the player |
| `travelled` | `Distance traveled` | Blocks moved, not gliding, measured every second. Includes walking, swimming, boats and minecarts. Not counted while AFK, so a water stream or minecart loop doesn't climb the board |
| `flown` | Elytra distance | Blocks moved while gliding |
| `joins` | Times joined | Each join |

- Movement faster than `maxSpeed` blocks/s is treated as a teleport and not counted. Respawning isn't counted either.
- Each stat is the scoreboard objective **`stats_<id>`** (e.g. `stats_deaths`). Scores are stored under the player's **name** (a "fake player" participant), not the player entity. Bedrock shows offline entity participants as "Player Offline", so this keeps real names on leaderboards and the sidebar when people are offline.
- Vanilla commands work too, e.g. `/scoreboard players list "Steve"`.
- If someone changes their gamertag, their stats start again under the new name, and the old name stays on the leaderboard.
- Scores from the first Stats pack (v1.0.0, before the Realm Bundle), which stored them on the player entity, move to the name automatically the next time that player joins. Until then they're hidden from the menus, and the vanilla sidebar may still show them as "Player Offline".
- First-joined date is saved per player, from the first join after the pack was added.

### The stats ticker

- **On until a player turns it off** (`tickerDefaultOn`, default enabled), with **Stats ticker** in `/realm:stats`, `/realm:stats_ticker` or **Stats ticker above my hotbar** in `/realm:prefs` (all the same switch). An explicit on or off stays saved even if it matches the realm default; later default changes affect only players who never chose. Existing saved realm defaults and player choices are kept. While an operator disallows it (`tickerEnabled`), nobody sees it, and the menu and `/realm:stats_ticker` say `The stats ticker is disabled on this realm.`
- **Older off choices:** the old helper erased a choice equal to the default. An off choice made while the default was off may therefore have no saved record; it cannot be distinguished from never choosing. If it comes back after updating, turn it off once more. Choices that were actually saved are preserved.
- **Which stats:** one switch per stat, **Ticker shows Playtime** and so on. Players start with Playtime, Deaths, Mob kills, Blocks mined and Distance traveled (`tickerStats`). With none chosen, the ticker shows nothing.
- **Speed:** **Ticker seconds per stat**, 2 to 60 (default 5, `tickerSeconds`), when it shows **One stat at a time** (`tickerMode`). **Every chosen stat on one line** shows them all at once, which gets long with many stats in the full style.
- **Style:** **Name, value and rank** (`Mob kills 120 #2 of 7`) or **Compact: short name and value** (`Kills 120`, with the short names `Time`, `Deaths`, `Kills`, `PvP`, `Mined`, `Placed`, `Walked`, `Flown` and `Joins`) (`tickerStyle`).
- **Colors:** **Ticker name color** (default gray) and **Ticker number color** (default white): White, Gray, Dark gray (dim), Gold, Yellow, Green, Aqua, Blue, Light purple or Red (`tickerLabelColor`, `tickerValueColor`). Dark gray for both is the closest to a faint, see-through ticker.
- **Transparency:** scripts can't change how see-through the bar's dark background is. Each player sets that in Bedrock's own **Settings > Accessibility > Text Background Opacity**, which also changes chat and other text backgrounds.
- **Sharing the bar:** the ticker uses the bar above the hotbar, like other packs' short notes. It waits while one is showing (packs that send `realm:actionbar`, such as Mob Health and the Elytra HUD while you glide) and redraws right after. With the [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) on, the ticker is a second line under your coordinates instead, so the two don't take turns.
- It checks your stats once a second and resends the line every 2 seconds, so it doesn't fade. A new stat, a setting you change or the end of another pack's note shows at once; a number that changed on the same stat (your distance while you walk) shows with the next resend, within 2 seconds. Your own rank moves as soon as your score does; the other players' scores behind it can be up to 5 seconds old.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:stats` | Everyone | Opens **Realm Stats**: **My stats** (every stat with your rank `#2 of 7`, plus first-joined date), **Leaderboards** (pick a stat to see the top 10, `leaderboardSize`, with your own position underneath if you're outside it), **Stats ticker** (shows or hides yours), **My ticker settings** (which stats, seconds per stat, style and colors). Operators also get **Sidebar (everyone)** |
| `/realm:stats_ticker` | Everyone | Shows or hides your own stats above the hotbar (default on, `tickerDefaultOn`). Your choice is remembered between sessions and across later default changes. Says so when an operator has disallowed the ticker for the realm (`tickerEnabled`) |
| `/realm:stats_sidebar <stat>` | Ops | Shows a stat on everyone's sidebar. `<stat>` is a stat ID, **`cycle`** (rotates through the chosen stats every 30 seconds, `sidebarCycleSeconds`, `sidebarStats`) or **`off`** (hides it). The same setting as **Sidebar (everyone)** |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `afkTag` | `afk` | Playtime isn't counted while a player has this tag. Must match the AFK pack's `tag`. `""` = always count |
| `leaderboardSize` | `10` | Number of players on a leaderboard |
| `sidebar` | `off` | What everyone's sidebar shows until an operator chooses: `off`, `cycle` or a stat ID |
| `sidebarCycleSeconds` | `30` | Seconds per stat in `cycle` mode |
| `sidebarStats` | every stat | The stats the sidebar rotates through in `cycle` mode |
| `tickerEnabled` | `true` | Allow the stats ticker. Disabled: nobody sees it, whatever they chose; their saved choices are kept |
| `tickerDefaultOn` | `true` | Show the ticker to players who never chose. This Realm starts with it on |
| `tickerMode` | `cycle` | What players start with: `cycle` (one stat at a time) or `all` (every chosen stat on one line) |
| `tickerSeconds` | `5` | What players start with: seconds per stat in `cycle` mode (2 to 60 in game) |
| `tickerStyle` | `full` | What players start with: `full` (name, value and rank) or `compact` (short name and value) |
| `tickerLabelColor` | `gray` | What players start with: the color of the stat names. One of `white`, `gray`, `dark_gray`, `gold`, `yellow`, `green`, `aqua`, `blue`, `light_purple`, `red` |
| `tickerValueColor` | `white` | What players start with: the color of the numbers (same colors) |
| `tickerStats` | `playtime`, `deaths`, `mobkills`, `mined`, `travelled` | What players start with: the stats the ticker shows |
| `maxSpeed` | `100` | Faster movement (blocks/s) counts as a teleport and isn't added to distance |

Operators can change every option except `afkTag` and `maxSpeed` in game with `/realm:config` (28 settings; `sidebarStats` and `tickerStats` as one switch per stat, such as **Sidebar rotation includes Deaths** and **Ticker shows Deaths (players start with)**). A new cycle length applies from the next second. Each player chooses their own ticker (on or off, mode, seconds, style, both colors and a switch per stat: 15 preferences) in `/realm:prefs` or **My ticker settings**; a player who never chose follows the realm's value, including later changes to it.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `stats_playtime`, `stats_deaths`, `stats_mobkills`, `stats_pvpkills`, `stats_mined`, `stats_placed`, `stats_travelled`, `stats_flown`, `stats_joins` | World scoreboard | The stats, one participant per player name. **Kept** when switching between the individual pack and a bundle |
| `stats:sidebar` | World | Current sidebar choice (`<stat>`, `cycle` or `off`) when it differs from `sidebar`. Set by `/realm:stats_sidebar`, **Sidebar (everyone)** and `/realm:config` |
| `stats:firstJoin` | Player | First join time (ms since epoch) |
| `stats:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's ticker choices. An explicit `ticker` on/off is always retained; other settings are kept when they differ from the realm's. Existing valid choices and unknown fields are preserved |
| `stats:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- The sidebar is a scoreboard display slot, which Bedrock has one of per world: everyone sees the same sidebar, and scripts can't hide it for one player. That's why the per-player display is the ticker on the bar above the hotbar (`onScreenDisplay.setActionBar`), which is each player's own.
- Once a second the pack builds each ticker from the player's own score, read then. Every player's ticker is handled in that one pass (spreading players over 4 passes a second was measured slower), from a list of the players online kept by join and leave events. A player's bar is written only when the stat shown, the place (bar or HUD) or a setting changed, after another pack's note, or 2 seconds after the last write (the refresh, which also carries a changed number), since writing the bar is the ticker's biggest cost. In the seconds between, and while another pack's note holds the bar, no score is read for that player. Ranks in the full style come from each board read at most once every 5 seconds for everyone, however many tickers are on (a board holds everyone who ever played); the player's own live score is placed in it with a binary search. Drawing on its own, the ticker is the bottom line of the action bar protocol: it writes without a `realm:actionbar` request and waits for every other pack's. While the [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) is on for that player, it sends the line to the HUD with the script event `realm:hud_line` (`{"player":"<id>","key":"stats","text":"...","ticks":80}`) instead of drawing it; the HUD says who sees it with `realm:hud_state`. The packs don't import each other: without the HUD, the ticker draws on its own.

### Resetting stats

Use vanilla commands (cheats needed):

- `/scoreboard players reset * stats_deaths` resets one stat for everyone.
- `/scoreboard players reset "Steve" stats_deaths` resets it for one player.
- `/scoreboard objectives remove stats_deaths` removes the stat entirely.

 The pack recreates missing objectives automatically.
