## Quick Stack & Sort — `stash_bp`

Sneak-tap a chest, barrel or shulker box with an empty hand to sort it at once; holding a tool, weapon or armor opens its menu to sort, lock or quick stack into storage that already holds each item (like Terraria). The **5 native-persistent inventory pages** share your hotbar, have previous/menu/next controls together at the top right, and let you move a stack or whole row to a page you choose. When the viewed page has at most one free slot, auto-store routes new pickups through the other pages; **Fill earlier pages** tidies all later pages on demand without sorting them.

### How to use

1. **Sort storage:** sneak and tap a chest, trapped chest, copper chest, barrel or shulker box with an empty hand. It sorts at once and the bar says `Sorted 31 stacks`. **Open the menu:** sneak-tap holding a tool, weapon or armor. An ender chest gets the menu with an empty hand too. A **Quick Stack & Sort** menu opens instead of the container, with these buttons:
   - **Sort this chest** (or barrel, shulker box): the same as the empty-hand sort.
   - **Lock this chest:** only you can open, sort or break it. Once it's yours, the button reads **Share or unlock**: share it with players who are online, stop sharing, or unlock it.
   - **Quick stack my inventory:** the same as `/realm:stash`, below.
   - **Sort my inventory:** the same as `/realm:sort`, below.
2. **Quick stack:** stand near your storage and run `/realm:stash`. Every item in your main inventory goes into a chest, copper chest or barrel within 8 blocks that already holds the same item. Your gear, shulker boxes, bundles, totems, maps and compasses stay with you. The bar says `Stashed 143 items into 3 chests`, and each container that got something sparkles.
3. **Sort your inventory:** run `/realm:sort`. Your main inventory is sorted; the hotbar stays as it is.
4. **Your way:** in `/realm:prefs`, choose what sneak-tapping a container does for you (**When I sneak-tap a container**: `Empty hand sorts, gear opens menu`, `Sort it right away` with an empty hand or gear, or `Nothing (opens as usual)`), and whether sorting your inventory includes your hotbar.
5. **Help:** run `/realm:stash_help` for a page that explains the menu, chest locks and every command with its usage. `/help realm:stash` and `/help realm:sort` also describe them.
6. **Inventory pages:** open your inventory. The last three slots of the main inventory's top row hold `<` (previous page), the current page number/menu, and `>` (next page), together from left to right. A page change replaces the other 24 slots. The hotbar, armor and offhand are the same on every page. `/realm:inv` opens a menu with every page and how full it is, **Scan all items across pages** (pick an item to jump to a page that holds it), **Move to page**, **Sort this page**, **Quick stack to nearby chests** and **Inventory settings**. Click the menu button, then close your inventory, and the same menu opens. **Move to page** asks for a stack or a whole row of your current page, then a destination. The top row has six usable slots; the other two rows have nine each. Matching stacks fill first, then empty slots. The whole move is refused if it cannot fit, a chosen stack changed, or you left, died, changed dimension or switched page. Your hotbar, cursor and page controls never move.
7. **Hotbar refill from other pages:** with [Hotbar Refill](#hotbar-refill--refill_bp) on, a hotbar stack you use up is refilled from another page when the page you're on has none (`realm:refill_need` `{ player, slot, id, name?, lore?, loreHash? }`, the lore cut to its first 1500 characters and `loreHash` a hash of all of it: the fullest stack on another page with the same item, name and lore moves into that empty hotbar slot, in one saved step like a page switch). Tipped arrows, ominous bottles, banners and firework stars never come from another page (what tells them apart isn't compared), and nothing is moved for a player who just died.
8. **Auto-store:** when the viewed page has at most one free slot, genuinely new pickup amounts try the other pages in order, each page's compatible stacks before its empty slots. Routing stops once the viewed page has two free slots; while it has more room, pickups stay there. Your hotbar stays as it is. **Fill earlier pages** in `/realm:inv` pulls items from every later page toward page 1, in page and slot order without sorting; it also works with auto-store disabled.
9. **Settings:** in `/realm:prefs` or **Inventory settings**, turn the in-inventory buttons (`invButtons`) and auto-store (`autoStore`) off for yourself. With the buttons off you still switch pages with `/realm:inv`. **Expansive inventory (5 pages)** (`invOff`, on by default) switches the extra pages off entirely: you get a normal 27-slot inventory with no buttons, and the items on pages 2 and up move back to page 1 or your hotbar. If there is no room, overflow stays safely saved until you make room or re-enable those pages; it is not dropped on the ground. `/realm:inv` has a one-click **Use normal inventory (turn off pages)** button, and **Enable Expansive Inventory (5 pages)** brings the pages and buttons back. Operators' personal page count (`/realm:inv_pages`, or the slider in **Inventory settings**) also takes `1` for a normal inventory.
10. **Operators:** sneak-tap someone else's locked container holding gear for **Remove the lock (operator)**. To switch chest locks off for the realm, disable **Chest locks** in `/realm:config` (existing locks are kept for when they're enabled again). `/realm:inv_pages <count>` gives you your own number of pages (2 to 25, `1` for a single page with no buttons, `0` to follow the realm again) without changing everyone else's; **Inventory pages** in `/realm:config` (`pages`, 1 to 15) sets the realm's. If a failed inventory save has paused a player's pages, back up the world, run `/realm:inv_recover <player>` for that online player, and read its confirmation: it lists the stacks from the retained before-image that the player no longer carries (a stack they kept in their inventory, on the cursor, as armor or in the offhand, or the part of one they kept, is left out). A tool, armor piece or other single item they still have one of but used, renamed, enchanted or dyed since is listed apart as changed: **Export to chests** leaves those out, **Also export the changed items** copies them too (a second copy if it is the same item, so ask the player first). Confirming puts only those stacks into empty chest spots near you; it never takes anything from the player. While the player is dead it refuses: run it again once they have respawned. If it stops part way, run it again: it places only what it hasn't placed yet, never refilling a stack someone already took out of a chest.

### What players see

- **Inventory pages (Expansive Inventory):** with `pages` at its default of `5`, your main inventory (slots 9 to 35) is five pages of 24 slots, 120 slots in all, plus the hotbar, which is shared by every page. All pages are open from the start. The buttons sit together in slots 15 (previous), 16 (current page/menu), and 17 (next): `Page 5/5 (Prev)`, `Page 1/5 Inventory Menu`, `Page 2/5 (Next)`. Previous and next show their destinations; the middle button shows the committed active page. Clicking one (or dropping it, or shift-clicking it out of its slot) restores the control and requests its action, and the bar says `[Page #2/5] 2/24 slots used`. A button that ends up in your hand when you right-click it goes back to its slot and does its job too. Buttons can't be dropped, and `/realm:sort` and `/realm:stash` never touch them.
- **Native, durable pages:** every stack belongs to its page, including filled shulker boxes, bundles, potions, maps, books, fireworks and trimmed armor. Inactive pages preserve native item data in World structure snapshots, not a script's memory or a partial JSON item copy. They survive logging out, dying on another page and clean server restarts without being dropped. A page and both inventory images are saved and restored for readback before live slots change. An error cancels the switch and rolls the inventory back; if recovery itself fails, the durable recovery images are retained and the pack reports it rather than silently discarding data.
- **Items on the cursor and button slots:** only a page-button item is cleared from the cursor; ordinary held items are untouched. A real item placed in a button slot is moved to the current page, hotbar or another page. If all storage is full, it stays in that slot and the pack asks you to move it; the button never overwrites it.
- **Fewer pages:** when your page count goes down (an operator lowers `pages`, you run `/realm:inv_pages 1`, or you disable extra pages), you are moved to page 1 and saved items move into your current inventory, hotbar or remaining pages. Overflow stays durably saved on its original page and is retried once a second while your inventory is changing, and every 5 seconds otherwise; re-enabling the pages also makes it accessible. Merely hiding buttons does not remove pages. Slots 15, 16 and 17 are ordinary slots while buttons are absent.
- **Auto-store** (`autoStore`) looks every half second while your inventory is changing (for a second after any change) and every 25 seconds otherwise. Only new amounts attributable to an acquisition move, and only while the viewed page has 1 or no free slots. Other pages are tried earliest first, each page's compatible partial stacks before its empty slots, until two viewed-page slots are free. A saved page with no free slot and no stack of that item with room left is skipped without being loaded (the page index records which items each page could still top up). Hotbar pickups stay there; moving existing items between the hotbar, main slots, cursor or worn gear is not a pickup. To tell the two apart it compares everything you carry (page, hotbar, cursor, worn gear) between looks, but only while the viewed page has 4 or fewer free slots; with more room a look reads just the page. If one look sees the page go from 5 or more free slots to 1 or none at once (a broken chest, mob loot, or several pickups between two quiet 25-second looks), every new stack on the page counts as a pickup and is routed, since there is nothing to compare the rest with; in that one case a stack you moved from the hotbar onto the page within that look goes to another page too (nothing is lost). Turning auto-store off and back on does not route items acquired while it was off. A failed save reports the error and discards its old pickup baseline rather than retrying it as another acquisition.
- **Fill earlier pages:** available whenever you have more than one page, including while viewing page 1. It pulls from pages 2 through your last page in page/slot order, preserving names, lore and native data without alphabetical sorting. Slot-locked stacks, the hotbar and controls never move. All changed pages commit together or the move is rolled back.
- **The menu** shows how full the container is and how full your inventory is (`Barrel - 18 of 27 slots used`, `Your inventory - 22 of 27 slots used`). Close it to do nothing. Holding anything other than gear (a block, a hopper, honeycomb) skips both sorting and the menu, so sneak-placing a hopper on a chest or waxing a copper chest works as usual. To scrape a copper chest with an axe, don't sneak.
- **Move to page** moves a selected stack or whole row without sorting either page. Native names, lore, enchantments, damage, filled shulker contents and potion data stay intact. A full or unreadable destination, changed stack, stale form or pending recovery leaves the source untouched. Slot-locked stacks are refused. The menu uses one ordinary durable page transaction, including verified snapshots and rollback/quarantine; manual moves do not create pickup signals.
- **Ender chests** get the menu without **Sort this**: add-ons can't see inside an ender chest, so it can't be sorted or stashed into.
- **Sorting** merges partial stacks of the same item, then orders the slots by item id, the biggest stack first, with empty slots at the end. A chest with 3 partial stacks of cobblestone ends with 1 full stack plus the rest.
- Items with a custom name, lore or enchantments are never merged, only moved, and moving keeps every item exactly as it was: enchanted gear, named items, written books, filled maps, banners and shulker boxes with their contents.
- `/realm:stash` only takes from your main inventory (slots 9–35): never the hotbar, armor or offhand. It also leaves you your gear (anything with durability: tools, weapons, armor, elytra; `stashGear`), named items (`stashNamedItems`) and everything in `keepItems`: shulker boxes, bundles, the totem of undying, filled maps, compasses and clocks. A container that holds the item gets matching stacks topped up first, then its empty slots, nearest container first.
- **What receives stashes:** chests, trapped chests, copper chests and barrels (`stashTypes`). Placed shulker boxes don't: they're a kit you pick up and carry, so they only get the menu and sorting.
- Double chests (copper ones too) count once. Ender chests never receive anything. Containers in chunks that aren't loaded are never touched. Another player having the chest open is fine.
- Containers you can't open get nothing: someone else's locked container, and any container in someone else's [Land Claims](#land-claims--claims_bp) claim, so nothing lands where you couldn't take it back. When those are the only ones around, the bar says `Nothing to stash: the containers nearby aren't yours to open`.
- Each player can sort or stash once per second (`cooldownTicks`). A menu button pressed sooner says `Too fast. Try again in a moment.`

#### Chest locks

- **Locking** (`locks`, enabled): the menu's **Lock this chest** (or barrel, copper chest, shulker box…) locks it to you; the bar says `Locked: only you can open this chest`. Both halves of a double chest are locked, and a chest added next to a locked one later is locked with it.
- **Someone else's locked container** doesn't open for anyone else: they see `Locked by Sam` above the hotbar. Their sneak-tap menu shows `Chest: locked by Sam.` with only the inventory buttons. They can't break it, `/realm:stash` never puts anything in it, and nobody else can place a hopper or a chest right next to it (a hopper could drain it; a chest could join it into a double chest).
- **Sharing:** **Share or unlock** lists the players online now (up to 10 per container, `maxShared`); a shared player can open, sort and break it like you, and sees `Locked by Sam, shared with Alex` in the menu. The same menu stops sharing or unlocks it.
- Explosions never break a locked container; the blast still hurts as usual.
- Each player can have up to 50 locked containers (`maxLocks`); a double chest counts once.
- Breaking a locked container (you can, as its owner) removes its lock. Breaking one half of a locked double chest leaves the other half locked, and it still counts once toward `maxLocks`.
- **What a lock can't stop:** a hopper (or hopper minecart) that was already under it before it was locked, a copper golem that takes from a locked copper chest, and pistons. [Chest Finder](#chest-finder--find_bp) doesn't list a locked container for anyone who can't open it.
- Locks only show in the sneak-tap menu while holding a tool, weapon or armor. A player who chose `Sort it right away` or `Nothing (opens as usual)` locks nothing until they switch back to `Empty hand sorts, gear opens menu`. Existing locks still hold. Sorting and opening an editable storage menu ask the Claims/locks access protocol before acting, whichever pack loads first. Gear can still show a locked container's owner and your own inventory actions without granting access to its contents.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:stash` | Everyone | Quick stack: puts your main inventory into chests and barrels within 8 blocks that already hold the same items, keeping your gear and carried items. Same as the menu's **Quick stack my inventory** |
| `/realm:sort` | Everyone | Sorts your inventory, slots 9–35. The hotbar is untouched, unless you turned that on in `/realm:prefs` (default off, `sortHotbar`). Same as the menu's **Sort my inventory** |
| `/realm:stash_help` | Everyone | Opens the help page: the sneak-tap menu, then each command with its usage and what it never touches |
| `/realm:inv` | Everyone | Opens the Expansive Inventory menu: your current page (`Page #1 of 5`), every page with how many of its 24 slots are used (click one to switch), **Scan all items across pages**, **Move to page** (one stack or whole row, all or nothing), **Sort this page**, **Quick stack to nearby chests** and **Inventory settings**. When your inventory screen is open it waits and appears as soon as you close it |
| `/realm:inv_pages [pages]` | Operators | Sets how many pages you have, only for yourself (`pages`: 0 to 25; with no number, `0`, which follows the realm's `pages`, default `5`): `2` to `25` is your own total, `1` is one vanilla page with no buttons, `0` or no number follows the realm's setting again. Items on pages that go away move to the pages you keep. The realm's setting is not changed |
| `/realm:inv_recover <player>` | Operators | Shows the stacks from one online player's retained failed-save before-image that they no longer carry (inventory, cursor, armor and offhand count as carried; a single item of the same type that was used, renamed, enchanted or dyed since is listed apart and exported only with **Also export the changed items**), then, after confirmation, puts only those into empty chest spots near you and clears that recovery journal. Proven page controls are omitted; real items and native metadata are kept. Their live inventory is untouched and nothing they still carry is copied. A run that stopped part way continues where it stopped. No normal save or healthy inventory is recovered by this command |

`/realm:stash`, `/realm:sort` and `/realm:stash_help` take no parameters. The help page follows the settings in force, yours from `/realm:prefs` included; the `/help` description of `/realm:stash` follows `stashRadius` in `config.js`.

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `stashRadius` | `8` | Blocks around the player to look for containers (a 17 × 17 × 17 cube) |
| `containerTypes` | chest, trapped chest, copper chest (all 8: every stage, waxed or not), barrel, placed shulker boxes (all 17 colors) | Block ids that get the sneak-tap menu and can be sorted. Ender chests get the menu regardless and are never sorted or stashed into |
| `stashTypes` | chest, trapped chest, copper chest (all 8), barrel | Block ids that receive `/realm:stash`. Ids this game version doesn't have are skipped. Shulker boxes are left out on purpose |
| `sneakTap` | `"menu"` | `"menu"` sorts with an empty hand and opens the menu with gear in hand; an ender chest gets the menu because it cannot be sorted. `"sort"` sorts with an empty hand or gear (no menu, no ender chests). `"off"` does nothing so it opens as usual. With `"menu"` or `"sort"`, sneak-tapping never opens the container |
| `stashNamedItems` | `false` | `/realm:stash` also moves items with a custom name |
| `stashGear` | `false` | `/realm:stash` also moves gear: anything with durability (tools, weapons, armor, elytra, shields…) |
| `keepItems` | shulker boxes (17), bundles (17), `totem_of_undying`, `filled_map`, `compass`, `lodestone_compass`, `recovery_compass`, `clock`, `custom:inv_prev`, `custom:inv_menu`, `custom:inv_next` | Item ids `/realm:stash` never moves (the last three are the inventory page buttons) |
| `sortHotbar` | `false` | `/realm:sort` and the menu's **Sort my inventory** also sort the hotbar |
| `pages` | `5` | Expansive Inventory: how many pages of the main inventory everyone has, 1 to 15 (`1` = the vanilla inventory, no buttons). Each page is 24 slots. Operators can set their own with `/realm:inv_pages` |
| `invButtons` | `true` | The three page buttons together in slots 15, 16 and 17 of the inventory's top row. Each player can turn them off for themselves in `/realm:prefs` |
| `autoStore` | `true` | Only when the viewed page has at most one free slot, route genuine pickup amounts through other pages earliest first until two slots are free. Each player can turn it off in `/realm:prefs` |
| `cooldownTicks` | `20` | Minimum time between sorts and stashes per player (20 = 1 s). Opening the menu, the help page or a lock button doesn't count |
| `locks` | `true` | Chest locks: the sneak-tap menu's **Lock this chest**. Disabled: no lock buttons and no lock is enforced; the locks are kept and apply again once it's enabled |
| `maxLocks` | `50` | Most containers one player can have locked at a time (a double chest counts once) |
| `maxShared` | `10` | Most players one locked container can be shared with |

Operators can change `pages`, `invButtons`, `autoStore`, `sneakTap`, `sortHotbar`, `stashGear`, `stashNamedItems`, `cooldownTicks`, `locks` and `maxLocks` in game with `/realm:config`. Each player can choose their own `invOff` (shown as **Expansive inventory (5 pages)**), `invButtons`, `autoStore`, `sneakTap` and `sortHotbar` in `/realm:prefs`, which wins over the realm's for them. `stashRadius` and the lists stay in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `stash:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `stash:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's own `invOff`, `invButtons`, `autoStore`, `sneakTap` and `sortHotbar` from `/realm:prefs` |
| `stash:native` | Player | Versioned committed index: active page, active-image `layout: 2`, each page's World structure identifier, occupied slots and optional independent `layout: 2`, plus `idx` snapshot-bound item/name counts (`k`) and, since 1.8.9, the item/name kinds that have a stack with room left (`p`), capped at 30,000 bytes. An entry without `p` (written by 1.8.8 or older) is still used for counts; that page is loaded once when it might take an item, and rewritten with `p` the next time it changes. Unknown, stale or unindexed pages are read, never assumed empty. The optional rollback journal keeps native before/after images; `pending.out` is `{ d, p, x?, f? }`: the export dimension and chest spots, the plan of what the player no longer carries (`x`, before-image `[slot, count]` pairs) and the plan indexes already placed (`f`), saved before recovery starts. A journal from 1.8.7 or older has no `x` and finishes exporting its whole before-image in the old chest layout. Missing layout fields mean the old layout for that image only. Empty references prevent old JSON being restored twice |
| `stash:snapshot_next` | World | Monotonically allocated native snapshot identifier; `stash:page_<n>` structures use World save mode and contain an inert, private native inventory entity |
| `stash:cur` | Player | Legacy active-page number, read only before the native index exists (absent = page 1) |
| `stash:page:<n>` | Player | Legacy saved JSON stacks. Large pages use `#<count>` plus `stash:page:<n>:<k>` chunks. Each page is validated in full and migrated to native snapshots on use; original legacy properties are shadowed, not treated as a second source of items |
| `stash:op_pages` | Player | An operator's own page count from `/realm:inv_pages` (absent = the realm's `pages`) |
| `stash:lock:<dimension>:<x>,<y>,<z>` | World | One per locked block (both halves of a double chest): JSON `{ o, n, s, h? }`, the owner's id and name, the players it's shared with (`[{ i, n }]`), and `h: 1` on a double chest's second half so it counts once |

### How it works

- **Inventory pages:** the active page is the real inventory; inactive pages are native `realm:stash_page_store` inventories captured in `StructureSaveMode.World` snapshots. Snapshot creation and restoration are verified before any live inventory mutation. A single player dynamic property commits all changed page references, layout, active-page number, and matching controls together. A failed or interrupted rollback retains native before/after images and pauses page operations for operator recovery. These images are never replayed automatically: matching visible item signatures cannot prove that items were not dropped or that hidden contents stayed unchanged. The player is notified once per session, not every tick. Operators can export what the player lost with `/realm:inv_recover`: it compares the before-image with the live inventory, the stack held on the cursor and the worn armor and offhand (by everything a script can read about a stack, ignoring its size, so part of a stack counts) and exports only the difference (it refuses while the player is dead and asks to be run again after they respawn, and anything they dropped or stored elsewhere since counts as missing, which the form says). A before-image item with a stack size of 1 that matches nothing exactly while a live item of the same type is left over (most likely the same tool or armor, used, renamed, enchanted or dyed since) is listed apart as changed and exported only when the operator picks **Also export the changed items**. Saved pages are not compared: they stay frozen while a journal is pending, so the before-image was never on them. The plan (before-image slot and count) and the chest spots are saved in the journal (`pending.out.x`, `pending.out.p`) before the first chest, and every stack placed is recorded (`pending.out.f`) after each chest, so an interrupted export continues in the same chests and never places a stack twice, even one someone took out in between; a slot already holding the planned kind counts as placed. An export started by an older version (no saved plan) keeps exporting its whole before-image in the same layout. Recovery refuses a changed journal or a live inventory that changed while the form was open, a stale operator form or a different recorded dimension, and retries its form while the operator's chat is still closing. Hidden contents (a shulker box's items) can't be compared, so a kept shulker box of the same look counts as kept. The images stay in the world as `stash:page_<n>` structures; a `realm:stash_page_store` entity loaded by hand is removed at once, so do not use `/structure load` to recover it. No JavaScript map owns saved items. For a second after an inventory or setting change the pack checks slots 15, 16 and 17 every two ticks, otherwise every 5 seconds (spread over the ticks); inventory events also observe live slots/cursor and queue distinct gestures in order, with writes deferred outside event dispatch. Historical event payloads cannot request extra switches, and a co-observed clear restores controls without navigating. Only actual button items are cleared from the cursor. The menu button opens `/realm:inv`; each busy retry rebuilds the body, active marker, usage and corresponding action list together. `/realm:sort`, `/realm:stash` and menu sorting skip button slots. Button textures remain in `build_rp`.
- **Snapshots in every dimension:** snapshots are placed with the `structure load` command, because the script API's structure placement puts entities into the Overworld while a player is in the Nether or the End. Any `realm:stash_page_store` entity found outside a save or load is a leftover and is removed (it never holds the only copy). The staging spot is 8 to 32 blocks above the player, moved aside when something is in the way; a player whose save can't be staged (an unloaded chunk right after a teleport) waits 2 seconds before the next try, and the same warning is logged at most once a minute.
- **Slot-layout upgrade (1.7.0):** old pageable slots `[10,11,12,14,15,16,18..35]` map by logical order to `[9,10,11,12,13,14,18..35]`. Active images migrate transactionally before new controls appear; each inactive native image keeps its own layout marker and migrates on access, as does validated old JSON. Full 27-slot normal/hidden-button inventories retain real items occupying old or new control positions; enabling controls rescues reserved-slot items into the hotbar or native pages without overwriting them. Interrupted transactions retain the same quarantine behavior. Back up the world before upgrading, and do not downgrade a world with layout-2 saves to an older stash pack that does not understand them.
- **Validation limit:** delayed script events, ordered gestures, busy-menu retries, layout upgrades, opaque items and real server restarts have headless/native regression coverage. Physical open-inventory mouse/touch transactions remain unverified; simulated slot mutations are not client acceptance.
- **Upgrading from 1.6.2 or 1.6.3:** those releases can hold inactive shulker boxes, potions and other opaque stacks only in RAM. Before stopping/reloading a server that is still running either release, each affected player should open every page with `/realm:inv` and move its items into ordinary placed chests, without disconnecting between pages. Alternatively, operators can run `/realm:inv_pages 1` while that old script is still alive to return extra-page items, but must collect any overflow it drops at their feet before the restart. Only then install the update. The new release migrates saved JSON; it cannot reconstruct RAM items already lost by an earlier restart or failed disconnect drop.
- **Menu:** `world.beforeEvents.playerInteractWithBlock` cancels the tap when the player is sneaking, the hand is empty or holds an item with a `minecraft:durability` component, and the block is a listed container or an ender chest. On the next tick an `ActionFormData` from `@minecraft/server-ui` shows the menu; a player can have one open at a time. The chosen action re-reads the block, so a container broken while the menu was open is left alone.
- **Sort:** stacks are merged by changing the amount of the slot that stays (`ContainerSlot.amount`) and ordered with `swapItems`. Both are native moves, so no item is ever copied or re-created and nothing about it can be lost.
- **Stash:** one `dimension.getBlocks` query finds the `stashTypes` containers in the cube (loaded chunks only), and they are read a few per tick with `system.runJob`. The pack then asks the other packs which of them the player may not open (`realm:access_check`, below) and leaves those out. Each main-inventory slot is then moved with `transferItem` into the nearest container holding that item, then the next.
- When both halves of a double chest report the whole 54 slots, the second half is recognized (same kind of chest, same contents, same facing, side by side; in a row of identical chests, counted from the row's end) and skipped. Copper chests of different stages count as the same kind.
- If `transferItem` ever hands a leftover back instead of leaving it in the slot, the pack puts it back, so nothing is lost.
- **Locks:** every lock is read into memory once and kept in step as it changes. `beforeEvents.playerInteractWithBlock` cancels opening someone else's locked container, and tapping a block with a hopper or chest in hand when the spot it would go is next to one (the stable API has no "before place" event, and placing starts with that tap). `beforeEvents.playerBreakBlock` cancels breaking it, and `beforeEvents.explosion` takes locked blocks out of the blast. A double chest's other half is found the same way as for stashing. A lock left where its block is gone some other way (a piston, a command) is removed when something is placed there.
- **Access checks:** packs that keep players out of blocks answer `realm:access_check` `{ id, player, spots: [[dim, x, y, z], ...] }` (at most 40 spots a message) with `realm:access_check_result` `{ id, from, closed: [i, ...] }`, the indexes of the spots that player may not open. This pack answers for someone else's locked container (none while `locks` is disabled), Land Claims for someone else's claim. Every check is answered, so an asker learns who answers: it waits for each pack that has answered before (2 seconds at most), or 5 ticks while none has; it says hello 3 seconds after the world loads. Quick stack asks; so do [Chest Finder](#chest-finder--find_bp) and [Chairs](#chairs--chairs_bp) (before seating someone on a stair or slab).
- Messages above the hotbar send `realm:actionbar` first, so the [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) leaves them on screen for a moment.

---

## Chest Finder — `find_bp`

Answers "which chest has the iron?" for a shared base: it remembers what each container held the last time anyone opened it, and points you to it.

### How to use

1. Open chests as usual. The pack quietly remembers what's in them.
2. Run `/realm:find iron`, or just `/realm:find` while holding the item. A menu lists the containers that have it, nearest first, for example `Chest - 23 Iron Ingot` with `35 blocks NE - seen 2h ago` under it.
3. Tap a result: a bright downward arrow above the container marks it for 10 seconds (`highlightSeconds`), and the bar above your hotbar says which way and how far, such as `Chest 12 blocks NE`. Only you see the arrow and line; chat still gives its coordinates. Marking another container replaces the first mark. Leaving, dying, changing dimension or reaching the timeout stops it. A container in another dimension only gets its coordinates in chat.

### What players see

- **Matching:** the item id first. `/realm:find diamond` finds diamonds only, because an item is called exactly that. When nothing is called exactly what you typed, every item whose id contains it is listed: `/realm:find iron` finds iron ingots, iron blocks, raw iron, iron swords and so on. Type one word, or use `_` for a space: `/realm:find iron_ingot` (or quote it: `/realm:find "iron ingot"`).
- **Always current nearby:** containers within `liveScanRadius` (16 blocks) are read at search time, so a chest filled by hoppers that nobody ever opened is still found. Farther ones show what they held when last seen, hence `seen 2h ago`: hoppers and the copper golem sorter may have changed them since.
- Results in your dimension are sorted by distance; containers in other dimensions are listed after them, without a distance.
- Copper chests count, in every stage, waxed or not, and the result names the exact one (`Waxed Oxidized Copper Chest`), which helps tell them apart.
- A double chest (copper ones too) is listed once. A broken container disappears from the results. One that was removed some other way (an explosion, say) disappears the next time a search finds its spot loaded and empty.
- Containers you can't open aren't listed: someone else's locked container ([Quick Stack & Sort](#quick-stack--sort--stash_bp)) and any container in someone else's [Land Claims](#land-claims--claims_bp) claim. Their owners (and the players they're shared with) still find them. When only such containers hold the item, chat says `Only containers you can't open (locked, or in someone else's claim) have "diamond".`
- Only containers and their contents are remembered, never who opened them.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:find [item]` | Everyone | Searches remembered and nearby containers for `item` (any part of an item id), or for the item in your hand if you leave it out |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `liveScanRadius` | `16` | Containers this close (blocks) are read live at search time, so nearby results are always current |
| `maxContainers` | `2000` | Most containers remembered; the ones seen longest ago are forgotten first |
| `maxResults` | `20` | Rows in the results menu |
| `highlightSeconds` | `10` | How long the bright arrow and direction line show |
| `privateIndex` | `true` | Players find only containers they opened themselves (or that were shared with them). `false` = the old world-wide index, where anyone finds any remembered container they may open. A world where Chest Finder had already saved an index or its settings before this option was added is set to `false` once, so it keeps the world-wide index until an operator turns this on. Only Chest Finder's own saved data counts: other packs' data (in the Realm Bundle they share one store and write when a world loads) never makes a new world look old |
| `containerTypes` | chest, trapped chest, copper chest (all 8: every stage, waxed or not), barrel, placed shulker boxes (all 17 colors) | Block ids that are remembered and searched. Ids this game version doesn't have are skipped |

Operators can change `liveScanRadius`, `maxResults` and `highlightSeconds` in game with `/realm:config`; they apply to the next search.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `find:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `find:mig` | World | Set once the world's index mode (private or world-wide) was decided, from `find:idx:0` and `find:cfg` alone. Old worlds keep the world-wide index until an operator changes `privateIndex` |
| `find:idx:0`, `find:idx:1`, ... | World | The index as JSON shards under 30,000 characters each: `{ "<dimension>:<x>,<y>,<z>": { t: [[itemId, count], …], at: epochMs, b: blockId, w: [openers], o: [placers] } }`, ids without the `minecraft:` prefix. `w` (who opened it) and `o` (who placed it) are kept separately, up to 8 each. Written at most once every 30 seconds, and whenever a player leaves |

### How it works

- **Remembering:** on `world.afterEvents.playerInteractWithBlock` with a listed container, its contents are counted per item id right away, again 10 seconds later, after the player has put things in or taken them out, and once more after a minute, for long sorting sessions. `playerBreakBlock` removes the entry. Empty containers aren't kept. A save serializes only the entries that changed since the last one.
- **Searching:** one `dimension.getBlocks` query finds the containers within `liveScanRadius`, which are read a few per tick with `system.runJob`, then the whole index is matched in one pass and sorted by distance. The nearest matches (twice `maxResults`) are checked with Quick Stack & Sort and Land Claims over `realm:access_check` (see Quick Stack & Sort's **How it works**), and the ones the player may not open are dropped. Without either pack installed, the search waits 5 ticks at most for an answer.
- **Double chests:** when both halves report the whole 54 slots, both are stored under the half with the smaller coordinates. Copper chests of different stages count as the same kind of chest. The halves are told apart from a neighboring double chest with the same contents by their facing and, in a row of identical chests, by counting from the row's end.
- **Marking:** a bounded yellow/orange arrow is redrawn every 10 ticks with `player.spawnParticle`, never a world-wide particle. Its direction line requests `realm:actionbar` with `from: "find_bp"`, `ticks: 30`, `steady: 25`, waits for notes and higher-ranked lines, and never clears somebody else's bar when it ends. Each mark owns its cleanup generation, so an old callback cannot clear a newer mark. Actual prominence against chests and signs still needs a private PC/phone check.

---

## Land Claims — `claims_bp`

Claim the land around your base so other players can't break, place or open anything there. **Off until an operator enables it**: until then `/realm:claim` only says so and nothing is protected.

### How to use

1. Once an operator has enabled land claims, stand in the middle of your base and run `/realm:claim`, then pick **Claim this land**. You get 33 × 33 blocks around you (default radius 16, `radius`), from the bottom of the world to the top, and green sparkles show its borders.
2. Inside it, only you and the players you share it with can break or place blocks, open chests, furnaces and doors, press buttons, pour buckets, or use armor stands and chest minecarts or boats. Anyone else sees `This land is claimed by Sam`.
3. **Share it:** `/realm:claim` → **My claim: 120, -340** → **Share with Alex** (players online now). In a [party](#parties--party_bp), **Share with my party** shares it with everyone in your party, now and later, in one tap. The same menu stops sharing, shows its borders or removes the claim (it asks first). The same menu has **Visitors may open doors**, which lets visitors open doors, trapdoors and gates (off by default).
4. **Where are the borders?** `/realm:claim` → **Show claim borders** sparkles the edges of every claim near you for 10 seconds (asking again starts over). Walking in or out of one says `Entering Sam's claim` / `Leaving Sam's claim` above the hotbar.
5. Claims are safe zones for world events too: meteors, storm lightning and the other world-event packs break no blocks in them (see [Safe Zones](#safe-zones--zones_bp)).
6. **Operators:** enable it in `/realm:config` → **Land Claims** → **Land claims**, and set the claim size and how many each player gets there. `/realm:claim` → **All claims (operator)** lists every claim to remove any of them. **Protect claims from world events** (`protectWorldEvents`) turns the safe zone part off.

### What players see

- **While disabled** (`enabled`, disabled by default): `/realm:claim` answers `Land claims are disabled on this realm. An operator can enable them in /realm:config (Land Claims).` and nothing is protected. Disabling it later keeps every claim; they apply again once it's enabled.
- **The menu** says whose land you're on and how many claims you have (`You have 1 of 2 claims`), then **Claim this land** (when you're on unclaimed land and have one left), **Show claim borders**, one **My claim** button per claim, and for operators **All claims (operator)**.
- **Claiming** is refused with a reason when you already have 2 (`maxClaims`), or when the new square would overlap another claim (`That would overlap Sam's claim (-16, 48 to 16, 80). Move further away.`). Only operators can claim land reaching into a [Safe Zone](#safe-zones--zones_bp) or a [town](#town-projects--town_bp) with **Protect from world events** Enabled (`That would overlap the safe zone Spawn. Only operators can claim land there. Move further away.`, or `the town Riverside`); claims made there before stay. A claim keeps the size it was made with when operators change `radius` later.
- **What's protected** from everyone who isn't the owner or shared: breaking and placing blocks, tapping any block (chests, doors, trapdoors, buttons, levers, beds, crafting tables, buckets), and using the entities in `protectedEntities`. A block placed from outside onto the edge of a claim is refused too; with an empty hand you can still open a door or chest just outside the border.
- **Your own pets** go where you go: a pet you tamed (a wolf, cat or parrot you fed, a horse, donkey, mule or llama you rode until it was tame) can be leashed, ridden, fed or told to sit by you in anyone's claim, while other visitors still can't. A vanilla pet doesn't keep who tamed it in a way packs can read, so Land Claims writes the tamer down when the taming happens: pets tamed before this update, bred from your pets, or tamed by a command are locked in other people's claims like any tamed animal. When two players fed the same animal at about the same time and it can't tell whose feed tamed it, nobody is written down and the pet stays locked in other people's claims too; a horse is the rider's who tamed it, whoever else tapped it.
- **Explosions** break no blocks inside a claim (`protectExplosions`), whatever caused them; the damage is unchanged, and the part of the blast outside the claim breaks blocks as usual.
- **World events** (`protectWorldEvents`, default enabled): every claim is a safe zone, so no meteor crater, storm cell lightning or other world event changes blocks in it, and [Safe Zones](#safe-zones--zones_bp) lists it under **Towns and claims** as `Sam's claim`.
- **Sharing with your party** (only offered while you're in a [party](#parties--party_bp)): **Share with my party** lets every member of your party build and open things in the claim, without using up the `maxShared` places. The claim follows the party you're in now, checked once a second while you're online: a player who joins your party gets in, a member who leaves loses access, and if you join another party, that party gets it instead (nobody, while you're in none). The menu says `Shared with your party: everyone in it can build here.` (or `Shared with your party, once you're in one.`), the **My claim** button adds `and your party`, and **Stop sharing with my party** ends it.
- **Operators** can't build in other players' claims unless **Operators can build in any claim** is enabled (`operatorsBypass`), so a realm where everyone is an operator still gets protection. They can always remove a claim.
- **Containers in a claim** are also kept from other players' [Quick Stack & Sort](#quick-stack--sort--stash_bp) (`/realm:stash` puts nothing in them) and [Chest Finder](#chest-finder--find_bp) (`/realm:find` doesn't list them).
- **Other packs' blocks in a claim** follow the same rule, since tapping them is refused like any other tap: only the claim's players can collect a charged lightning rod's Storm Glass ([Storm Chasing](#storm-chasing--storm_bp)), sit on its stairs and slabs ([Chairs](#chairs--chairs_bp)), cook in its pots ([Kitchen](#kitchen--cooking_bp)), play its slot machines ([Slot Machine](#slot-machine--slots_bp)) or use its waystones ([Waystones & Inns](#waystones--inns--waystone_bp)).
- **What a claim doesn't stop:** mobs, hurting animals or pets (the stable API can't cancel damage, so `protectAnimals` covers leashing, riding, feeding, milking, shearing, naming, sitting and taming, not hits), fire spreading, lava or water flowing in, pistons pushing blocks in from outside, hoppers or minecarts pulling items across the border, and hits: punching an armor stand to break it, or punching the item out of an item frame, isn't stopped (only tapping them is).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:claim` | Everyone | Opens the Land Claims menu: claim the land around you (default 33 × 33 blocks, `radius` 16), show nearby claim borders, share or remove your claims (default 2 each, `maxClaims`), including with your whole party while you're in one; operators also get every claim, to remove any. Only works once an operator has enabled land claims (default disabled, `enabled`) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` | Land claims for the whole realm. Disabled: `/realm:claim` only says so and nothing is protected; claims are kept |
| `radius` | `16` | How far a new claim reaches from where you stand, each way: 16 = 33 × 33 blocks, top to bottom (4–64 in game) |
| `maxClaims` | `2` | Most claims one player can have (1–10 in game) |
| `maxShared` | `10` | Most players one claim can be shared with |
| `protectExplosions` | `true` | Explosions break no blocks inside a claim |
| `protectWorldEvents` | `true` | Claims are safe zones: meteors, tornadoes, storm lightning and other world events break no blocks in them |
| `operatorsBypass` | `false` | Operators can build, break and open things in anyone's claim |
| `protectedEntities` | `armor_stand`, `chest_minecart`, `hopper_minecart`, `chest_boat` | Entities only a claim's players can use inside it |
| `protectAnimals` | `true` | Others can't leash, ride, feed, milk, shear, name or tame the animals in `protectedAnimals` inside a claim, and any tamed animal in a claim is covered too, except for its own tamer, who can always use it (tamed since this update; see What players see). Doesn't stop damage. `false` = anyone can use them |
| `protectedAnimals` | cow, mooshroom, sheep, pig, chicken, goat, horse, donkey, mule, llama, camel, wolf, cat, parrot, trader llama, skeleton horse, zombie horse, fox, axolotl, allay, rabbit, bee, frog, sniffer, armadillo, turtle, panda, ocelot, strider | Which animals `protectAnimals` covers (`minecraft:` ids) |
| `borderSeconds` | `10` | How long **Show claim borders** draws them |

Operators can change `enabled`, `radius`, `maxClaims`, `protectExplosions`, `protectWorldEvents` and `operatorsBypass` in game with `/realm:config`. The rest stays in `config.js`. The realm has room for 500 claims in all.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `claims:c:<id>` | World | One per claim: JSON `{ id, o, n, dim, x, z, r, s, pt?, pc? }`, the owner's id and name, the dimension, the center, the radius, the players it's shared with (`[{ i, n }]`), whether it's shared with the owner's party (`pt`) and the owner's party code (`pc`, `""` for none; access also needs the owner and the player on the Parties pack's current member list). The owner's and shared players' names are updated when they join with a new gamertag. `dr` (true when set) lets visitors open doors, trapdoors and gates. `lv` is the owner's last visit (ms), refreshed at most once every 60 seconds while the owner is inside that claim; when it's missing the claim shows the owner's last visit as unknown |
| `claims:next` | World | The next claim id |
| `claims:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `claims:tamer` | Entity (a tamed pet) | The id of the player who tamed it, written when Land Claims saw the taming; lets that player use the pet in other people's claims |

### How it works

- Claims are read into memory once and kept in step as they change, so the checks below never read saved data.
- `beforeEvents.playerBreakBlock` and `beforeEvents.playerInteractWithBlock` are canceled inside someone else's claim. The tap is checked at the block and at the spot a block would be placed, since the stable API has no "before place" event and placing starts with that tap. `afterEvents.playerPlaceBlock` breaks anything that still got placed (`setblock ... air destroy`, so the block and what it holds drop as items). `beforeEvents.playerInteractWithEntity` is canceled for `protectedEntities`.
- `beforeEvents.explosion` takes the blocks inside claims out of the blast without canceling it.
- **Party sharing:** a claim with `pt` lets a player in only while both the owner and that player are on party `<pc>`'s current member list, which [Parties](#parties--party_bp) sends with `realm:party_members` (kept in memory and asked for with `realm:party_members_ping` about 3 seconds after the world loads). The `realm_party:<code>` tag alone isn't enough, so an owner removed from the party while offline, or a later party that got the same code, opens nothing. Once a second, for each such claim whose owner is online, `pc` is set to the owner's current party code and saved when it changed.
- The pack is the `claims` provider of the safe zones protocol: while claims are enabled and `protectWorldEvents` is on, it sends every claim as a square zone (`realm:zones`) whenever claims change, when the world starts and when asked (`realm:zones_ping`); otherwise it sends an empty list. It also listens to the other providers (Safe Zones' `zones`, Town Projects' `town`) to refuse a player's new claim that would reach into one of their zones (operators may claim there).
- Other packs ask before changing blocks in a box (Easy Building): `realm:claims_check` `{ id, player, dim, x1, z1, x2, z2 }` is answered with `realm:claims_check_result` `{ id, claims: [{ n, x1, z1, x2, z2 }] }`, the owner's name and corners of up to 10 claims in that box the player may not build in (none while claims are disabled; shared players, and operators with `operatorsBypass`, may build). It is always answered, so the asker also learns that Land Claims is installed.
- Quick Stack & Sort, Chest Finder and Chairs ask which blocks a player may not open: `realm:access_check` `{ id, player, spots: [[dim, x, y, z], ...] }` is answered with `realm:access_check_result` `{ id, from: "claims_bp", closed: [i, ...] }`, the spots in a claim that player may not open (the same rule as tapping a chest there; none while claims are disabled). See Quick Stack & Sort's **How it works**.
- Once a second, each player's claim is looked up to say when they walk in or out of one. Messages above the hotbar send `realm:actionbar` first, so the [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) leaves them on screen.

---

## Death Point — `death_bp`

Tells you where you died once you respawn, and points you back there. On a world that keeps inventories nothing is lying on the ground; otherwise your items wait at the death point for 5 minutes before they despawn. Either way this is for finding your way back to where you were, say a cave you were exploring or a long trip through the Nether.

### How to use

1. Nothing to set up: when you respawn after dying, chat says `You died at 120, 64, -340 in the Overworld.`
2. Run `/realm:death` any time to see your last death point again, how far it is from where you stand and in which direction, for example `It's 245 blocks to the NE, 12 blocks down.` When teleporting back is enabled (or you're an operator) it opens the **Death Point** menu with that text and the buttons `Where I died` (the same in chat), `Teleport back` and, for operators, `Settings`; otherwise it answers in chat right away. `/realm:death_info` always answers in chat.
3. In a [party](#parties--party_bp), your online mates are told where you died, with how far and which way it is from them, so they can come help. Don't want to hear about theirs? Disable **Tell me where party mates die** in `/realm:prefs`.
4. Don't want the chat message? Disable **Tell me where I died** in `/realm:prefs`. `/realm:death` still works.
5. If an operator has enabled it, tap `Teleport back` in `/realm:death`, or run `/realm:death_back`, to teleport to your last death point, once per death. It only lands you somewhere safe to stand, and says so when there isn't such a place.
6. **Operators:** enable `/realm:death_back` in `/realm:config` → **Death Point** → **Teleport back to the death point (/realm:death_back)**. The same page turns the respawn message and the party message off for everyone.

### What players see

- **On respawn** (`announce`): `You died at 120, 64, -340 in the Overworld. Run /realm:death to see where that is from here.` A player who leaves on the death screen gets it when they next spawn.
- **Party mates** (`tellParty`, each player's own **Tell me where party mates die** in `/realm:prefs`): right when a [party](#parties--party_bp) member dies, every other online member gets `[Party] Ann died at 120, 64, -340 in the Overworld (40 blocks W of you).`, the distance along the ground and one of 8 directions from where they stand, or `(right where you are)` within 2 blocks. A mate in another dimension gets the line without the distance.
- **`/realm:death`** (or `/realm:death_info`) shows the block you died in and its dimension, then the distance along the ground, rounded to whole blocks, with one of 8 directions (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW; north is toward negative Z) and how far up or down. Within 2 blocks it says `You're standing on it.` In another dimension it says which one you're in, with no distance. When `/realm:death_back` is enabled it adds whether you can still use it for this death.
- **`/realm:death_back`** while disabled (`backEnabled`, disabled by default): `Teleporting back is disabled on this realm. An operator can enable it in /realm:config (Death Point). /realm:death still shows the way.`
- **`/realm:death_back`** while enabled looks for the nearest safe spot within 2 blocks sideways (`backSearchRadius`) and 8 blocks up or down (`backSearchHeight`) of the death point: two blocks of air (or grass, ferns, flowers, a dead bush, vines, glow lichen or a torch) to stand in, on a block that isn't air, water, lava, magma, fire, a campfire, cactus, a berry bush, a wither rose, powder snow or pointed dripstone, with no lava or fire right beside it. It works across dimensions. Then:
  - it teleports you and says `Teleported back to your death point (120, 65, -340).` Once per death: a second try says `You already went back to this death point.`
  - with no safe spot (you died in lava, deep water, inside a wall or below the world) it says so and doesn't move you, and you can try again after the lava cools or the water is drained.
  - a death point far from every player isn't loaded: it's loaded for a moment (up to 5 seconds, `backLoadSeconds`) and the search runs then. If it can't be loaded it says so.
- `/realm:death_back` doesn't bring back dropped items or experience. On a world without the `keepInventory` game rule, go back for them within 5 minutes, before they despawn.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:death` | Everyone | The **Death Point** menu: your last death point in its text, with `Where I died`, `Teleport back` (when `backEnabled` is on) and, for operators, `Settings`. With nothing else to choose it answers in chat like `/realm:death_info` |
| `/realm:death_info` | Everyone | Shows your last death point (x, y, z and dimension), with the distance and direction from where you stand, or which dimension it's in |
| `/realm:death_back` | Everyone, once an operator enables it | Teleports you to a safe spot at your last death point, once per death (default disabled, `backEnabled`). Refuses with a reason when there's no safe place to stand |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `announce` | `true` | Tell players in chat where they died once they respawn. Each player can change it for themselves |
| `tellParty` | `true` | Tell a player's online party mates ([Parties](#parties--party_bp)) in chat where they died, with the distance and direction from each mate. Each player can change it for themselves |
| `backEnabled` | `false` | `/realm:death_back` teleports players to their last death point, once per death |
| `backSearchRadius` | `2` | How far sideways (blocks) from the death point `/realm:death_back` looks for a safe place to stand (0 to 4 in game) |
| `backSearchHeight` | `8` | How far up and down (blocks) it looks (0 to 16 in game) |
| `backLoadSeconds` | `5` | How long `/realm:death_back` waits for a faraway death point to load before giving up |

Operators can change `announce`, `tellParty`, `backEnabled`, `backSearchRadius` and `backSearchHeight` in game with `/realm:config`. `backLoadSeconds` stays in `config.js`. Each player can disable the respawn message (**Tell me where I died**) and the party mates' deaths (**Tell me where party mates die**) for themselves in `/realm:prefs`; each follows the realm's setting until they choose.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `death:last` | Player | JSON `{ d, x, y, z, told, used }`: the dimension and block of the last death, whether the respawn message was sent and whether `/realm:death_back` was used for it |
| `death:pref` | Player | The player's choices for **Tell me where I died** and **Tell me where party mates die**, when they differ from the realm's |
| `death:areas` | World | JSON list of the temporary ticking areas `/realm:death_back` is using right now; any left after a restart are removed when the world loads |
| `death:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- `world.afterEvents.entityDie` saves the block a player died in; `world.afterEvents.playerSpawn` sends the message once.
- **Party message:** right after saving, the pack finds the dead player's `realm_party:<code>` tag (from [Parties](#parties--party_bp)) and messages every other online player with the same tag whose own `tellParty` is on.
- `/realm:death_back` checks the blocks around the death point with `Dimension.getBlock`, nearest first. When the death point isn't loaded, it runs `tickingarea add circle <x> <y> <z> 1 "death_back_<id>" true` in that dimension, checks again every 5 ticks until the blocks can be read, and removes the ticking area right after (`tickingarea remove`). While it's there it counts toward Bedrock's 10 ticking areas per world (see [Farm Loader](#farm-loader--farm_bp)); if all 10 are taken, `/realm:death_back` says it can't load the death point now.
- The teleport uses `Entity.tryTeleport` with `checkForBlocks`, so the game refuses it too if the spot became blocked meanwhile. It is marked used only after it succeeds.
- **Minimap:** after each death the pack sends `realm:death_point` `{ player, dim, x, z }`, and on `realm:death_point_ping` `{ player? }` the point of every online player (`{ player }` alone when there is none).

---

## Hotbar Refill — `refill_bp`

When the stack in your hand runs out, or your tool breaks, the same slot is refilled from your inventory, so you keep building, eating or fighting without opening it.

### How to use

1. Nothing to set up: keep spare stacks and spare tools in your main inventory (above the hotbar). Place your last block, eat your last steak, throw your last snowball or ender pearl, or break your pickaxe, and a matching stack or tool from your inventory moves into that hotbar slot.
2. Don't want it? Run `/realm:refill` to disable it for yourself; run it again to enable it. The same switch is **Refill my hotbar** in `/realm:prefs`. The choice is remembered.
3. **Operators:** `/realm:config` → **Hotbar Refill** disables it for the whole realm, stops it replacing broken tools, or changes what new players start with.

### What players see

- **A stack runs out** (the last block placed, the last food eaten, the last snowball, egg, ender pearl or firework used, the last bone meal or seeds used on a block): the fullest stack in your main inventory that would have stacked with it moves into the same slot. With [Quick Stack & Sort](#quick-stack--sort--stash_bp)'s inventory pages, a stack on another page counts too: when the page you're on has none, the fullest one with the same item, name and lore on your other pages moves into the slot (never tipped arrows, ominous bottles, banners or firework stars, whose differences aren't compared across pages), and the bar says `[Page #2] Refilled 64x Firework rocket into your hotbar` (before Hotbar Refill 1.1.0 and Quick Stack & Sort 1.8.0, only the open page was searched, so a last rocket with 64 more on page 2 wasn't refilled). "Would have stacked" means the same item with the same name, enchantments and other data, so a renamed stack never replaces a plain one, and the other way around.
- **Rocket flight duration across pages:** while gliding, cross-page refill can replace a Flight 3 rocket with a Flight 1 rocket. Flight duration is not compared across saved pages; rockets intentionally remain eligible. Keep only the duration you want in refillable storage if this matters to your flight.
- **A tool, weapon or other item with durability breaks** while you use it (mining, hitting, tilling, shearing, lighting, fishing; `refillTools`): a spare of the same item moves in, the one with the most uses left. Two rules keep your special gear where it is:
  - a spare with a name (renamed on an anvil) only replaces a broken tool with that same name;
  - a plain (unenchanted) tool is only replaced by a plain spare, so a Silk Touch or Fortune pickaxe isn't pulled out when an ordinary one breaks. A broken enchanted tool is replaced by the spare sharing the most of its enchantments (any spare of that item counts, enchanted or not), then the one with the most uses left.
- **Not refilled:** a stack you drop, move or put away by hand, armor and elytra you put on from the hotbar, a thrown trident, an item that turns into another (a bucket, a bowl, a glass bottle), slots other than the one in your hand, items locked in their slot, and anything when there's no match in the main inventory (the 27 slots above the hotbar, and the other inventory pages for stacks; the other hotbar slots aren't used). A broken tool is replaced only from the open page.
- The item is moved, not copied: it keeps its enchantments, name, lore, durability and everything else.
- Nothing is shown or played; the slot just fills.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:refill` | Everyone | Enables or disables hotbar refills **for yourself** (default enabled, `defaultOn`). Remembered between sessions. Chat says `Hotbar refill: Disabled. Run /realm:refill again to enable it.` |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Hotbar refill for the whole realm. Disabled: nothing is refilled, whatever players chose |
| `refillTools` | `true` | Also replace a tool, weapon or other item with durability that breaks |
| `defaultOn` | `true` | Players get refills until they disable them for themselves |

Operators can change all three in game with `/realm:config`. Players whose own choice differs from `defaultOn` keep it when `defaultOn` changes. Each player switches it for themselves with `/realm:refill` or **Refill my hotbar** in `/realm:prefs`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `refill:pref` | Player | The player's choice from `/realm:refill` or `/realm:prefs`, when it differs from `defaultOn` |
| `refill:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- `world.afterEvents.playerInventoryItemChange` reports a hotbar slot going from an item to empty. Only the selected slot counts.
- A slot that empties within 3 ticks of a use counts as used up: placing a block (`playerPlaceBlock`), mining (`playerBreakBlock`), tapping a block or mob (`playerInteractWithBlock`, `playerInteractWithEntity`), hitting (`entityHitEntity`), or using, eating or releasing an item (`itemUse`, `itemCompleteUse`, `itemReleaseUse`). Moving items by hand fires none of these, which is how a deliberate move is told apart. Items that don't stack only come back when they broke: they had 2 uses or fewer left, or vanished while being used in hand.
- Two ticks later, if the slot is still empty, `Container.swapItems` swaps it with the chosen inventory slot. A native swap keeps the item exactly as it was.

## Coordinates HUD — `hud_bp`

Your own coordinates, the direction you're facing and the day and time, on the bar above the hotbar (or in a [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box, if you prefer), for players who enable it. Handy for building, mapping and meeting up without opening a map.

### How to use

1. Run `/realm:hud`. Above your hotbar you now see one line in sections, `X 120  Y 64  Z -340  |  Facing NE  |  Day 12  6:30 AM`, updated as you move. Only you see yours.
2. Run `/realm:hud` again to hide it. The choice is remembered. The same switch is **Coordinates HUD** in `/realm:prefs`.
3. Only want the coordinates? Disable **HUD shows the day and time** in `/realm:prefs`.
4. Want it off the hotbar bar, where other packs' notes push it aside? Set **Where my HUD shows** in `/realm:prefs` to one of the side boxes (**Right 1** to **Right 4**, **Left 1** to **Left 4**). Pick one no other pack of yours uses (Mob Health now defaults to Left 1, the Elytra HUD Left 2, Warmer / Colder Right 3 and the story tracker Right 4; existing saved choices are kept).
5. **Operators:** `/realm:config` → **Coordinates HUD** disables it for the whole realm (for servers that play without coordinates), shows it to new players from the start, switches the facing to 4 directions, or changes where it shows for players who haven't chosen.

### What players see

- **Coordinates** are the block your feet are in, as in the game's own coordinates. **Facing** is one of 8 directions, `N`, `NE`, `E`, `SE`, `S`, `SW`, `W`, `NW` (`eightWay`; 4 directions when disabled); north is toward negative Z.
- **Day and time** (`showTime`): the in-game day, counted from 1, and the time on a 12-hour clock in 10-minute steps, with sunrise at 6:00 AM and noon at 12:00 PM (an in-game day lasts 20 minutes, so 10 in-game minutes pass in about 8 seconds).
- Off for every player until they enable it (`defaultOn`). While an operator has disabled it for the realm (`enabled`), nobody sees it and `/realm:hud` says `The coordinates HUD is disabled on this realm.`
- It updates at most twice a second (`intervalTicks`), and only when the text changes, or every 2 seconds (`refreshTicks`) so it doesn't fade while you stand still.
- **The stats ticker:** a player who also has the [Stats pack](#stats--leaderboards--stats_bp)'s ticker on sees it as one more section of the line, such as `... |  Mob kills 120 #2 of 7`, instead of the two taking turns on the bar; so does the [Parties](#parties--party_bp) HUD's mate line (`|  Bob 20hp 2m E`). In a side box each takes a line of its own.
- **In a side box** (`showAt`, default **Above the hotbar**; each player's **Where my HUD shows**): the same text in a [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box, the day and time on a second line. There it never waits for other packs' notes, and it shows next to the other packs' boxes. It is sent again only when it changes or every 5 seconds. Without Side HUD the text shows in the middle of the screen.
- **Sharing the bar with other packs:** above the hotbar, the same bar also shows other packs' short messages: low-durability warnings, `Sorted 31 stacks` and other Quick Stack & Sort results, entering or leaving a claim, the Chairs reminder, the smart sleep count, [Mob Health](#mob-health--mobhp_bp) after a hit, [Daily Quests](#daily-quests--quests_bp) progress notes and others. Each of them asks the HUD to wait (usually 2 to 3 seconds) so the message stays readable, and the HUD redraws right after. While you glide with the [Elytra HUD](#elytra-hud--elytra_bp) above the hotbar, it keeps the bar to itself; the coordinates come back a second or two after you land. Other packs can do the same (see How it works).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:hud` | Everyone | Shows or hides your coordinates, facing and the day and time above the hotbar, **for yourself** (default hidden, `defaultOn`). Remembered between sessions. Says so when an operator has disabled it for the realm (`enabled`) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | The HUD for the whole realm. Disabled: nobody sees it, whatever they chose |
| `defaultOn` | `false` | Show the HUD to players who never ran `/realm:hud` |
| `showTime` | `true` | Show the day and time after the coordinates. Each player can change it for themselves |
| `eightWay` | `true` | Facing in 8 directions; `false` shows `N`, `E`, `S` and `W` only |
| `intervalTicks` | `10` | How often (ticks) the HUD updates. 10 is the fastest it goes (twice a second). Read when the world starts |
| `refreshTicks` | `40` | Send an unchanged HUD again after this many ticks, so the bar doesn't fade |
| `showAt` | `"hotbar"` | Where the HUD shows for players who haven't chosen: `hotbar` (the bar above the hotbar) or a [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box, `right1` to `right4` or `left1` to `left4` (top to bottom) |

Operators can change `enabled`, `defaultOn`, `showTime`, `eightWay` and `showAt` in game with `/realm:config`; `intervalTicks` is fixed when the world starts, so `/realm:config` only shows it. `refreshTicks` stays in `config.js`. Each player chooses **Coordinates HUD** (`/realm:hud`), **HUD shows the day and time** and **Where my HUD shows** in `/realm:prefs`; a player who never chose follows `defaultOn`, `showTime` and `showAt`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `hud:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's choices (HUD shown, day and time, where it shows) that differ from the realm's |
| `hud:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- Every `intervalTicks`, for each player with the HUD on, the pack builds the text from the player's location, `getRotation()` (the yaw), `world.getDay()` and `world.getTimeOfDay()`, and calls `onScreenDisplay.setActionBar` only if it changed or `refreshTicks` have passed. In a side box it shows the text with the side boxes protocol instead (`scripts/side.js`, see [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)), for 140 ticks, sent again when it changes or after 100 ticks; `realm:actionbar` requests don't pause it there.
- Another pack that puts a message on the bar can send the script event `realm:actionbar` with `{"player":"<player id>","ticks":40}`; the HUD then leaves that player's bar alone for that many ticks (up to 200) and redraws right after. Every pack that writes the bar does this; the HUD itself and the stats ticker, the bottom lines, are the only ones that write without a request (see the action bar protocol in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)); the packs never import each other.
- Turning the HUD off (or moving it) clears the bar or its box right away.
- Another pack can add a section to the HUD (a line of its own in a side box) for one player with the script event `realm:hud_line` (`{"player":"<player id>","key":"stats","text":"...","ticks":80}`): it shows while the HUD is on, until `ticks` pass (up to 400; resend to keep it) or a message with `"text":""` removes it. Sections show in `key` order, after the coordinates, facing and time, each after a dark gray `|`. The Stats pack's ticker (`stats`) and the Party HUD (`party`) use it.
- So those packs know whether to draw on their own, the HUD sends `realm:hud_state` (`{"part":1,"parts":1,"seq":7,"players":["<player id>", ...]}`, the players who see it, in parts under 1900 bytes, so any number of them) when that changes, every 5 seconds while anyone sees it (an empty list goes once: Stats and Parties treat a list not heard for 10 seconds as empty), and in reply to `realm:hud_ping`.
