## Mob Health — `mobhp_bp`

Hit a mob and its name and health show in a small box on the left side of your screen (or in your existing chosen box, above the mob's head, or above your hotbar), so you know how close it is to going down.

### How to use

1. Nothing to set up: hit a mob with anything, or shoot it, and **Left 1** in the centered left-side group shows something like `Zombie  14/20 HP ||||||||||` (a killing blow shows `Zombie  defeated`; it's the mob's health, not a quest counter) with the bar in color. Only you see it. Existing realm or player placement choices are not reset.
2. Prefer it somewhere else? Set **Where the health of mobs I hit shows** in `/realm:prefs`: another [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box, **Above the mob** (the health floats over the mob's head for 2 seconds) or **Above the hotbar**.
3. Don't want it? Run `/realm:mobhp` to hide it for yourself; run it again to show it. The same switch is **Show the health of mobs I hit** in `/realm:prefs`. The choice is remembered.
4. **Operators:** `/realm:config` → **Mob Health** disables it for the whole realm, shows players' health too when one player hurts another, changes the bar length, or changes what new players start with (on or off, and where it shows).

### What players see

- **Name:** the mob's name tag if it has one, otherwise its name made from its id (`Zombie`, `Iron Golem`; above the hotbar, in the game's language).
- **Health** after the hit, rounded up to whole points, out of its maximum (`14/20 HP`; 2 points are one heart; `defeated` after a killing blow), then a bar of 10 `|` characters (`barLength`): green above half health, yellow above a quarter, red below that, with the lost part in dark gray.
- Shown for melee hits and for arrows, tridents and other projectiles you fired, every time the mob is hurt by you.
- **Other players** only when an operator enabled **Show players' health too** (`players`, disabled by default): then hurting a player shows their name and health the same way.
- Enabled for every player until they disable it (`defaultOn`). While an operator has disabled it for the realm (`enabled`), nobody sees it.
- **Where it shows** (`showAt`, default **Left 1**): the first occupied box in the centered left-side group, for 2 seconds (`holdTicks`). The native text, colors and bar are unchanged. Existing saved realm and player placement choices are kept. [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) draws independent boxes, so the other readouts can show together; without it the text appears as a vanilla subtitle. Pick **Right 1-4**, **Left 1-4**, **Middle of the screen**, **Above the mob** or **Above the hotbar** in `/realm:prefs`. Above the hotbar the Coordinates HUD waits 2 seconds after each hit.
- **Above the mob:** the health, like `14/20 HP ||||||||||`, becomes the mob's name tag for 2 seconds, then the mob is unnamed again. A killing blow never writes it: the name comes off at once and the `0/20` shows in the realm's default box instead. It's a name tag, so **everyone nearby sees it**, and it shows as name tags do (when you look at the mob). Players and mobs that already have a name keep it: their health shows in the realm's default box instead (**Left 1** when the realm default is Above the mob or Above the hotbar).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:mobhp` | Everyone | Shows or hides the health of mobs you hit, **for yourself** (default shown, `defaultOn`). Remembered between sessions. Chat says `Mob health: Disabled. Run /realm:mobhp again to show it.` |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Mob health for the whole realm. Disabled: nobody sees it, whatever they chose |
| `defaultOn` | `true` | Players see it until they disable it for themselves |
| `players` | `false` | Also show a player's health when you hurt another player |
| `barLength` | `10` | How many `\|` characters make up the bar (5 to 20 in game) |
| `showAt` | `"left1"` | Where it shows for players who haven't chosen: a [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box, `right1` to `right4` or `left1` to `left4` (top to bottom) or `middle`; `overhead` (the hit mob's name tag, which everyone nearby sees); or `hotbar`. Existing saved choices are kept |
| `holdTicks` | `40` | How long (ticks) the health stays on screen or above the mob; above the hotbar, how long the Coordinates HUD leaves it before drawing itself again |

Operators can change `enabled`, `defaultOn`, `players`, `barLength` and `showAt` in game with `/realm:config`. Players pick their own place with **Where the health of mobs I hit shows** in `/realm:prefs`. `holdTicks` stays in `config.js`. Each player switches it for themselves with `/realm:mobhp` or **Show the health of mobs I hit** in `/realm:prefs`; players whose own choice differs from `defaultOn` keep it when `defaultOn` changes.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `mobhp:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's choices from `/realm:mobhp` or `/realm:prefs` (shown or hidden, where it shows) that differ from the realm's |
| `mobhp:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `mobhp:tag` | Entity | While the health shows above a mob: the name tag the pack wrote, so it only takes off its own. The mob also carries the tag `mobhp_tag` |

### How it works

- `world.afterEvents.entityHurt` gives the hurt mob and the damage source. When the damaging entity (the shooter, for a projectile) is a player with it on, the pack reads the mob's `minecraft:health` component and shows it: in the player's [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box for `holdTicks` with the side boxes protocol (`scripts/side.js`, see [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)), or on the action bar with the mob's name as a translated text so it reads in each player's language. When one hit hurts several mobs in the same tick (a sweep), the readout is drawn once, after the tick, with the last mob hit.
- **Above the mob:** the pack sets the mob's `nameTag` to the health, adds the tag `mobhp_tag` and saves what it wrote in `mobhp:tag`; every 5 ticks it takes the name off mobs whose `holdTicks` passed (only if the name is still what it wrote: a player or another pack may have named the mob meanwhile, and a mob named that way keeps its name on the next hit too, with its health in the box instead). Another player who hits a mob showing it, with a box chosen, sees the mob's own name there, not the health. A mob that unloaded or a server that stopped mid-display is cleaned up when the mob loads again (`entityLoad`) and when the world loads (every mob tagged `mobhp_tag`), because named mobs never despawn. Players and mobs with a name tag are never renamed.
- Above the hotbar it also sends the script event `realm:actionbar` with `{"player":"<id>","ticks":40}` (`holdTicks`), which the Coordinates HUD understands. Without the HUD nothing listens and nothing happens.

## Elytra HUD — `elytra_bp`

While you glide, a small box on the left side of your screen (or your existing chosen box, or the line above your hotbar) shows your speed, height, how much durability your elytra has left and how many firework rockets and **NOS Rockets** you carry. This pack also adds the **NOS Rocket** (`custom:nos_rocket`), a high-powered nitrous Elytra booster crafted from 8 gunpowder around 1 firework rocket that delivers roughly 3.5x the forward acceleration burst of a normal firework rocket with cyan/blue and orange flame particles. It also adds the **Music Disc - Run Away** (`custom:music_disc_run_away`), a custom music disc that plays in a Jukebox or in your hand.

### How to use

1. Put on an elytra and glide. **Left 2** in the centered left-side group shows something like `31.4 blocks/s  Y 142` and under it `Elytra 87%  Rockets 12  NOS 4`, updated 4 times a second. Existing realm and player placement choices are kept. Prefer another place? **Where my Elytra HUD shows** in `/realm:prefs`.
2. Craft a **NOS Rocket** (`custom:nos_rocket`) at a crafting table by placing **1 Firework Rocket** in the center and **8 Gunpowder** around it (`GGG / GFG / GGG`). Right-click / use a NOS Rocket while gliding with an elytra for a hard 3.5x nitrous acceleration burst in the direction you're looking, complete with blue/cyan + orange flame particles and pressurized boost audio. (Using it on the ground does not consume it.)
3. Don't want the HUD? Run `/realm:elytra`, or disable **Elytra HUD while gliding** in `/realm:prefs`. Chat says `Elytra HUD: Disabled. Run /realm:elytra again to enable it.` The choice is remembered.
4. **Operators:** run `/realm:elytra_nos [count]` to give yourself NOS Rockets directly. To turn the HUD or NOS Rockets off, or tune the NOS boost multiplier (`nosMultiplier`) and max flight speed cap (`nosMaxSpeed`), open `/realm:config` → **Elytra HUD**.
5. Craft a **Music Disc - Run Away** (`custom:music_disc_run_away`, a red CD with a gold and black center) at a crafting table with **1 Gold Ingot** in the center, **4 Redstone** on the edges and **4 Coal** in the corners (`CRC / RGR / CRC`), or run `/realm:disc` to get one. Right-click a Jukebox with it to play the song for everyone nearby (it's taken from your hand outside Creative); right-click the Jukebox again, or break it, to pop the disc back out and stop the song. Right-click the disc in the air to listen on your own, and again to stop.

### What players see

- **Speed** in blocks per second (your total speed, diving included), **Y** (your height), **Elytra** durability left in percent, **Rockets** (firework rockets in your inventory and offhand) and **NOS** (NOS Rockets carried, when at least 1).
- **NOS Rocket** (`custom:nos_rocket`, stack size 64, 128x128 `nos_rocket` icon in `build_rp`): when activated while gliding, consumes 1 item (outside Creative), spools up the turbo for 0.55s at regular firework-rocket speed (~32 to 36 blocks/s), kicks up to and holds a `nosMultiplier` (`3.5`x) forward nitrous boost over `nosBurstTicks` (`50` ticks = 2.5s at peak speed, clamped to `nosMaxSpeed` = `3.6` blocks/tick, ~72 blocks/s), and then carries its momentum through a slow 4.5s taper down to ~31 blocks/s with a `"stu-tu-tu-tu"` wastegate turbo flutter (`realm.nos.boost`) and cyan-blue + orange slipstream flames: a four-point slipstream ring streams past the corners of your view well ahead of the camera (it leads by your speed, so it stays in front even at ~72 blocks/s) and a continuous, gap-free afterburner ribbon trails behind you. Even without a NOS Rocket, gliding at 24+ blocks/s (`1.2` blocks/tick) shows faint wingtip sparks ahead and a puff of smoke behind. Normal vanilla firework rockets remain completely unchanged.
- **Music Disc - Run Away** (`custom:music_disc_run_away`, stack size 1, `music_disc_run_away` icon and `realm.disc.run_away` / `realm.disc.run_away_personal` sounds in `build_rp`): the song lasts 5m 50s. In a Jukebox it plays in 3D for players nearby with note particles above the Jukebox and a `Now Playing: Run Away` note on the bar; any Jukebox disc already inside is popped out first. Right-clicking the Jukebox or breaking it drops the disc and stops the song. In Creative the disc stays in your hand when you put it in a Jukebox. Using the disc in the air plays the song only for you (`Now Playing`) and using it again stops it (`Stopped`).
- The speed readout is a 3-sample moving average, so it doesn't flicker from tick to tick. **Elytra** shows `--` when you wear nothing in the chest slot or the item has no durability; vanilla and armored elytras show their percentage.
- Durability shows green, yellow at 30 percent or less, and red at 10 percent or less (`lowPercent`). An elytra stops working at 1 durability left, which shows as 0%.
- It only shows while you're gliding: the box goes away as you land (above the hotbar, the bar fades a moment after). Nothing is shown for players who aren't gliding.
- When it shows above the hotbar and the [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) is on, the coordinates pause while you glide, so the two don't take turns on the bar; they come back a second or two after you land. In a side box, both show at once.
- **Where it shows** (`showAt`, default **Left 2**): a [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box in the centered left group, with the original speed, height, durability and rocket text/colors. Existing saved choices are not reset. Other packs' boxes remain independent. Pick another **Right 1-4**, **Left 1-4**, **Middle of the screen** or **Above the hotbar** in `/realm:prefs`; above the hotbar it waits for other packs' held notes.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:elytra` | Everyone | Enables or disables the gliding HUD **for yourself** (enabled by default). Remembered between sessions. Works while the HUD is enabled for the realm (default enabled, `enabled`) |
| `/realm:elytra_nos [count]` | Operators | Gives yourself `count` (1 to 64, default 16) **NOS Rockets** (`custom:nos_rocket`) |
| `/realm:disc` | Everyone | Gives yourself 1 **Music Disc - Run Away** (`custom:music_disc_run_away`) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | The gliding HUD for the whole realm. Disabled: nobody sees it and `/realm:elytra` says so |
| `intervalTicks` | `5` | Ticks between HUD updates while gliding (5 = 4 times a second) |
| `lowPercent` | `10` | Elytra durability left (percent) at or below which it shows in red (1 to 50 in game) |
| `showAt` | `"left2"` | Where it shows for players who haven't chosen: a [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box, `right1` to `right4` or `left1` to `left4` (top to bottom), `middle`, or `hotbar`. Existing saved choices are kept |
| `nosEnabled` | `true` | Allow using NOS Rockets (`custom:nos_rocket`) while gliding with an elytra |
| `nosMultiplier` | `3.5` | NOS Rocket boost multiplier relative to a normal firework rocket baseline (2.0 to 5.0 in game) |
| `nosBaseline` | `0.75` | Normal firework rocket impulse baseline in blocks/tick |
| `nosMaxSpeed` | `3.6` | Maximum total flight speed cap in blocks/tick (~72 blocks/s) so repeated NOS Rockets stay steerable and do not compound infinitely |
| `nosBurstTicks` | `50` | Sustained full-boost turbo hold duration in ticks (2.5s at peak speed, preceded by a 0.55s regular-speed spool-up and followed by a 4.5s slow momentum taper with wastegate flutter) |

Operators can change `enabled`, `lowPercent`, `showAt`, `nosEnabled`, `nosMultiplier`, `nosBaseline`, `nosMaxSpeed` and `nosBurstTicks` in game with `/realm:config`; `intervalTicks` shows there but is read when the world starts, so change it in `config.js`. Each player can disable the HUD for themselves in `/realm:prefs` (**Elytra HUD while gliding**), the same switch as `/realm:elytra`, and pick where it shows (**Where my Elytra HUD shows**).

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `elytra:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's own choices: `"off": true` when they disabled the HUD (`/realm:elytra` or `/realm:prefs`), and `where` when they picked where it shows |
| `elytra:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `elytra:jukeboxes` | World | JSON list of Jukebox positions (`"dimension|x|y|z"`) that hold a Run Away disc, so the discs survive restarts |

### How it works

Every `intervalTicks` the pack looks at each player's `isGliding`. For gliding players who haven't disabled it, it reads `getVelocity()` (blocks per tick, times 20), their Y, the chest slot's durability through the equippable component, and counts rockets in the inventory and offhand, then writes it: in the player's [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box for `intervalTicks` + 10 ticks with the side boxes protocol (`scripts/side.js`, as Mob Health does), taken off as soon as the player stops gliding, or with `onScreenDisplay.setActionBar`. The same look keeps the list of gliding players: every 2 ticks, those of them gliding faster than 24 blocks a second without a NOS burst (and with the HUD enabled) get the slipstream, two `realm:sky_spark` ahead and a puff of smoke behind; nobody else is looked at between rounds.

Above the hotbar, it also sends the script event `realm:actionbar` with `{"player":"<id>","ticks":30,"from":"elytra_bp","steady":50}` (renewed every 10 ticks; `ticks` is at least 3 times `intervalTicks`), the same request Mob Health makes, so the Coordinates HUD leaves that player's bar alone until they stop gliding. `steady: 50` is the highest steady line rank (see the action bar protocol in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)), so the other steady lines (a run line, the build mode line, the story tracker, the Relics readouts) wait while you glide. It also listens to `realm:actionbar`: while another pack's note lasts (not its own, not a `background` one like the Party HUD's, and not a lower steady line's) it skips its redraws but keeps sending its own request, so steady lines still wait and it gets the bar back first when the note ends.

## Minimap — `map_bp`

A compass strip across the top of your screen shows which way you're facing, the region you're in and what's around: your destination or quest target (a gold star with its distance), party mates, other online friends, wanderer camps, the Atlas sites you found, the nearest town, your bed, a rainbow's pot of gold, and nearby mobs in red. A 21 x 21 (441-cell) topographic minimap radar at the top right below the compass strip (above the Elytra speed HUD) samples visible water, roofs, vegetation and ground, with elevation shading, live block-change updates, and automatic cave layers below solid roofs or in the Nether. Gold route breadcrumbs (`Q_ROUTE`) point toward your destination or quest target; markers show nearby townsfolk, friendly wanderers, mobs, camps and sites, with edge arrows for off-map party mates, online friends and destinations. The radar reclaims its old thick border for terrain, protects all four direction labels, and makes your arrow and real-player markers slightly larger without changing the grid or world coverage. **Mara's Field Map**, Minecraft's own locator map, shows the land itself. The strip, radar and icons are drawn by [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp), part of **Realm Resources**.

### How to use

1. Look at the top of your screen and the top right below it. The compass strip shows N, E, S and W with a tick every 15 degrees (60 degrees to each side of where you face) and, under it, the [Atlas](#atlas-of-the-realm--atlas_bp) region you're in. Icons on the strip: a **gold star** is your destination (or active quest target), **blue dots** are party mates, **white dots** are other online players (`showOthers`, enabled by default), **red dots** are mobs within 24 blocks, a **tent** is a wanderer camp, a **purple diamond** is an Atlas site you found, a **house** is the nearest town ([Town Projects](#town-projects--town_bp)), a **red bed** is where you respawn (your bed or respawn anchor) and a **rainbow** is where an unfound [pot of gold](#rainbows--the-pot-of-gold--rainbow_bp) is. Your destination, party mates, other online players, mobs and the rainbow show as arrows in their color at the ends of the strip when they're out of view (behind you); the rainbow's arrows are striped like a rainbow. Ordinary townsfolk (**yellow dots**) and friendly wanderers (**green dots**) show only on the 21 x 21 minimap radar so they don't clutter the compass strip, unless you picked one as your destination or have an active quest reporting to them (when the gold star points to them on both the strip and the minimap).
2. Run `/realm:map` and pick **Get Mara's Field Map** to get an empty locator map. Use it once to draw the land around you, then hold it in your other hand (offhand): Minecraft shows it at the side of your view with your arrow and other players' arrows on it. The pack doesn't draw on it.
3. Want to go somewhere? Run `/realm:map`, pick **Pick a destination**, then choose from **Townsfolk**, **Waystones I know**, **Towns**, **Wanderer camps**, **Atlas sites I found**, **Where I died**, **Party mates** or **My marked spots** (each list is nearest first, with the direction and distance). The star points there. When you get within 8 blocks (`arriveDistance`), chat says `Arrived at ...` and the destination clears.
4. With no destination picked, the star follows your [story tracker](#story-questlines--saga_bp)'s current goal (the place to go or the townsfolk or wanderer to report to). That one never clears on its own: it moves on with the story. During a [Choir siege](#realm-calendar--calendar_bp) the star points to the siege instead, for everyone in the Overworld: the besieged town during the warning (`Siege: Lanternford`), then the nearest Ritual Circle still singing (`Choir circle (3 left)`); after the siege it goes back to the story. A destination you picked still wins.
5. Mark a spot with `/realm:map_mark "Iron cave"` (or **Mark this spot** in `/realm:map`). You can keep 5 (`maxMarks`); marking one more forgets the oldest, and **My marked spots** has **Forget a spot**. `/realm:map_clear` clears your destination.
6. Toggle your minimap radar at any time with `/realm:minimap` and your compass strip with `/realm:compass` (or use the quick toggles in `/realm:map`). Change your settings in `/realm:prefs` → **Minimap**: **Compass strip** (enabled by default), **Radar** (enabled by default; a 21 x 21 topographic minimap at the top right below the compass strip and above the Elytra speed HUD, with you in the middle), **Terrain colors on my minimap** (enabled by default, `radarTerrain` / `terrain`), **Radar keeps north up** (disabled: the radar turns with you, so ahead is always up), **Show mobs on my minimap**, **Show the nearest town** and **Show my bed** (both enabled by default, `showTown` and `showHome`) and **My mob and radar range** (default 24 blocks, `mobRadius`).
7. **Operators:** `/realm:config` → **Minimap** turns the strip and radar off for everyone (`enabled`), sets what new players start with (`compassDefault`, `radarDefault`, `radarTerrain`), the largest mob range anyone may pick (default 32, `mobRadiusMax`), whether players outside your party show (**Show players outside your party**, enabled by default, `showOthers`) and **Minimap script time a tick** (default normal, `budgetLevel`): on a big server, low costs the server less. **Server size** in [Realm Configuration](#realm-configuration--admin_bp)'s Operator Tools sets it to low for a Large server. `/realm:map_reset` explains the reset; `/realm:map_reset confirm` clears everyone's picked destination and saved marks, including offline players once they next join. A form opened before the reset cannot restore old marks. To show everyone a title, use `/realm:admin_title "Text" "Subtitle" 5` instead of `/title`: the strip draws over a plain `/title` within about 1.5 seconds.

### See and hear it

![Render (made from the glyph font itself, not a screenshot) of the compass strip facing east-northeast, with a mob arrow on the left, a town, a townsfolk, the destination star, a mob, E, a wanderer, an Atlas site, a bed and a rainbow arrow on the right, and the radar below turning with the player](media/map/map-hud.png)

### What players see

- **The strip** is 25 icons wide at the top center of the screen (5 degrees each), on a light dark background. The middle shows a white mark where you face, unless a letter or an icon is there. Each icon sits at its bearing from you; when two land on the same spot the more important one shows (destination, then party mate or rainbow, then mob, then other online player, then camp or site, then town or bed; nearer wins between equals). Ordinary townsfolk and friendly wanderers stay on the 21 x 21 minimap only, unless picked as your destination or active quest target (shown as the gold star).
- **Its second line:** the destination as `<star> Mara 57m` (or `<star> Mara (in the Nether)`), then the region in gray (`The Gray Downs`; in the Nether or the End, `In the Nether`). A picked party mate who is offline shows as `Mate is offline`. Arriving shows `Arrived: Mara` with a green check for 3 seconds. A story goal with no place to point at shows its label in gray, with no star.
- **What shows where:** townsfolk (and caravan traders) and friendly wanderers within 64 blocks (`npcRange`) on the 21 x 21 minimap radar only (and as the gold star on both the strip and minimap when you have an active quest reporting to them or picked them as your destination); mobs within your mob range, the nearest 8 (`maxMobs`); wanderer camps and the Atlas sites you found within 256 blocks (`placeRange`); party mates anywhere in your dimension; other online players in your dimension within 128 blocks (`showOthers`, enabled by default); the nearest town in your dimension at any distance (none while you're within 24 blocks of its middle: you're there); your respawn point (`getSpawnPoint`: your bed or respawn anchor) at any distance in its dimension, hidden within 4 blocks; and an unfound rainbow's pot of gold anywhere in the Overworld, until someone finds it or it expires (it has no distance or name on the strip, so it stays a race). Only your own death point, the waystones you know and the sites you found are offered as destinations.
- **Wanderers:** a wanderer at their camp always shows on the minimap. One on the road shows on the minimap only once the Wanderers pack has said they're friendly, so a hostile in disguise never shows (no green dot, and no red one either until it drops the disguise and becomes a mob). When you have an active quest to report back to a wanderer (`realm:track`), the gold star points to them on both the compass strip and the minimap. A wanderer already on the road when the realm started stays hidden until they leave.
- **The radar** (`realm_side_radar`) sits at the top right below the compass strip and above the Elytra speed HUD: a 21 x 21 (441-cell) topographic grid with you in the middle as a white arrow, where its edge is your mob range (24 blocks by default, ~2.4 blocks a cell). With **Terrain colors on my minimap** (`radarTerrain` / `terrain`, enabled by default), cells show actual sampled material and elevation: sunlit hills, shaded slopes, grass, sand, snow, stone, forest, paths, crops, wood and masonry, biome palettes, shallow/deep water and lava. Placements or breaks refresh terrain live. A solid roof more than 6 blocks above you (or the Nether) selects the cave slice at your elevation: solid walls (`Q_CAVE_WALL`), floors (`Q_CAVE_FLOOR`), and underground pools; water above a diver is not a solid roof. Gold route breadcrumbs (`Q_ROUTE`) point toward your destination or quest target. Turning with you, a small red `N` on the edge shows north. Off-map destinations/quest targets, party mates and online friends use 8-way edge arrows (gold `Q_STAR_0..7`, blue `Q_PARTY_0..7`, cyan/white `Q_FRIEND_0..7`); the rainbow's pot of gold also appears on the edge, while ordinary townsfolk, wanderers, the town and your bed show only within range.
- **Radar directions and players:** all four N, E, S and W badges are protected from marker overwrites; a marker sharing a badge's edge cell uses an adjacent cell on that same edge when one is available. The terrain fills the space previously used by the thick black border, with a thin boundary and no dark vignette over the letters. Your white arrow, other real players' white markers and real party members' blue markers are slightly larger within their cells; NPC, mob and wanderer icon art is unchanged. The strip above the map is unchanged. Generated pixel tests cover the larger player art, but a simulated player or single-client screenshot does not prove how a second real player's marker looks.
- **Titles** from other packs (a region banner, a card, a level-up) hide the strip and radar until they fade, like the side boxes. A `/title` typed by an operator or run by a command block isn't announced to the packs, so while the strip is on it replaces such a title within about 1.5 seconds (titles and the strip share one channel). Operators: use `/realm:admin_title` ([Realm Configuration](#realm-configuration--admin_bp), also its **Show a Title** quick action) instead; the strip steps aside for it.
- **Without Realm Resources** (or with an older Side HUD) the icons show as boxes and the strip shows in the middle of the screen as a subtitle. Turn **Compass strip** and **Radar** off in `/realm:prefs` (or run `/realm:compass` and `/realm:minimap`) until you have it.
- **Turning a part off** (the realm option, or your own radar or compass preference) sends its empty segment. The resource binding hides that whole panel, including its background, rather than leaving an empty black square.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:map` | Everyone | The **Minimap** menu: your destination, **Get Mara's Field Map** (an empty locator map), **Pick a destination**, **Mark this spot**, **Clear destination**, and quick toggles for the Minimap and Compass strip |
| `/realm:minimap` | Everyone | Shows or hides your minimap radar at the top right below the compass strip |
| `/realm:compass` | Everyone | Shows or hides your compass strip at the top of the screen |
| `/realm:map_mark [name]` | Everyone | Marks where you stand (default name `Spot 1`, `Spot 2`...); you keep 5 (`maxMarks`), the oldest goes first. Pick it later in `/realm:map` |
| `/realm:map_clear` | Everyone | Clears your destination: the star follows your story again |
| `/realm:map_reset [confirm]` | Operators | With no argument, explains what will be cleared. With `confirm`, clears online players' destinations and marked spots now and offline players' once on their next join. Only a player who had a destination or spots to clear gets the chat line saying so; a player who joins later with nothing saved is not told. New marks saved after the reset stay; preferences, known waystones and native map items are untouched |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | The compass strip and radar for the whole realm. Disabled: nobody sees them; `/realm:map`, destinations and Arrived still work |
| `compassDefault` | `true` | The compass strip for players who haven't chosen |
| `radarDefault` | `true` | The minimap radar for players who haven't chosen |
| `radarTerrain` | `true` | Terrain colors on the minimap radar (`terrain` in `/realm:prefs`) for players who haven't chosen |
| `radarNorthUp` | `false` | The radar keeps north up for players who haven't chosen (disabled: it turns with them) |
| `showMobs` | `true` | Mobs show as red dots, for players who haven't chosen |
| `mobRadius` | `24` | How far mobs show and how far the radar reaches (blocks), for players who haven't chosen (8 to 48 in game) |
| `mobRadiusMax` | `32` | The largest mob range a player may pick (8 to 48); a player's own range is cut to it |
| `maxMobs` | `8` | Mobs drawn at most per player, the nearest (1 to 16) |
| `showTown` | `true` | The nearest town (Town Projects) shows as a house, for players who haven't chosen |
| `showHome` | `true` | Your bed or respawn anchor shows as a red bed, for players who haven't chosen |
| `showOthers` | `true` | Online players outside your party show on the compass strip and minimap (with directional arrows at the minimap edge when off-map). Party mates always show |
| `npcRange` | `64` | Townsfolk and wanderers this close show on the minimap (16 to 96) |
| `placeRange` | `256` | Wanderer camps and found Atlas sites this close show on the strip (32 to 512) |
| `arriveDistance` | `8` | A picked destination clears this close (2 to 32 blocks). The story goal never does |
| `maxMarks` | `5` | Spots each player keeps with **Mark this spot** (1 to 10) |
| `budgetLevel` | `normal` | How much script time the minimap may use a tick, for everyone together: `low` (about 2 ms a tick: with many players the radar's land and mob dots lag a little more), `normal` (about 2.9 ms) or `high` (about 4.4 ms, smoother with many players moving). In `/realm:config` as **Minimap script time a tick**; changes at once |
| `intervalTicks` | `10` | How often (ticks) the markers, destination and region are looked up (10 at the fastest); the strip and radar turn with you every tick in between. Read when the world starts |

Operators can change every option but `intervalTicks` in game with `/realm:config`. Each player picks **Compass strip**, **Radar**, **Terrain colors on my minimap**, **Radar keeps north up**, **Show mobs on my minimap**, **Show the nearest town**, **Show my bed** and **My mob and radar range** in `/realm:prefs` (or toggles the minimap and compass strip directly with `/realm:minimap` and `/realm:compass`).

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `map:wp` | Player | JSON `{ k, id?, n, dim, x, z }`: the picked destination (kind: `npc`, `waystone`, `town`, `camp`, `site`, `death`, `party` or `mark`; townsfolk, camps, the death point and party mates are followed live, the rest stay where they were picked) |
| `map:marks` | Player | JSON list of `{ n, dim, x, z }`: the marked spots, oldest first |
| `map:pref` | Player | The player's choices in `/realm:prefs`, when they differ from the realm's |
| `map:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `map:reset` | World | The reset generation, a whole number set by each `/realm:map_reset confirm` to the larger of the previous value plus 1 and the time in Unix seconds (so it is not a count of resets: it stays above every player's `map:gen` even if this property was forgotten). Missing or 0 means no reset has run |
| `map:gen` | Player | The `map:reset` generation last applied to this player (written on their first join after a reset even when they had nothing to clear), so an offline player resets once without erasing later marks; a player whose value is lower than `map:reset` is reset on their next join |

Everything else (townsfolk, waystones, towns, camps, sites, regions, death points, story goals, the rainbow's pot) is what the other packs send; it lives in memory and is asked for again when the world loads and when a player joins.

### How it works

- **Drawing:** scripts can't draw on the HUD or on map items, so the strip and radar are text made of icons from a glyph font: Side HUD's `font/glyph_F3.png` draws U+F300 to U+F3FF (Unicode's Private Use Area, a page away from the ones add-ons usually use). The icons carry their own colors and are each drawn edge to edge, so they line up like cells. The characters are named in `scripts/glyphs.js`, the only pack file allowed characters outside ASCII; both are generated by `tools/gen-glyphs/gen.mjs` (`npm run gen:glyphs`; `npm run check` runs it with `--check`).
- **Terrain:** a scanner reads the land a little every tick within a time budget (about 1 ms a tick, saved up while there is little to read) and at most 48 columns a tick (24 for one player). Walking or standing, it reads what your radar's own picture is missing (the exact block columns near you once you stop); flying or riding fast, also the ground ahead of you. Liquid-inclusive downward rays find river water instead of its sandy bottom; water plants resolve to water, while a visible bridge, slab, roof or waterlogged built block keeps its solid material and height. Depth/material probes use the same operation budget, not uncounted vertical loops. Canonical 4-block outer samples and separate exact 1-block samples within 6 blocks keep thin nearby structures from aliasing into a neighbor's cache entry; outer coverage is filled first and known coarse data can fill a missing fine sample. Resolution is part of the collision-free cache identity. Unknown ground stays blank; failed reads preserve known data and become eligible for retry after 5 ticks under the same budget. Surface and per-floor underground stores stay separate (the floor is the height you stand at: a jump keeps the floor you jumped from, a fall or climb of 3 blocks or more changes it at once), water above a diver does not count as a solid roof, and placing or breaking a block invalidates both resolutions and affected elevation shades for every viewer.
- **Elevation and shared compass data:** relief uses actual sampled heights with stronger grass, rock and path/wood contrast, distinct pale sandstone masonry, and farmland/crop rows. Shaded glyphs are reused per column until that column or an affected neighbor changes. Compass and radar already share one render pose, heading, dimension, destination, region and marker set; vertical movement now refreshes that pose too, including ascent/descent through cave layers. The compass and radar still toggle independently, and off-dimension targets do not appear as local arrows. The unchanged 21 x 21 grid and default 24-block radius are not a native map's 128 x 128 detail.
- **A full cache:** separate adaptive coarse/fine queues retain useful near detail within a 6000-column store cap (300 more per player with the radar on); reading a viewer's exact origin promotes it so another viewer cannot evict its roof probe immediately. Flowering azalea leaves remain canopy, not ground-level flowers. Cached terrain also has a 2400-tick freshness limit (stale columns are found when the radar is next built, at least every 200 ticks); periodic refresh reads are distinct from cache-eviction churn and unloaded-chunk retries.
- **Layout:** the accepted minimap stays fixed at the top right, offset `[-4, 48]`, with a 100.8 x 105.8 widget, 98.8 x 103.8 terrain window and 108-unit reserve. The original top compass is unchanged. Right readouts center only in the remaining region below the map; left readouts and the full native Stats scoreboard center below the compass band. The one-pixel generated frame, measured 8.5/9-pixel native advance, dual-mesh offsets and rounding allowance retain the complete 21 x 21 grid without changing world radius, terrain cache or subtitle slices. Player art remains selectively enlarged (self/edge-player arrows 8%, other-player radius 3.2 to 3.8, party-player radius 4.2 to 4.8); NPC/mob/wanderer and compass art stay unchanged. The frame/font/render come from `tools/gen-glyphs/gen.mjs`. The calibrated map passed four-heading Windows client checks at the prior layout; the latest centered readout layout has separate acceptance.
- **Sending it:** the strip and the radar travel in the [side boxes protocol](#how-the-packs-work-together) as two more slots after the nine boxes: `top` (the strip, 25 icons of 3 bytes, a spacer line holding one space, a new line and the second line, within 159 bytes) and `radar` (21 rows of 21 icons, 1343 bytes in a 1352-byte segment / 1351 text bytes), the radar as the part `map/radar`. A readout is drawn again only when it changed, or every 30 ticks to keep it up (it lasts 40); a player who hasn't turned, moved or got new markers since gets the same title again without the strip and radar being built. The Minimap is the side boxes' compositor: it draws the title of every player it shows something to, with the other packs' boxes in it, and never sends its own parts to the other packs (`realm:side_comp`, see the side boxes protocol in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).
- **Each pass** (every 10 ticks per player with the strip or radar on, spread over the ticks in between, at most two a tick and within a time budget of about 0.5 ms: with more than about 15 players a pass comes a little less often; mob markers then refresh about every 1.3 seconds with 40 players): one `getEntities` for `monster` family mobs within the player's range (`closest: maxMobs`, without `realm:npc`), and one for `realm:npc` within `npcRange`, done every other pass and kept while the player moves less than 8 blocks. Townsfolk are those with `realm:npc_owner:npc_bp` (and caravan traders); wanderers carry `realm:npc_owner:wander_bp`: those with a `wander:c:` tag (at their camp) show, those on the road only once `realm:wander_spawn` said they aren't hostile (`realm:wander_turn` hides them again). Party mates are the players with the same `realm_party:<code>` tag. The respawn point is `player.getSpawnPoint()`, read once a pass. Everything else is arithmetic on what other packs broadcast (the minimap events in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)). A pass draws the strip and radar again only when it found something new: a marker that moved a quarter block or more, another second line, or other settings. Between passes, every tick (up to 12 players a tick, the rest in turns), players who turned at least 2 degrees or moved at least half a block, including vertically, or whose land nearby was just read, get the strip and radar drawn again; only a part whose text changed is sent, and each part again every 30 ticks so it never fades (a player whose title is due for that is always looked at that tick, whatever their turn). Drawing and building the radar's terrain picture each have a time budget a tick (about 1 ms and 0.4 ms), the players waiting longest first: with many players moving at once, each one's strip comes a few ticks later and the terrain under the radar may lag behind its markers for a moment. The terrain grid moves in whole blocks and turns in 2-degree steps; markers, arrows and the strip are exact. Each radar's terrain picture is also built again every 10 seconds, each player at their own moment (not everyone's in the same tick), so land read more than 2 minutes ago is found and read again. After a change of dimension, a move of more than 256 blocks since the pass (a teleport) or a change of settings or destination, it waits for the next pass.
- **Cost:** the minimap keeps to time budgets instead of a per-player cost: about 4.2 ms a tick with 40 players moving around and 2.7 ms with 10 (measured with the harness profiler on a 4-core dedicated server, October 2026; it was 108 and 25). One player alone is drawn every tick, and players standing still cost no redraws. A title about to fade is drawn first, and drawn again as it is (cheap) even when the drawing budget is spent, so with many players moving a strip can lag a little but never goes off. The budgets are constants at the top of `scripts/main.js` (drawing 1 ms a tick, terrain pictures 0.4, passes 0.5, scanner 1; each saves up a little for bursts), at `budgetLevel` normal: about 2.9 ms a tick at most. `low` keeps the drawing budget (it is what keeps every strip and radar from fading with many players) and gives the terrain pictures and scanner half and the passes 0.6: about 2.0 ms a tick at most (measured with 40 players: 3.5 ms a tick instead of 4.2; with 10: 2.4 instead of 2.7). `high` is 1.5 times every budget, about 4.4 ms. `realm:map_state` reports `budgetLevel` and `perTick`.
- **For players on a big server:** with `budgetLevel` low, or many players moving at once, your strip and radar still keep up, but the land under the radar and the mob dots can lag a second or two behind; standing still, everything catches up.
- **The field map** is `give @s minecraft:empty_map 1 2` (data 2 is the empty locator map; the stable API can't set an item's data), then named `Mara's Field Map` with a hint in its lore. Locator maps draw the land and the players' arrows themselves.
- **Checked** on a dedicated server (`tools/test-bds/examples/map.js`: the strip and radar for known positions, the title decoded byte for byte, destinations, Arrived, the story goal, wanderers, party mates, every broadcast and ping, the cost), not in a game client: how the glyphs and the strip look on screen hasn't been seen (a dedicated server doesn't draw the HUD). If the strip sits in the wrong place, the numbers are `offset` and `$slot_max` of `realm_side_top` and `realm_side_radar` in Side HUD. In game each icon turned out about 17 units wide, so 25 cells take about 430: before Side HUD 1.3.0 the strip's limit was 420 and its last cell (the right edge arrow) wrapped onto a line of its own under the middle; it's 440 now (the 21 x 21 radar sits in its own 1352-byte slot). The icons are also taller than a line of text (about 16 units against 10), so a second line right under them was drawn over the strip's baseline: since Minimap 1.2.1 a spacer line goes between them (and under a strip on its own, so the box covers the icons), and the top box may be 40 high (it was 30).
- **Testing hook:** `/scriptevent realm:map_debug {"player":"<id or name>","action":"state"}` (operators and scripts) answers `realm:map_state` with the last strip, second line and radar, the destination, what the pack heard and the cost so far; `"action":"cost"` also starts the cost count again.

---

## Realm Mail — `mail_bp`

Write letters to anyone who has played on the realm, online or not. Letters to offline players wait in their inbox, and they're told about them when they join. Letters carry words only: for items, see the [Player Mailroom](https://mc.nish.software/mailroom/) build.

### How to use

1. Run `/realm:mail` and pick **Write a letter**. Choose who it's for from the list (online players, with `(online)` after their names, and those seen most recently: 60 names at most), or, once more players have joined than the list holds, type a name in **Or type their name** (the whole name, or enough of it to match one player; offline players get it when they're back; a typed name wins over the list). A name nobody has brings the form back with `No player called "..." has joined the realm.` Then type a subject and the letter, and press **Send**. Minecraft's text boxes hold only 100 characters each, so the letter has several boxes (6 for the default 600 characters): a full box runs straight on into the next, and after a box that isn't full the next one starts a new line. You can also type `\n` for a new line.
2. **Write to your whole party:** in a [party](#parties--party_bp), the first choice in the list is **My party (Bob, Dan)**: it sends a copy of the letter to every mate, offline ones included.
3. If they're online, they see `New letter from Sam: "Hello!". Read it with /realm:mail` in chat. If not, the letter waits: the next time they join, chat says `You have 2 unread letters: /realm:mail`.
4. **Read your letters:** `/realm:mail` → **Inbox**. New letters are marked `[New]`. Open one to read it, then **Reply** or **Delete** it. **Delete all read letters** clears out the rest and shows the inbox again.
5. **Block a sender:** open one of their letters and tap **Block sender** (their later letters to you aren't delivered). **Blocked players** in `/realm:mail` lists who you've blocked; tap a name to unblock it.
6. **See what you sent:** `/realm:mail` → **Sent** shows your recent letters and whether each was read yet.
7. Don't want the chat line on joining? Disable **Unread letters notice on join** in `/realm:prefs`.
8. **Operators:** `/realm:config` → **Realm Mail** sets how many letters an inbox holds, how many are kept in Sent, the wait between letters, and whether players are told about unread letters on joining. `/realm:mail` → **Delete letters from a player** (operators only) finds a writer by gamertag and removes all their letters from every inbox and Sent list after you confirm; it can't be undone.

### What players see

- **The menu** says how many unread letters you have, then **Inbox** (`3 letters, 1 unread`), **Write a letter** and **Sent**.
- **Writing:** the recipient list holds every player who has joined since the pack was added (up to 400, `maxRoster`; the ones seen longest ago are forgotten first). The subject is shortened to 40 characters (`subjectLength`) and the letter to 600 (`bodyLength`); chat says `(It was shortened to fit.)` when that happens. An empty letter brings the form back with `Write something in the letter first.` A letter without a subject gets `(no subject)`. Color and format codes (`§` and the character after it) are taken out of the subject and the letter, so a letter can't pass for a message from the realm. The subject is at most 100 characters whatever `subjectLength` says, the most a text box takes.
- **To your party:** while you're in a [party](#parties--party_bp), the recipient list starts with `My party (Bob, Dan)`: every member of your party, offline ones included, from the Parties pack's member list. It sends each of them their own copy, to read, answer and delete like any letter, and each copy shows in your Sent list. Chat says `Letter sent to your party: Bob, Dan.`; a mate whose mailbox is full of unread letters is skipped and named (`Dan's mailbox is full of unread letters, so they didn't get it.`), and when every mailbox is full the form comes back with `Every mailbox in your party is full of unread letters (Bob, Dan). Try again once they've read some.` The wait between letters counts once for the whole party letter.
- **Waiting between letters:** each player can send one letter every 10 seconds (`sendCooldownSeconds`); sending sooner brings the form back, filled in, with `Wait 4 more seconds before sending another letter, then press Send again.` at the top
- **Full inboxes:** an inbox holds 50 letters (`inboxLimit`). For an ordinary player letter, the oldest letters its owner has already read are dropped to make room. If every letter in it is still unread, the letter isn't sent: the form comes back, filled in, with `Alex's mailbox is full of unread letters. Try again once they've read some.` at the top, so you can pick someone else or keep the text. Pack letters use the stricter policy below and never evict player-written letters.
- **Reading** a letter shows who sent it and when (`3h ago (2026-10-06 14:05 UTC)`), and marks it read. **Reply** opens the letter form with the sender picked and the subject `Re: ...`.
- **Sent** keeps your last 30 letters (`sentLimit`), each marked `read`, `not read yet` or `deleted` (by the recipient). **Remove from Sent** removes your copy only; the recipient keeps theirs.
- **No items:** letters can't carry items, because an item's full data can't be stored safely by an add-on. To send items, use the [Player Mailroom](https://mc.nish.software/mailroom/) build (the mail menu points to `mc.nish.software/mailroom`; another realm can change or remove that line with `itemsHint`).
- **Letters from the realm:** other packs can send letters (a townsfolk writes when you become Close with them, in [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)). They show the sender's name (`From: Old Tobin`), have no **Reply** button, skip the wait between letters and keep no Sent copy. New arrivals keep at most 20 pack letters per inbox (`systemInboxLimit`), replacing an older pack letter rather than a player's letter. Pack letters expire after 30 days (`systemLetterDays`) even if unread; a missing or invalid old timestamp is not treated as ancient. At the realm-wide 5,000-letter bound, 1,000 places are reserved from pack senders for player correspondence (`systemReserve`); a pack letter that cannot fit is not delivered, and none of the recipient's letters are deleted to make room for it (only expired pack letters are cleared). Existing player letters are not evicted to meet this reserve.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:mail` | Everyone | Opens Realm Mail: your **Inbox** (read, reply, delete; default 50 letters each, `inboxLimit`), **Write a letter** to any player who has joined, even offline, or to your whole party, and **Sent** (your last 30 letters, `sentLimit`) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `inboxLimit` | `50` | Most letters one inbox holds. A new letter in a full inbox drops the oldest read letters first; if all are unread, it isn't sent (10–200 in game) |
| `systemInboxLimit` | `20` | Most pack-originated letters kept in one inbox when a new one arrives; only older pack letters are replaced |
| `systemLetterDays` | `30` | Pack-letter retention in real days, read or unread; `0` disables expiry. Player-written letters and unknown legacy sender records are not expired by this policy |
| `systemReserve` | `1000` | Places reserved from pack senders at the 5,000-letter realm cap: by default pack letters stop at 4,000. Does not delete player letters |
| `sentLimit` | `30` | Most letters kept in each player's Sent list; the oldest drop off first. `0` keeps none (0–100 in game) |
| `subjectLength` | `40` | Longest subject, in characters |
| `bodyLength` | `600` | Longest letter, in characters. The form gets one 100-character box per 100 characters |
| `notifyOnJoin` | `true` | Players with unread letters get `You have 2 unread letters: /realm:mail` in chat on joining |
| `notifyDelaySeconds` | `8` | Seconds after joining before that line, so it comes after the welcome and news popups |
| `sendCooldownSeconds` | `10` | Seconds a player waits between two letters. `0` = no wait (0–120 in game) |
| `maxRoster` | `400` | Most players remembered as recipients; the ones seen longest ago are forgotten first. Their letters stay |
| `itemsHint` | `"To send items, use the Player Mailroom build (mc.nish.software/mailroom)."` | The mail menu's line on how to send items. `""` = no line |
| `senderUnreadCap` | `5` | Most unread letters from one player that one inbox holds; they can send again once some are read or deleted. `0` = no cap (menu range 0 to 50). Letters from packs aren't counted |
| `blockListMax` | `30` | Most players one player can block (config only). A blocked player's letters aren't delivered; letters from packs still are |

Operators can change `inboxLimit`, `systemInboxLimit`, `systemLetterDays`, `systemReserve`, `sentLimit`, `notifyOnJoin` and `sendCooldownSeconds` in game with `/realm:config`; changes apply without a restart. Each player can switch the join notice off or on for themselves with **Unread letters notice on join** in `/realm:prefs`, which follows `notifyOnJoin` until they choose. The rest stays in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `mail:l:<id>` | World | One per letter: JSON `{ id, f, fn, t, tn, s, b, at, r, di, ds }`, the writer's and recipient's ids and names, subject, letter, when it was sent (ms), read, deleted from the inbox, removed from Sent. Removed once both the recipient deleted it and it left the writer's Sent list |
| `mail:next` | World | The next letter id |
| `mail:roster` | World | JSON list of players who have joined: `[{ i, n, t }]`, id, name and last join (ms), newest first, up to `maxRoster` |
| `mail:b:<id>` | World | One per recipient who blocks senders: JSON list `[{ i, n }]` of blocked players (id and name), up to `blockListMax` (default 30) |
| `mail:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's own `joinNotice` choice from `/realm:prefs` |
| `mail:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- Each letter is its own small world property (a few hundred bytes up to about 2 KB), so no property comes near the 32 KB limit however many letters a player keeps. The realm holds up to 5,000 letters in all. Letters are read into memory once and kept in step as they change.
- The roster is updated on every join (`afterEvents.playerSpawn` with `initialSpawn`), so a player who changes their gamertag shows under the new name. Letters are addressed by player id, so they still arrive.
- **Party letters:** [Parties](#parties--party_bp) sends every party's members, offline ones included, with `realm:party_members` (kept in memory and asked for with `realm:party_members_ping` about 3 seconds after the world loads). **My party** lists the other members of the writer's party (by their `realm_party:<code>` tag), as long as the writer is on that party's list, with each mate's roster name when there is one (else the gamertag Parties saved). Mates who are offline still get the letter; it is sent as one ordinary letter per mate.
- The unread notice is sent `notifyDelaySeconds` after joining. A letter to someone online reaches them straight away with a chat line and a sound.
- The forms are `ActionFormData` and `ModalFormData` from `@minecraft/server-ui`.
- **Letters from other packs:** `realm:mail_send` `{ to, from, subject, body }`: `to` a player id or name from the roster, `from` any name to show as the sender, the subject and letter shortened to `subjectLength` and `bodyLength`. The letter has an explicitly empty writer id (`f === ""`), so it cannot be answered and uses the system inbox/expiry/reserve policy. A missing or unknown legacy writer field is not silently reclassified. The recipient gets the usual chat line if online.
- **Test hook:** `realm:mail_test` `{ roster: n }` adds n long-gone players to the roster. It only works from the server console, and it changes the world's saved data: for tests only.

## Nicknames — `nick_bp`

Pick a nickname and a color to show above your head instead of your gamertag. Chat, the player list and death messages still show gamertags: the stable Script API can't change chat. With [Titles & Trails](#titles--trails--titles_bp), the title a player wears shows in gray on a line under the name, with or without a nickname.

### How to use

1. Run `/realm:nick`, type a nickname (3 to 16 letters A-Z, digits, spaces or `_`), pick a color and tap **Save**. It shows above your head right away, with your gamertag in gray underneath.
2. Run `/realm:nick` again to change it, or enable **Remove my nickname** there to show your gamertag again. Your nickname stays when you leave, die or the realm restarts.
3. Wear a title from `/realm:titles` (the Titles & Trails pack) and it shows in gray on its own line under your name, whether or not you have a nickname. Choose **None** there to take it off.
4. **Operators:** `/realm:nick` → **Players' nicknames (operator)** lists saved nicknames 20 to a page (**Previous page** / **Next page**), with **Search by name** (part of a nickname or gamertag) and **Show everyone**; tap one to clear it, even for players who are offline. If the nickname changed while the question was open, nothing is cleared. To turn nicknames off for everyone, disable **Nicknames** in `/realm:config` → **Nicknames**.

### What players see

- **Above your head:** your nickname in the color you picked, and your gamertag in gray on a second line (`showGamertag`), so everyone still knows who is who. With the AFK pack, an AFK player's tag reads `[AFK] Nickname`. A title from Titles & Trails adds one more gray line under that, and shows under the plain gamertag for players without a nickname.
- **Chat still shows your gamertag**, and so do the player list, death messages, `/realm:` command messages and other packs' messages. The stable Script API has no chat events, so a pack can't change the name in chat.
- **Rules:** 3 to 16 characters: letters A-Z, digits, spaces and `_` (spaces at the ends are trimmed, repeated spaces become one). A nickname cannot be another player's remembered gamertag or nickname, whatever the case: the form says `Alex is someone else's gamertag.` or `Sam already has that nickname.` and opens again. Offline gamertag protection starts on the player's first join after the October 2026 update. Remembered gamertags expire after 365 inactive days by default (`forgetGamertagsAfterDays`); `0` keeps them indefinitely. Saved nicknames are not pruned by this setting.
- **Colors:** White, Gray, Red, Dark red, Gold, Yellow, Green, Dark green, Aqua, Dark aqua, Blue, Light purple, Dark purple.
- **Operators** clearing a nickname see `Cleared Nick (Gamertag).`; the player, if online, gets `An operator cleared your nickname.` An operator who is de-opped while the question is open clears nothing.
- **While nicknames are disabled** (`enabled`): `/realm:nick` answers `Nicknames are disabled on this realm. An operator can enable them in /realm:config (Nicknames).`, everyone shows their gamertag, and saved nicknames come back once it's enabled again. Titles still show under the gamertag.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:nick` | Everyone | Set, change or remove your nickname and its color, shown above your head (3 to 16 letters, digits, spaces or `_`). Operators also get the saved nicknames, 20 to a page and searchable, to clear any of them. Works while nicknames are enabled (default enabled, `enabled`) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Players can set nicknames. Disabled: everyone shows their gamertag; nicknames are kept |
| `showGamertag` | `true` | Show the gamertag in gray on a second line under the nickname |
| `forgetGamertagsAfterDays` | `365` | Forget remembered gamertags after this many real inactive days; `0` disables pruning. Online players are skipped, saved nicknames stay, and untimestamped legacy records start counting when first observed |
| `reservedNames` | `"Admin, Owner, Server"` | Nicknames players can't take (comma separated; any case, spaces and underscores ignored, so "Ad min" is "Admin"). Operators may use them. Saved nicknames are kept |
| `reservedGamertags` | `""` | Gamertags reserved even while their player is offline or has never joined (comma separated), so nobody else can take them. The game doesn't tell packs who the operators are, so list the offline ones here. A player may still use their own gamertag. Online operators are reserved automatically; never-seen offline operators need this list |
| `afkTag` | `afk` | The tag the AFK pack gives AFK players. Keep it the same as AFK `tag` |
| `afkPrefix` | `§7[AFK]§r ` | Shown before a nickname while the player has `afkTag`. Keep it the same as AFK `nameTagPrefix` |

Operators can change `enabled`, `showGamertag` and `forgetGamertagsAfterDays` in game with `/realm:config`; name tags update at once. Pruning reads the live setting again before each deletion. `afkTag` and `afkPrefix` stay in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `nick:p:<player id>` | World | One per nicknamed player: JSON `{ n, c, g }`, the nickname, its color code and the player's gamertag when last seen (for the operators' list) |
| `nick:g:<lowercase gamertag>` | World | The player id of each gamertag seen joining, so nobody takes an offline player's name as a nickname |
| `nick:t:<player id>` | World | Last observed join in real milliseconds, refreshed at most once a day, for remembered-gamertag pruning. A missing timestamp starts now rather than at the epoch |
| `nick:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- The nickname is the player's `nameTag` (`§<color><nickname>§r`, then `\n§7<gamertag>`, then `\n§7<title>` when the player has the tag `realm_title:<title>`). Bedrock forgets a player's name tag when they leave, so it's set again whenever a player spawns.
- The pack compares a player's name tag with what it should be and sets it again if it differs: at once when the AFK pack marks them away or back or the Titles pack changes the title they wear (both send `realm:nametag` `{ player, from }` right after), and for everyone every 5 seconds (for anything that says nothing, such as an operator's `/tag`, or the [Deck of Many Things](#deck-of-many-things--domt_bp) rainbow or false-title name and the name it puts back when that ends: those can show for up to 5 seconds). That puts the tag back whatever else changed it, and adds `afkPrefix` itself for players with the `afk` tag (the AFK pack only adds and removes its prefix in front of the existing tag, so the two agree). The same check picks up a title being put on or taken off, and puts the plain gamertag back once a player has neither a nickname nor a title.
- Nicknames are read into memory once and kept in step as they change.
- Inactive gamertags are checked shortly after load and every six hours. Deletions are logged; online players and the live disable setting are rechecked across yielded work. This removes remembered gamertags and their timestamp, not a player's saved nickname.
