Rewards up to 10 levels, 200 Crowns, 4 diamonds and 4 echo shards, and the title **Deep-Listener** at the end |

Hearth and Table's *A Champion's Heart* asks for Champion's Hearts, which champions drop only with both the [Kitchen](#kitchen--cooking_bp) and the [Champions](#champions--elite_bp) pack installed; without either, the story spawns its own champion instead: Grandmother Gristle, a spider at the Ruined Watchtower (with two ordinary spiders), whose heart Bea takes. The cook-off's Champion's Heart Stew needs the Champions pack too; without it Bea asks for 2 rabbit stews. Without the Kitchen, Bea's *Rations for the Wardens* offers only **The old way** (plain food instead of the Kitchen's dishes), and a player who chose **The new kitchen** before the Kitchen pack was removed gets the old way's steps again.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:saga` | Everyone | The story log menu: current quests, available and finished stories, the codex, daily favors; for operators also story places and operator tools (your operator rights are checked again on every press, and after an Are you sure? question) |
| `/realm:saga_log` | Everyone | Straight to **Current quests**: each story you're on with its current step |
| `/realm:saga_places` | Operators | Every story place with its status (set, picked, built, missing), coordinates and the stories that use it: Teleport, Set here, Build here (outline preview with Build here, Rotate, Look around, Cancel), Rebuild, Remove (terrain restored), Relocate |
| `/realm:saga_place [name]` | Operators | Sets a story place where you stand, without a building (an earlier building of it is removed first). Without a name, lists the places in chat. `town` (Overworld only) is the anchor for the seven town stories' near-town spots; it is not a place other packs show, and the list gives the stories that use it. No default location is stored: until set, world spawn is used |
| `/realm:saga_step <player> [story]` | Operators | Finishes a stuck player's current step, as if they did it: in the story named (its id, such as `act1_signs`), or without one their only chapter or their main-story chapter (with several going, it lists their story ids to pick from). A party quest they only help with isn't theirs to finish: run it for a mate on the chapter. Each one is written to the content log (`[saga] operator Ann finished Bob's step "..."`). Also in `/realm:saga` → **Operator tools** → **Finish a player's current step**, and in `/realm:config` |
| `/realm:saga_reset <player>` | Operators | Starts the player's stories over: progress, finished chapters, choices, codex and favors. Rewards already given are kept |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Stories can be started and make progress. Disabled, the story log still opens (`Stories are paused by an operator`) but nothing counts and NPCs offer nothing |
| `tracker` | `true` | The story tracker, for players who haven't chosen in `/realm:prefs` |
| `trackerAt` | `"right4"` | Where the tracker and progress notes show for players who haven't chosen in `/realm:prefs`: a [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box, `"right1"` to `"right4"` or `"left1"` to `"left4"` (top to bottom) or `"middle"` (under the crosshair), or `"hotbar"` (above the hotbar). The boxes show at the same time as other packs' boxes, and add-ons that redraw the action bar every tick can't cover them |
| `partyShare` | `true` | Party mates on the same chapter share progress for defeat, survive and reach objectives |
| `partyStory` | `true` | A party works on one main-story chapter at a time (the one of the member online who is furthest behind); members on it share its progress anywhere, members past it help and their own story waits |
| `partyRange` | `64` | How close (blocks) a party mate must be to share progress |
| `skipCreative` | `true` | Players in creative mode make no story progress |
| `opHints` | `true` | Tell operators online when a player's chapter needs a place nobody has set and the pack can't pick it (at most every 10 minutes per place) |
| `championFallback` | `true` | When no [Champions](#champions--elite_bp) pack answers a story champion request within 3 seconds, spawn the story's mob itself: named, with extra health (the champion's `health`), resistance and strength. Story bosses Champions can't make (an elder guardian, pillagers, a phantom) are always spawned this way |
| `championRetrySeconds` | `120` | Seconds before a story champion is asked for again, once the last one is gone |
| `offerOrder` | `20` | Where story offers sit among an NPC's buttons (lower is higher up; other offers default to 50) |
| `hintPenalty` | `0.25` | Share of a chapter's levels and Crowns a hint costs (once per chapter). `0` = free hints |
| `autoPlaces` | `true` | Places nobody set are picked by the pack and built when a player comes close. Disabled, operators set every place |
| `buildRange` | `64` | How close (blocks) a player must come to a picked place before its building is built |
| `farScale` | `0.5` | Story spots (`offset` from world spawn) and auto-picked place bands farther than 300 blocks from world spawn keep their direction, but only this share of their distance past 300 blocks counts: `0.5` puts a spot written 1,200 blocks out at 750. `1` = as written. Story text with `{far:x,z}`, `{leg:x1,z1,x2,z2}` and `{band:place}` tokens shows the scaled distances. Places already set or picked don't move |
| `actorTimeoutSeconds` | `300` | How long a story character (a ghost, guards, someone to escort) waits for its player to come back before it's removed; it comes back when needed |
| `favors` | `true` | Questgivers offer a daily favor |
| `campDays` | `7` | A Recurring Wanderer's camp nobody comes within 48 blocks of for this many real days is taken down (terrain put back); it comes back when a player on that chain meets the wanderer |

Operators can change every option but `offerOrder` in game with `/realm:config`. Each player can switch the tracker for themselves with **Story tracker** in `/realm:prefs`, which follows `tracker` until they choose, and move it with **Where my story tracker shows** (follows `trackerAt`). **Show quest spot outlines** (`spotGuides`, default Enabled) turns the quest spot outlines off for themselves.

**The stories** are data: the prologue in `scripts/stories.js` (with `NPC_NAMES` and `PLACES`), the acts, side questlines and favors in `scripts/stories/*.js`, typed by `scripts/types.js`. A story is `{ id, title, short, giver, kind, act?, tones, summary, requires?, chapters }` (`kind`: `main`, `side`, `heart` or `wander`; a heart story must require `g:aff_<giver>`; a wanderer's chain is told by `w_<id>` from `WANDERERS` and its first chapter has a `camp`); a chapter `{ id, title, npc?, end?, when?, sequential?, intro, introChoices?, teach?, camp?, objectives, outro, choices?, reward, rep?, hint }` (`teach`: [Kitchen](#kitchen--cooking_bp) recipes sent with `realm:recipe_learn` when the chapter is accepted; `camp: { prefab, near }`: accepting it builds or moves the giver's camp, near `"wanderer"` or a place); a choice may have `cost: { crowns }` (shown on the button and taken when picked; without enough Crowns nothing is chosen and the form can be opened again); a reward may add `skill: { skill, amount }` ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp) XP with `realm:skill_xp`) and `relicRoll: { chance, relics }`; Strangers' one-offs are templates `{ id, label, archetypes, guild, params?, requires?, intro, objectives, outro, reward, hint }` whose text and objectives use `{name}`, `{item}`, `{count}`, `npc: "{npc}"` and `at: "wanderer"`, and hostiles `{ id, label, title, intro, toll?, reveal, champion, adds, outro, reward }`; flags are a story's own, `g:<name>` (player-wide, also counters with `inc`), `<story>.<flag>`, or set by other packs (`pack:<folder>`, `g:aff_<npc>`, `g:w_accused`, `g:calling_ready`, `g:calling`, `cal:day`, `cal:season`, `cal:festival`), matched exactly, with `!x` (not x, also unset), `>=n` or `<=n` (an unset counter counts as 0). `requires` checks finished stories and chapters, flags, counters (`minCount`) and guild reputation. Each objective type and its fields are listed in `types.js`; the place prefabs are in `scripts/prefabs.js`. `npm run check` runs `tools/check-stories.mjs`, which fails on unknown objective types, missing fields, unknown places or NPCs, duplicate ids, bad champion tags, item, block and mob ids this Minecraft version doesn't have (from `@minecraft/vanilla-data`), an interact objective whose blocks aren't within reach in its place's building, a wanderer's chain without a camp, a template with a placeholder it has no param for (each template is checked with its first params), a camp prefab of 120 blocks or more, and Kitchen dish names out of step with the Cooking pack; it walks every story through every combination of choices (and of the flags other stories set) and fails when a reachable chapter has no objective, no intro or outro page, or only locked choices, when a story requires a chapter some endings skip, or when stories require each other; and it warns about flags that are read but never set and pages over 450 characters. Keep every `id`: progress is saved by story, chapter and choice id.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `saga:p` | Player | JSON `{ s: { <story id>: { dn, a?, cur?, o?, t?, f, ch, fin?, h?, x? } }, g?, cx?, fv? }`: per story the finished chapter ids, whether the current chapter is accepted, its id, objective progress, when it was accepted, the story's flags, the choices made (by chapter, `<chapter>#<step>` for a meet, `<chapter>@` for an intro choice), when it was finished, whether a hint was bought, and step extras (clues found, timer and wait starts; with the daylight cycle stopped, `w<step>` is the real time a wait started). The save is limited to 30,000 UTF-8 bytes (the property's hard limit is 32,767). Past it the pack drops, in this order, the stopped-tracking list, finished daily favors (oldest first) and the oldest codex entries; stories, choices, flags, progress and fields this version doesn't know are never trimmed. A new codex entry that would not fit even after that trim is refused with `Your saved progress is full` in chat. `tr` the story id of the quest the player tracks (`fv:<npc>` for a favor, `wv:<template>` for a wanderer's job), `ut` the ids of the quests they stopped tracking, `g` is the player-wide flags and counters, `cx` the codex entries found, `fv` the daily favors by NPC `{ id, d, a?, o?, x?, c?, t?, h? }`, `wv` the player's wanderer encounter `{ w, ar, nm, hk?, at: { d, x, y, z }, m, tp?, p?, a?, o?, x?, t?, h?, c?, g?, tn? }` (its id, kind, the stranger's name, hostile kind, where and when you met, the template and params picked, then a favor's fields, `g` they moved on, `tn` the disguise dropped) and `wn` how many Strangers' requests you finished. A finished story keeps only its chapters, flags and choices; saved a few seconds after a change and when the player leaves |
| `saga:places` | World | JSON `{ <name>: { dim, x, y?, z, by?, f?, b?, a?, p?, mv?, s?, pf?, w?, yh?, u?, v?, pv?, fd? } }`: each place's spot, who set it, the building's facing, whether it's built, picked by the pack, still waiting to be built, how often it moved, its terrain snapshot (structure ids and corners), the prefab revision it was built with, and 1 when the snapshot covers the ground under it; `town` is `{ dim, x, y, z, by }` only (the Overworld town anchor, no building or snapshot); a wanderer's camp (`camp:<id>`) also has its prefab, the wanderer, the height it was asked for, the players on that chain (id and when) and when someone was last near it |
| `saga:place_<name>_<build>_<n>` | World structures | The terrain under a built place, saved before building (`structureManager`; `<build>` is a stamp of that build, so moving a place never deletes the new spot's snapshot; older builds have `saga:place_<name>_<n>`), put back by Remove (`saga:place_camp_<id>_...` for a camp). Building again on the same spot keeps the first snapshot |
| `saga:weather` | World | The overworld weather at the last change: `Clear`, `Rain` or `Thunder`. The stable Script API can't read the current weather |
| `saga:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's own `tracker` and `trackerAt` choices from `/realm:prefs` |
| `saga:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- **Modules:** `data.js` (saved progress, flags, requirements, which chapter is current), `objectives.js` (what counts for each objective type, scenes), `actors.js` (story characters and mobs), `places.js` (places, building, snapshots, the places menu), `scale.js` (`farScale`: scaled offsets and bands, and the distance tokens in story text, filled at world load and again when the option changes), `party.js` (the party's shared main story), `ui.js` (offers, dialogues, hints, rewards, tracker, story log), `main.js` (commands, script events, loops).
- **Townsfolk:** the pack answers `realm:npc_talk` with `realm:npc_offer` (keys `start:`, `end:`, `info:` plus the story id, `ans:` for riddles, `fvstart:`/`fvinfo:`/`fvend:` plus the NPC for favors) and opens its dialogues on `realm:npc_choose`. The same `realm:npc_talk` counts talk objectives and takes deliveries first, so delivering the last item lets you report back in the same tap.
- **The current chapter** is the accepted one, else the first unfinished chapter whose `when` matches; a story is finished when none is left. Objectives with a `when` that doesn't match don't exist for that player. In a `sequential` chapter only the first unfinished step counts, spawns and shows on the tracker.
- **Counting:** events count defeat (`entityDie`, killer from the damage source), mine, place, interact, inspect taps, tend, tame (checked a few times after the interaction), use (`itemUse` and item taps on blocks) and fish (a hook followed as in Daily Quests). Collect (items to have) is counted when the player's inventory changes, at once for a step not counted yet, and every 10 seconds. A loop once a second checks only the steps the player is working on (indexed by type): reach, survive (overworld weather from `weatherChange`, accepting `overworld` and `minecraft:overworld`; nothing over the player's head), vigil, wear, ride (distance while the riding component's entity matches), wait, sleep, timers, champions, races, and starts or ends scenes. A fast loop every 5 ticks moves guards and wisps; escorts take a short step every 2 ticks.
- **Story characters** are spawned per player with the tags `saga:actor`, `saga:o:<player>` and `saga:k:<step>`, their own `nameTag` set to `§r` (so they never despawn or draw a duplicate close-range nameplate), and a single invisible, zero-hitbox helper (`realm:saga_label` with `always_show: true`) pinned at `headLocation + 0.4y` for their canonical name. Characters you talk to and guards get resistance 5, weakness and slowness and are healed back each second; what they throw or summon near them (potions, arrows, tridents, fireballs, fangs, vexes) is removed. Escorts and wards can be hurt, except an escort marked `invul` (Pell) and a ward that is itself a monster (Vesna, a witch): she can't be hurt and what she throws is removed, so she never fights you. A villager character (`minecraft:villager_v2`) spawns as a village's newcomer (`minecraft:spawn_from_village`) and is then dressed with its `look` (`minecraft:become_cleric` for Pell, `minecraft:become_fisherman` for Barnaby Pike; unskilled without), checked once a second until it took. No story character trades or takes a lead or name tag: every interaction with one (tagged `saga:actor`) is canceled. One struck by lightning (a witch) or turned by a zombie (a zombie villager) keeps its name (`§r`) but not our tags: that mob is removed, and a witch's character is spawned again where it stood (a zombie villager's counts as hurt).
- **Escorts walk** the player's trail: crumbs dropped every block while the player is on the ground (80 at most), and every 2 ticks a teleport of 0.42 blocks along them (0.6 when the player is 5 blocks ahead, 1 when 8), facing the way they go, stopping 2.5 blocks behind the player and skipping ahead when 13 or more crumbs behind. One escort per player, so only a few at once.
- **Races** (`race` on a `defeat` with `bounty: true`, or on an `event` with `quest: { pack: "maps_bp" }`): the pack keeps Bounty Board's `realm:bounty_targets` and each player's last legs from `realm:map_leg` in memory (asked for with `realm:bounty_targets_ping` and `realm:map_leg_ping` 6 seconds after the world loads). Once a second, a race objective with no race on starts one for the nearest target (or last leg) within `radius` (300) that it hasn't raced yet, and sends `realm:bounty_rival` `{ id, player, until }` (or `realm:map_rival` `{ player, hunt, until }`; `until` in ms). A `realm:champion_slain` with the target's tag `realm:bounty:<id>` (killer, helpers, or within 32 blocks) or the treasure's `realm:quest_done` before `until` wins: progress +1 and `tally` (`g:rook_won`) +1; after it, or when the clock runs out first, the race is lost (`lose` flags, `rook_lost`). A target claimed by someone else, or a hunt given up, calls the race off. The race is saved with the chapter's progress. **Fights at a place** (`spawn: { count, every, mobs?, warn? }` on a `defeat` whose mobs never come there by themselves: the Gray Choir's illagers, the Sky Seal's vexes and phantoms, the Fen's bogged): once a second while the player is within the step's radius (and, with `night`, at night, or at any time while the daylight cycle is stopped, as night steps count then; before 1.16.12 such a fight never started on a world that keeps it day), its mobs are topped up to `count` alive (3 by default, never more than are left to defeat) every `every` seconds (20), around the place, with the `warn` line in chat the first time; they stay while the player is within 24 blocks past the edge and count wherever they fall, but only for that step and only for the player (or party) they came for: another player's fight, a champion's adds or a stealth ambush never count toward it (before 1.16.12 any story mob of the right kind did, wherever it fell). Before 1.16.4 these steps spawned nothing and waited for mobs that never came (the Haddock farm ambush, the Smugglers' Cove, the Gray Ring, the Hollow Gate, the Sky Seal's vexes, the waking reeds). Monsters of ambushes, fights at a place, waves, champion adds and wrong answers are tagged `saga:add` (and `saga:choir` for the Gray Choir, which the Relics pack's Gray Choir Mask reads). All of them go when the step is done, the chapter ends, the player leaves, after `actorTimeoutSeconds` away, after 10 minutes (story monsters; a defense's wave only counts from when its player stops fighting it), or at a restart; leftovers are removed when their chunk loads. Whatever the pack spawns or moves near a spot with a height to start from (wave and ambush monsters, champions with no place, characters beside a spot, guards, clues, lost animals, an escort waiting by the player) stands on the ground within 6 blocks of that height or, over water, at the water's surface; sea creatures (drowned, guardians, squid, dolphins, fish, axolotls, turtles, tadpoles) and the characters and clues of a place built on the sea bed (the Sunken Bell, the Tide Seal) may be on the bottom.
- **Stealth detection** every 5 ticks: distance to each guard's eyes against `detect` or `detectSneak` (sneaking or wearing the `disguise`), within 60 degrees of the guard's facing, and a block ray (`getBlockFromRay`) for walls. It checks everyone in the scene (in a party, helpers too); reaching the goal (within `goalRadius`, 2.5 blocks by default; the Gray Ring's goal is its middle with 7) finishes the step for whoever still needs it, also when no guard could be posted. Guards are frozen (they can't walk by themselves) and walk their rounds 0.07 blocks every tick, facing the way they go, so the vanilla AI never gets a tick to turn or nudge one: before 1.16.12 they were moved 0.35 blocks every 5 ticks and the nearest ones drifted toward players in between, then jumped back (up to 127 snaps back in 2 minutes in `saga-party-stealth.js`, none now). Guards more than 32 blocks from everyone in the scene walk every 4 ticks instead (nobody is there to see them, nor for their AI to turn to). The ground under a guard is looked up only when it steps onto a new block. Measured on BDS with `saga-stealth-perf.js` (60 s next to the Gray Ring): one player 0.67 ms/tick for the pack before, 0.76 after; a party of three 0.94 before (12 watchers) and 0.95 after (4). "Song in the Dark" goes one step at a time since 1.16.12 (the light, the ring, the Cantor): before, "Listen to the Cantor" played as soon as anyone came within 16 blocks of the ring, sneaking or not.
- **Champions:** the pack sends `realm:champion_spawn` `{ dim, x, y, z, mob, trait?, name, tag, health }` (at most once per `championRetrySeconds`, and not while a living mob with that tag is loaded in that dimension: anything else carrying the tag, such as a dropped item, loses it) for the mobs Champions can make (zombie, husk, drowned, zombie villager, skeleton, stray, spider, creeper, witch), spawns its own after 3 seconds with `championFallback` (without it, asks again 5 seconds later when none came; and always for any other mob, such as the elder guardian, pillagers or the phantom, which Champions would swap for one of its own), and spawns the `adds` when a champion with that tag drops below half health. A `realm:champion_slain` with the story's tag (or the fallback's death) credits the killer, helpers, everyone within 32 blocks on that step, and their party mates. A tagged fallback champion left over from an earlier session is removed when its chunk loads (`entityLoad`), not only at the startup sweep; one this session spawned is kept. The pack remembers the ids it spawned in memory only, forgets one when that champion dies, and keeps at most the latest 256.
- **Places:** a picked place is built by a job that tries the picked spot and 32 spots around it within 48 blocks, asks the prefab's `siteOk` whether the column suits the place, checks that the building's box holds nothing player-made, saves the box with `structureManager.createFromWorld` (tiles of up to 64 by 64, saved in the world), then runs the prefab's build steps. After 3 moves any open land will do (on the ground block itself: before 1.15.3 this fallback stood one block high, on a slope with the foundation hanging in the air); after 6 it gives up and tells operators. A prefab with a `footing` (the Lighthouse, 32 blocks) fills under its own foundation blocks down to solid ground or the sea bed (only air, water and plants: sand and gravel count as ground), and its snapshot covers that ground too. A prefab has a revision (`rev`): a place built with an older one is touched up once when a player comes within `buildRange`, only into empty space, clearing the old blocks it lists (`stale`) and filling the footing, so players' builds stay; old Lighthouses get their walkway and foundation this way. Remove places the snapshot back and deletes it.
- **Seals:** for the Relics pack's Lantern Shard, the pack sends `realm:seals` `{ player, seals: [{ name, dim, x, z }] }` with the seal places that are set and whose Act IV relight chapter that player hasn't finished, when it changes (checked every 5 seconds), at load and in reply to `realm:seals_ping`.
- **Finishing a chapter** gives the reward (levels and Crowns cut by `hintPenalty` after a hint) and sends `realm:quest_done` `{ player, pack: "saga_bp", id: "<story>:<chapter>", label, kind: "story", npcs }` (`npcs`: who gave and who ended it; `kind: "favor"` with `npc` for favors; Townsfolk adds affinity for both), `realm:gossip` `{ kind: "act", player, name, place, n }` when an act of the main story is finished, `realm:rep_add` for the choice's and chapter's reputation, `realm:relic_give`, `realm:title_unlock` and `realm:journal` (page `story`). Crowns go straight onto the `crowns` scoreboard.
- **Party story** (`party.js`): once a second, online players with the same `realm_party:` tag ([Parties](#parties--party_bp)) are grouped. The party chapter is the earliest first-unfinished main chapter among them; other main chapters wait for party members (hidden from progress and the tracker, saved progress untouched; their NPC says `Waiting for your party`). Members without it accepted get an in-memory party quest entry. Progress is merged into each member's entry (counts add, timers take the furthest, single steps done for all, `collect` done for all once one member has the items; before 1.16.0 it stayed per player, so a member without the items had to report back alone and fell a chapter behind). The 64-block `partyShare` skips the party's chapter so nothing counts twice.
- **Shared scenes** (`objectives.js`): a party that plays a chapter together (the main story with `partyStory`, side and festival stories with `partyShare`) gets one scene per place and step, owned by the party (`party|<tag>`), instead of one per member (meet, escort, lead, defend, follow, stealth and `defeat` with `spawn`; clues, riddles, waits, sleeps, wearing and visions stay each player's own and spawn nothing): one character to meet, escort or protect, one wisp, one herd and one set of waves for the party (before 1.16.12 each mate on the step got their own copy standing in the same spot), a stealth step posts one set of guards for the party (before 1.16.12 each mate on the step had their own set, and a mate's guards never saw the other mates or a helping member, so at the Gray Ring half the watchers ignored you), a `defeat` with `spawn` sends one group for the party, never more alive than the member furthest from done still has to defeat (before 1.16.12 each member got their own group: 4 mates at a fight of 4 meant 16 mobs). The scene lasts while anyone in the party there still needs the step; a member who finishes, leaves or is reset leaves it, and nothing a member's earlier solo scene left behind carries over.
- **Accept and report once** (`ui.js`): accepting the party chapter accepts it for every online mate who could start it (the intro choice applied for all; a mate for whom the talker's choice has a cost or whose `requires` don't hold is skipped and told to talk to the NPC themselves), with a listening-in popup (the NPC's pages and the steps) closed with `uiManager.closeAllForms` when the talk ends or after 2 minutes, and skipped for a mate with a form already open (chat is enough). **Not now** by the talker tells the listeners. Reporting back completes the chapter for mates on it whose steps are done and for whom the talker's choice fits (same rule): the talker's choice and its flags, each mate's own rewards, reputation and `realm:quest_done`, act gossip once. Mates not done yet are told what's left. Side and festival stories (with `partyShare`) offer mates a Join / Not now popup (60 s) and share reports the same way; heart stories and wanderers stay personal. `trackedFirst` puts the party chapter first unless the player tracked a quest.

- **The tracker** shows in [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp)'s quest box, next to the box chosen with `trackerAt` (default `right4`), with the side boxes protocol (`scripts/side.js`, see [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)): it is recomputed every 2 seconds (half the players each second) but sent only when it changed, or again shortly before its 15 seconds run out, and taken down when no quest is left. After a respawn or a change of dimension it is drawn again within 2 seconds. Progress notes (a defense's waves; quarter counts while the tracker is off) show in the small box at `trackerAt` beside it, as a second readout; when another pack's readout holds that box, the note takes the quest box's place for its length and the tracker waits. Above the hotbar it listens to other packs' `realm:actionbar` and skips its update while their note holds the bar (up to 10 seconds), and sends its own with `from: "saga_bp"` and `steady: 20`; its own progress notes there make it wait. It is the lowest-ranked steady line (see the action bar protocol in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)): it waits for an Elytra HUD, a Relics readout, an expedition's run line or the build mode line, and draws over the Party HUD (`background`).
- **Townsfolk (Hearth & Hearsay):** every 5 seconds the pack checks each player's story flags and sends `realm:npc_flags` `{ player, flags }` when they changed (and on join): `g:ending`, `g:hollis`, `g:quill`, `g:vesna`, `g:fen`, `g:allies`, `g:mercy`, `g:iron`, `g:gull` (also read by [Relics](#relics--relics_bp) for Hal's Compass), 15 story flags (`drowned_bell.bell`, `act1_signs.act1:path`, `act3_deep.elsie`, `act3_deep.keys`, `act4_seals.act4:promise`, `mayors_burden.plaque`, `hollis_faith.forgive`, `wardens_oath.oath`, `singing_forge.blade`, `smugglers_run.profits`, `hearth_and_table.marty`, `graveyard_shift.stone`, `lost_lambs.cat`, `inn_ghost.lily`, `edges_of_map.wonder`) and `fin:<story>` = `1` for 18 finished stories; only flags that are set go, and `realm:npc_flags_ping` sends them all again. It saves `realm:affinity` levels as `g:aff_<npc>` (`0` Stranger to `4` Confidant), so heart stories and any `when` can read them; a locked heart story says `become Close with Old Tobin (Townsfolk)`. It keeps `realm:calendar` as the live flags `cal:day`, `cal:season` and `cal:festival` (never saved, like `pack:`; asked for with `realm:calendar_ping` 4 seconds after the world loads). From [Skills](#skills--skills_bp)' `realm:calling` it saves `g:calling_ready` (`1` once `ready`) and `g:calling` (the Calling id, or `none`), asking with `realm:calling_ping` 4.5 seconds after the world loads.
- **Atlas of the Realm:** in the same 5-second check the pack sends `realm:saga_progress` `{ player, act }` when it changed (and on join): how many main acts the player has finished in order (0 to 5); `realm:saga_progress_ping` sends it again for everyone. Atlas reads it for its Starwright tablets.
- **Minimap:** every 2 seconds the tracker's target goes out as `realm:track` `{ player, label, dim?, x?, z?, npc? }` when it changed (also for players who hide the tracker; `{ player }` when there's nothing to point at), and again on `realm:track_ping`. `realm:place_ready` for a camp carries its `label`.
- **Wanderers of the Wilds** (the events in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)): `realm:wander_spawn` from the wanderer pack makes the player's encounter (a Stranger's template is picked then, seeded by the encounter id); `realm:npc_talk` with `npc: "w_<wid>"` gets the chain's offers, the request (`wvstart:`, `wvinfo:`, `wvend:` plus the encounter id) or a disguise's talk (`wvh:`); `realm:wander_turn` (or refusing the toll) starts a fight: the champion (`realm:saga:wh_<wid>`, a Choir spy's `realm:saga:whc_<wid>` with the `saga:choir` tag) where it stood, its adds at once (plus one per party mate within 32 blocks, up to 3; illagers never wear a banner); `realm:wander_gone` ends an offer, lets an accepted request finish without them (or ends it, when a step still needs them) and, for an accusation, adds 1 to `g:w_accused`. Every 5 seconds the pack sends each player's `realm:wander_state` when it changed (and on `realm:wander_ping`); it sends `realm:wander_done` when a request is accepted, paid, given up or a fight starts, or a camp is set up; `realm:wander_hide` every 10 seconds while a Recurring Wanderer is the one you escort; `realm:place_ready` whenever a place (or camp) is picked, built, moved or removed, 5 seconds after the world loads and on `realm:place_ping`. A request done pays its reward and sends `realm:quest_done` `{ kind: "wander", guild }` (the guild of the Stranger's kind; Wardens for a fight, plus `realm:rep_add` 15 and `realm:gossip` kind `wander_hostile`); a chain's chapters send `kind: "story"` with the wanderer's `guild`, the first one a `realm:journal` entry on the **Wanderers** page, the last one `realm:gossip` kind `wander_chain`.
- **Installed packs:** the pack sends `realm:help_ping` 3 seconds after the world loads and every 10 minutes and keeps the folders that answer `realm:help_pong` (late answers count at once); `pack:<folder>` in a `when` is `on` for those. Until the first answers are in, a chapter with a step gated on a pack can't be finished and a story gated on one isn't offered, so nothing is skipped by mistake.
- **World events:** it listens to `realm:sky_event` (kinds `meteor`, `rainbow`, `storm_cell`, `tornado` with x, z; `aurora`, `blood_moon`, `harvest_moon`) and `realm:moon` (a moon lasts until `normal`, dawn, or 20 minutes), and to `realm:quest_done` for `event` steps with `quest` (Expeditions' `dungeon`, `level`, `tier`, `nightmare`, `gauntlet`). Events are kept in memory only.
- **Asking for events:** a chapter's `sky` (on accept) or a step's `sky` (when it starts or is done) sends `realm:sky_request` `{ kind, from: "saga_bp", player, dim, x, z, reason: "<story>:<chapter>" }` once per player (saved as `st.x["s<i>"]`); a `survive` or a thunder or rain `vigil` that a player waits at in the wrong weather sends `{ kind: "thunder" or "rain", minutes: 6, within: 8 }` at most once per player and step every 30 minutes. The receiving packs decide (see their `storyEvents` options).
- **Testing hook:** `/scriptevent realm:saga_debug {"player":"<name>","action":"state"}` prints a player's saved progress to the content log; `"action":"finish","story":"<id>"` marks a whole story finished; `"action":"places"` sends the player every saved place as JSON; `"action":"jump","story":"<id>","chapter":"<id>"` marks every chapter before that one finished; both take `"flags":{...}` to set (a `g:` key is player-wide); `"action":"answer","text":"..."` answers the player's open riddle; `"action":"bump","story":"<id>","i":0,"n":1` adds progress to objective `i` of the player's entry (or party quest); `"action":"wander_finish"` finishes every step of the player's Stranger's request or fight; `"action":"race_expire"` ends the player's running races now (lost, unless the target falls first); `"action":"age_adds","seconds":600` makes every story monster and the player's running defenses that much older, then runs the 10-minute story monster expiry. Script events need operator rights.

---

## Wanderers of the Wilds — `wander_bp`

Out past the town lamps you meet people on the road: a footsore pilgrim, a hermit on a peak, a ghost by old stones, a miner deep underground, a storm-chaser in the thunder, an exile in the Nether, a rival bounty hunter, and a few who aren't what they seem. Eight **Recurring Wanderers** have chains of three to five chapters and set up a camp where they wait for you; passing **Strangers** ask a short favor (24 kinds, randomized); and once you've finished the prologue some are **hostile** in disguise. Every quest runs in [Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp), which this pack needs: without it nobody appears.

### How to use

1. Go exploring: at least 300 blocks from world spawn (`spawnDistance`) and 160 blocks from any town, land claim or safe zone (`zoneDistance`), in survival or adventure, in the Overworld or the Nether. About twice an hour of exploring, chat says `[Wanderers] Someone is on the road ahead (NE): Hob Fairweather.`
2. Walk up and tap them: they stroll around the spot where they appeared (or their camp) and stand still while you talk. Tapping one never opens a trade screen. Their menu shows what they say and their offers: a Recurring Wanderer's chain (`Wanderer: Hob's Tall Tales`), a Stranger's `Request: Hungry on the Road`, or a report when you're done. Green sparkles over someone (only you see them) mean they have something for you.
3. Accept, then do it like any story step: the tracker and `/realm:saga` show it. A Stranger waits half an hour at most, and leaves if you go more than 96 blocks away for a minute; a job you can finish without them (fight some monsters, mine some rock) still pays, and one that needs them (bring them something) ends when they go.
4. A Recurring Wanderer's first chapter sets up their camp near where you met them (or by a story place): a small tent or ruin with a lodestone and a `Waystone: <Name>'s Camp` sign. Tap the lodestone to make it a [waystone](#waystones--inns--waystone_bp). They wait there for the rest of the chain, whenever someone on their chain comes within 48 blocks. If another player's chapter moves the camp, Realm Mail brings you a letter with where it went.
5. **Hostile wanderers** (after both prologue stories): a toll man who wants 20 Crowns for a road that isn't there, a lost sailor dripping seawater by the shore at night, a Choir spy dressed as a pilgrim (after Act II), a hermit who never blinks (after Act III). Each one gives itself away in what it says. Pay the toll or refuse it; the others drop their disguise a little after you talk, and a fight starts right there.
6. **Something's off...** shows in a wanderer's menu once Warden Reyes is your Friend ([Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)), you've made three or more hard choices in the story (`g:iron`), or you wear the Gray Choir Mask. Accuse a hostile one and it reveals itself early and stumbles (Slowness II for 5 seconds; +10 Wardens reputation). Accuse a friendly one and they walk away hurt, with no reward, and other wanderers hear about it.
7. `/realm:wander` lists the Recurring Wanderers you know and where their camps are, and who's on the road for you now. Don't want to meet anyone? Disable **Meet wanderers** in `/realm:prefs`.
8. **Operators:** `/realm:wander` also has **On the road now** (and a button to send everyone away) and **Someone appears here** (pick a wanderer, a Stranger's kind or a hostile). `/realm:wander_clear` sends every wanderer on the road away. Camps show among the story places in `/realm:saga_places` (Teleport, Rebuild, Remove).

### What players see

- **Who you meet** depends on where you are (the first that fits): a deep miner below height 0 with rock overhead; a ghost at night within 64 blocks of a graveyard, observatory or watchtower story place (or old mossy stones nearby); a pilgrim by day within 200 blocks of the Old Chapel, the Stargazer's Ruin or Starfall Crater; Rook, a rival, within 300 blocks of a live [Bounty Board](#bounty-board--bounty_bp) champion target or of your own [treasure map](#treasure-maps--riddles--maps_bp)'s last clue (with neither live anywhere, within 20 minutes after you finish a bounty or a treasure map); a hermit above height 100 or in snowy, spruce country; a storm-chaser in a thunderstorm; an exile in the Nether; else a traveler. When the Recurring Wanderer of that kind has a chain you can start, it's them half the time (`namedShare`); otherwise a Stranger with a name like `Wil the Footsore` (40 first names, 20 epithets).
- **The roll:** once a minute per player (`scheduleTicks`), 7% (`rollChance`), times 1.5 within 128 blocks of a story place (`siteBonus`) and 1.25 at night for ghosts and when a hostile could come (`nightBonus`). After a meeting where you took a job (or fought), nobody new comes for 8 minutes (`cooldownMinutes`); after one you walked away from, 20 (`declineCooldownMinutes`).
- **Where they stand:** 24 to 40 blocks ahead of you, on solid ground with room to stand, under open sky above ground (the stable Script API can't read light levels, so open sky stands in for "lit"), on a floor near your height underground and in the Nether; 12 tries, else nobody comes this time. Never within 256 blocks of another wanderer or a camp (`wandererDistance`).
- **Limits:** one wanderer on the road per player, 5 on the road realm-wide (`maxOnRoad`), 2 of them hostile (`maxHostile`), 8 camps (one per Recurring Wanderer), 13 wanderer entities in all (`maxEntities`). A Stranger nobody took a job from leaves after 15 minutes (`lifeMinutes`), one whose job was taken after 30 (`acceptedLifeMinutes`), and anyone leaves once the player they came for has been 96 blocks away (`leaveDistance`) for 60 seconds (`leaveSeconds`) or has left the game.
- **What they look like:** they walk. Strangers who are travelers are wandering traders (without their llamas); everyone else is a villager dressed for their kind, in the clothes of the biome they appeared in: pilgrims as clerics, deep miners as armorers, hermits as shepherds, storm-chasers as cartographers, Nether exiles as leatherworkers, Rook as a weaponsmith, Hob as a toolsmith, and a drowned sailor in disguise as a fisherman. Ghosts are allays that hover on their spot.
- **Where they walk:** with the vanilla villager or trader AI, but they don't wander off. A camp's wanderer stays within about 3 blocks of the camp, and one on the road within about 6 blocks of where they appeared. A wanderer who walks past that slows down, turns and walks back, so you don't see them jump. One stuck behind a wall or fence on the way back (the back of a tent, a house wall) walks at its own pace for about 10 seconds to find the way around instead of being pushed into the wall. They're only put back by a teleport as a last resort: in water or lava, 3 blocks down a hole for 3 seconds, or more than 12 blocks away. Then they land on a free spot near the middle, on the camp's own ground level (never up on a wall or roof, or behind a fence or wall they couldn't walk through), and if it keeps happening, they wait longer before each teleport. They stand still (Slowness) while their menu is open.
- **World-fixed names near and far:** one invisible, zero-hitbox `realm:wander_label` with `always_show: true` follows the wanderer's head plus 0.4 blocks vertically. Its native caption uses a format-code-only ownership marker while the helper carries readable text; the nonempty marker also retains named-mob behavior. A transformed actor is recovered only through that exact marker (including its resend toggle), never by guessing from a nearby witch or zombie. Helper failures restore a readable native name while preserving the marker. The final near-player resend has native tests, not recaptured production client pixels.
- **Wanderers can't be hurt:** Resistance V (no damage but `/kill` and the void), Fire Resistance and Water Breathing, re-applied if they go (a trader's milk at dawn clears them) and topped up to full health, so zombies can't make zombie villagers of them. A wanderer struck by lightning (a villager turns into a witch) or a trader whose own despawn timer runs out is spawned again on their spot while their player is within 96 blocks (5 times at most). Tapping one never trades, takes a name tag or a lead, opens the NPC editor or hands an allay your item; real villagers and traders still trade. They don't breed (no beds that far from town) and what a villager picks up (bread, carrots, seeds) drops when they leave. They never turn invisible: a wandering trader's invisibility potion (vanilla traders drink one when a zombie or illager comes within 6 blocks) doesn't take, and one already invisible shows again within a second. Before 1.2.2 a traveler on the road could vanish, leaving only his name, sparkles and minimap dot.
- **The Recurring Wanderers** (their chains are listed in [Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp)): Pell the Pilgrim (after The Drowned Bell), Anwen the Surveyor's Ghost (after Signs in the Sky), Brannoch Deepdelve the deep miner, Rook the Rival, Marigold of the Heights the hermit, Tamsin Galeward the storm-chaser, Vesk the Exile (met in the Nether; his camp is by the Ruined Watchtower) and Hob Fairweather the tinker. Each finale gives 8 levels, 100 to 140 Crowns, a title, a Codex entry and a 15% chance of a relic; meeting all eight (their first chapters) fills the Field Journal's **Wanderers** page (10 levels, 200 Crowns, the title `Friend of the Road`).
- **Strangers' requests:** bring them food, firewood, ore, candles, flowers, milk or snow; clear monsters off the road; guard their fire; build a wayside shrine; light the dark for a ghost; mine rock or Nether quartz; stand in the rain with a storm-chaser; race a rival. 1 to 3 levels, 15 to 30 Crowns, skill XP ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp)) and 10 reputation with the guild of their kind ([Guilds](#guilds--reputation--guilds_bp)).
- **Hostile wanderers:** at most one per player every 30 minutes (`hostileGapMinutes`), a share of 20% of meetings (`hostileShare`) once allowed; never for a player in an expedition, AFK or below half health. The fight: the Toll Man (a pillager) and 2 pillagers, the Drowned Sailor (a drowned) and 2 drowned, the Choir Spy (a vindicator) and 2 pillagers, the Hollow-touched Hermit (a witch) and 3 vexes, plus one more for each party mate within 32 blocks (up to 3). None carry banners, so no Bad Omen. Beat it for 40 to 60 Crowns, 1 or 2 Relic Shards, 25 Wardens reputation and Combat XP; the town gossips about it.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:wander` | Everyone | The Recurring Wanderers you know and their camps, who's on the road for you, and when someone new may come; for operators also **On the road now** and **Someone appears here** |
| `/realm:wander_clear` | Operators | Sends every wanderer on the road away (camps stay) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Wanderers appear. Disabled, nobody new comes, those on the road leave within a second and camps stand empty |
| `scheduleTicks` | `1200` | Ticks between each player's rolls (1200 = a minute). Read when the world starts |
| `rollChance` | `0.07` | The chance someone appears in an eligible minute |
| `siteBonus` | `1.5` | The chance is multiplied by this within 128 blocks of a story place (or an Atlas site) |
| `nightBonus` | `1.25` | ...and by this at night for ghosts and when a hostile could come |
| `spawnDistance` | `300` | Nobody appears closer than this to world spawn (in the Nether, measured as the Overworld distance) |
| `zoneDistance` | `160` | ...or closer than this to the edge of a town, a land claim or a safe zone ([safe zones protocol](#how-the-packs-work-together)) |
| `wandererDistance` | `256` | ...or closer than this to another wanderer or a camp |
| `cooldownMinutes` | `8` | Minutes before the next meeting after one where you took a job or fought |
| `declineCooldownMinutes` | `20` | Minutes before the next meeting after one you walked away from |
| `lifeMinutes` | `15` | A wanderer nobody took a job from leaves after this many minutes |
| `acceptedLifeMinutes` | `30` | A Stranger whose job was taken leaves after this many |
| `leaveDistance` | `96` | A wanderer leaves when their player has been this far away... |
| `leaveSeconds` | `60` | ...for this many seconds (or has left the game) |
| `maxOnRoad` | `5` | Most wanderers on the road realm-wide |
| `maxHostile` | `2` | Most hostile ones among them |
| `maxEntities` | `13` | Most wanderer entities, camps included |
| `hostileShare` | `0.2` | Share of meetings that are hostile, once a player may meet them (0 to 0.5) |
| `hostileGapMinutes` | `30` | Minutes between hostile wanderers for one player |
| `namedShare` | `0.5` | When a Recurring Wanderer of that kind could come, the chance it's them rather than a Stranger |
| `campRange` | `48` | A camp's wanderer stands there while someone on their chain is within this many blocks |
| `sparkles` | `true` | Green sparkles over a wanderer who has something for you, seen only by you |

Operators can change `enabled`, `rollChance`, `spawnDistance`, `zoneDistance`, `cooldownMinutes`, `declineCooldownMinutes`, `maxOnRoad`, `hostileShare`, `hostileGapMinutes` and `sparkles` in game with `/realm:config` (**Wanderers of the Wilds**; `scheduleTicks` is shown there but read at start). Each player has **Meet wanderers** in `/realm:prefs` (Enabled by default). Who the wanderers are, their chains and requests are Story Questlines content (`stories/wanderers.js`, `stories/wander_oneoffs.js`); their names, Strangers' name pools and greetings are in this pack's `scripts/lines.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `wander:live` | World | JSON `{ <wid>: { w, n, ar, h?, o, d, x, y, z, b, a?, e?, t?, r?, tt?, ta? } }`: each wanderer on the road: id, name, kind, hostile kind, the player they came for, where (their tether's center), when they came, when a job was taken, their entity and its type, how often it was spawned again, the first talk and when a disguise drops |
| `wander:camps` | World | JSON `{ <wanderer>: { d, x, y, z, e? } }`: where each camp's wanderer stands (from `realm:place_ready`) and their entity while there |
| `wander:p` | Player | JSON `{ cd?, lh?, ac?, q? }`: nobody new until, the last hostile, how many friendly wanderers they accused, the last bounty or treasure map finished |

Bounty targets and treasure legs (below) are kept in memory only and asked for again after a restart.
| `wander:weather` | World | The Overworld weather at the last change (for storm-chasers) |
| `wander:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `wander:pref` | Player | **Meet wanderers** from `/realm:prefs` |

What each player did with a wanderer (one-offs, chains, camps) is saved by Story Questlines (`saga:p`, `saga:places`).

### How it works

- **Cost:** one roll per online player a minute (a few block reads; at night a 9 x 9 x 5 sample for old stones), a 1-second upkeep over the wanderers that exist (13 at most: timers, camp wanderers, sparkles, ghosts kept on their spot and turned to face their player), and every 10 ticks a tether check per walker (13 at most): its position, one block read, one effect and one health read. A walker past its soft radius also gets its movement value and a small push toward home (`scripts/tether.js`, shared with the Caravan, Townsfolk and Story Questlines through `tools/sync-tether.mjs`). A teleport happens only as the last resort. The tether pass was measured on the BDS test server at about 0.35 ms over 13 walkers, about 0.035 ms a tick on average (a just-spawned villager's look check adds about 0.02 ms each until it took). Name labels: once a second every wanderer's label is synced and sorted by whether a player is within 64 blocks; between those passes, every 2 ticks, only those near wanderers are synced (a label shows within 40 blocks, so the resends after a new viewer comes near keep their timing), and a wanderer nobody is near costs one sync a second. Entity handles are kept while they stay valid instead of being looked up every pass. Plus a 10-second orphan sweep; the vanilla AI still does the walking.
- **Entities:** vanilla `minecraft:villager_v2` (spawned with `minecraft:spawn_from_village`, then the profession's `minecraft:become_<job>` event), `minecraft:wandering_trader` for Strangers who are travelers (its `trader_llama`s are removed as they spawn) and `minecraft:allay` for ghosts (wanderers saved before 1.1.0 may still be `minecraft:npc` until they leave), tagged `realm:npc`, `realm:npc_owner:wander_bp`, `realm:npc_id:w_<wid>` and `wander:k:<wid>` on the road or `wander:c:<wanderer>` at a camp, named in gold (Recurring Wanderers) or yellow. Taps (`beforeEvents.playerInteractWithEntity`) on them are canceled and open this pack's menu; untagged villagers and traders are left alone. Townsfolk and the Caravan leave them alone (another owner tag); Tornadoes and Relics (the Hollow Crown) skip `realm:npc`.
- **Leaving:** a wanderer on the road whose entity unloads or is removed (`entityRemove`, which also fires on chunk unload; `entityDie` for a villager killed somehow) is gone for good unless their player is within 96 blocks and the spot is loaded, when they're spawned again (a copy that was only unloaded is removed when it loads); a witch or zombie villager that one of ours turned into (`entitySpawn`, cause `Transformed`: it keeps the name tag, not the tags) is removed; one whose time is up, or whose player is far or offline, leaves with a puff. At world load and whenever one of our entities loads (`entityLoad`), any that belongs to no wanderer on the road and no camp is removed. A camp's wanderer is spawned again when someone on that chain comes near, and removed 30 seconds after the last one leaves.
- **Talking:** the same offer round as Townsfolk: `realm:npc_talk` `{ req, player, npc: "w_<wid>", roles: ["wanderer", "w_<wid>"], name }`, `realm:npc_offer` answers for 4 ticks (at most 16, labels cut to 80 characters), `realm:npc_choose` to the pack picked. Story Questlines answers with the chain, the request or the report.
- **With Story Questlines** (the events below): this pack sends `realm:wander_spawn` when someone appears, `realm:wander_turn` when a disguise drops and `realm:wander_gone` when someone leaves; Story Questlines sends `realm:wander_state` (what each player may meet), `realm:wander_done` (a job accepted, finished, a fight started, a camp set up), `realm:wander_hide` (a camp's wanderer walks with you in an escort, so the camp's copy hides) and `realm:place_ready` (story places and camps). It also listens to `realm:bounty_targets` from Bounty Board and `realm:map_leg` from Treasure Maps (Rook comes near a live target or a player's own last leg; both are asked for with `realm:bounty_targets_ping` and `realm:map_leg_ping` 5 seconds after the world loads), `realm:quest_done` from both (Rook follows when nothing is live), `realm:zones` (towns, claims, safe zones) and `realm:poi` from [Atlas of the Realm](#atlas-of-the-realm--atlas_bp) (its sites count like story places).
- **Testing hook:** `/scriptevent realm:wander_debug {"player":"<name>","action":"spawn","archetype":"traveler","stranger":true}` makes someone appear (or `"named":"hob"`, `"hostile":"toll"`); `"action":"roll"` runs the minute's roll with every rule but the chance; `"action":"tap","wid":"<id>"` taps a wanderer for a simulated player; `"action":"accuse"`; `"action":"state"` prints what's on the road to the content log; `"action":"tether"` sends `realm:wander_tether` `{ camp, road }` with each tether's counters (`snaps`: last-resort teleports, `steers`: times a walker was turned back, `steering`: walkers being turned back now). Scenarios: `tools/test-bds/examples/wander.js`, `wander-walk.js` (walking, tether, looks, protection), `wander-tether.js` (a camp wanderer on open flat ground for 5 minutes: no snap-backs, still at the camp), `wander-visible.js` (a trader stays visible with a zombie next to him).

## Atlas of the Realm — `atlas_bp`

Every stretch of land has a name now. The Overworld is cut into **regions** of 512 by 512 blocks on a grid centered on world spawn, and crossing into one shows its name, like `The Gray Downs`, with how many of its sites you've found. Out in the miles between the story places stand **sites** the pack builds the first time someone comes near: wayside shrines that bless you, 60 **Starwright tablets** that tell the world's oldest secret a little at a time (and read differently as the main story goes on), Gray Choir cairns, abandoned camps, hermit huts, sunken wrecks, fallen watch posts, fossil digs, starglass pools and Aldous Fenn's old survey markers. Finding them pays Crowns, skill XP and guild reputation, and fills a codex.

### How to use

1. Go exploring in the Overworld. When you cross into another region, a banner shows its name and `Region 3 - 0 of 2 sites`; a region you've never been to also says so in chat. Each region has 2 to 4 sites, never near world spawn, a town, a land claim or a safe zone.
2. A site appears when you first come within 64 blocks of its spot (`buildRange`), and you find it by walking up to it (within 10 blocks, `findRange`). Chat says what it is and what to do there.
3. Use it: tap a **Wayside Shrine**'s carved stone for its blessing (10 minutes, once a Realm day), tap a **Starwright Tablet** to read it, break a **Choir Cairn**'s bell and beat its three keepers, open an **Abandoned Camp**'s barrel or a **Sunken Wreck**'s sea chest, ring a **Fallen Watch Post**'s bell and hold the post for 60 seconds, mine the 12 bones of a **Fossil Dig**, tap the amethyst stone by a **Starglass Pool**, or tap one of **Fenn's Survey Markers** to read his note. Each pays its reward once per player.
4. `/realm:atlas` shows the regions and sites you've found, your Starwright tablets (read them again there), Fenn's notes, whether your shrine blessing is ready, and which way the nearest site you haven't found is.
5. Tablets come in order: the first one you read is tablet 1, the next tablet 2, and so on to 60. Some are worn and only a few words make sense until you've seen more of the main story ([Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp)); when you finish an act, chat tells you how many of yours read in full now.
6. Don't want the banner? Disable **Region banners** in `/realm:prefs`.
7. **Operators:** `/realm:atlas` also has **Sites Near Here** (the nearest 20, with a teleport). Settings are in `/realm:config` (**Atlas of the Realm**).

### What players see

- **Region names:** an adjective (24: Gray, Lantern, Drowned, Brine, Hollow, Ember, Saltmarsh, Silver...) and a noun for the land the first visitor found there (30 in six groups: Downs, Wolds, Reach, Leas, Vale for open land; Weald, Holt, Wildwood, Thicket, Greenwood for forest; Spires, Crags, Fells, Tors, Heights for high or snowy land; Barrens, Dunes, Wastes, Flats, Scarps for dry land; Fen, Mire, Marsh, Bog, Carr for swamps; Shallows, Deeps, Sound, Strand, Narrows for the sea). The stable Script API can't read biomes, so the land is guessed from the top blocks around the first visitor, as the Field Journal does, and saved: everyone sees the same name. Region numbers count up in the order the realm found them.
- **The banner** is a title (`realm:title` first, so the side boxes step aside) when you cross 8 blocks into another region; a region you know shows it again at most every 20 seconds.
- **Sites:** each region's 2 to 4 spots are fixed by the world (one per quarter of the region, at least 40 blocks from its edge). When someone comes near, the pack checks the land: open, fairly flat ground (deep, even water for a wreck), nothing anyone built, not within 128 blocks of a town, claim or safe zone (`avoidRadius`), 48 of a story place or wanderer's camp (`placeDistance`), 160 of world spawn (`spawnDistance`), and all of it loaded. It tries the spot and 8 nudges around it; a spot that suits nothing is skipped for good. Then it builds the site block by block and keeps it: sites are permanent, like the land (nothing is saved to put the ground back).
- **What's built where:** the land picks the kind: a deep sea spot gets a wreck; on land each spot leans to one of eight kinds (tablets most often, then shrines, camps, survey markers, cairns, fossil digs, watch posts, hermit huts); within 300 blocks of where a meteor fell ([Meteor Strikes](#meteor-strikes--meteor_bp)), half the spots become starglass pools.

| Site | Looks like | What you do | First time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wayside Shrine | A little roofed stone with a candle and flowers | Find it; tap the carved stone | 10 Crowns and 30 Exploration XP for finding it; a blessing every Realm day: Regeneration (open land, forest), Speed (high, snowy or dry land) or Hero of the Village (swamp, sea), 10 minutes (`blessingMinutes`). Bedrock has no Luck effect, so Hero of the Village (better trades) stands in |
| Starwright Tablet | A carved stone on a tuff step | Tap it | 8 Crowns; the next tablet of the 60 you haven't read joins your codex |
| Choir Cairn | Gray stones with a bell on top, four standing stones | Break the bell; beat its 3 keepers (2 pillagers and a vindicator, no banners) | 15 Crowns and 10 Wardens reputation. The bell comes back for the next player; a broken bell drops nothing |
| Abandoned Camp | A wool lean-to, a dead campfire, a barrel | Open the barrel | 10 Crowns and three things (bread, arrows, torches, iron nuggets, string, leather, salmon, an emerald or a compass), rolled for you |
| Hermit Hut | A one-room spruce cabin | Find it | Counts as a site; wanderers count it as a place to be ([Wanderers of the Wilds](#wanderers-of-the-wilds--wander_bp)) |
| Sunken Wreck | A broken hull on the sea floor, 2 drowned | Open the sea chest | 15 Crowns and three things (gold nuggets, iron, prismarine shards, kelp, emeralds, gold, a nautilus shell) |
| Fallen Watch Post | A broken stone ring with a bell on a post | Ring the bell, then stay within 48 blocks for 60 seconds (`watchSeconds`) against three waves (2 zombies; a skeleton, a zombie and a husk; a vindicator and 2 skeletons) | 15 Crowns and 10 Wardens reputation. Leaving or dying ends it; ring again to retry |
| Fossil Dig | A pit with a skeleton of 12 bone blocks | Mine the 12 bones (they drop nothing; the action bar counts) | 12 Crowns, 10 Miners reputation and 60 Mining XP. The bones come back for the next player |
| Starglass Pool | A still pool rimmed with calcite, amethyst and tinted glass | Tap the amethyst stone with the end rod | 2 Starwright Flour ([Kitchen](#kitchen--cooking_bp); without it, 4 glowstone dust) and 20 Exploration XP |
| Fenn's Survey Marker | A stone post with a carved cap and a lantern | Tap it | One of Aldous Fenn's 10 notes joins your codex |

- **Every site found** gives 10 Exploration XP ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp)), and the first of each kind adds an entry to the Field Journal's **Places** page ([Field Journal](#field-journal--journal_bp)). Each first reward also sends `realm:quest_done` (kind `explore`), which [Guilds](#guilds--reputation--guilds_bp) turns into 10 reputation: Wardens for cairns and watch posts, Miners for fossil digs, Wayfarers for the rest.
- **The Starwright tablets** are 60 in 5 tiers of 12. Tier 1 reads from the start; tiers 2 to 5 read in full after Act I, II, III and IV of the main story. Until then a tablet shows its first few words and says the rest is in an older script. Finishing an act upgrades every tablet you've already found. After all 60, a new tablet site shows one you've read. Without Story Questlines every tablet reads in full.
- **Milestones** ([Titles & Trails](#titles--trails--titles_bp)): titles `Surveyor`, `Pathfinder` and `Atlas-Maker` for 10, 25 and 50 regions; `Wayfarer of Stones`, `Wayfinder` and `Keeper of the Atlas` for 10, 25 and 60 sites, and the **Starwright glyphs** trail at 25 sites (`trailSites`); `Tablet Reader` and `Starwright Scholar` for 12 and 60 tablets. The town gossips about each ([Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)) and about cairns silenced and watch posts held.
- **Fights** (a cairn's keepers, a watch post's waves, a wreck's drowned) are tagged as this pack's own: whatever is left when one ends (or after a restart) is removed.
- **Gossip about Atlas milestones and sites** follows the same limit as every other pack: at most one piece of news per in-game hour from this pack, and each milestone or site once per player (see Town news in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:atlas` | Everyone | Regions and sites you've found (by kind), your Starwright tablets and Fenn's notes to reread, your shrine blessing, the way to the nearest site you haven't found; for operators also **Sites Near Here** (teleport) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Banners, new sites and site rewards. Disabled, nothing new is built and nothing pays; built sites stay |
| `banners` | `true` | The region banner. Each player can also disable it (**Region banners** in `/realm:prefs`) |
| `cellSize` | `512` | A region's side in blocks. Read when the world starts; never change it once players explore (every region and site would move) |
| `poiMin` | `2` | Fewest sites per region (read at start) |
| `poiMax` | `4` | Most sites per region, up to 4 (read at start) |
| `buildRange` | `64` | A site is built when someone first comes this close to its spot |
| `avoidRadius` | `128` | No site within this many blocks of a town, a land claim or a safe zone |
| `placeDistance` | `48` | ...nor of a story place or a wanderer's camp |
| `spawnDistance` | `160` | ...nor of world spawn |
| `findRange` | `10` | You find a site within this many blocks of it |
| `blessingMinutes` | `10` | How long a shrine's blessing lasts |
| `watchSeconds` | `60` | How long a watch post must be held |
| `crowns.shrine`, `crowns.tablet`, `crowns.cairn`, `crowns.camp`, `crowns.hermit`, `crowns.wreck`, `crowns.watch`, `crowns.fossil`, `crowns.pool`, `crowns.survey` | `10`, `8`, `15`, `10`, `0`, `15`, `15`, `12`, `0`, `0` | Crowns for each kind, the first time a player earns its reward |
| `findXp` | `10` | Exploration XP for finding any site |
| `shrineXp` | `30` | ...and the extra for a shrine |
| `fossilXp` | `60` | Mining XP for clearing a fossil dig |
| `poolFlour` | `2` | Starwright Flour from a starglass pool |
| `milestones.regions`, `milestones.sites`, `milestones.tablets` | see above | `[count, title]` pairs: the titles for regions, sites and tablets found |
| `trailSites` | `25` | Sites found for the Starwright glyphs trail |

Operators can change `enabled`, `banners`, `buildRange`, `avoidRadius`, `spawnDistance` and `blessingMinutes` in game with `/realm:config` (**Atlas of the Realm**; `cellSize`, `poiMin` and `poiMax` are shown there but read at start). Each player has **Region banners** in `/realm:prefs` (it starts as the realm's `banners`). Region words, the tablets and Fenn's notes are in `scripts/lore.js`; what each site looks like is in `scripts/prefabs.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `atlas:origin` | World | JSON `{ x, z, s }`: the grid's center (world spawn when the pack first ran, so moving the spawn later moves nothing) and the salt that makes this world's names and spots |
| `atlas:cells` | World | How many parts; the parts `atlas:cells:<n>` hold `cx,cz,group;...` for each region found, in the order the realm found them (about 9 characters a region) |
| `atlas:built` | World | How many parts; the parts `atlas:built:<n>` hold `cx,cz,slot,kind,x,y,z,facing,state;...` for every spot looked at: built, being built, or skipped for good (about 30 characters a spot, 24,000 characters a part) |
| `atlas:meteors` | World | JSON `[[x, z], ...]`: the last 24 meteor impacts (for starglass pools) |
| `atlas:p` | Player | JSON `{ r, p, x, s, t, b, m, f, a, j }`: regions found (their numbers), sites found and sites whose reward was earned (keys like `4,-2,1`), which tablet each tablet site showed you, the 60 tablets as a 15-digit hex mask, the Realm day of your last blessing, milestones, bones mined at digs you haven't cleared, the last act heard, kinds sent to the Journal. About 12 characters per site and 4 per region: a player with 300 regions and 600 sites keeps about 16 KB; the pack stops saving more past 30,000 characters |
| `atlas:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `atlas:pref` | Player | **Region banners** from `/realm:prefs` |

### How it works

- **Cost:** every 2 seconds per player in the Overworld, the region math and a distance check against the sites of the 9 regions around (no block reads). Block reads happen only when a region is found for the first time (5 top blocks for its land) and while a site is checked and built: one at a time, as a job of a few hundred blocks a tick, and only once the area is loaded (else it waits and tries again). Nothing is built in the first 15 seconds after the world loads, so the zones, claims and story places have been heard.
- **Keeping away:** towns, claims and safe zones come in with the [safe zones protocol](#how-the-packs-work-together) (`realm:zones`); every land claim is also asked with `realm:claims_check` (answered by Land Claims); story places and camps come from Story Questlines' `realm:place_ready` (asked again with `realm:place_ping` at load). A spot near any of them waits 10 minutes and is looked at again, so a zone removed later lets its region fill in.
- **With other packs:** sites anchor the wanderers: each built hermit hut, shrine, tablet, cairn, watch post and camp is sent as `realm:poi` `{ kind, dim, x, z, name }` when built and again after every world load (wander_bp keeps them in memory). Story progress comes from Story Questlines' `realm:saga_progress` `{ player, act }` (asked with `realm:saga_progress_ping`). Rewards go out as `realm:quest_done`, `realm:skill_xp`, `realm:journal`, `realm:title_unlock`, `realm:trail_unlock`, `realm:gossip` (kinds `atlas` and `atlas_site`) and `realm:ingredient_give`; meteors come in as `realm:sky_event`, and the shrine's day is the Realm day from `realm:calendar` (the world's day without it).
- **Testing hook:** `/scriptevent realm:atlas_debug {"player":"<id>","action":"state"}` answers with `realm:atlas_state` (counts, the nearest 8 spots, the player's data); `"action":"slots"` lists the spots of the region you're in (or, with `"cell":[cx,cz]`, of any region, so a test can pick kinds before anyone walks in); `{"action":"prefer","key":"<cx,cz,slot>","kind":"cairn"}` picks a spot's kind before it's built; `"action":"use"` or `"break"` with a `key` uses a site for a simulated player, `"kill"` ends its fight, `"tablets"` with a `count` marks the first tablets read. Scenario: `tools/test-bds/examples/atlas.js`.
- **Minimap:** `realm:atlas_region` `{ player, name }` when a player enters a region, `realm:atlas_site` for each site found and `realm:atlas_sites` (all of a player's found sites, in parts) on `realm:atlas_ping` (see the minimap events in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).
