## Titles & Trails — `titles_bp`

Collect titles and wear one on a line under your name, like `Stormchaser` or `Master Miner`, and pick a particle trail that follows you as you move: a little rain cloud over your head, falling leaves, embers or sparkles. Some titles you earn by playing (travel far, stay up at night, stand out in thunderstorms); other packs give more, such as [Skills](#skills--skills_bp) at level 50.

### How to use

1. Play: three titles count up by themselves. `Wanderer` after traveling 10,000 blocks, `Night Owl` after 2 hours played at night, and `Stormchaser` after 10 minutes outdoors in thunderstorms. Each comes with a trail. Unlocking one says `New title unlocked: Stormchaser. Wear it with /realm:titles` in chat.
2. Run `/realm:titles` to see your title, your trail and how far along you are with each title to earn (`Wanderer: 3,400/10,000 blocks traveled`).
3. Tap **Choose a title** and pick one (or **None**). With the [Nicknames](#nicknames--nick_bp) pack installed, it shows in gray on a line under your name above your head.
4. Tap **Choose a trail** and pick one (or **None**). It follows you whenever you move. Trails need the Realm Skies resource pack (`sky_rp`) on the realm; without it nothing shows.
5. **Operators:** `/realm:titles` also has `Give or take a title or trail` (pick a player online or type a name, the title or `trail:ember`, and tick **Take it away instead of giving it** to remove it) and `Settings` (which points to `/realm:config` → Titles & Trails). In chat, `/realm:titles_give Steve "Hero of the Realm"` gives a player a title, `/realm:titles_give Steve trail:ember` a trail, and `/realm:titles_take Steve "Hero of the Realm"` (or `trail:ember`) takes one away (players who are offline too, if they've played since the pack was added). Taking the title a player wears also clears it from under their name. `/realm:config` → **Titles & Trails** switches the built-in titles and trails and sets how often trails puff.

### What players see

- **Built-in titles** (`builtins`):

  | Title | How to earn it | Trail that comes with it |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Wanderer` | Travel 10,000 blocks, any way but teleporting (faster than `maxSpeed`), in any dimension | Falling leaves |
  | `Night Owl` | Play for 2 hours while it's night in the Overworld (from dusk to dawn, wherever you are) | Sparkles |
  | `Stormchaser` | Spend 10 minutes outdoors in the Overworld during a thunderstorm, with open sky above you (standing on sand or terracotta, as in deserts and badlands, doesn't count: no storm reaches the ground there; swimming over a sandy lake or sea bed does) | Rain cloud |

- **Titles from other packs** arrive the same way, with the same chat line: [Skills](#skills--skills_bp) gives `Master Miner`, `Master Woodcutter`, `Master Farmer`, `Master Angler`, `Master Warrior` and `Master Explorer` at level 50; [Guilds & Reputation](#guilds--reputation--guilds_bp) gives `Expert Miner` and `Master Miner` (and so on) at its top two ranks; [Blood Moon](#blood-moon--harvest-moon--moon_bp) gives `Blood Moon Survivor`; [Field Journal](#field-journal--journal_bp) pages and [Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp) chapters give some too. A title you already have is never announced twice.
- **Wearing a title:** you wear one at a time, or none. It shows under your name (and under the gamertag line, if you have a nickname) through the Nicknames pack. Titles are plain text up to 32 characters (`maxTitleLength`).
- **Trails:** `Rain cloud` (a small gray cloud with a drip, over your head), `Falling leaves`, `Embers`, `Sparkles` (behind you) `Hearts` (over your head, the game's own heart particle; a Confidant of a townsfolk in [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) gets it) and `Starwright glyphs` (enchanting-table glyphs behind you, the game's own particle; 25 sites found in [Atlas of the Realm](#atlas-of-the-realm--atlas_bp)), `Confetti` (the game's totem sparkles behind you) and `Festival notes` (music notes over your head), both from the [Realm Calendar](#realm-calendar--calendar_bp)'s ribbon stall. Everyone sees them. A puff every 4 ticks (`trailTicks`) while you move, none while you stand still, are invisible (the Invisibility effect) or in spectator mode. At most 12 puffs at a time are shared by everyone (`trailBudget`), so a busy realm stays smooth. Fast movement (sprinting quickly or gliding) leaves 3 puffs along the way instead of one, so the trail stays a smooth ribbon, and trails keep working during fast elytra flight (up to 45 blocks between checks, 20 on foot). While you glide, 2 more puffs of your trail stream past on both sides in front of you, so you see it in first and third person.
- **The menu** (`/realm:titles`) shows `Title: Stormchaser`, `Trail: Rain cloud`, and each built-in title as `[x] Wanderer` when you have it or `[ ] Night Owl: 45/120 minutes played at night` while you're earning it. The title and trail lists mark the one you use with `(now)`.
- **Announcements:** with `announceUnlocks` on, everyone else sees `Ann unlocked the title Stormchaser!`.
- **While the pack is disabled** (`enabled`), trails stop and the built-in titles stop counting; titles from other packs and operators are still recorded, and worn titles stay.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:titles` | Everyone | Shows your title, trail and progress toward the built-in titles; choose the title under your name and the trail that follows you (a puff every 4 ticks while moving, default `trailTicks`). Operators also get `Give or take a title or trail` (like `/realm:titles_give` and `/realm:titles_take`) and `Settings` |
| `/realm:titles_give <player> <title>` | Ops | Gives a player a title (quote titles and names with spaces), or a trail with `trail:cloud`, `trail:leaves`, `trail:ember`, `trail:sparkle`, `trail:hearts`, `trail:glyphs`, `trail:confetti` or `trail:notes`. Works for offline players this pack has seen |
| `/realm:titles_take <player:String> <title:String>` | Ops | Takes a title away from a player (quote names and titles with spaces), or a trail with `trail:cloud`, `trail:leaves`, `trail:ember`, `trail:sparkle`, `trail:hearts`, `trail:glyphs`, `trail:confetti` or `trail:notes`. Works for offline players this pack has seen. Says so, and changes nothing, when the player never had it; a player's worn title or active trail is cleared when it is the one taken. |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Built-in titles count up and trails show. Disabled: neither; titles from other packs are still recorded and worn titles stay |
| `trails` | `true` | Trails follow the players who chose one |
| `trailTicks` | `4` | A trail puff every this many ticks while a player moves (2 to 20 in game; 20 ticks = 1 second) |
| `trailBudget` | `12` | At most this many trail puffs each time, shared by everyone |
| `announceUnlocks` | `false` | Tell everyone in chat when a player unlocks a title |
| `maxSpeed` | `100` | Movement faster than this (blocks per second) is a teleport and doesn't count for `Wanderer` |
| `maxTitleLength` | `32` | Longest title in characters; longer ones from other packs are cut |
| `forgetAfterDays` | `365` | Remove an inactive player's saved titles, trails and built-in stats after this many real days; `0` disables pruning. Online or in-use cached records are skipped; a missing legacy timestamp starts now |
| `builtins` | `Wanderer`, `Night Owl`, `Stormchaser` (above) | `{ title, stat, amount, trail? }`: `stat` is `distance` (blocks), `night` (seconds played at night) or `storm` (seconds outdoors in thunderstorms); `trail` is unlocked with the title |

Operators can change `enabled`, `trails`, `trailTicks`, `trailBudget`, `announceUnlocks` and `forgetAfterDays` in game with `/realm:config`. Set `forgetAfterDays` to `0` to retain inactive players' earned records indefinitely. `maxSpeed`, `maxTitleLength` and `builtins` stay in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `titles:p:<player id>` | World | One per player: JSON `{ n, t, r, tr, s, ls }`, the gamertag, unlocked titles (at most 300), unlocked trails, chosen trail, built-in stats `{ d, n, w }`, and last-seen real milliseconds. Unknown fields are preserved. Untimestamped records start their inactivity clock when observed |
| `realm_title:<text>` | Player tag | The title the player wears (at most one); the Nicknames pack shows it |
| `titles:n:<lowercase gamertag>` | World | A name index: the player id the gamertag belongs to, so an offline name resolves without reading every record. The first writer of a name wins until that player's next join or a lookup proves another holder. On a miss a lookup reads at most 500 records, continuing where the last miss stopped, and repairs the index; the entry is removed when the record is pruned |
| `titles:weather` | World | The Overworld weather from the last change (`Clear`, `Rain` or `Thunder`) |
| `titles:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- Other packs unlock with the script events `realm:title_unlock` `{ player, title, from }` and `realm:trail_unlock` `{ player, trail, from }` (`player` is the player id; `trail` is `cloud`, `leaves`, `ember`, `sparkle`, `hearts`, `glyphs`, `confetti` or `notes`). The data is a world property per player, so an unlock for someone offline is kept for them. Repeats are ignored quietly. A `realm:title_unlock` with `ack` (the sender's folder, at most 40 characters) is answered with `realm:title_ack` `{ player, title, ack }` once handled, whether the title was new or already owned (Milestones uses it to stop re-sending its backfill).
- The chosen title is the player tag `realm_title:<text>`; only this pack sets or removes it. The [Nicknames](#nicknames--nick_bp) pack reads it; after each change this pack sends `realm:nametag` `{ player, from: "titles_bp" }` so Nicknames shows it at once.
- **Stats** are counted once a second and saved every minute and when the player leaves. The weather can't be read by scripts, so the pack follows `weatherChange` in the Overworld and keeps the last value in `titles:weather`, as Rain Extras does. Outdoors means the highest block above you is at most one block above your feet.
- **Trails** use `dimension.spawnParticle` with `realm:trail_cloud`, `realm:trail_leaves`, `realm:trail_ember` and `realm:trail_sparkle` from the Realm Skies resource pack, so every player nearby sees them. The pack checks every 2 ticks whether `trailTicks` have passed, then starts at a different player each time so the budget is shared fairly. When nobody online has chosen a trail the pass is skipped.
- Inactive-record pruning runs shortly after load and every six hours. Each deletion rechecks the live retention setting and whether the player is online or the record is in use, then logs the removal. Unlike Nicknames' gamertag-only pruning, this deletes the earned title/trail record and its stats.

---

## Relics — `relics_bp`

Seventeen rare relics, each a named item with a power of its own: a staff that calls lightning in a thunderstorm, boots that speed you through the rain, a lamp that helps you mine, a pendant that saves you from fire. Ten come from adventures in other packs (champions, bounties, treasure maps, caravans) or are forged from 8 Relic Shards at a relicsmith; seven more are story relics, earned only in the [Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp). Relics never break and stay with you when you die. Ida can **ascend** a relic three times (+1 Awakened, +2 Ascended, +3 Starlit: a shorter cooldown or a longer reach, then a unique bonus and a gold name) for Relic Shards, Storm Glass and Crowns, and breaks a duplicate into Relic Essence. Carry all three relics of a **set** (Storm, Tide, Deep or Sun) for a set bonus.

### How to use

1. Find relics: other packs hand them out as rewards, and champions drop **Relic Shards** (purple amethyst shards named `Relic Shard`). Getting one says `You received a relic: Storm Staff (Legendary). Use in a thunderstorm: lightning strikes what you look at.` in chat.
2. Keep a relic where it works: some in your main hand, some anywhere in your hotbar or offhand, helmets and boots worn. Its lore says what it does, and its last line where it works (`Works in your main hand`, `Works anywhere in your hotbar or offhand`, `Works worn on your head` or `Works worn on your feet`); **Your relics** in `/realm:relics` says where it works.
3. Bring 8 Relic Shards to a relicsmith (Ida the Relicsmith, from the [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) pack): tap her and pick **Relic forge**, then **Forge a relic**. You get a random relic you haven't had yet; rarer ones are less likely. Story relics are never forged.
4. Run `/realm:relics` for the menu: **Your relics** (also `/realm:relics_list`) lists the relics you've found, what each does and how many are left to find.
5. **Ascend** a relic at Ida: **Relic forge** → **Ascend a relic**, pick a relic you carry and **Ascend**. +1 takes 6 Relic Shards, 1 Storm Glass and 60 Crowns; +2 takes 12, 3 and 150; +3 takes 20, 5 and 400 (`ascension.costs`). Story relics stop at +1 until a story or a friendship allows more (Hal's Compass: Old Tobin as a Confidant, or *The Gull's Last Voyage* sailed).
6. Got the same relic twice? **Break a duplicate** in the forge turns your lower copy into 4 **Relic Essence** (`ascension.essencePerBreak`), which counts like Relic Shards for ascension and is spent first.
7. Carry a whole **set** in your hotbar, offhand or armor: Storm Staff + Storm Meter + Rain Charm, Tide Boots + Hal's Compass + Compass of Echoes, Miner's Lamp + Lantern of the Deep + Lantern Shard, or Sun Pendant + Frost Band + Wayfarer Boots. The bar above the hotbar names the bonus when it starts; **Your relics** lists the sets.
8. Holding the Storm Meter shows the nearest storm cell above the hotbar. It waits while another pack's note shows there (skill XP, mob health, a sort result). Don't want that? Disable **Storm Meter readout** in `/realm:prefs`.
9. **Operators:** the `/realm:relics` menu also has **Give a relic** (pick a player and a relic; or `/realm:relics_give <player> <relic>`) and **Place a relicsmith here** (or `/realm:relics_smith`), which asks the Townsfolk pack to place Ida where you stand. `/realm:config` → **Relics** enables or disables the abilities, sets the shards a forge takes, lets players forge anywhere, and sets whether relics wear out, whether the Storm Staff can strike players and how close to spawn it may strike.

### What players see

- **The relics** (`relics`). The first ten are found or forged:

  | Relic | Item | Rarity | Where it works | What it does | How to get it (other packs' defaults) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Storm Staff (`storm_staff`) | Trident | Legendary | Main hand | Use it in a thunderstorm in the Overworld: lightning strikes the mob or block you look at, up to 48 blocks away (`staffRange`). Cooldown 30 s | Forge |
  | Rain Charm (`rain_charm`) | Goat horn | Common | Hotbar or offhand | Regeneration I while you stand in the rain | Forge, pot of gold, treasure maps |
  | Tide Boots (`tide_boots`) | Blue leather boots | Rare | Worn | Speed I and Jump Boost I while you're in the rain | Forge, expeditions, the story (The Drowned Bell) |
  | Lantern of the Deep (`lantern_deep`) | Warped fungus on a stick | Common | Hotbar or offhand | Night Vision below y 0 | Forge, expeditions |
  | Storm Meter (`storm_meter`) | Spyglass | Rare | Main hand | Shows `Storm Meter: Cell: 340m NE, strength 7/10` above the hotbar, or `No storm cell` | Forge |
  | Compass of Echoes (`compass_echoes`) | Music disc (5); older ones are a brush | Rare | Main hand | Use it: chat says where the nearest champion is within 128 blocks (`compassRange`), e.g. `Compass of Echoes: a champion (Gerald the Unexploded) is 84m NE.` Cooldown 10 s | Forge, expeditions, treasure maps, the story (The Last Map) |
  | Frost Band (`frost_band`) | Music disc (wait) | Rare | Hotbar or offhand | Your melee hits give Slowness I for 3 s | Forge, expeditions |
  | Sun Pendant (`sun_pendant`) | Music disc (blocks) | Epic | Hotbar or offhand | When you catch fire: Fire Resistance for 10 s. Cooldown 120 s | Forge, pot of gold, treasure maps |
  | Miner's Lamp (`miners_lamp`) | Golden helmet | Common | Worn | Haste I below y 30 | Forge, expeditions |
  | Wayfarer Boots (`wayfarer_boots`) | Chainmail boots | Common | Worn | Speed I while you sprint outdoors in the Overworld | Forge, treasure maps |

  The seven **story relics** are rewards from the [Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp) only (never forged, never in random drops):

  | Relic | Item | Rarity | Where it works | What it does |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Lantern Shard (`lantern_shard`) | Music disc (otherside) | Epic | Hotbar or offhand | Night Vision in the dark (at night, under cover below y 50, or in the Nether and the End). Held in your main hand, every few seconds it says where the nearest unlit seal is: `Lantern Shard: The Tide Seal pulls 340m NE` (when the story reports its seals) |
  | Gray Choir Mask (`choir_mask`) | Gray leather helmet | Epic | Worn | Choir enemies (the story's mobs tagged `saga:choir`) only do half damage to you, unless you've hit one in the last 10 s; Darkness (wardens, sculk shriekers) is removed. Sneaking is already silent to sculk in the game |
  | Hal's Compass (`hal_compass`) | Music disc (13) | Rare | Main hand | Use it: `Hal's Compass: Your last death: 340m NE (y 12). Home: 120m S (y 70).` (home is your bed or respawn point, else `World spawn`). Cooldown 5 s |
  | Fen Charm (`vesna_charm`) | Music disc (chirp) | Rare | Hotbar or offhand | Poison never takes hold, and witches (their potions too) can't hurt you, unless you've hit a witch in the last 10 s |
  | The Singing Blade (`singing_blade`) | Iron sword | Epic | Main hand | Each melee hit rings a bell note: monsters within 6 blocks of what you hit (`auraRange`) get Slowness II for 2 s; at most once every 2 s |
  | The Hollow Crown (`hollow_crown`) | Chainmail helmet | Legendary | Worn | At night in the Overworld: Night Vision and Strength I. Villagers and wandering traders shun you: tapping one says `The villager shrinks away from the Hollow Crown` (no trading while you wear it; [wanderers](#wanderers-of-the-wilds--wander_bp) dressed as villagers still talk to you) |
  | Keeper's Lamp (`keeper_lamp`) | Music disc (strad) | Rare | Hotbar or offhand | In the dark: a ring of end rod light around you (everyone sees it), and monsters within 6 blocks (`auraRange`) slow down (Slowness I) |

- **A relic** has a colored name (green common, blue rare, purple epic, gold legendary) and lore: its rarity, what it does and its cooldown. Relics are kept when you die (`keepOnDeath`) and their durability is restored while you hold or wear them (`autoRepair`), so they never break. The Storm Staff is a trident that can't be thrown or charged (using it calls lightning instead), so it can't be lost in lava or the void; it still hits like a trident. Relics can't go in a jukebox. Don't put a relic in a crafting grid (to dye the Tide Boots, say): what comes out is a plain item.
- **"In the rain"** means in the Overworld while it rains or thunders, with nothing 2 or more blocks over your head (leaves count as cover), and not on sand, terracotta, snow or ice, where it doesn't rain (in water over a sandy lake or sea bed it does).
- **Effects** last about 10 seconds, are topped up while the condition holds and are removed within a second of it ending. A stronger or longer effect, such as a potion, is never shortened.
- **The Storm Staff** answers when the pack knows it's thundering: the weather changed to a thunderstorm while the pack was running, a lightning bolt it didn't make struck in the Overworld in the last minute (so it also works in a storm that started before the pack was installed, once the first bolt falls), or you're within 160 blocks of a storm cell from [Storm Chasing](#storm-chasing--storm_bp). A strike says `Storm Staff: lightning! Ready again in 30s`. Otherwise it says why, above the hotbar: `Storm Staff: it only answers in a thunderstorm`, `Storm Staff: ready in 12s`, `Storm Staff: nothing to strike within 48 blocks`, `Storm Staff: the sky won't strike within 24 blocks of spawn` (`avoidSpawn`, 0 = anywhere), or `Storm Staff: too close to you`. It doesn't strike players (`staffHitsPlayers`) or townsfolk; it hits what's behind them. It won't strike within 5 blocks of you, another player (unless `staffHitsPlayers`), a villager or wandering trader, a tamed pet, a townsfolk NPC, an armor stand or a painting, and any fire the bolt starts is put out (checked for 4 seconds), so it can't burn a build.
- **The forge** takes 8 shards (`shardsPerForge`) from anywhere in your inventory and gives a random relic you haven't had yet from the first ten, picked by rarity: common 50, rare 30, epic 15, legendary 5 (`rarityWeights`). Once you've had all ten, any of them. Without shards it says `You need 8 Relic Shards to forge a relic. You have 3.`
- **`/realm:relics`** opens a menu: **Your relics**, **Forge a relic** (only when operators let players forge anywhere, `forgeAnywhere`), and for operators **Give a relic** and **Place a relicsmith here**. **Your relics** shows `Relics found: 3 of 10`, each relic you've had with its rarity, ability, cooldown and where it works (`- not with you` when it isn't in your inventory), how many of each rarity are still to find, then `Story relics: 1 of 7` and the story relics you've had. Opened from a relicsmith, it's the **Relic forge** with a **Forge a relic** button.
- **Place a relicsmith here** (operators) asks the [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) pack to place Ida the Relicsmith (`relicsmithId`) at your spot, facing your way, like `/realm:npc_add ida`: `The relicsmith is here.` Without the Townsfolk pack it says `No answer from the Townsfolk pack, so no relicsmith was placed.` and that the pack is needed. A relicsmith is any townsfolk with the `relicsmith` role (`npcRole`).
- **Gifts for players who are offline** (from another pack) wait and are handed over 5 seconds after they next join.
- The first time you get each relic, the [Field Journal](#field-journal--journal_bp) records it on its Relics page.
- **Ida's friends:** a player who is a Friend of Ida ([Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)) needs 10% fewer Relic Shards to forge (8 to 7 by default, rounded down, at least 1) and to ascend, from `realm:affinity`.

#### Relic Ascension

- **At the relicsmith** (`ascension.enabled`): **Ascend a relic** lists the relics you carry below +3 with the next stage's cost (`needs a story or a friend` for a gated story relic); picking one shows what the stage adds, the cost and what you have, and **Ascend** takes it all at once, only if everything is there: Relic Essence first, then Relic Shards, Storm Glass (`minecraft:prismarine_crystals` with the lore `Charged by a lightning strike`, from [Storm Chasing](#storm-chasing--storm_bp), tornadoes or the caravan) and Crowns. Chat says `Storm Staff is now +1 Awakened: 20% shorter cooldown.`
- **Costs** (`ascension.costs`): +1 Awakened 6 shards or essence, 1 Storm Glass, 60 Crowns; +2 Ascended 12, 3, 150; +3 Starlit 20, 5, 400. All 17 relics at +3 take 646 shards, 153 Storm Glass and 10,370 Crowns.
- **What a stage does:** relics with a cooldown (Storm Staff, Compass of Echoes, Sun Pendant, Hal's Compass, the Singing Blade) wait 20%, 35% and 50% less; the Frost Band's slow lasts, the Keeper's Lamp's ring reaches, and the Gray Choir Mask and Fen Charm protect 25%, 50% and 75% more (the mask: 62%, 75%, then 87% of Choir damage back; the charm: that much of a witch's damage back even after you hit one); the other passive relics keep working 10, 20 and 30 seconds after their condition ends (out of the rain, back above y 0, morning). +2 adds a lore line; +3 adds a unique bonus and a gold name (`Storm Staff +3`):

  | Relic | Starlit (+3) bonus |
  |---|---|
  | Storm Staff | Answers in any rain, not only in thunder |
  | Rain Charm | Also works while you swim |
  | Tide Boots | Water Breathing while you swim |
  | Lantern of the Deep | Works below y 30, not only y 0 |
  | Storm Meter | Says if the cell is closing in or moving away |
  | Compass of Echoes | Also tells the champion's health |
  | Frost Band | Slowness II instead of I |
  | Sun Pendant | Also Regeneration I while the fire burns out |
  | Miner's Lamp | Haste II below y 0 |
  | Wayfarer Boots | Works under cover too, not only outdoors |
  | Lantern Shard | Night Vision anywhere, dark or not |
  | Gray Choir Mask | Choir enemies can't hurt you while you sneak |
  | Hal's Compass | Each use also gives Speed I for 15 s |
  | Fen Charm | Wither can't take hold either |
  | The Singing Blade | The note also gives Weakness I |
  | The Hollow Crown | Works from dusk to dawn |
  | Keeper's Lamp | Monsters in the ring get Weakness I too |

- **Story relics** stop at +1 until (`storyGates`, the townsfolk at `ascension.gateLevel` 4, Confidant, from `realm:affinity`, or the story flag from Story Questlines' `realm:npc_flags`): Hal's Compass, Old Tobin or *The Gull's Last Voyage* sailed (`g:gull`); Lantern Shard, Mara or *The Three Seals* finished; Gray Choir Mask, Warden Reyes or *Lantern Night* finished; Fen Charm, Moss or Vesna set free (`g:vesna` = `free`); the Singing Blade, Ida; the Hollow Crown, Quill; Keeper's Lamp, Elsie.
- **Starlit** news: chat tells everyone (`announceStarlit`) and the town gossips (`relic_starlit`; at most one piece of news from this pack per in-game hour, see Town news in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).
- **Break a duplicate:** with two or more of the same relic on you, the forge breaks the copy with the lowest stage into 4 Relic Essence (`ascension.essencePerBreak`): `minecraft:echo_shard` named `Relic Essence` with the lore `From a broken relic: ascends relics`. The menu asks first and warns when the copy had a stage.
- A relic renamed on an anvil keeps your name; only its lore follows the stage.

#### Relic sets

Checked every second over your hotbar, offhand and armor (`setsEnabled`); the bar says `Storm set: ...` when one starts:

| Set | Relics | Bonus |
|---|---|---|
| Storm | Storm Staff, Storm Meter, Rain Charm | Lightning can't hurt you (nor the fire it starts on you), and a charged lightning rod gives 1 more Storm Glass ([Storm Chasing](#storm-chasing--storm_bp)) |
| Tide | Tide Boots, Hal's Compass, Compass of Echoes | Conduit Power in water (Bedrock has no Dolphin's Grace effect) |
| Deep | Miner's Lamp, Lantern of the Deep, Lantern Shard | Night Vision below y 0, and no Darkness there (sneaking is already silent to sculk in the game) |
| Sun | Sun Pendant, Frost Band, Wayfarer Boots | Fire Resistance at dawn and dusk (time 23000-1000 and 11500-13500), and freezing can't hurt you then |

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:relics` | Everyone | Opens the relics menu: your relics, the forge when players may forge anywhere (default disabled, `forgeAnywhere`), and for operators giving a relic and placing a relicsmith |
| `/realm:relics_list` | Everyone | Lists the relics you've found and what they do |
| `/realm:relics_give <player> <relic>` | Operators | Gives the player a new relic: `storm_staff`, `rain_charm`, `tide_boots`, `lantern_deep`, `storm_meter`, `compass_echoes`, `frost_band`, `sun_pendant`, `miners_lamp`, `wayfarer_boots`, or a story relic: `lantern_shard`, `choir_mask`, `hal_compass`, `vesna_charm`, `singing_blade`, `hollow_crown`, `keeper_lamp` |
| `/realm:relics_smith` | Operators | Places the relicsmith (Ida, `relicsmithId`) where you stand; needs the Townsfolk pack |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Relic abilities work. Disabled, relics are only keepsakes; the forge and the commands still work |
| `shardsPerForge` | `8` | Relic Shards it takes to forge one relic (1-64 in game) |
| `forgeAnywhere` | `false` | Players can forge from `/realm:relics` anywhere, not only at a relicsmith |
| `npcRole` | `"relicsmith"` | The townsfolk role that offers **Relic forge** |
| `relicsmithId` | `"ida"` | The townsfolk **Place a relicsmith here** places (a Townsfolk pack id with the `npcRole` role) |
| `keepOnDeath` | `true` | New relics stay with their owner on death (set when a relic is made) |
| `autoRepair` | `true` | A relic's durability is restored while it's held or worn, so it never breaks |
| `rarityWeights.common` | `50` | How likely the forge picks a common relic (relative to the others) |
| `rarityWeights.rare` | `30` | The same for rare relics |
| `rarityWeights.epic` | `15` | The same for epic relics |
| `rarityWeights.legendary` | `5` | The same for legendary relics |
| `staffRange` | `48` | How far the Storm Staff reaches (blocks) |
| `staffHitsPlayers` | `false` | The Storm Staff can strike players |
| `avoidSpawn` | `24` | No Storm Staff lightning within this many blocks of world spawn (0 = anywhere; 0-256 in game). Fires a bolt starts are put out either way |
| `compassRange` | `128` | How far the Compass of Echoes looks for a champion (blocks) |
| `auraRange` | `6` | How far the Singing Blade's note and the Keeper's Lamp's slowing reach (blocks); the lamp's ring of light is drawn at up to 4 (both farther once the lamp is ascended) |
| `ascension.enabled` | `true` | Relics can be ascended and duplicates broken at the relicsmith. Disabled: stages already made still work |
| `ascension.costs` | `[{ shards: 6, glass: 1, crowns: 60 }, { shards: 12, glass: 3, crowns: 150 }, { shards: 20, glass: 5, crowns: 400 }]` | What +1, +2 and +3 cost: Relic Shards or Essence, Storm Glass and Crowns |
| `ascension.essencePerBreak` | `4` | Relic Essence a duplicate breaks into |
| `ascension.gateLevel` | `4` | The affinity level (Townsfolk: 4 = Confidant) with a story relic's townsfolk that lets it past +1 |
| `ascension.announceStarlit` | `true` | Tell everyone in chat when a relic becomes Starlit |
| `setsEnabled` | `true` | Relic sets give their bonus |
| `storyGates` | the seven above | `{ relic, npc, flag, value, text }`: what lets a story relic past +1, the townsfolk at `ascension.gateLevel` or the story flag `flag` = `value` (`""` for none); `text` is what the forge shows |
| `relics` | the 17 above | `{ id, name, item, rarity, where, cooldown, ability, story? }` per relic. `id` is saved on items, so keep it. `item` must be an item that doesn't stack (relics carry data, which only those can); a stacking one is replaced with a brush. `where` is `hand`, `carry` (hotbar or offhand), `head` or `feet`. `cooldown` in seconds. `ability` is the lore text. `story: true` relics are never forged. The powers belong to the ids, so a new id would only be a keepsake |

Operators can change `enabled`, `shardsPerForge`, `forgeAnywhere`, `autoRepair`, `staffHitsPlayers`, `avoidSpawn`, `ascension.enabled` and `setsEnabled` in game with `/realm:config`. Each player can switch the Storm Meter's readout with **Storm Meter readout** in `/realm:prefs`. The rest stays in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `relic:id` | Item | The relic's id, on the relic item itself |
| `relic:serial` | Item | A number unique to each relic made on this realm (the ascension menu finds the relic you picked by it) |
| `relic:asc` | Item | The relic's ascension stage, 1 to 3 (none = 0) |
| `relics:found` | Player | JSON array of the relic ids the player has had |
| `relics:death` | Player | JSON `{ dim, x, y, z }`: where the player last died, for Hal's Compass |
| `relics:pref` | Player | The player's own **Storm Meter readout** choice |
| `relics:serial` | World | The last serial number handed out |
| `relics:pending:<player id>`, `relics:pending_idx` | World | Each offline player's relic/shard reward record and the bounded oldest-first player index, under the [offline reward storage limits](#offline-reward-storage). Each value allows up to 20 relics and 6,400 shards |
| `relics:pending` | World | Legacy all-player reward map, retained only for unmigrated leftovers |
| `relics:weather` | World | The Overworld weather at the last change (`Clear`, `Rain` or `Thunder`); the stable Script API can't read it |
| `relics:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

Cooldowns are kept in memory, so a restart makes every relic ready again. Stages live on the items and sets are worked out from what you carry, so both survive restarts.

### How it works

- A relic is a vanilla item with a name, lore and the item dynamic property `relic:id`. Only items that don't stack can carry dynamic properties, which is why the relics are tools, armor, horns and discs. Compasses stack in Bedrock (64, lodestone compasses too), so the compass relics are discs; Compasses of Echoes made before 1.1.0 are brushes and still work. An anvil can rename any item but can't add the property, so a fake relic does nothing.
- Each player's hotbar, offhand, head and feet (12 slots) are read again after an inventory change or a new selected slot, and otherwise every 5 seconds (every second while a relic is in the main hand and `autoRepair` is on); the conditions are checked every second from what was read. So a relic put in the offhand or worn without an inventory change is noticed within 5 seconds. Wanted effects are added for 210 ticks (Night Vision 400, so it doesn't flicker) when they're missing or run low, and removed when no longer wanted if they're still level I and no longer than that. A durability-damaged relic in hand or worn is mended (`autoRepair`), and a relic whose lore is out of date (an ability that changed in an update) gets the current lore. "In the rain", "outdoors" and "under cover" use one `getTopmostBlock` over the player, only when a relic needs it. The stable API can't read light levels, so "in the dark" is night (time 13000-23000), under cover below y 50, or the Nether and the End.
- **Used relics** (Storm Staff, Compass of Echoes, Hal's Compass) run from `beforeEvents.itemUse`; the staff's use is canceled so the trident never charges or flies. A tap that arrives as `beforeEvents.playerInteractWithBlock` (aiming at the ground) does the same, and `afterEvents.itemStartUse` is a safety net for the staff; one tap does one thing (4 ticks apart). `playerInteractWithBlock` also keeps relics out of jukeboxes.
- **Weather:** the stable API can't read it, so it comes from `weatherChange` (saved as `relics:weather`, so it survives a restart; the event's dimension is matched with or without `minecraft:`), from `entitySpawn` of a `minecraft:lightning_bolt` the staff didn't make (a thunderstorm for the next minute), and from Storm Chasing's `realm:storm_cell` reports.
- **The Storm Staff** aims with `getEntitiesFromViewDirection` (players, items, projectiles and townsfolk skipped) and falls back to `getBlockFromViewDirection` (water counts as a target), then spawns `minecraft:lightning_bolt` and removes `minecraft:fire` (nothing else) in the 7 x 7 x 7 blocks around the strike 1, 5, 15, 40 and 80 ticks later. The compass finds the closest entity tagged `realm:champion` ([Champions](#champions--elite_bp)).
- **Hits** use `afterEvents.entityHurt`: the Frost Band and Singing Blade on a melee hit by the player (the blade's monsters are `families: ["monster"]`, its note is `note.bell`); the Sun Pendant when fire, burning, lava, magma or a campfire hurts the player (also checked every second while on fire). The stable API can't cancel damage or clear a mob's target, so the Gray Choir Mask and the Fen Charm give back the damage right after the hit (half for the mask, all for the charm), unless the player hit a mob tagged `saga:choir` (or a witch) in the last 10 s. `beforeEvents.effectAdd` cancels Poison for the Fen Charm; `beforeEvents.playerInteractWithEntity` turns villagers away from the Hollow Crown (not those tagged `realm:npc`, which another pack's menu answers); `afterEvents.entityDie` saves the death point.
- The Storm Meter shows the last `realm:storm_cell` report from [Storm Chasing](#storm-chasing--storm_bp) (sent every 2 s); without one in the last 5 seconds it says `No storm cell`.
- **Seals** (Lantern Shard): the pack listens for `realm:seals` `{ player?, seals: [{ name, dim, x, z }] }`, the seals still unlit (for that player when `player` is given, else for everyone; an empty list clears it), and asks with `realm:seals_ping` `{}` 5 seconds after the world loads. The [Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp) is the pack meant to send it; without it the shard only gives Night Vision.
- The Storm Meter and Lantern Shard readouts are steady lines of the action bar protocol (see [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)): each write sends `realm:actionbar` with `from: "relics_bp"` and `steady: 45`, and they skip their redraw while another pack's note lasts. Since they show only while you hold that relic, they outrank the lines that are always there: an expedition's run line, the build mode line and the story tracker wait for them, and they wait only for notes and the Elytra HUD while you glide (requests marked `background`, the Party HUD's, don't hold them).
- **The relicsmith:** **Place a relicsmith here** sends `realm:npc_summon` `{ id: "ida", player }` to the [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) pack and waits 1 second for `realm:npc_summoned` `{ id, player, ok, error? }`.
- Other packs give relics and shards with the script events `realm:relic_give` `{ player, relic }` (story relics included: Story Questlines rewards them by id) and `realm:shard_give` `{ player, amount }` (at most 640). A Relic Shard is `minecraft:amethyst_shard` named `Relic Shard` whose first lore line is `Bring 8 to a relicsmith`; that lore line is how the forge counts them. Townsfolk with the `relicsmith` role get the **Relic forge** offer in answer to `realm:npc_talk`, and `realm:npc_choose` opens the forge.
- The first time a player has a relic (given, forged, or seen in their hotbar or armor, for one traded to them), the pack sends `realm:journal` `{ page: "relics" }`.
- **Sets** go out as `realm:relic_sets` `{ player, sets, from: "relics_bp" }` (`sets`: `storm`, `tide`, `deep`, `sun`) when a player's sets change (and once on join), and again for everyone on `realm:relic_sets_ping`; [Storm Chasing](#storm-chasing--storm_bp) reads it. The story relic gates keep every `realm:affinity` level and each player's `realm:npc_flags` in memory (`realm:npc_flags_ping` 5.5 seconds after the world loads). The +3 news is `realm:gossip` `{ kind: "relic_starlit", place: <relic> }`. Lingering passives remember when each condition last held, in memory.

## Field Journal — `journal_bp`

A journal that fills itself as you play: the mobs you've defeated, the places you've been, the fish you've caught, the weather and sky events you've seen, the relics you've had, the story chapters you've finished and the wanderers you've befriended. Each page shows how complete it is, and finishing a page gives XP levels, Crowns and a title.

### How to use

1. Play: entries are added on their own. The first time you defeat a creeper, chat says `Journal: New entry in Mobs - Creeper`.
2. Run `/realm:journal` to open the journal: your overall completion, then a button per page with its progress (`Mobs 12/30 (40%)`). Open a page to see what you've found (`[x]`) and what's still missing (`[ ]`), with a short note on each mob you've met.
3. Find every entry on a page to finish it: chat says `Journal page complete: Mobs! Reward: 10 levels, the title Naturalist` and `+200 Crowns (Journal: Mobs)`.
4. Don't want a chat line for every entry? Disable **New journal entry notes** in `/realm:prefs`.
5. **Operators:** `/realm:config` → **Field Journal** enables or disables new entries, the page rewards and the entry notes. The pages, their entries and rewards, and how biomes are recognized are in `config.js`.

### What players see

- **Mobs** (30 entries): the first time you defeat each kind of mob (arrows and tridents count): zombie, husk, drowned, skeleton, stray, bogged, creeper, spider, cave spider, enderman, witch, slime, phantom, pillager, vindicator, guardian, silverfish, breeze, blaze, ghast, magma cube, wither skeleton, piglin, hoglin, shulker, cow, pig, sheep, chicken and rabbit. Each found mob shows a one-line note (`Silent until it hisses. Keep your distance.`). Other mobs you defeat are listed under "Also found". Reward: 10 levels, 200 Crowns, title **Naturalist**.
- **Places** (29 entries): the Overworld, the Nether and the End; below y 0 and below y -55; above y 200 and above y 300 (in the overworld); 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000 blocks from world spawn (`farDistances`); and biomes, recognized from the blocks around you (below). The page also shows your deepest and highest y and the farthest you've been from spawn. Reward: 10 levels, 200 Crowns, title **Explorer**. The first site of each kind you find in [Atlas of the Realm](#atlas-of-the-realm--atlas_bp) (a Wayside Shrine, a Choir Cairn...) is listed under "Also found".
- **Biomes** can't be read by a pack, so they're guessed from blocks (`biomes`): the surface block over you for Desert (sand, cactus or dead bushes, above y 66), Badlands (red sand or terracotta), Snowy lands (snow or ice), Jungle (jungle leaves), Mushroom Fields (mycelium), Cherry Grove (cherry leaves or pink petals), Swamp (mangrove or lily pads), Taiga (spruce leaves or podzol), Dark Forest, Savanna (acacia leaves) and Pale Garden; water at least 9 blocks deep, with you on it or up to 16 blocks under its surface, for Ocean; the block under your feet for Lush Caves (moss, below y 50), Dripstone Caves, the Deep Dark (sculk, below y 0) and the four Nether biomes (crimson or warped nylium, soul sand or soil, basalt or blackstone). A build of the right blocks can count too.
- **Fish** (4 entries): cod, salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish caught with a fishing rod. Species from [Fishing 2.0](#fishing-20--fishing_bp) are listed under "Also found". Reward: 5 levels, 100 Crowns, title **Angler**.
- **Weather** (9 entries): rain and a thunderstorm (being in the overworld, not deep underground, while it happens), a storm cell ([Storm Chasing](#storm-chasing--storm_bp)), a tornado ([Tornadoes](#tornadoes--tornado_bp)), a rainbow ([Rainbows & the Pot of Gold](#rainbows--the-pot-of-gold--rainbow_bp)), a meteor ([Meteor Strikes](#meteor-strikes--meteor_bp)), an aurora ([Aurora & Shooting Stars](#aurora--shooting-stars--night_bp)), a Blood Moon and a Harvest Moon ([Blood Moon & Harvest Moon](#blood-moon--harvest-moon--moon_bp)). A sky event counts for everyone in its dimension within 256 blocks of it (`skyEventRadius`), or everyone there when it has no spot. Reward: 10 levels, 250 Crowns, title **Stormwatcher**.
- **Relics** (10 entries): the first time you have each relic from [Relics](#relics--relics_bp). Reward: 15 levels, 500 Crowns, title **Relic Keeper**.
- **Story**: the chapters you finish in [Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp), in order. It has no fixed list, so no completion.
- **Wanderers** (8 entries): the Recurring Wanderers of [Wanderers of the Wilds](#wanderers-of-the-wilds--wander_bp), each once you finish the first chapter of their chain: Pell the Pilgrim, Anwen the Surveyor's Ghost, Brannoch Deepdelve, Rook the Rival, Marigold of the Heights, Tamsin Galeward, Vesk the Exile and Hob Fairweather, each with a one-line note. Reward: 10 levels, 200 Crowns, title **Friend of the Road**.
- **Overall** completion counts every entry on the pages with a list. Rewards are given once per page; Crowns go on the shared `crowns` scoreboard ([Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp)) and titles to [Titles & Trails](#titles--trails--titles_bp). Without those packs the levels are still given.
- **Entry notes**: the first one each session ends with `(/realm:journal)` so new players find the book.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:journal` | Everyone | Opens your journal: completion overall and per page, then each page's entries (default rewards, `pages`) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | New entries are recorded. Disabled, nothing new is added; the journal can still be read |
| `notes` | `true` | A chat line for each new entry. Each player can choose in `/realm:prefs` |
| `rewards` | `true` | Finishing a page gives its reward |
| `skyEventRadius` | `256` | Players within this many blocks of an announced sky event get its Weather entry |
| `farDistances` | `[1000, 5000, 10000]` | Distances from world spawn (blocks, overworld) that are Places entries, `far_<distance>`; each needs an entry in the Places page |
| `pages` | 7 pages (above) | `{ id, label, entries, reward }` per page, in menu order. `entries`: `{ id, label, blurb? }` (keep each `id`: players' journals are saved by it). `reward`: `{ levels, crowns, title }`. Mob ids are the mob's id without `minecraft:`; fish ids are the fish item's |
| `biomes` | 18 rules (above) | How biomes are guessed: `{ entry, at, blocks, dim?, minY?, maxY? }`. `at` is `top` (the surface block over you, while you're near the surface) or `feet` (the block you stand on or in). The first rule that matches wins |

Operators can change `enabled`, `rewards` and `notes` in game with `/realm:config`. Each player can switch the entry notes for themselves with **New journal entry notes** in `/realm:prefs`, which follows `notes` until they choose. The rest stays in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `journal:data` | Player | JSON `{ e, l, r, lo, hi, far, d }`: entry ids found per page, labels of entries that aren't in `config.js` (a label is only saved when it differs from the name made from the id), pages already rewarded, deepest and highest y, farthest from spawn, and (once one was dropped) per page a mark for each "Also found" entry dropped to make room (6 characters, a hash of its id; the newest 100 per page, at most 4,200 characters in all). A page keeps up to 100 entries that aren't in `config.js` (its "Also found", with the count shown); a new one past that drops the page's oldest. Kept under 30,000 characters (one such entry takes at most about 180): past that, the oldest "Also found" entries of the page with the most of them are dropped until it fits, so the newest finds are always saved |
| `journal:pref` | Player | The player's own **New journal entry notes** choice |
| `journal:weather` | World | The overworld weather at the last change; the stable Script API can't read it |
| `journal:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- **Mobs:** `afterEvents.entityDie` with a player as the damaging entity. Things that aren't mobs (armor stands, townsfolk NPCs, end crystals, boats, minecarts, paintings, item frames, leash knots) never make an entry.
- **Places, rain and thunder:** every 4 seconds (one in 10 players every 8 ticks, so they're spread out) each player's dimension, height and distance from world spawn are checked, plus one `getTopmostBlock` and two `getBlock` lookups for biomes (and a climb through the water over a sea bed, also for a diver standing on it). A player still on the same block only gets the rain and thunder check. The deepest, highest and farthest are saved with the next entry, within 30 seconds, or when the player leaves. Weather comes from `weatherChange` and is saved as `journal:weather`.
- **Fish:** a fishing hook belongs to the nearest player when it appears. A catch is an item that appears within 2 blocks of the hook while it's reeled in (the hook goes within 4 ticks of the item appearing), from a hook that was in water and out for at least 1.5 seconds, the same check as [Skills](#skills--skills_bp). An item that appears at a player's head (dropped, not caught) never counts, so dropping a fish next to your hook doesn't add it.
- **Other packs** add entries with `realm:journal` `{ player, page, entry, label }` (pages `mobs`, `places`, `fish`, `weather`, `relics`, `story`, `wanderers`). Those that aren't in `config.js` show under `Also found (N)`: up to 100 per page, the newest kept (the oldest goes to make room, also when the journal nears its save limit). One that went to make room and is found again comes back quietly, without another `Journal: New entry` note (the journal remembers the last 100 dropped per page). The pack also listens to `realm:sky_event` (only kinds on the Weather page) and `realm:moon` (`blood`, `harvest`: everyone in the overworld).
- Finishing a page adds the levels, adds Crowns to the `crowns` scoreboard and sends `realm:title_unlock` `{ player, title, from: "journal_bp" }`.

## Fishing 2.0 — `fishing_bp`

Every fish you catch with a rod is one of 40 species, from the common Atlantic Cod to the legendary Old Whiskers, with a size in cm. By default the fish itself stays a plain cod, salmon, tropical fish or pufferfish so every catch stacks, while your log, the records and Old Tobin remember the species and size. Which species bite depends on the weather, the time of day and the water you fish in (ocean, river, frozen water, swamp, jungle or cave). Your fish log keeps your personal bests, the realm keeps the biggest fish of each species, and every Sunday evening there's a fishing tournament with Crowns for the top three. Old Tobin the fisherman, from [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp), buys your fish.

### How to use

1. Fish with a rod as usual. When a cod, salmon, tropical fish or pufferfish comes up, it's a species: chat says `You caught a Storm Eel (82 cm)!`, with `New realm record!`, `Personal best!` or `New species for your log (12/40).` when it is one.
2. Fish in different places and weathers to find more: some only bite in thunderstorms, at night, at dawn, in caves, in frozen water, in swamps or in the jungle.
3. Run `/realm:fishing` for the fishing menu: **Fish log**, **Realm records**, **Make my fish stackable** and **Fishing settings** (operators also get **Start a tournament now**).
4. **Fish log** (or `/realm:fishing_log`) shows how many species you've caught out of 40, how many of each and your biggest. Species you haven't caught yet show as `???` with a hint, like `??? (Rare: thunderstorms)`. **Realm records** (or `/realm:fishing_top`) shows the realm's biggest fish of each species and who caught them.
5. All your fish stack, whatever the species or rarity: by default every catch (common, rare, a personal best or a legendary) is a plain cod, salmon, tropical fish or pufferfish, so a whole fishing trip takes one stack per kind (up to 64). Each catch still rolls its own species and size for chat (`You caught a Moonscale Cod (88 cm)!`), your fish log, the realm records and the tournament, and your **basket** remembers it so Old Tobin pays the full rarity and size price for every fish in the stack. Fish with a species name (caught with **Separate named items per species** enabled, or before version 1.1.5) are turned into plain fish, with their value kept, the next time the fish reaches your inventory or you open **Sell fish**. **Make my fish stackable** (or `/realm:fishing_stack`) does it on request.
6. In **Fishing settings** (or `/realm:prefs` → **Fishing 2.0**), enable **Separate named items per species** (disabled by default) to get a colored, named fish per species that stacks only with its own species, or enable **Only measure notable catches** to get a named fish only for a new species, a personal best or a realm record. Either way, every catch still counts in your log, the records and the tournament.
7. Join the weekly tournament (Sundays at 18:00 UTC, for an hour): the biggest fish for its kind wins. Chat tells everyone 10 minutes before and when it starts.
8. Sell your fish: tap Old Tobin (or any NPC with the `fisher` role) and pick **Sell fish**. **Fish records** there shows the realm's records. Fishers buy your plain fish stacks at the price of the catches in your basket (a shiny Moonscale Cod pays its Rare price, a big fish more than a small one, best catches first); plain fish with no catch behind them count as the common species of their kind (Atlantic Cod, Silver Salmon, Clownfish, Pufferfish) at its average size. Named species fish are bought too. **Sell fish** first turns named fish into plain ones (with their value kept) unless you enabled **Separate named items per species**.
9. **Operators:** **Start a tournament now** in the menu, or `/realm:fishing_tournament`, starts one. `/realm:config` → **Fishing 2.0** switches the species and the tournament, sets the tournament's day, hour and length, and whether legendary catches are announced. The species themselves are the `species` list in `config.js`.

### What players see

- **A catch:** by default the fish that flies out of the water stays a plain vanilla fish, and chat names what it was (`You caught a Moonscale Cod (88 cm)!`). With **Separate named items per species** enabled, the fish is named after its species in its rarity's color (white Common, green Uncommon, blue Rare, purple Epic, gold Legendary), with two lore lines that are the same for every fish of that species: the species' average size (`<avg> cm`, like `90 cm`) and its rarity (`Common catch`). That is why fish of the same species stack automatically, up to 64. The exact size the catch rolled (`82 cm`) is what chat, your fish log, the realm records and the tournament use. Only cod, salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish change; junk and treasure stay as they are. A cod becomes one of the cod species, a salmon one of the salmon species, and so on. Different species of the same vanilla fish don't stack with each other.
- **Plain fish (the default):** with **Separate named items per species** disabled, every fish you reel in stays a plain vanilla fish that stacks; with it enabled and **Only measure notable catches** enabled, only a new species, a personal best or a realm record comes named. Chat still says what you caught (`You caught an Atlantic Cod (54 cm)!`), and the catch still goes in your log, the records, the tournament, the Field Journal and Skills. A plain catch is also written to your basket (below), and 15 ticks later your plain fish (and, with the setting disabled, any named fish) are merged into one stack per kind.
- **Make my fish stackable** (menu, or `/realm:fishing_stack`): asks `Turn your 5 measured raw fish into plain cod, salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish that stack?`, then replaces every measured raw cod, salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish in your inventory with plain vanilla ones, merged with the plain ones you already carry into as few stacks as possible, and says `5 fish are plain now and stack.` Their species and sizes go into your basket first, so Old Tobin still pays for them. Cooked fish, renamed fish and anything this pack didn't measure are left alone. The plain fish are exactly vanilla (no name, no lore), so every species of the same fish stacks together and the [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp) market buys them too.
- **Your basket:** for each of cod, salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish, the pack keeps the species and size of up to 128 of your best catches (`fishing:basket`, a few KB at most). **Sell fish** values a plain stack of 14 cod with the 14 best entries (the rest at the common species' average size), adds Old Tobin's friend bonus and shows `Cod catch stack x14` with the Crowns, and selling uses those entries up. Fish you eat, cook or drop leave their entries in the basket until the cap pushes the cheapest out.
- **A bobber stuck near you:** Raiyon's Dynamic Lightning light blocks (`rdl:light_block*`) next to a bobber are turned back into their base block (`rdl:base`) as it spawns and every tick it lives, and a bobber that is still (under 0.05 blocks per tick) in the air within 2.5 blocks of you in the first 5 ticks of a cast gets the cast impulse again along your view direction (at most twice), so it arcs into the water.
- **Which species:** among the species of that fish that can bite right there and then, rarer ones bite less often: Common 60, Uncommon 25, Rare 10, Epic 4 and Legendary 1 (`rarities`). Sizes lean small, so fish near the top of their range are rare.
- **Conditions** (a species with several must have all of them):
  - **Weather:** clear, rain or thunderstorms, in the Overworld (elsewhere counts as clear). The Rainbow Trout only bites in the first 10 minutes after rain stops.
  - **Time:** dawn (game time 23000 to 1000), day, dusk (11500 to 13500) and night.
  - **Place**, guessed from the blocks around the bobber, since the game doesn't tell packs the biome: **ocean** when at least 70% of the water level around it, up to 16 blocks away, is water (`oceanShare`), otherwise **rivers and lakes**; **frozen water** with ice or snow nearby; **swamps** with lily pads, mangrove roots or mud; **jungle** with jungle trees or bamboo nearby; **caves** when the water is below height 50 (`caveBelowY`) with blocks over it.
- **Chat:** `You caught a Storm Eel (82 cm)!`, plus `New realm record!` (the biggest of that species yet), `Personal best!` or `New species for your log (12/40).`, and `(Tournament: 2nd)` during a tournament. A level-up sound plays for a record or a new species. When someone catches a legendary fish, everyone else sees `Alex caught a legendary Old Whiskers (164 cm)!` (`announceLegendary`).
- **The menu** (`/realm:fishing`): the tournament line, then **Fish log**, **Realm records**, **Make my fish stackable** (with how many measured raw fish you carry), **Fishing settings** (with your **Measure my catches** setting) and, for operators, **Start a tournament now**.
- **The fish log** (**Fish log**, or `/realm:fishing_log`): `Species caught: 12/40   Fish caught: 57`, the tournament line, then every species by rarity: caught ones as `Storm Eel x3, best 82 cm`, the others as `???` with their rarity and conditions. A button opens the realm records.
- **Realm records** (`/realm:fishing_top`, or **Fish records** at a fisher): each species' biggest fish, `Storm Eel: 160 cm by Alex, Oct 10, 2026`, and the tournament line: `Tournament on! Ends in 23m. Leader: ...` or `Next tournament: Sunday at 18:00 UTC (in 2d 5h).`
- **The tournament:** every week on `tournamentDay` (0 = Sunday) at `tournamentHourUtc` (18) UTC for `tournamentMinutes` (60). Chat says `A fishing tournament starts in 10m! Grab a rod.` 10 minutes before (`tournamentWarnMinutes`) and `The fishing tournament has begun! ... Prizes: 50, 30, 15 Crowns.` at the start. Each player's best fish counts, measured against its species' biggest size (an 82 cm Storm Eel is 46% of 180 cm), so a big Clownfish can beat a small Storm Eel. A tie goes to whoever caught their fish first. At the end chat lists the top three with their fish, and they get 50, 30 and 15 [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp) (`tournamentPrizes`): `+50 Crowns (Fishing tournament: 1st place)`. A winner who left before the end is paid the next time they join. If the realm was down when a tournament was due, it starts when the realm comes back, as long as it's still within the tournament's hour.
- **Selling** (tap an NPC with the `fisher` role, `npcRole`, and pick **Sell fish**): the menu lists the fish you carry with what each pays, and **Sell all**. A fish pays its rarity's price (Common 2, Uncommon 5, Rare 12, Epic 30, Legendary 80 Crowns) x (0.5 + its size / the species' biggest size), so a record-sized fish pays one and a half times the price. Chat says `+25 Crowns (Sold 3 fish)`. A species stack is priced with the size on its lore (the species' average), and the menu shows it as `Atlantic Cod 90 cm x12`. Only fish this pack named are bought: a renamed vanilla fish has no size lore. The [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp) market doesn't buy named fish.
- **Other packs:** each catch is a `fish` page entry in the [Field Journal](#field-journal--journal_bp) (`realm:journal`, the species id) and Fishing XP in [Skills](#skills--skills_bp) (5, 10, 25, 50 or 100 by rarity, `rarities`). Tournament prize winners finish a `tournament` quest for packs that count them. The tournament start is a `tournament` sky event, which the innkeepers of [Waystones & Inns](#waystones--inns--waystone_bp) remember for **Hear the news**.

| Sunburst Wrasse | Tropical fish | Rare | 15-40 | clear skies, day, ocean |
| Starlight Koi | Tropical fish | Epic | 30-80 | clear skies, night, rivers and lakes |
| Golden Koi | Tropical fish | Legendary | 40-90 | dawn, rivers and lakes |
| Pufferfish | Pufferfish | Common | 10-40 | anywhere, any time |
| Spiny Puffer | Pufferfish | Uncommon | 20-50 | ocean |
| Swamp Toadfish | Pufferfish | Uncommon | 15-35 | swamps |
| Moon Puffer | Pufferfish | Rare | 10-35 | night |
| Glacier Puffer | Pufferfish | Rare | 15-45 | frozen water |
| Stormblower | Pufferfish | Epic | 30-70 | thunderstorms |
- **Tobin's friends:** a player who is a Friend of Old Tobin ([Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)) gets 10% more Crowns for fish sold to a fisher, from `realm:affinity`.
- **Lucky Line:** a Hearthkeeper with the Lucky Line talent ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp) Callings, `bonus.luckyLine` in `realm:calling`) gets 50% more weight on rare, epic and legendary species when a fish is picked. A legendary catch is also town gossip (`realm:gossip`; at most one piece of news from this pack per in-game hour, see Town news in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:fishing` | Everyone | The fishing menu: fish log, realm records, make your fish stackable, your fishing settings, and (operators) start a tournament |
| `/realm:fishing_log` | Everyone | Your fish log: species caught out of 40, how many of each and your biggest, hints for the rest, and the tournament |
| `/realm:fishing_stack` | Everyone | Turns every measured raw fish in your inventory into plain fish that stack (asks first) |
| `/realm:fishing_top` | Everyone | The realm's biggest fish of each species, who caught it and when, and the tournament |
| `/realm:fishing_tournament` | Operators | Starts a tournament now, for the usual length (default 60 minutes, `tournamentMinutes`) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Vanilla fish caught with a rod become a species with a size and the catcher's name |
| `announceLegendary` | `true` | Tell everyone in chat when someone catches a legendary fish |
| `rarities` | Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary | `{ id, label, weight, color, price, xp }` per rarity: how often it bites (60, 25, 10, 4, 1), the name's color code, the Crowns a fisher pays before the size factor (2, 5, 12, 30, 80) and the Fishing skill XP a catch gives (5, 10, 25, 50, 100) |
| `caveBelowY` | `50` | Water below this height with blocks over it is a cave |
| `oceanShare` | `0.7` | Share of the water level around the bobber (up to 16 blocks) that must be water for the ocean; less is rivers and lakes |
| `npcRole` | `"fisher"` | The NPC role whose NPCs buy fish and show the records |
| `tournamentEnabled` | `true` | Hold the weekly tournament |
| `tournamentDay` | `0` | Its day of the week, UTC: 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday |
| `tournamentHourUtc` | `18` | The hour it starts, UTC |
| `tournamentMinutes` | `60` | How long it lasts, in minutes (10 to 180 in game) |
| `tournamentWarnMinutes` | `10` | Chat warns this many minutes before it starts (0 = no warning) |
| `tournamentPrizes` | `[50, 30, 15]` | Crowns for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place; add or remove numbers for more or fewer places |
| `species` | 40 species (above) | `{ id, name, item, rarity, min, max, weather?, time?, places?, afterRain? }`: the fish `item` it replaces, its size range in cm and its conditions: `weather` (`Clear`, `Rain`, `Thunder`), `time` (`day`, `night`, `dawn`, `dusk`), `places` (`ocean`, `river`, `frozen`, `swamp`, `jungle`, `cave`) and `afterRain` (only this many minutes after rain stops). Keep each `id` when editing: logs and records are saved by it. Keep one species without conditions for each fish item, or some catches stay vanilla |

Operators can change `enabled`, `announceLegendary`, `tournamentEnabled`, `tournamentDay`, `tournamentHourUtc` and `tournamentMinutes` in game with `/realm:config` (**Fishing 2.0**). The rest stays in `config.js`.

Player preferences, in `/realm:prefs` (**Fishing 2.0**) or the menu's **Fishing settings**:

| Preference | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| **Separate named items per species** (`measure`) | Disabled | Disabled: all caught fish (common, rare or record) stack together as plain cod, salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish, while your log, records and Old Tobin still remember every catch. Enabled: each species has its own colored name and lore |
| **Only measure notable catches** | Disabled | A catch that isn't a new species, a personal best or a realm record comes as a plain fish that stacks |

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `fishing:log` | Player | JSON `{ speciesId: [count, best cm] }`: the player's fish log |
| `fishing:basket` | Player | JSON `{ item typeId: [[speciesId, cm], ...] }`: the species and size of up to 128 best catches per fish item (cod, salmon, tropical fish, pufferfish) carried as plain fish, so a fisher pays for them |
| `fishing:records` | World | JSON `{ speciesId: [cm, name, player id, time] }`: the realm's biggest fish of each species |
| `fishing:tourney` | World | JSON `{ s, e, en }` of the running tournament: start and end times and each player's best fish `[share of the species' biggest, name, species, cm, time]`. Cleared when it ends |
| `fishing:tmeta` | World | JSON `{ last, warned }`: the scheduled tournament starts already started and warned about |
| `fishing:owed:<player id>`, `fishing:owed_idx` | World | Each offline winner's `[Crowns, note, quest id]` prize and the bounded oldest-first player index; paid on join under the [offline reward storage limits](#offline-reward-storage) |
| `fishing:owed` | World | Legacy all-player prize map, retained only for unmigrated leftovers |
| `fishing:weather` | World | The Overworld weather at the last change (`Clear`, `Rain` or `Thunder`): the stable Script API can't read the current weather |
| `fishing:rainEnd` | World | When rain last stopped (ms), for the Rainbow Trout |
| `fishing:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `fishing:pref` | Player | JSON `{ measure?, notableOnly? }`: the player's own choices, only where they differ from the default |
| `crowns` | Scoreboard | Prizes and fish sales are added to the shared Crowns balance |

### How it works

- **Catches:** there is no "caught a fish" event in the stable API, so the pack recognizes one much as [Daily Quests](#daily-quests--quests_bp) does: a fishing hook belongs to the player who cast it (its projectile owner, else the player nearest to it when it appears), and its place is followed every tick. A single unnamed cod, salmon, tropical fish or pufferfish that appears within 2 blocks of a hook, as that hook is reeled in (the hook is gone then or within 3 ticks), is that player's catch, once per hook. A fish dropped from an inventory (it appears within 1 block of a player's head), a stack of several, or a fish that turns up next to a hook still in the water is never a catch, so dropping fish next to your bobber doesn't turn them into species. Then (a tick later, so other packs like Daily Quests see the vanilla fish first) the pack spawns the named fish at the same spot with the same velocity, so it still flies to the player, and removes the vanilla one. If the player picks the vanilla fish up first, it simply stays vanilla. When the player's settings ask for a plain fish, the vanilla fish is left where it is and only the catch is recorded.
- **Stacking by species:** `fishStack` gives every fish of a species identical name and lore (`<avg> cm`, `<Rarity> catch`), so the game stacks them. 15 ticks after a catch, and when the fishing menu, **Sell fish** or **Make my fish stackable** opens, `mergeSpeciesStacks` upgrades legacy fish (`Caught by ...` lore) to that lore and merges split stacks of a species into as few stacks of up to 64 as possible. The rolled size is only used for chat, the log, the records and the tournament. The `<avg> cm` line still matches the size line that [Kitchen](#kitchen--cooking_bp) and [Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp) read, so the Storm Eel keeps working as an ingredient.
- **Making fish stackable:** the pack finds measured fish the way the sell menu does (name and lore) and plain fish of the same four kinds (ignoring renamed fish and other items), and for any kind that isn't already in full stacks it writes each measured fish's species and size to the basket (`recordInBasket`), empties those slots and adds back fresh vanilla `ItemStack`s of the total, up to 64 a stack; anything that wouldn't fit (it always should) drops at the player's feet. It runs 15 ticks after a plain catch, when **Sell fish** opens (unless **Separate named items per species** is on) and from **Make my fish stackable**. The log and the records were written when the fish was caught.
- **Place:** one scan per catch, about 100 block reads: the water surface at the bobber, 48 samples at the water level 4 to 16 blocks around it (and the blocks above the nearer ones, for lily pads and snow), and the highest block of 12 columns 6 and 12 blocks away for trees and snow. Weather comes from `afterEvents.weatherChange` (whose `dimension` is `overworld` on current servers, `minecraft:overworld` on older ones; both count), saved so it survives a restart. Time of day is `world.getTimeOfDay()`.
- **Fish are recognized** for selling by their name (a known species in a rarity color) and their lore (`<size> cm`, then `<Rarity> catch`, or `Caught by ...` on fish from before 1.1.4), which an anvil can't add, or as plain unnamed cod, salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish, priced from the basket. The sell menu checks each slot again before taking the fish.
- **The tournament clock** checks every 5 seconds; the running tournament is saved, so it survives a restart and is finished on schedule. Prizes go into the `crowns` scoreboard; winners get `realm:quest_done` with `kind: "tournament"`.
- **Fishers:** on `realm:npc_talk` with the `fisher` role the pack answers `realm:npc_offer` with **Sell fish** (`order` 20) and **Fish records** (21).
- Events sent: `realm:journal` `{ page: "fish", entry: <species id> }` and `realm:skill_xp` `{ skill: "fishing" }` on every catch, `realm:quest_done` `{ kind: "tournament" }` for prize winners, `realm:sky_event` `{ kind: "tournament" }` at the start.

---

## Kitchen — `cooking_bp`

Cook real dishes at a cooking pot (a cauldron over a lit campfire). Each dish is a food with a gentle, long-lasting buff when you eat it, like Haste I for 5 minutes or Night Vision for 10, and a few rolling dishes roll for a surprise instead: mostly a good buff, sometimes something silly. Everyone knows 6 basic recipes; Bea the Cook (from [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)) teaches more in her **Kitchen** for Crowns or ingredients, and the best dishes need rare ingredients like the Champion's Heart, dropped by [Champions](#champions--elite_bp), or the Storm Eel of [Fishing 2.0](#fishing-20--fishing_bp). There are 27 recipes and 8 rare ingredients.

### How to use

1. Build a cooking pot: put a cauldron on top of a lit campfire (or soul campfire). Water in the cauldron is optional.
2. Tap the cauldron with an empty hand, or sneak and tap it with anything. The `Cooking Pot` menu lists the recipes you know, the ones you have everything for first (`Ready: 2 servings`), the others with what's missing (`Missing: 1 Kelp`).
3. Pick a recipe to see its ingredients and effects, then **Cook 1 batch** or **Cook 3 batches**. The ingredients are taken, the pot bubbles for 3 seconds, and the dishes land in your inventory: `You cooked 2 Miner's Pasty.`
4. Eat a dish like any food (when you're hungry). Chat says what you got: `Miner's Pasty: Haste I for 5m`. A rolling dish says what it rolled: `Mystery Stew: A rush of speed! (Speed II for 2m)`.
5. Learn more recipes: tap Bea the Cook (or any NPC with the `chef` role) and pick **Kitchen**. She teaches each recipe for Crowns or for ingredients (`Learn: Warden's Ration` for `30 Crowns or 8 Cooked Beef`), and the rare ones for one of their rare ingredient plus Crowns. Story Questlines also teaches recipes, and recipe cards (paper named `Recipe Card: Lantern Cake`) dropped by champions teach theirs as soon as you open a pot, the Kitchen or `/realm:cooking`.
6. Collect rare ingredients: defeat champions, catch a Storm Eel in a thunderstorm, harvest full beehives at night, and harvest crops during a Harvest Moon or after an aurora or a meteor, and hunt monsters under a Blood Moon (see the table below). When one of those windows opens, chat says so: `Stardust settles on the fields. Ripe wheat harvested in the next 15 minutes may give Starwright Flour (Kitchen).` `/realm:cooking` → **Rare ingredients** lists them, what they're for and how many you carry.
7. Run `/realm:cooking` for your recipes (**What can I cook?**, **My recipes**), the **Cookbook** of every recipe and how to learn it, and the rare ingredients. Disable the bubbling sounds in `/realm:prefs` → **Kitchen** → **Cooking sounds**.
8. **Operators:** `/realm:cooking` also has **Teach or forget recipes** (one or all, for any online player) and **Give dishes and ingredients** (any dish, rare ingredient or recipe card). `/realm:config` → **Kitchen** sets the effect length multiplier, rolling dishes, the champion ingredient and recipe card chances, foraging and cooking anywhere.

### What players see

- **The cooking pot:** any cauldron with a lit `campfire` or `soul_campfire` right under it (`potFires`). An empty-hand tap or a sneak-tap opens the menu; a tap with a bucket or bottle without sneaking fills or empties the cauldron as usual (to use a bucket on a pot, don't sneak). A pot in someone else's [land claim](#land-claims--claims_bp) is only for that claim's players: anyone else's tap is refused (`This land is claimed by Sam`). With `cookAnywhere` on, the recipe pages of `/realm:cooking` have the cook buttons too.
- **Cooking** takes `cookSeconds` (3) for any number of batches, up to `maxBatch` (16) at once: smoke rises from the pot, it bubbles (`bubble.pop`, if **Cooking sounds** is on) and ends with happy-villager sparkles and a ding. One cooking at a time per player. If you walk away the dish still goes to your inventory (or drops at your feet when it's full); if you leave the game, it drops at the pot, or, when nobody is near the pot to keep it loaded, it waits for you and lands in your inventory when you next join (`You cooked 10 Miner's Pasty.`).
- **Ingredients:** a plain ingredient (`Wheat`, `Cooked Beef`) only counts items without a custom name, so cooking never uses up a named dish or fish. A rare ingredient counts only the real thing (its name and its `Rare ingredient` lore with the line saying where it comes from). Honey-Glazed Ham gives back the glass bottle.
- **A dish** is the vanilla food item named after the dish, in plain text without color codes (`Harbor Chowder` is a `minecraft:rabbit_stew` named exactly `Harbor Chowder`), with lore: a gray line about it (`Warm and salty, like the docks at dawn`), its effects in blue with their base length (`Water Breathing I (8:00)`) or `Rolls for a surprise`, and `Kitchen dish` (gray) or `Rare dish` (gold). Servings of the same dish always have the same lore, so they stack like the food they are (stews and soups don't stack, as in vanilla, and give back their bowl when eaten). A dish cooked since this update ends its lore with a dark gray `Dish: <name>`, so Story Questlines can tell it from a rare dish renamed to another rare dish of the same food; older dishes lack that line and are still accepted there. An older serving gets the line (and the dish's current lore) as soon as it lands in a player's inventory (picked up, taken from a chest or moved) and once when they join, so it stacks with new servings again; the item, amount and name stay, and a line another pack added at the end (a Silly Enchant) is kept. Servings still in a chest change when someone takes them. An anvil-renamed food is not a dish (anvils can't add lore), and neither is a dish renamed to another dish: the first lore line must be that dish's own.
- **Eating:** the effects are added without particles. Lengths are multiplied by **Effect durations** (`durationMultiplier`, 1x) except Saturation, Levitation and Nausea. An effect never makes one you already have weaker or shorter, so eating the same dish twice doesn't stack the time; eating it when the effect is running low tops it up. The lore always shows the base length; chat shows the real one. Like any food, a dish can only be eaten when you're hungry (in survival).
- **Rolling dishes** (Mystery Stew, Hiccup Cookies, Gambler's Goulash) roll one result: Speed II 2 min (weight 12), Strength I 3 min (10), Haste II 2 min (10), Regeneration I 40s (10), Absorption II 4 min (8), Jump Boost II and Slow Falling 2 min (8), Night Vision 10 min (8), Hero of the Village 10 min (4), the jackpot `JACKPOT! Everything at once!` (Strength, Speed and Absorption 4 min and Regeneration 30s, weight 3), or something silly: floating up for 3 seconds with Slow Falling to land softly (5), Nausea for 8 seconds (4), sparkles all over for 15 seconds (5), six hiccup hops (5), or a burp everyone within 16 blocks hears about (`Alex burps loudly.`, 4). Hiccup Cookies double the silly weights; Gambler's Goulash has 0.3x the silly weights and triple the jackpot. With **Rolling dishes** disabled (`rollingDishes`) they give their plain effect instead (table below).
- **Bea's Kitchen** (tap an NPC with the `chef` role, `chefRole`, and pick **Kitchen**): Bea says a line (`Bea: "Hungry? Of course you are. Sit, sit!"`), how many recipes you know and your Crowns, then a **Learn: <dish>** button for each recipe she teaches that you don't know yet with its prices, **What can I cook?** and **Rare ingredients**. Picking a recipe shows each way to pay (`Pay 30 Crowns`, `Pay 8 Cooked Beef`); one you can't afford is gray. Paying teaches it: `New recipe: Warden's Ration! (taught by Bea)`.
- **Recipe cards** drop from champions (`recipeCardChance`, 10%, killer only), one of the recipes marked "recipe card" below, at random. Opening a pot, the Kitchen or `/realm:cooking` with a card for a recipe you don't know teaches it and uses up the card; a card for a recipe you know stays, to give to someone else. Each card names its recipe in its lore (`Recipe: Lantern Cake`), so a card renamed on an anvil teaches nothing; its last lore line says `Works anywhere in your inventory`.
- **Champions** (`realm:champion_slain`): the killer has a 60% chance (`championDropChance`) of a Champion's Heart, the same chance of its trait's ingredient (Stormcaller: Storm Eel, Frostbound: Frost Pepper, Vampiric: Moon Salt) and of an Ember Truffle when it died in the Nether; each helper has half the chance of a Champion's Heart. They go straight into your inventory: `Rare ingredient: Champion's Heart (Gerald the Stormcaller)`.
- **Other packs:** each serving cooked gives 3 Farming XP in [Skills](#skills--skills_bp) (`skillXp`).
