Foraging (everything but champions) can be disabled with **Foraging** (`foragingEnabled`). Harvesting counts both ways: breaking a ripe crop, or tapping it with [Right-click Harvest](#right-click-harvest--harvest_bp). At the start of an aurora or meteor window, a Harvest Moon or a Blood Moon, chat names the ingredient it can bring: `Kitchen: ripe crops harvested tonight may give Harvest Saffron.`, `Kitchen: monsters slain tonight may drop Moon Salt.`
- **Bea's friends:** a player who is a Friend of Bea ([Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)) pays 10% fewer Crowns to learn a recipe (rounded down), from `realm:affinity`.
- **Hearty Dishes:** a Hearthkeeper with the Hearty Dishes talent ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp) Callings, `bonus.dishPct` in `realm:calling`) gets dish effects 25% longer, on top of `durationMultiplier` (not the effects that never scale).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:cooking` | Everyone | The Kitchen menu: what you can cook now, your recipes, the cookbook (every recipe, its ingredients, effects and how to learn it) and the rare ingredients you carry. Operators also teach or forget recipes and give dishes, ingredients and recipe cards |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Dishes give their effects when eaten. When `false` they are plain food |
| `durationMultiplier` | `1` | Every dish effect's length is multiplied by this (0.25 to 4 in game), except Saturation, Levitation and Nausea |
| `rollingDishes` | `true` | Rolling dishes roll on the surprise table; when `false` they give their plain effect |
| `championDropChance` | `60` | Percent chance that a champion's killer gets a Champion's Heart, and the same for its trait's ingredient; helpers get half this chance of a heart |
| `recipeCardChance` | `10` | Percent chance that a champion's killer also gets a recipe card |
| `foragingEnabled` | `true` | Rare ingredients from harvesting, beehives and hunting (the chances below). Champions drop them either way |
| `forage.glowHoney` | `30` | Percent: Glow Honey from a full beehive or bee nest harvested at night |
| `forage.starwrightFlour` | `25` | Percent: Starwright Flour from ripe wheat soon after an aurora or a meteor |
| `forage.harvestSaffron` | `8` | Percent: Harvest Saffron from a ripe crop during a Harvest Moon |
| `forage.moonSalt` | `8` | Percent: Moon Salt from a hostile mob killed during a Blood Moon |
| `forage.emberTruffle` | `3` | Percent: Ember Truffle from ripe nether wart |
| `forage.frostPepper` | `4` | Percent: Frost Pepper from a stray |
| `starMinutes` | `15` | After an aurora or a meteor, ripe wheat can give Starwright Flour for this many minutes |
| `potFires` | `["minecraft:campfire", "minecraft:soul_campfire"]` | Blocks that make a cauldron on top of them a cooking pot (lit ones only) |
| `cookAnywhere` | `false` | Players can cook from `/realm:cooking` anywhere, without a pot |
| `cookSeconds` | `3` | How long one cooking takes, in seconds, for any number of batches |
| `maxBatch` | `16` | Most batches cooked at once |
| `chefRole` | `"chef"` | The NPC role whose townsfolk open the Kitchen (Bea the Cook has it) |
| `chefName` | `"Bea the Cook"` | Who teaches recipes, in menus |
| `skillXp` | `3` | Farming XP (Skills pack) per serving cooked; `0` = none |

The dishes, rare ingredients, champion trait ingredients and the rolling table are in `scripts/recipes.js` (`DISHES`, `INGREDIENTS`, `TRAIT_INGREDIENT`, `ROLLS`): `{ id, name, base, tier, yield, needs, effects, blurb, learn?, card?, returns?, roll? }` per dish, where `needs` are `[item id, count]` (`"ing:<id>"` for a rare ingredient), `effects` are `[effect id, amplifier, seconds]` and `learn` the ways Bea teaches it (`{ crowns?, items? }`, any one). Keep the ids and names of existing dishes: players' recipes are saved by id, and stories use the names.

Operators can change `enabled`, `durationMultiplier`, `rollingDishes`, `championDropChance`, `recipeCardChance`, `foragingEnabled` and `cookAnywhere` in game with `/realm:config` (**Kitchen**). Each player can disable **Cooking sounds** in `/realm:prefs` (**Kitchen**). The rest stays in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `cooking:known` | Player | JSON `[recipe id]`: the recipes the player learned (the 6 basics aren't saved; everyone knows them) |
| `cooking:stats` | Player | JSON `{ c, e }`: servings cooked and dishes eaten, shown in `/realm:cooking` |
| `cooking:pending:<player id>`, `cooking:pending_idx` | World | Recipe ids taught to each offline player and the bounded oldest-first player index; learned on join under the [offline reward storage limits](#offline-reward-storage) |
| `cooking:pending` | World | Legacy all-player recipe map, retained only for unmigrated leftovers |
| `cooking:moon` | World | JSON `{ s, t, a }`: the Blood or Harvest Moon announced by `realm:moon`, when (ms) and the game tick it rose (`a`); forgotten a game day (24000 ticks) after it rose, or when it sets. Game time stands still while the realm is closed, so a moon still up after a restart keeps its window |
| `cooking:owed:<player id>`, `cooking:owed_idx` | World | Each cook's `{ dish id: batches }` owed servings, from when the pot starts until delivery, plus the bounded oldest-first player index. A cook who leaves gets them on return (a batch still in the pot when they come back is handed over when the pot is done, not early: before 1.1.15 a cook started in a player's first 5 seconds online, or the world's, was handed over at once); only failed delivery parts are re-owed. When the pot finishes, only the dishes that really came off this list are handed over: if that save fails, they stay owed for the next join instead of being paid twice. A save that fails after the value was written counts as saved (since 1.1.16), so neither the pot's start nor the join's keep of a batch still in the pot pays it a second time. See the [storage limits and crash boundary](#offline-reward-storage), not an unconditional exactly-once guarantee |
| `cooking:owed` | World | Legacy all-player dish map; unknown or oversized migration leftovers stay here |
| `cooking:star` | World | When the last aurora or meteor was announced (ms), for Starwright Flour |
| `cooking:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `cooking:pref` | Player | The player's **Cooking sounds** choice |
| `crowns` | Scoreboard | Bea's lessons are paid from the shared Crowns balance |

### How it works

- **Pots:** `beforeEvents.playerInteractWithBlock` on a `minecraft:cauldron` whose block below is a lit `potFires` block (its `extinguished` state isn't set), with an empty hand or while sneaking, is canceled and opens the menu on the next tick (once per tap, `isFirstEvent`).
- **Eating:** `afterEvents.itemCompleteUse` from a player with an item that is a dish (its type is the dish's `base`, its name without § codes is the dish's name, and its first lore line is that dish's gray line). The vanilla food points are the base item's.
- **Foraging:** `afterEvents.playerBreakBlock` on ripe crops (`growth` 7) and nether wart (`age` 3), plus a first tap (`beforeEvents.playerInteractWithBlock`) on a ripe one that 3 ticks later is unripe, or air still on farmland (soul sand for nether wart), so Right-click Harvest replanted or removed it (a crop broken in those ticks counts once, through the break; one trampled off farmland doesn't count); `afterEvents.entityDie` with a player as the damaging entity; full hives (`honey_level` 5) tapped with a glass bottle or shears, checked a tick later (the hive must have emptied). Scripts can't read the moon or the sky, so the pack remembers the last `realm:moon` (`{ state: "blood" | "harvest" | "normal" }` from [Blood Moon & Harvest Moon](#blood-moon--harvest-moon--moon_bp)) and `realm:sky_event` with `kind` `aurora` ([Aurora & Shooting Stars](#aurora--shooting-stars--night_bp)) or `meteor` ([Meteor Strikes](#meteor-strikes--meteor_bp)).
- **Townsfolk:** on `realm:npc_talk` with the `chef` role the pack answers `realm:npc_offer` with **Kitchen** (`order` 15), and opens it on `realm:npc_choose`.
- **Script events it listens to** (JSON; other packs and `/scriptevent` can send them):
  - `realm:champion_slain` `{ player?, helpers, name, trait, dim, ... }` from Champions: rare ingredients and recipe cards.
  - `realm:recipe_learn` `{ player, recipe }`: teaches a recipe, by id (`starwright_bread`) or name (`Starwright Bread`; case, spaces and punctuation ignored). A player who is offline learns it when they next join. Story Questlines sends it when a chapter that asks for a story recipe starts (Lantern Cake, Starwright Bread in Hearth and Table).
  - `realm:dish_give` `{ player, dish, amount? }` and `realm:ingredient_give` `{ player, ingredient, amount? }`: give real dishes or rare ingredients (by id or name), with the right lore. Stories that reward a dish should use these (or give the item with the dish's `base`, exact name and any lore).
  - `realm:cooking_cook` `{ player, recipe, times? }`: cooks a known recipe at the player's position from what they carry, like the pot (for tests and automation).
  - `realm:cooking_eat` `{ player, dish }`: gives a dish's effects as if eaten, without an item (for tests).
  - `realm:cooking_owed_ping` `{}`: answered with `realm:cooking_owed` `{ players, batches }`, what is owed right now (for tests).
- Events sent: `realm:npc_offer` (above) and `realm:skill_xp` `{ skill: "farming" }` for each cooking.

---

## Deck of Many Things — `domt_bp`

Draw a card from the Deck of Many Things for a random effect: 132 cards, from a stack of bread or an hour of night vision to a lightning strike, a sky arena, a champion on your heels, a trip to the Nether or, once in a hundred draws, a wish or the Fates' coin flip. The deck is dangerous: bad cards hurt, and a few can kill you if you don't move fast. Good cards are worth it, and their effects last a long time (15 minutes to an hour, some until you die). Most cards are common (79), some are a real treat or a real threat (36 uncommon), a few are big swings (15 rare) and two are legendary. 15 more **wild cards** (swap places with another player, the floor is lava, a warden...) wait switched off until an operator turns them on. Everyone draws, with a cooldown between draws, or, if an operator sets it up that way, only operators draw, for themselves or for any player.

### How to use

1. Run `/realm:domt` and pick **Draw a card**. The deck shuffles, the card's name shows on screen in its rarity's color, and chat says what it does, like `[Deck] You drew The Merchant (Uncommon): A wandering trader appears with wares to sell.`
2. Read the card and react: `Look up!`, `RUN!` or a countdown above the hotbar means you have a second or a few to get out of the way.
3. Then the deck rests: you can draw again after 20 real minutes. **My draws** shows your last cards and when you can draw next.
4. **The odds** lists every card and the chance of each rarity: Common 70%, Uncommon 20%, Rare 9%, Legendary 1% by default. Gray cards are switched off, and a purple `*` marks a wild card.
5. If you draw **The Wish**, choose one of the three boons it offers. If you close the window, the wish waits: **Make your wish** is at the top of `/realm:domt` until you choose.
6. **Operators:** `/realm:domt_draw <player>` draws for a player (no cooldown), and **Draw for a player** in the menu can pick the card too. **Cards on/off** (or `/realm:domt_effects`) switches each card on or off, a page per rarity, plus a **Wild cards** page and buttons to enable or disable every wild card at once. **Reset a cooldown** lets a player draw again at once. `/realm:config` → **Deck of Many Things** sets who draws (everyone with a cooldown, or operators only), the cooldown, the rarity weights, whether rare draws are announced, whether block-changing cards are allowed and how long The Spore lasts.

### What players see

- **The draw:** three page turns with enchanting sparkles and `The deck shuffles...` above the hotbar, then the card's name as a title, in white (Common), green (Uncommon), aqua (Rare) or light purple (Legendary), with a sound and particles to match. Chat gives the card's line, and sometimes a second gray line with details (`You landed at 812, 71, -340.`, `It is a husk, 8 blocks to the west.`).
- **A card that can't happen where you are** (no open sky for The Sky or Anvil Drop, no creature to swap with, no wild ground for mushrooms, a safe zone for a block-changing card) says `The Merchant crumbles to dust: it can't happen here. The deck draws again...` and another card is drawn, up to 5 times. If nothing works, your cooldown is given back.
- **Rare and legendary draws** are told to everyone in chat (`announceRare`), like `[Deck] Alex drew The Gate and fell into the Nether!`. So are The Storm, The Sun and The Warden.
- **Danger:** the bad cards are meant to hurt. The Sky throws you 14 to 22 blocks up with nothing to slow your fall (a second and a half after `The ground lets go of you...`): land in water, or take the fall damage. Up, Up floats you about 6 blocks up and lets you drop. Smite and Doom call lightning onto you (5 damage a strike, and it sets you on fire; any fire it lights on blocks is put out at once, so builds never burn, while a fire that was already burning there, like a fireplace, is left alone). Anvil Drop drops an anvil from up to 8 blocks above your head about a second after `Look up!`: step aside, or take up to about 7 hearts of damage (it needs solid ground under you, so it fizzles in water or while you fly). The anvil is removed about 8 seconds after it drops (within 10 seconds of a restart, or once its chunk loads again), and only if an anvil (plain, chipped or damaged) is still where it landed, so an anvil a player placed is never taken; a flower or grass it landed on comes back. Lit Fuse explodes where you stood 4 seconds later (`RUN! 4...`), hard enough to kill anyone still standing on it, but it breaks no blocks. Reaper's Touch and The Reaper drop you to half a heart, Glass Cannon to two hearts, Withering and Nightshade can poison you to death, and Hiss puts a creeper right behind you. Poison II from Sour Berry stops at half a heart, as poison does.
- **Teleports** that aren't meant to hurt (The Hop, The Wanderer, The Void, The Comet, The Gate) land you on a full block with two open blocks above, never in lava, water, fire or a wall, only in loaded chunks, and near your own height first (so a card drawn in a cave keeps you in caves). The far ones (The Comet, The Gate) hold you high in the air with Slow Falling and Resistance for a moment while the place loads (with a ticking area for a few seconds if it loads slowly), then land you; an ocean or lava sea makes them try up to 3 other places nearby, and if none is safe, you are put back and the deck draws again. If you leave the game (or the server restarts) while you're held in the air, you're put back where you drew the card when you join.
- **Who The Void swaps you with:** never a pet (a tamed wolf, cat, horse...), a named or leashed mob, a ridden mount or a villager.
- **Dropped things stay in sight:** Butterfingers drops your item a few blocks away where you can see it (at your feet in a narrow tunnel). The Magpie drops its stack 8 to 16 blocks away in sight, and fizzles where there's no such spot. Neither ever takes a locked item (such as the Realm Configuration item), The Hex never curses one, and The Juggler and Chaos Pockets leave an item locked in its slot where it is.
- **Long effects:** status effects from good cards last 15 minutes to an hour (Night Vision an hour, Health Boost 30 minutes, Haste 20 minutes); bad ones 1 to 15 minutes (Blindness and Nausea 1 minute, Slowness and Weakness 15 minutes). Guardian Angel (Resistance) and The Albatross (Slowness) last until you die, or until you drink milk (6 hours at most).
- **Mobs** appear on safe spots around you, 2 to 14 blocks away and near your own height (at your feet when there is no room, as on a small sky platform; Hiss puts its creeper right behind you). Wolves and the horse are already tamed to you.
- **Skill XP** cards (The Mentor, The Archmage) send XP to a random skill through the [Skills](#skills--skills_bp) pack; without it, that part does nothing.
- **Crowns** cards add to or take from the `crowns` scoreboard, never below 0, with or without the [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp) pack.
- **The Rainbow** cycles your name above your head through rainbow colors for 20 minutes, then puts it back. If Nicknames or AFK change your name meanwhile, the rainbow stops and leaves theirs. The wild card Cursed Name works the same way with a silly red name (`Sir Bonks-a-Lot`, `Captain Soggy`...).
- **The rare cards:**
  - **The Gate:** to the Nether (near your Overworld position divided by 8), or out of it to the Overworld, on a safe spot, with 5 minutes of Fire Resistance, 10 obsidian and a flint and steel to build a portal home. Not in the End.
  - **The Arena:** in the Overworld, a 15 by 15 platform appears about 24 blocks above you, or above the ground over your head (only where that space is completely empty), walled with invisible barriers, and you fight three husks, a vindicator and a pillager for up to 2 minutes. Win for an enchanted book and 15 Crowns. Win, lose or run out of time, you're sent back where you were and every arena block is removed. The arena's blocks can't be mined while it stands. If the server restarts mid-fight, the arena is removed within 10 minutes, its leftover mobs vanish within 10 seconds, and you're sent back when you join.
  - **The Champion:** a champion monster appears 6 to 10 blocks away, where you can see it (within 3 blocks of your height, nothing solid in between), and chat says what it is and which way (`It is a skeleton, 9 blocks to the north-east.`). With the [Champions](#champions--elite_bp) pack it's one of theirs (`realm:champion_spawn`, a zombie, husk, skeleton, stray or witch named `the Deck's Champion`); without it, or if no champion shows up within 1.5 seconds, the deck sends its own: `The Deck's Champion`, a vindicator with extra health, Strength and Resistance. If the champion is gone 3 seconds later without being killed, the deck sends its own instead (`The champion slipped away, so the deck sends its own...`). Only one champion ever comes: if the deck sent its own and the Champions pack's turns up late after all, the late one is removed.
  - **The Spore:** in the Overworld, wild grass and dirt within 9 blocks turns to mycelium, with a few red and brown mushrooms and two mooshrooms, for 60 minutes (`sporeMinutes`). It only changes the top block of open ground with nothing on it, and fizzles if it sees anything built or farmed within 13 blocks (planks, glass, bricks, farmland, paths, torches, fences, chests and the like). When time is up, every block it changed that is still mycelium or its mushroom goes back to what was there (and mycelium that spread around the field turns back to grass); anything a player built meanwhile stays. Bedrock scripts can't change biomes, so the grass color and mob spawning stay as they were.
  - **The Eclipse:** the time jumps to midnight for everyone.
  - **The Horde:** 5 zombies, 2 husks, 3 skeletons, 2 spiders and a vindicator, 8 to 14 blocks around you.
  - **Doom:** a countdown above your hotbar (`Doom: 3 more strikes (60s)`), and lightning strikes wherever you stand 20, 40 and 60 seconds after the draw.
  - **The Evoker**, **The Reaper**, **The Titan**, **Mother Lode**, **The Archmage**, **The Knight**, **Second Chance** and **The Gamble:** see the card table.
- **The legendary cards:**
  - **The Wish:** fireworks, a totem burst and a dragon's growl for everyone, then a choice of three boons drawn from eight: an enchanted netherite pickaxe (`Worldbreaker`) or sword (`Kingslayer`), an elytra with 64 rockets, 30 levels, 500 Crowns, an enchanted trident (`The Tide`) with a Heart of the Sea, a beacon with 9 iron blocks, or full diamond armor with Protection IV. Nothing is destroyed and nobody is hurt.
  - **The Fates:** a coin flip. Heads: full health, then Health Boost V, Strength II, Resistance II, Regeneration, Speed and Fire Resistance for an hour. Tails: half a heart, and 4 zombies, 3 skeletons and 2 vindicators on their way.
- **Wild cards** (off until an operator switches them on): see their table. The Swap tells the other player who swapped with them, and fizzles when nobody else is in your dimension or when either of you is in a Deck arena or by an [Expeditions](#expeditions--expedition_bp) dungeon (its mobs or pets within 64 blocks); Hot Potato (its lore says `Goes off anywhere in your inventory`) shows its countdown to whoever carries it and, at zero, explodes on whoever has it (or where it lies), hard enough to leave an unarmored player at half a heart, without breaking blocks; Chicken Rain's chickens are removed after 3 minutes (even across a restart: leftovers go when their chunk loads again); Zero G spares tamed and named mobs and other packs' characters.
- **Safe zones:** block-changing cards (The Arena, The Spore, Anvil Drop, Hiss, Hot Headed, and the wild Creeper Party and The Ghast) never work inside a safe zone from the `realm:zones` protocol (Safe Zones, towns, land claims that share theirs), or close enough to one for a blast or a fireball to reach it; they fizzle there and the deck draws again. Operators can also disable block-changing cards altogether (`blockCards`). Explosions from Lit Fuse and Hot Potato never break blocks, but they do knock down armor stands and paintings, so Lit Fuse fizzles within 8 blocks of a safe zone and a Hot Potato that goes off in one just pops harmlessly. Lightning's fire is put out, so Smite and Doom work anywhere, but within 8 blocks of a safe zone they call no real bolt (it would turn villagers into witches and pigs into piglins): you take the same hit and catch fire, with thunder and sparks.
- **What a card leaves behind:** nothing it doesn't mean to. The arena and the mushroom field are undone on time, Anvil Drop's anvil goes after about 8 seconds, lightning's fire is put out, Chicken Rain's chickens leave after 3 minutes, and a Hot Potato still in an inventory or on the ground after a restart is quietly removed when its holder joins or its chunk loads (it never goes off late). All of these survive a restart. On purpose, these stay: the mobs a card summons (hostile ones despawn like any other when nobody is near; tamed wolves, the horse, sheep, mooshrooms and the trader stay as vanilla ones do), the items it gives, and the holes Hiss's creeper and The Ghast's fireballs blow in the ground (that's the danger of those cards, which never work near a safe zone).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:domt` | Everyone | Opens the deck: **Draw a card** (once every 20 minutes, `cooldownMinutes`), **My draws**, **The odds**, and **Make your wish** when one is waiting; operators also get **Draw for a player**, **Cards on/off** and **Reset a cooldown** |
| `/realm:domt_draw <player>` | Operators | Draws a random card for the players picked (`@a` works), with no cooldown. If a player's last card is still running, it says so (`Alex is still drawing a card. Wait for it to finish.`) |
| `/realm:domt_effects` | Operators | Switches each of the 147 cards on or off, a page per rarity and a page of wild cards (saved in the world); the 15 wild cards start disabled |

With **Who draws** set to **Operators only** (`mode` `operators`), only operators can draw, with no cooldown; everyone else can still see their draws and the odds.

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `"cooldown"` | `"cooldown"`: everyone draws, once every `cooldownMinutes`. `"operators"`: only operators draw (no cooldown), for themselves or for any player |
| `cooldownMinutes` | `20` | Real minutes between a player's draws in `"cooldown"` mode. `0` = no cooldown |
| `weights.common` | `70` | How likely a common card is, relative to the other weights |
| `weights.uncommon` | `20` | How likely an uncommon card is |
| `weights.rare` | `9` | How likely a rare card is |
| `weights.legendary` | `1` | How likely a legendary card is |
| `announceRare` | `true` | Rare and legendary draws are told to everyone in chat |
| `blockCards` | `true` | Cards that place or break blocks (The Arena, The Spore, Anvil Drop, Hiss, Hot Headed, Creeper Party, The Ghast) can be drawn |
| `sporeMinutes` | `60` | Minutes before The Spore's field turns back to grass |
| `disabled` | `[]` | Card ids (from the tables below) that start disabled, besides the wild cards, which always start disabled; the operators' choices in `/realm:domt_effects` win over both |
| `historySize` | `20` | How many past draws each player's history keeps |

A rarity whose cards are all disabled is skipped, and its weight shared out among the others. Operators can change `mode`, `cooldownMinutes`, the four weights, `announceRare`, `blockCards` and `sporeMinutes` in game with `/realm:config` (**Deck of Many Things**), and switch cards in `/realm:domt_effects`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `domt:off` | World | JSON `{ card id: true (disabled) or false (enabled) }`: the operators' choices that differ from the default (`disabled` in `config.js`, and every wild card off) |
| `domt:draws` | World | JSON `{ card id: times drawn }` |
| `domt:tasks`, `domt:task:<id>` | World | Block changes waiting to be undone (an arena, a spore field, Anvil Drop's anvil): where, when, and what to put back; checked every 10 seconds, so a restart doesn't keep them |
| `domt:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `domt:next` | Player | When the player may draw again (milliseconds since 1970) |
| `domt:history` | Player | JSON list of the last draws: `[time, card id, operator who drew it]` |
| `domt:wish` | Player | The three boons The Wish offered, until one is chosen |
| `domt:arena` | Player | Where to send the player back if the server restarts mid-arena |
| `domt:far` | Player | JSON `{ dim, x, y, z }`: where a far teleport (The Comet, The Gate) started, until the player lands. Used to put them back if they leave or the server restarts mid-flight |
| `domt:name` | Player | The name to put back after The Rainbow or Cursed Name, if the server restarts first |
| `domt:gone` | Entity | On Chicken Rain's chickens (tagged `domt:temp`): when they leave (ms); checked every 20 seconds and when their chunk loads, so a restart doesn't keep them |

### How it works

- A draw picks a rarity by the weights (only rarities with a card enabled), then a card of that rarity at random. A card whose handler can't work where you are says so, and the deck draws again without that card.
- Block changes (The Arena, The Spore, Anvil Drop's anvil) are saved with the time to undo them and checked every 10 seconds, so a restart doesn't leave them behind. A block is only put back where the block the deck placed is still there.
- Countdowns (Doom, Lit Fuse, Anvil Drop, The Sky, The Floor Is Lava, Gravity Flip, Hot Potato) send `realm:actionbar` `{ player, ticks, from: "domt_bp" }` before each line above the hotbar. Timers run only while the server does: a restart ends them early, and a Hot Potato whose time ran out meanwhile is removed without a bang when its holder joins (or, lying on the ground, when its chunk loads). Timers that follow you (Doom, The Floor Is Lava, Gravity Flip, Topsy Turvy) also end when you die or leave; Hot Potato keeps its own clock, so it goes off on time whoever has it.
- Safe zones arrive as `realm:zones` `{ src, part, parts, zones }` script events; the pack keeps the latest list from each provider and asks for them with `realm:zones_ping` after loading. Every zone counts as the full square around its center, to be safe.
- Other packs: The Champion sends `realm:champion_spawn` `{ dim, x, y, z, mob, name, tag }` (a tag starting `realm:domt_champ_`, `mob` one of zombie, husk, skeleton, stray or witch), looks for that tag for 1.5 seconds and spawns its own if no champion appears, and checks again 3 seconds later. The Mentor and The Archmage send `realm:skill_xp` `{ player, skill, amount }`, and the Crowns cards use the `crowns` scoreboard.
- **Testing:** an operator (or the server console) can run `/scriptevent realm:domt_test {"effect":"<card id>"}` to run one card's handler on themselves (several ids separated by commas work too, wild cards included), or `{"effect":"all","player":"<name>"}` for all 147 in a row on that player (The Swap needs a second player online). Each card is checked for its main effect (an effect, an item, a mob, a move, lost health...) and the result goes to the content log as `[domt] TEST PASS ...` or `TEST FAIL ...`, ending with `TEST SUMMARY 147/147 passed`, and to a `realm:domt_tested` script event per card. Cards that hurt give the test player Resistance IV first, and timers are a few seconds long. After each card the test puts the player back, clears their effects, heals them and removes the mobs it made, so it isn't meant for a busy realm.

### The cards

Every card here is enabled until an operator switches it off.

| # | Card | Id | Rarity | Kind | What happens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Swift Feet | `swift_feet` | Common | good | Speed II for 15 minutes. |
| 2 | The Frog | `the_frog` | Common | good | Jump Boost II for 15 minutes. |
| 3 | Owl's Eyes | `owl_eyes` | Common | good | Night Vision for an hour. |
| 4 | Iron Skin | `iron_skin` | Common | good | Resistance for 15 minutes. |
| 5 | The Miner | `the_miner` | Common | good | Haste II for 20 minutes. |
| 6 | The Fish | `the_fish` | Common | good | Water Breathing for 30 minutes. |

## Slot Machine — `slots_bp`

A slot machine with three reels, played for [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp) or emeralds. Play it anywhere from the **Slot Machine** item, or at a fixed machine an operator made from a block (a note block or a jukebox at the tavern, say). The reels are honest: each one is drawn at random on its own and stops on exactly what was drawn, and the pay table, with each line's odds and the exact return, is one tap away. Every player has a daily loss limit, a short pause between spins and can block themselves from the slots for a while.

### How to use

1. Run `/realm:slots` and pick **Spin**, use a **Slot Machine** item (its lore: `Use it to play the slots`, `Hold it in your hand and use it`), or tap a slot machine block.
2. Pick what to play for (**Crowns** or **Emeralds**), then a stake: 1, 5, 10 or 25 Crowns, or 1, 2, 4 or 8 emeralds. The stake is taken at once.
3. The reels spin above your hotbar for 2 seconds and stop one by one. Chat says what you won, like `2x Cherry! +30 Crowns (stake 10. Balance: 510)` or `No win. -10 Crowns (Balance: 490)`.
4. Pick **Spin again** for the same stake, **Change stake**, or **Close**.
5. `/realm:slots` also has **My stats**, the **Pay table** and **Limits and breaks**, where you can block yourself from playing for 1, 7 or 30 days, or until an operator lifts it.
6. **Operators:** `/realm:slots` → **Operator tools** makes the block you look at a machine (or removes it), gives Slot Machine items (also `/realm:slots_give`), lifts a player's self-block and shows the realm's totals. `/realm:config` → **Slot Machine** sets the currencies, the daily loss limits, the pause between spins and jackpot announcements.

### What players see

- **The reels** spin in the bar above the hotbar (`[ Cherry | Lemon | Bell ]`) with ticking sounds; the first stops after 1 second, the second after 1.5 and the third after 2, each with a click. Spinning reels flash random symbols, and a stopped reel shows the real result.
- **Wins** pay a multiple of the stake, which includes the stake (a 3x win on 10 Crowns gives 30, so you're up 20). Only the best matching line counts. A win of 10x or more plays a level-up sound.
- **The jackpot** (three Crowns, 300x) shows `JACKPOT!` on screen, sets off four fireworks around you and, with `announceJackpots`, tells everyone: `[Slots] Steve hit the JACKPOT for 7,500 Crowns!`
- **Emeralds** are counted and taken from your inventory (plain emeralds only, not renamed ones); emerald wins go into your inventory, and what doesn't fit drops at your feet.
- **Refusals** say why and take nothing: not enough money, `Wait 2s before the next spin.`, `That stake is over what's left of today's loss limit (9 Crowns).`, `You reached today's loss limit for Crowns (200 Crowns). Come back tomorrow (UTC).`, or `You blocked yourself from the slots for 6 more days.`
- **Fixed machines:** tapping a machine block opens the machine instead of the block (sneak-tap in creative mode to use the block normally). Breaking the block removes the machine. A machine in someone else's [land claim](#land-claims--claims_bp) is only for that claim's players: anyone else's tap is refused (`This land is claimed by Sam`).

**The pay table** (default `symbols` and `payouts`). Each reel has 32 stops: Cherry 7, Lemon 8, Bell 6, BAR 5, Gem 3, 7 2, Crown 1.

| Result | Pays | Chance per spin |
|---|---|---|
| Crown Crown Crown (jackpot) | 300x | 1 in 32,768 |
| 7 7 7 | 100x | 1 in 4,096 |
| Gem Gem Gem | 40x | 1 in 1,214 |
| BAR BAR BAR | 30x | 1 in 262 |
| Bell Bell Bell | 18x | 1 in 152 |
| Cherry Cherry Cherry | 10x | 1 in 96 |
| Lemon Lemon Lemon | 10x | 1 in 64 |
| Any two Cherries | 3x | 1 in 9 |
| Any two Crowns | 8x | 1 in 352 |

**Return to player: 91.97%** exactly (30,137 of every 32,768 staked comes back on average; the machine keeps about 8%), and 15.26% of spins win something. The menu computes these from `config.js`, so they stay right if you change the table: the return is the sum over every line of its chance times its pay, over all 32,768 equally likely reel stops. A 100,000-spin simulation with the machine's own code came out at 92.79% at stake 1 and 90.73% at stake 10 (the jackpot makes short runs swing).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:slots` | Everyone | The menu: **Spin**, **My stats**, **Pay table**, **Limits and breaks** (and **Operator tools** for operators) |
| `/realm:slots_spin` | Everyone | Opens the machine straight away: pick a currency and a stake (Crowns and emeralds both allowed by default, `currencies`) |
| `/realm:slots_give [player]` | Operators | Gives the Slot Machine item to the players picked, or to you |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | The slots can be played. When `false`, machines and the item say they're closed |
| `currencies.crowns` | `true` | Players may stake Crowns (the `crowns` scoreboard of the Crowns pack) |
| `currencies.emeralds` | `true` | Players may stake emeralds from their inventory |
| `stakes.crowns` | `[1, 5, 10, 25]` | The Crowns stakes to choose from |
| `stakes.emeralds` | `[1, 2, 4, 8]` | The emerald stakes to choose from |
| `dailyLossLimit.crowns` | `200` | Most Crowns a player may lose per UTC day (stakes minus winnings). `0` = no limit |
| `dailyLossLimit.emeralds` | `32` | The same for emeralds |
| `cooldownSeconds` | `2` | Seconds between the end of one spin and the start of the next |
| `announceJackpots` | `true` | A jackpot is announced to everyone in chat |
| `symbols` | 7 symbols (above) | The reel symbols, `{ id, name, color, weight }`; `weight` is how many of a reel's stops show it |
| `payouts` | 9 lines (above) | The pay table, `{ symbol, count, pay, jackpot? }`: `count` reels showing `symbol` (anywhere) pay `pay` times the stake. The first matching line wins, so put bigger wins first |

Operators can change `enabled`, `currencies.crowns`, `currencies.emeralds`, `dailyLossLimit.crowns`, `dailyLossLimit.emeralds`, `cooldownSeconds` and `announceJackpots` in game with `/realm:config` (**Slot Machine**). Stakes and the pay table stay in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `slots:stats` | Player | JSON: spins, Crowns and emeralds staked and won, the biggest win and jackpots |
| `slots:day` | Player | JSON `{ day, crowns, emeralds }`: the UTC day and that day's net loss per currency, for the daily limit |
| `slots:block` | Player | When the player's self-block ends (milliseconds since 1970), or `-1` until an operator lifts it |
| `slots:machines` | World | JSON list of machine blocks, `[{ d, x, y, z, t }]` (at most 100; `t` is the block's id: a machine whose block was blown up or replaced is forgotten on the next tap) |
| `slots:totals` | World | JSON: all spins, Crowns and emeralds staked and paid out, jackpots |
| `slots:machine` | Item | `true` on a Slot Machine item (a carrot on a stick named `Slot Machine`) |
| `slots:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `crowns` | Scoreboard | Balances, shared with the Crowns pack: stakes are taken from it and wins paid into it |

## Silly Enchants — `silly_bp`

Fourteen silly "enchantments" for your gear. They only add particles, sounds and some very big bounces: none of them changes damage, armor, speed, drops or durability. Most effects come in a few random variants, so they rarely sound the same twice. Each one is a lore line on the item, like `Silly: Grunt Birthday`, and an item holds at most two. They come on **Silly Books** (enchanted books named `Silly Book`), which you apply from `/realm:silly` to the item in your hand. The confetti, disco lights, rainbow trail, bubbles and the Grunt Birthday cheer come from [Silly Enchants Sounds](#silly-enchants-sounds--silly_rp) (in Realm Resources).

### See and hear it

[The Grunt Birthday cheer: a party-horn toot and a squeaky little chorus cheering "yaaay", synthesized for this pack (no recordings)](media/silly/yay.mp3)

### How to use

1. Get a **Silly Book**: operators hand them out, and the realm may sell them (at the caravan or market, if an operator adds them). A book says what it holds (`Silly Book: Hyper Jump`), or `Silly Book: Random` for a surprise. Its last lore line says where that enchant works: `Works in your main hand`, `Works on boots you wear`, `Works on a helmet you wear` or `Works on any armor you wear` (a Random book doesn't say).
2. Hold the item to enchant (boots for Hyper Jump, a sword for Grunt Birthday...) and run `/realm:silly`.
3. Pick **Apply a Silly Book**, then the book. The book is used up and the item gets a line like `Silly: Hyper Jump`. Each item takes up to 2.
4. Wear or hold the item to see it work. Don't like it? `/realm:silly` → **Remove a silly enchant** takes it off for free (the book doesn't come back).
5. Don't want to see your own silly effects for a while? Disable **My silly effects** in `/realm:prefs`; the lore stays.
6. **Lock a Librarian's enchanted book trade:** right-click (interact with) a villager while holding any Enchanted Book to convert and lock them as a Novice Librarian trading that exact book (`librarianBookLock`, enabled by default).
7. **Operators:** `/realm:silly` → **Give Silly Books**, or `/realm:silly_give <player> <book> [amount]`. `/realm:config` → **Silly Enchants** switches the effects, sets the enchants per item, the Hyper Jump cooldown, **Hyper Jump soft landing** and **Librarian book lock** (`librarianBookLock`).

### What players see

| Enchant | Goes on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Grunt Birthday (`grunt_birthday`) | Held item | Mobs you defeat pop like a party: a party-horn toot and a squeaky little chorus cheering "yaaay" (`realm.silly.yay`, 1.4 seconds), with a shower of confetti in two bursts |
| Hyper Jump (`hyper_jump`) | Boots | Sneak and jump to launch. Each launch is a surprise (`hyperJumpOdds`): 60% a big jump (about 30 blocks up), 30% a huge one (about 50), and 10% the **Realm Space Program**: a `3`, `2`, `1`, `LIFTOFF!` countdown on screen, a harmless explosion, then a rocket burn with flames and smoke to about 150 blocks up, while players within 96 blocks read `[Space Program] <name> has left the atmosphere.` (or another line). You fall at full speed and land for real: wear Feather Falling or aim for water, because a big jump onto land is a deadly fall. Operators can switch on a soft landing (`hyperJumpSoftLanding`, off by default): a puff of slow falling just above the ground. Every 4 seconds (`hyperJumpCooldownSeconds`) |
| Squeak (`squeak`) | Boots | Your footsteps squeak (now and then a different squeak) |
| Bubbles (`bubbles`) | Any armor | You leave a trail of bubbles that float up and wobble, in the air as well as under water |
| Rainbow Trail (`rainbow_trail`) | Boots | Rainbow-colored dabs on the ground follow your steps, a new color every half block, and fade after about 2 seconds |
| Hat Trick (`hat_trick`) | Held item | A critical hit (hitting while falling) pulls a baby rabbit out of thin air (sometimes with a ta-da); it vanishes in a puff after 10 seconds (`hatTrickRabbitSeconds`). At most one every 10 seconds (`hatTrickCooldownSeconds`). Baby rabbits drop nothing |
| Disco (`disco`) | Any armor | A dance floor of colored tiles flashes under your feet, a ring of colored lights rises around you in a new color 2 or 3 times a second, and a music note pops up every 2 seconds, even while you stand still |
| Moo (`moo`) | Helmet | You moo when you get hurt. Sometimes the wrong animal answers: an oink, a baa, a cluck or a meow |
| Confetti Swing (`confetti_swing`) | Held item | Every hit throws a burst of confetti, with a pop, a bubble, a pling or a bell |
| Tiny Thunder (`tiny_thunder`) | Held item | A thunderclap and a shower of sparks when you defeat a mob, sometimes with a lightning crack |
| Fish Slap (`fish_slap`) | Held item | Your hits make a loud wet fish slap and a splash (or a dolphin's giggle). Best on a fish |
| Glow (`glow`) | Helmet | You sparkle softly at night |
| Duck (`duck`) | Any armor | You quack when you sneak; sometimes twice |
| Hiccups (`hiccups`) | Helmet | You hiccup now and then, with a few bubbles floating up from your head; some hiccups hop you off the ground a little |

- **Held item** means anything you hold that isn't armor or a book: swords, tools, a bow, even a raw cod. **Helmet** includes the turtle shell; **any armor** includes the elytra.
- **Applying** says `Silly: Hyper Jump! Sneak and jump: a big bounce, a huge one, or now and then a trip with the Realm Space Program.` with a burst of confetti in front of you. A book that doesn't fit says so (`Hyper Jump goes on boots.`), and an item with 2 already says `An item holds at most 2 silly enchants. Remove one first.` A relic says `Relics can't take silly enchants.` and keeps the book (relics rewrite their lore, which would wipe the line). A Random book picks one that fits the item.
- The effects follow the item in your main hand as soon as you switch to it, and your worn armor as soon as you put it on or take it off from your inventory, get hurt or die (armor put on by a dispenser or a command is noticed within a second with up to 5 players on and within about 8 seconds with 40: every player's gear is read again, one player every 4 ticks). Nothing in the pack runs every tick unless someone wears Hyper Jump boots or is in a Hyper Jump flight: the jump check and the landing watch start then and stop when they are no longer needed, and gear changes from events are read on the next tick. Other players see and hear them too.
- **Confetti** flakes burst out, tumble and settle on the ground. Without [Silly Enchants Sounds](#silly-enchants-sounds--silly_rp) you see only vanilla puffs (totem sparkles and colored swirls): no floor, lights, trail dabs or bubbles in the air, and Grunt Birthday makes no sound.
- **Librarian book lock** (`librarianBookLock`, `true` by default): right-clicking a villager with an Enchanted Book in your hand converts and locks them as a Novice Librarian trading that enchanted book.
- **For tests:** `/scriptevent realm:silly_trace on` makes every silly particle and sound also send a `realm:silly_fx` script event (`{ kind: "particle" | "sound", id }`), so a test server, which draws and plays nothing, can see them; `off` stops it.

**Selling Silly Books** (for operators). This pack doesn't change other packs, but a book is recognized by its lore line, so a shop can sell one. In the [Merchant Caravan](#merchant-caravan--caravan_bp)'s `goods` in `caravan_bp/scripts/config.js`, add for example:

```js
{ id: "silly_book", item: "minecraft:enchanted_book", amount: 1, price: 30, stock: 3, name: "Silly Book (random)", nameTag: "§r§dSilly Book", lore: ["§dSilly Book: Random", "§7A surprise silly enchant"] },
```

Use `Silly Book: Hyper Jump` (any enchant's name) instead of `Random` for a particular one. The [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp) market's `buy` list only sells plain items, so the caravan is the place for books.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:silly` | Everyone | The menu: apply a Silly Book to the item in your hand (up to 2 per item, `maxPerItem`), remove one for free, see every enchant (and give books, for operators) |
| `/realm:silly_give <player> <book> [amount]` | Operators | Gives Silly Books: `book` is `random` or an enchant id (`hyper_jump`, `grunt_birthday`...), `amount` 1 to 64 (default 1) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Silly effects play. When `false`, the lore stays on the gear but does nothing |
| `maxPerItem` | `2` | Most silly enchants one item can hold |
| `disabled` | `[]` | Enchant ids that never play and can't be applied, e.g. `["moo"]` |
| `hyperJumpStrength` | `1.0` | Scales every Hyper Jump launch (0.2 to 2). At 1 a big jump goes about 30 blocks up, a huge one about 50 and the Space Program about 150 |
| `hyperJumpOdds.big` | `60` | Weight of a big Hyper Jump (about 30 blocks up) |
| `hyperJumpOdds.huge` | `30` | Weight of a huge Hyper Jump (about 50 blocks up) |
| `hyperJumpOdds.space` | `10` | Weight of a Realm Space Program launch (about 150 blocks up). The three are weights: they needn't add up to 100 |
| `hyperJumpSoftLanding` | `false` | When `true`, a puff of slow falling just above the ground stops a Hyper Jump fall, so landings don't hurt. When `false` (the default), you fall for real (Feather Falling or water helps; a big jump onto land without them is deadly) |
| `hyperJumpCooldownSeconds` | `4` | Seconds between Hyper Jumps |
| `hatTrickCooldownSeconds` | `10` | Seconds between Hat Trick rabbits for one player |
| `hatTrickRabbitSeconds` | `10` | Seconds before a Hat Trick rabbit vanishes |
| `librarianBookLock` | `true` | Right-clicking a villager while holding an Enchanted Book converts and locks them as a Novice Librarian trading that book |

Operators can change `enabled`, `maxPerItem`, `hyperJumpCooldownSeconds`, `hyperJumpSoftLanding` (**Hyper Jump soft landing**) and `librarianBookLock` (**Librarian book lock**) in game with `/realm:config` (**Silly Enchants**). Each player can switch their own effects with **My silly effects** in `/realm:prefs`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Item lore `Silly: <name>` | Item | The enchants on a piece of gear (plain lore, so it survives anvils and trading) |
| Item lore `Silly Book: <name>` | Item | What a Silly Book holds (`Random` for a surprise) |
| `silly:applied` | Player | How many silly enchants the player has applied |
| `silly:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's preferences (**My silly effects**) |
| `silly:until` | Entity | When a Hat Trick rabbit (tagged `silly_rabbit`) vanishes |
| `silly:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

## Silly Enchants Sounds — `silly_rp`

The particles and the cheer of [Silly Enchants](#silly-enchants--silly_bp): confetti, the disco floor and lights, the rainbow trail, bubbles that float in the air and the Grunt Birthday cheer. A **resource pack**, part of **Realm Resources** (or on its own, together with Silly Enchants).

### How to use

1. Nothing to do as a player: when the realm has it, Minecraft downloads it as you join (accept the resource pack prompt if one appears).
2. Without it, Silly Enchants works the same, but you see only vanilla puffs: no confetti flakes, dance floor, lights, trail dabs or bubbles on land, and Grunt Birthday makes no sound.
3. **Operators:** it comes with Realm Resources: activate that under **Resource Packs**. To use it alone instead, download Silly Enchants Sounds from its card and activate it the same way, with Silly Enchants under **Behavior Packs**.

### What players see

- **Confetti:** small square flakes in six party colors burst up and out, tumble (they flip as they fall) and settle on the ground, fading after 2 to 3 seconds. Grunt Birthday throws 40 and then 24 more, Confetti Swing 14, and applying a Silly Book 20.
- **Disco floor:** nine colored tiles on a half-block grid, flat on the ground under your feet, flashing in new colors five times a second.
- **Disco lights:** a ring of eight soft glows around you in one color, drifting up and fading in under half a second.
- **Rainbow trail:** flat colored dabs on the ground that fade over about 2 seconds.
- **Bubbles:** vanilla-looking bubbles that wobble up through air as well as water (vanilla's bubbles vanish as soon as they leave water).
- **The Grunt Birthday cheer** (`realm.silly.yay`, 1.4 seconds): a party-horn toot and a squeaky little chorus cheering "yaaay", heard up to 24 blocks away, about as loud as a mob. It's synthesized from scratch: no recordings, nobody else's audio. Listen in [Silly Enchants](#silly-enchants--silly_bp)'s **See and hear it**.

### Saved data

None. It's a resource pack: no scripts and no commands.

### How it's made

`npm run gen:silly` (`tools/gen-silly/gen.mjs`, with the cheer in `tools/gen-silly/yay.mjs`) writes everything but `manifest.json`; `npm run check` fails if a file differs from what it makes. Writing the sound needs ffmpeg with libvorbis. Ogg Vorbis isn't byte-for-byte the same across ffmpeg versions, so the generator keeps `tools/gen-silly/sounds-lock.json` (the sha256 of the samples before encoding, and of the `.ogg`), and the check compares those without ffmpeg. `node tools/gen-silly/gen.mjs --audition docs/media/silly` also writes the listening clip `docs/media/silly/yay.mp3` (needs libmp3lame).

| Files | |
|---|---|
| `particles/silly_confetti.json` | `realm:silly_confetti`: `variable.count` flakes, each a random party color, that land and settle on blocks |
| `particles/silly_floor.json` | `realm:silly_floor`: nine flat tiles under your feet, living 0.3 seconds |
| `particles/silly_light.json` | `realm:silly_light`: a ring of eight glows in `variable.color`, living 0.45 seconds |
| `particles/silly_trail.json` | `realm:silly_trail`: one flat dab in `variable.color`, living 2.2 seconds |
| `particles/silly_bubble.json` | `realm:silly_bubble`: three bubbles (vanilla's bubble picture) that float up through air |
| `textures/particle/realm_silly.png` | The particles' pictures (32 x 16): a confetti square, a soft square for the trail and floor, and a round glow, white so they take any color |
| `sounds/silly/yay.ogg`, `sounds/sound_definitions.json` | The cheer, and `realm.silly.yay` (category `player`, volume 0.5, heard up to 24 blocks) |
| `pack_icon.png` | A party hat in a shower of confetti |

The particle files are named after their ids so they can't collide with another pack's when Realm Resources merges them.

## Dolphin Friends — `dolphin_bp`

Tame a dolphin with raw fish, then ride it through the sea: it swims where you look, and you breathe under water while you ride. Tamed dolphins stay (they never despawn), follow you in the water, can be named and called to you.

### How to use

1. Find a dolphin (oceans) and feed it **raw cod** or **raw salmon**: tap it with the fish. Each fish has a 25% chance (`tameChancePercent`) to tame it: hearts mean it worked, smoke means try again. Chat says `The dolphin trusts you!`. It takes 4 fish on average.
2. **Ride:** tap your tamed dolphin with an empty hand. It swims where you look: push forward to go, back to back up, left or right to drift sideways. Look up or down to rise or dive.
3. **Leap:** press jump while swimming at the surface and the dolphin jumps out of the water.
4. **Get off:** sneak.
5. Run `/realm:dolphin` for **My dolphins**: call one to you (it swims over when you're in the water, up to 128 blocks), name it or release it. **Call the nearest** calls the closest one; `/realm:dolphin_call` does the same.
6. **Operators:** `/realm:dolphin` → **Operator tools** lists every tamed dolphin with its owner and releases the one you look at. `/realm:config` → **Dolphin Friends** sets the taming chance, how many dolphins each player may have, whether others can ride yours, the top speed and whether riders breathe under water.

### What players see

- **Feeding** works as in vanilla too: a fed dolphin may still lead you to treasure. One fish is used per tap, whether or not the dolphin takes it as a vanilla treat. A player can have up to 3 tamed dolphins (`maxPerPlayer`); a fourth says `You already have 3 dolphins. Release one first (/realm:dolphin).`
- **Riding:** the dolphin turns to face where you look and speeds up while you push forward (`maxSpeed` 12 and `acceleration` 1.6 blocks per second each tick; the water's drag keeps it to about 6 blocks per second, a little faster than a sprinting player). It swims only where you steer: while someone rides it, its own swimming (wandering, breaching, following boats and players) is off, so without input it glides to a stop and stays there. While ridden it can stay under water as long as you like (it can't swim up for air on its own, so it breathes water then). It swims on its own again once you get off. Out of the water it doesn't steer. Leaps need 1.5 seconds between them. Others can ride your dolphins too unless an operator disables `othersCanRide`. Steering starts as you tap the dolphin, or within a quarter second of getting on any other way (such as `/ride`); a player is only looked at for that while a tamed dolphin is loaded, so a dolphin that has just come into a loaded area takes up to a second longer.
- **Breathing:** while you ride, you have Water Breathing (no particles), so you can dive as long as you like (`riderWaterBreathing`). It's a 3-second effect topped up every half second, so it runs out about 3 seconds after you get off; a longer one, like a potion's, is left alone.
- **Following:** an unridden tamed dolphin swims toward its owner when you're both in the water and more than 8 blocks apart (`followDistance`), up to 64 blocks away.
- **Calling:** the dolphin must be loaded (near a player) and in your dimension, and you must be in the water. It appears next to you with hearts. Calling, naming and releasing only work on a dolphin that is still yours (one an operator released and someone else tamed says `That dolphin isn't yours any more.`).
- A tamed dolphin that dies tells its owner: `Splash died.`
- **For operators and tests:** with cheats on, `/scriptevent realm:dolphin_feed` (run by an operator holding raw cod or salmon) feeds the nearest dolphin within 5 blocks exactly as a tap would.

**Compatibility note:** this pack carries a copy of the vanilla dolphin's behavior file (`entities/dolphin.json`, from Minecraft 1.26.50: Mojang's bedrock-samples `behavior_pack/entities/dolphin.json`, still the newest in 1.26.50.4) with two additions: a `realm:dolphin_tamed` group (a seat for one player, `minecraft:rideable`; `minecraft:is_tamed`; `minecraft:persistent`), added by the event `realm:dolphin_tame` and removed by `realm:dolphin_release`; and a `realm:dolphin_ridden` group (`minecraft:movement` and `minecraft:underwater_movement` 0, so its own AI can't swim while the script steers it, and a `minecraft:breathable` that also breathes water, since it can no longer swim up for air), added by `realm:dolphin_ridden` when someone gets on and swapped for `realm:dolphin_free` (the vanilla 0.1, 0.15 and air-only breathing again: removing a group that overrides a component removes the component, it doesn't bring back the vanilla one) by `realm:dolphin_unridden` when they get off, on release, when the pack is disabled, or the next time the pack sees the dolphin with nobody on it (after a restart mid-ride). Wild dolphins behave exactly as in vanilla: treasure leading, playing with items, swimming with players for Dolphin's Grace, breathing air, drying out on land. All components are stable ones, so no experiments are needed on the Realm. Two things to know: another behavior pack that also changes the dolphin wins or loses depending on pack order (only the top one's file is used), and if a future Minecraft update changes the vanilla dolphin, this copy keeps the old behavior until it is refreshed from the newest vanilla file.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:dolphin` | Everyone | Your tamed dolphins (up to 3, `maxPerPlayer`): call, name, release; **Call the nearest** (and **Operator tools** for operators) |
| `/realm:dolphin_call` | Everyone | Calls your nearest tamed dolphin to you (you must be in the water) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Dolphins can be tamed, ridden and called. When `false`, tamed dolphins stay tamed (and can still be sat on) but don't steer, follow or come when called |
| `tameChancePercent` | `25` | Chance in percent that one raw cod or salmon tames a dolphin |
| `maxPerPlayer` | `3` | Most tamed dolphins one player can have |
| `othersCanRide` | `true` | Other players may ride and steer your tamed dolphins |
| `maxSpeed` | `12` | Top speed while ridden, in blocks per second (the water's drag keeps a ridden dolphin to about 6 in practice) |
| `acceleration` | `1.6` | Blocks per second a ridden dolphin gains each tick |
| `riderWaterBreathing` | `true` | Riders breathe under water: Water Breathing while they ride, gone about 3 seconds after they get off |
| `leapStrength` | `0.9` | Upward push of a leap out of the water |
| `followDistance` | `8` | A tamed dolphin swims after its owner (in water) when farther than this many blocks |

Operators can change `enabled`, `tameChancePercent`, `maxPerPlayer`, `othersCanRide`, `maxSpeed` and `riderWaterBreathing` (**Riders breathe under water**) in game with `/realm:config` (**Dolphin Friends**).

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `dolphin:owner` | Entity | The owner's player id on a tamed dolphin |
| `dolphin:ownerName` | Entity | The owner's name when it was tamed |
| `dolphin:ridden` | Entity | `true` while the dolphin has the `realm:dolphin_ridden` group (its own swimming off) |
| `dolphin:idx:<player id>` | World | JSON `{ entity id: { o, on, n, d, x, y, z } }`: that player's tamed dolphins (owner, name and last known spot), for the lists while they're far away. A world from an older version has one `dolphin:index` for everyone; the pack splits it into these on its first load and removes it once every part is written |
| `dolphin:tamedCount` | Player | How many dolphins the player has tamed |
| `dolphin:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

## Platypus — `platypus_bp`

An uncommon new animal, the platypus (`realm:platypus`), lives along rivers and in swamps and mangrove swamps, always close to the water. Feed it fish to heal it or to raise baby platypuses. It is passive until you hit it: then it fights back, and its bite poisons you and makes your screen wobble (nausea). About 1 in 200 is a teal platypus in a brown fedora: Perry the Platypus. There is a spawn egg too. Needs [Platypus Models](#platypus-models--platypus_rp) (in Realm Resources) to look like a platypus.

### See and hear it

![A render of the platypus (left) and Perry (right)](media/platypus/platypus.png)

A render of the model and its two skins, not an in-game screenshot.

### How to use

1. Look along rivers and in swamps and mangrove swamps: platypuses spawn on the banks (grass, dirt, sand, gravel, clay, mud, mangrove roots), alone or in pairs, in daylight-bright spots. They are uncommon: you may walk a long river before you meet one.
2. Run `/realm:platypus` to see how many platypuses are within 64 blocks (`findRadius`) and how far, and in which direction, the nearest one is. If one of them is a Perry, it tells you where that one is too.
3. Leave it be and it wanders, swims and waddles back to the water. Hold **raw cod** or **raw salmon** and it follows you. You can put it on a lead and name it with a name tag (rename the tag on an anvil first).
4. **Feed it:** tap a hurt platypus with **raw cod**, **raw salmon**, **cooked cod**, **cooked salmon** or **tropical fish** to heal it (hearts show).
5. **Breed:** feed raw cod or raw salmon to two grown-up platypuses near each other: they fall in love and make a baby platypus. The baby follows a parent and grows up in 20 minutes; feeding it raw cod or salmon makes it grow faster.
6. Hit it and it bites back for 15 seconds: each bite does 1 heart of damage, 5 seconds of **Poison** and 8 seconds of **Nausea** (`nauseaSeconds`). Then it calms down.
7. **Creative:** the **Platypus Spawn Egg** (brown with teal spots) is in the creative inventory with the other spawn eggs, and every egg has the same 1 in 200 chance of hatching a Perry.
8. **Operators:** `/summon realm:platypus ~ ~ ~ 0 0 realm:platypus_make_perry` summons a Perry (`realm:platypus_make_brown` a brown one). `/realm:config` → **Platypus** sets the nausea length, the Perry message and the `/realm:platypus` search radius.

### What players see

- **The platypus:** a small, flat brown animal (10 health, 5 hearts) with a dark duck bill, a broad flat tail and four short legs with webbed feet. It walks, swims and paddles, wags its tail and looks at players nearby. It breathes air and water, so it never drowns.
- **Feeding:** a hurt platypus eats raw cod or salmon (heals 3 health, 1.5 hearts), cooked cod (5), cooked salmon (6) or tropical fish (2), and hearts float up. At full health it doesn't eat cooked fish or tropical fish; raw cod or salmon then goes to breeding (or, for a baby, to growing up).
- **Babies:** half the size of a grown-up, they follow a parent and grow up after 20 minutes (raw cod or salmon speeds that up). A baby has the same 1 in 200 chance of being a Perry.
- **Names and leads:** a name from a name tag always shows above the platypus, not only when you look at it. A lead ties on at its shoulders.
- **Perry:** 1 in 200 platypuses (from natural spawns, spawn eggs and `/summon`) is teal with an orange bill and feet, wearing a brown fedora with a dark band. Players within 64 blocks get `A teal platypus in a brown fedora is nearby. Perry the Platypus?!` when one appears (`perryMessage`). It acts like any other platypus.
- **When hit:** the platypus (and only that one) chases whoever hit it, player or mob, for 15 seconds and bites: 2 damage, Poison for 5 seconds, and for players Nausea for 8 seconds (`nauseaSeconds`, 0 = none). Hitting it again restarts the 15 seconds. Players in Creative are left alone.
- **Drops:** no items; 1 to 3 experience when a player kills it.
- **Spawning:** surface spawns in river biomes (not frozen rivers), swamps and mangrove swamps, on grass, dirt, coarse dirt, podzol, sand, gravel, clay, mud or mangrove roots, at light level 7 or more. Weight 2, groups of 1 or 2, and no more than 3 per area, counted with the other animals' cap. They never despawn (the entity has `minecraft:persistent` and no `minecraft:despawn`), so the density limit and the animal cap are what keep their numbers down.
- `/realm:platypus` answers in chat, for example `3 platypuses within 64 blocks. Nearest: 12 blocks northeast.`, or `No platypuses within 64 blocks. They live along rivers and in swamps and mangrove swamps, near the water.` when there are none.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:platypus` | Everyone | How many platypuses are near you (default 64 blocks, `findRadius`), how far and which way the nearest is, and where a Perry among them is |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `nauseaSeconds` | `8` | Seconds of Nausea a platypus bite gives a player (on top of the bite's 5 seconds of Poison, which is set in the entity file). `0` = no nausea |
| `perryMessage` | `true` | Players within 64 blocks get a chat line when a Perry spawns |
| `findRadius` | `64` | How far `/realm:platypus` looks, in blocks |

Operators can change all three in game with `/realm:config` (**Platypus**). The spawn chances, the 1 in 200 for Perry, the 15 seconds of anger, damage and Poison are in `entities/platypus.json` and `spawn_rules/platypus.json`, not in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `platypus:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

The platypus's color is its `minecraft:variant` (0 brown, 1 Perry), saved with the entity by the game.

### How it works

- **The mob** (`entities/platypus.json`) uses only stable components, so no experiments are needed: amphibious movement and navigation like the turtle's (`minecraft:movement.amphibious`, `minecraft:navigation.generic` with `can_swim` and `can_walk`), random strolling and swimming, `minecraft:behavior.move_to_water` so it returns to the water, and `minecraft:behavior.tempt` with raw cod and salmon. `minecraft:nameable` has `always_show`, and `minecraft:persistent` keeps it (and its name) for good.
- **Feeding and breeding:** `minecraft:healable` heals a hurt platypus (raw cod and salmon 3, cooked cod 5, cooked salmon 6, tropical fish 2). Grown-ups have the group `realm:platypus_adult` (`minecraft:breedable` with raw cod and salmon, `minecraft:behavior.breed`, and `minecraft:mark_variant` 1 to mark it); `minecraft:entity_born` gives a baby `realm:platypus_baby` (`minecraft:is_baby`, `minecraft:scale` 0.5, `minecraft:ageable` for 1200 seconds with raw cod and salmon, `minecraft:behavior.follow_parent`), and `minecraft:ageable_grow_up` swaps it for the adult group. The script shows the hearts (`world.afterEvents.playerInteractWithEntity`, when the fish was used up, or always in Creative).
- **Older platypuses:** ones that spawned before breeding existed (or from `/summon` with a variant event) have no adult group, so on `world.afterEvents.entitySpawn` and `entityLoad` the script fires `realm:platypus_grow_up` on any platypus that isn't a baby and has no `minecraft:mark_variant` of 1. That event adds `realm:platypus_adult` (only when `is_baby` is false).
- **Fighting back:** `minecraft:behavior.hurt_by_target` picks whoever hurt it, and a `minecraft:damage_sensor` trigger fires `realm:platypus_anger` when a player or mob hurts it. That event removes and re-adds the group `realm:platypus_angry` (so a new hit starts the 15 seconds again): `minecraft:angry`, a 15-second `minecraft:timer` whose `realm:platypus_calm` removes the group (`minecraft:angry` alone never calms down while it has a target), and `minecraft:behavior.melee_attack`. Its `minecraft:attack` does 2 damage with `effect_name` `poison` for 5 seconds. The script adds the Nausea: `world.afterEvents.entityHurt` for players, when the damaging entity is a `realm:platypus`.
- **Perry:** `minecraft:entity_spawned` (natural spawns, eggs, `/summon` without an event) picks `realm:platypus_brown` (weight 199, variant 0) or `realm:platypus_perry` (weight 1, variant 1). The events `realm:platypus_make_brown` and `realm:platypus_make_perry` switch it. The resource pack chooses the skin by `query.variant` and shows the fedora bone only for variant 1. The script reads the variant on `world.afterEvents.entitySpawn` (causes `Spawned` and `Event`, not chunk loads) for the Perry message.

## Platypus Models — `platypus_rp`

What the platypus from [Platypus](#platypus--platypus_bp) looks like: its model, the brown and Perry skins, the walk, swim and tail-wag animations, the spawn egg colors and the names `Platypus` and `Platypus Spawn Egg`. A **resource pack**, part of **Realm Resources** (or on its own, together with Platypus).

### How to use

1. Nothing to do as a player: when the realm has it, Minecraft downloads it as you join (accept the resource pack prompt if one appears).
2. Without it, platypuses still spawn and fight, but you can't see them properly and their name shows as `entity.realm:platypus.name`.
3. **Operators:** it comes with Realm Resources: activate that under **Resource Packs**. To use it alone instead, download Platypus Models from its card and activate it the same way, with Platypus under **Behavior Packs**.

### What players see

- A blocky platypus about 3/4 of a block long and half a block high: a flat body, a head with a wide flat bill (dark gray, with nostrils), a broad beaver tail with a crosshatched top, and four short legs with webbed feet. It looks at nearby players, swings its legs and tail as it walks and paddles in the water.
- **Perry** uses a teal skin with an orange bill and feet, and wears a brown fedora with a dark band (a separate bone, hidden on brown platypuses).
- The **Platypus Spawn Egg** is brown with teal spots.

### Saved data

None. It's a resource pack: no scripts and no commands.

### How it's made

`npm run gen:platypus` (`tools/gen-platypus/gen.mjs`) writes the model and the pictures from one list of cubes, so the texture layout always matches the geometry; `npm run check` fails if they differ from what it makes. The rest is hand-written.

| Files | |
|---|---|
| `models/entity/platypus.geo.json` | Generated. `geometry.realm_platypus`: bones `body`, `head`, `bill`, `tail`, `leg_front_left`, `leg_front_right`, `leg_back_left`, `leg_back_right` and `fedora`, on a 64 x 32 texture. A `lead` locator on top of `body`, at the shoulders, is where a lead ties on (without one the lead floats above the mob) |
| `textures/entity/platypus/platypus.png`, `perry.png` | Generated. The brown and the Perry skins, shaded with a little noise. The brown skin leaves the fedora area empty |
| `pack_icon.png` (both packs), `docs/media/platypus/platypus.png` | Generated renders of the model |
| `entity/platypus.entity.json` | The client entity: material `entity_alphatest`, the two textures, the animations and `spawn_egg` colors `#7a5233` and `#2aa59a` |
| `render_controllers/platypus.render_controllers.json` | Picks the skin by `query.variant` and shows `fedora` only when it is 1 |
| `animations/platypus.animation.json`, `platypus.animation_controllers.json` | Walk (legs and tail, by distance moved, blended by speed), idle tail wag, and a paddle while in water; vanilla's `animation.common.look_at_target` turns the head |
| `texts/en_US.lang`, `texts/languages.json` | The names. Realm Resources joins every pack's `.lang` lines into one file |
