## Treasure Maps & Riddles — `maps_bp`

Buy a treasure map from Mara the Cartographer and puzzle your way across the land. Each clue is a different kind of riddle: a heading and a distance, a set of compass steps, a coordinate puzzle, or a walk until your coordinates read right. Near where it points, the map names a real landmark there (the edge of a birch wood, a pond's shore, a hilltop...) and a marker stands at it: a cairn, a flag or a standing stone that holds the next clue. After two to four clues, 400 to 1,000 blocks from where you bought the map, a chest lies buried at the last landmark. The map only tells you warmer or colder once you're close, so the clues are how you get there. Finding the treasure pays Crowns, and the chest holds gold, iron, emeralds and sometimes a diamond or even a relic.

### How to use

1. Find Mara the Cartographer (or any NPC with the `cartographer` role, from [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)), tap her and pick **Buy a treasure map (50 Crowns)**. You get a piece of paper named `Treasure Map`, and chat reads the first clue, for example `"From where you got this map, walk 640 paces toward the dusk, then turn and go 560 paces north. Another traveler left a mark there."`
2. Work out the clue. The North Star (or Pole Star, the cold north wind) is north; the rising sun, the dawn and the way your shadow points at sunset are east; the warm south wind and "with the North Star at your back" are south; the setting sun, the dusk and the way your shadow points at sunrise are west. A pace is a block. Coordinate clues need your coordinates (the [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp), or the game's own **Show Coordinates**).
3. Close to where the clue points (within 96 blocks, once the land around that spot is loaded: about 50 blocks on a Realm's usual simulation distance), chat says `The map's ink darkens:` and names the landmark, for example `A pole flying a red flag stands at the edge of the birch wood.` Look for it.
4. Hold the map in your hand: every 2 seconds the third box on the right side of the screen (**Right 3**; another box or the line above the hotbar, if you choose it with **Where Warmer / Colder shows for me** in `/realm:prefs`) says `Warmer`, `Colder` or `Very warm`, with which clue you're on.
   Far from the marker or the chest (more than 64 blocks) the map only says `The map is cold.`, `The map is cool.` or `The map is faintly warm.`, so it can't steer you there.
5. Walk up to the marker (within 4 blocks) and the next clue appears in chat and on the map: `You found the cairn! Tucked between its stones: the next clue (2 of 3).`
6. On the last clue the ink names where the treasure lies buried (`The treasure lies buried on the shore of the wide water.`). Follow `Hot` to `Burning hot! Dig here.`; standing over it pays the Crowns. Then dig up the chest, 1 to 3 blocks down, for the rest.
7. Hunting with your [party](#parties--party_bp)? Mates within 32 blocks of you when you find the treasure each get half its Crowns on top of yours (nothing is taken from you), plus the journal entry and the Exploration XP. The chest's loot is yours to split.
8. Lost the map, or the clue? Run `/realm:maps` (or `/realm:maps_hunts`) for your hunt's clue, a new copy of the map, or to give the hunt up.
9. **Racing Rook** ([Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp)' Rook the Rival, chapter "The Map Room", optional): within 300 blocks of your last clue's spot, chat says `[Story] Rook is after your treasure too! Get there first: you have 5:00.` Find the chest in time to win the race. Too slow and Rook got there first: the chest and its loot are still yours, but he takes his cut of the coins (`Rook got here first: he left you the chest, but took his cut of the coins.`, half the Crowns, `rivalShare`).
10. **Operators:** `/realm:maps` opens the **Treasure Maps** menu instead: `Your treasure hunts`, `Give a treasure map` (pick a player online) and `Settings` (which points to `/realm:config` → Treasure Maps & Riddles). `/realm:maps_give <player>` gives a free map from chat. `/realm:config` → **Treasure Maps & Riddles** sets the price, how far maps lead, how many hunts a player can have, the Warmer / Colder range, whether markers are built, the Crowns found, the party mates' share and range, the distance from world spawn and the hints.

### What players see

- **Buying:** the cartographer's menu explains the hunt and the price (default 50 Crowns, `price`) and shows your balance. Chat says `-50 Crowns (Treasure map)` and `You bought a treasure map! The first clue: "..."`. You can follow one hunt at a time (`maxHunts`); with one going, the cartographer also offers **Your treasure hunt**, and buying another says `You're already following one of my maps. Find that treasure first, or give it up.` Maps only show the Overworld.
- **The hunt:** the treasure is 400 to 1,000 blocks (`minDistance`, `maxDistance`) in a straight line from where you bought the map, in a random direction away from world spawn, reached in 2 to 4 legs (`legsMin`, `legsMax`; each leg at least 170 blocks, so fewer on a short hunt) that wander a little sideways. Each clue is counted from where its leg starts: where you got the map, then each marker.
- **Clues:** each leg uses a kind of clue the hunt hasn't used yet, worded from large pools so sentences rarely repeat:
  - **Heading:** one of 16 compass points as a riddle (`halfway between the dawn and the cold north wind`, `toward the setting sun, bearing a little toward the Pole Star`) and a distance rounded to 50 (`about six hundred and fifty paces`, `some 1,200 strides`).
  - **Compass steps:** two or three straight walks rounded to 10 (`walk 340 paces the way your shadow points at sunrise, then 220 more toward the North Star`).
  - **Coordinates:** the spot's X and Z as small puzzles (`lies halfway between -771 and -435`, `is 1,300 minus 53`, `ends in 47 and lies between 1,200 and 1,300`, `is seven times 176, plus 3`).
  - **Mixed:** `go toward the dusk until your X reads -517; then turn north until your Z reads -603`.
- **Landmarks and markers:** within 96 blocks (`revealDistance`) of where a clue points, once that land is loaded, the pack looks at the ground within 32 blocks of it and picks a landmark the hunt hasn't used yet: water (`beside a little pond`, `on the shore of the wide water`), the edge of a wood by its tree (oak, birch, spruce, jungle, acacia, dark oak, cherry, mangrove, azalea, pale oak), the highest ground (`on the summit, about height 112`), the lowest ground (`down in the hollow`), sand, snow, flowers, or level ground. If you leave before it's done (fly on, teleport home), nothing changes: it looks again when you come back. It builds a marker there (`markers`): a cairn of mossy cobblestone with a lantern on top, a 4-block oak fence pole with a wool flag, or a column of stone bricks with a chiseled top (taken down again when the hunt is done with it, below). Where no marker can stand (open water, builds, a safe zone), chat says `A bottle with the next clue lies ..., within 30 paces of the spot.` and coming within 30 blocks (`legRadius`) finds it.
- **The map** is paper named `Treasure Map` with the clue and the landmark as lore, then `Clue 2 of 3`, `Hold it in your hand to sense warmth` (when `warmth` is on) and `Map 4QZ` (its hunt). While you hold it (`warmth`): within 64 blocks (`warmthRadius`) of the marker or the chest, `Warmer` or `Colder` (compared with 2 seconds ago), `The map is quiet` when you haven't moved, `Very warm` within 40 blocks (`veryWarm`), `Hot` within 12 and, over the chest, `Burning hot! Dig here.` Farther away it only says `The map is faintly warm.` (up to 3 times that range), `The map is cool.` (up to 8 times) or `The map is cold.` Before the landmark is settled, the range counts from where the clue points. Holding a map from a finished or abandoned hunt says so.
- **The chest:** on the last leg the landmark search also buries the chest within 8 blocks of the landmark, 1 to 3 blocks under natural ground: `The map grows warm in your hands. The treasure lies buried at the edge of the oak wood. Close by, follow the warmth, then dig.` If no landmark has a good spot, it tries within 32 blocks (`searchRadius`) of where the clue points; if there's none there either (water, a build, a cave), the treasure moves 60 to 120 blocks further and the map says `The map's ink shifts: the treasure isn't here after all.` with a heading from where you stand. After 4 tries the treasure is handed over directly (`You found the treasure, washed up and half buried!`).
- **Finding it:** standing within 3 blocks of the chest says `You found the treasure! The chest is buried right here, 1 to 3 blocks down: dig it up.` and pays 30 to 90 [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp) (`crownsMin`, `crownsMax`): `+40 Crowns (Treasure map)`. The map disappears. The chest holds what `loot` rolls: by default often gold and iron ingots, often emeralds or bottles o' enchanting, sometimes ender pearls, a diamond or two, a golden apple, a name tag or a saddle, and rarely a heart of the sea.
- **Older maps** (bought before markers) keep their route and any buried chest; the next time their holder is online the clue rewrites itself as a coordinate puzzle: `The ink on your treasure map stirs and rewrites itself.`
- **Other packs:** finding a treasure finishes a `treasure` quest (`realm:quest_done`), gives 10 Wayfarers reputation in [Guilds & Reputation](#guilds--reputation--guilds_bp) (`reputation`), 50 Exploration XP in [Skills](#skills--skills_bp) (`skillXp`) and a `Buried treasure` entry on the Places page of the [Field Journal](#field-journal--journal_bp) (listed under "Also found"). One treasure in 10 (`relicChance`) also holds a relic from [Relics](#relics--relics_bp) (`relics`): `Something old and strange glints among the coins...`
- **Party mates share the find:** when a player in a [party](#parties--party_bp) finds the treasure, every online mate in the same dimension within 32 blocks (`partyRange`) gets `[Party] You helped Ann find the treasure!`, 50% of the Crowns the finder got (`partyShare`, rounded down; paid on top, not taken from the finder): `+20 Crowns (Treasure map, with Ann)`, plus the `Buried treasure` journal entry and the 50 Exploration XP. Reputation and the finished quest are the finder's. With `partyShare` at 0 mates still get the journal entry and the XP.
- **Giving up** (`/realm:maps` → **Give up this hunt**) removes the hunt and its map; the Crowns aren't paid back.
- **The land is put back:** a marker comes down once the hunt is done with it (you reached it and read the next clue, found the treasure or gave up), and an empty treasure chest is turned back into the ground it replaced. The pack remembers exactly which blocks each marker and chest placed and what was there before (grass, flowers and snow too), and puts them back at least 30 seconds later, once nobody is within 32 blocks (or 10 minutes later even with someone close). It only puts back a block that is still what the hunt placed, so a block a player broke, changed or built on is left alone, and a chest that still holds anything stays (items are never destroyed; after 30 days it is left for good). Land that isn't loaded is put back when its chunk loads again, even after a restart. A bottle spot never places anything. Markers and chests from before Treasure Maps 1.5.0 come down too, with air under a marker and dirt under a chest, except markers of legs already passed before the update.

**Treasure chests and markers never touch builds.** A chest only replaces natural ground (grass, dirt, sand, gravel, clay, stone, snow, natural terracotta and the like), with natural ground above it; a marker only stands on natural ground and only replaces air, grass, flowers and snow layers. Before burying a chest, the pack checks the 9 x 9 columns around the spot, from 4 blocks over the ground to 4 below (5 x 5 top blocks for a marker), and skips the spot if it finds anything a player likely made: planks, glass, chests, barrels, signs, beds, torches, lanterns, doors, fences, wool, carpet, concrete, glazed terracotta, terracotta in colors the badlands don't have, bricks, tiles, slabs, stairs, crafted wood, metal and other crafted blocks, heads, crafting tables, furnaces, rails, farmland, paths, cobblestone and more. Neither goes within 64 blocks of world spawn (`avoidSpawn`), inside or touching a safe zone, town or land claim (the safe zones protocol, from [Safe Zones](#safe-zones--zones_bp), [Town Projects](#town-projects--town_bp) and [Land Claims](#land-claims--claims_bp)), or where it can't read the columns.
- **Mara's friends:** a player who is a Friend of Mara ([Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)) pays 10% less for a treasure map (50 to 45 Crowns by default, rounded down), from `realm:affinity`.
- **Map Sense:** a Pathfinder with the Map Sense talent ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp) Callings, `bonus.mapReveal` in `realm:calling`) has the spot built from 128 blocks away instead of `revealDistance` (at most 160).
- **A found treasure** is town gossip about the finder (with [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp); at most one piece of news from this pack per in-game hour, see Town news in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:maps` | Everyone | Your treasure hunt, like `/realm:maps_hunts`. Operators get the **Treasure Maps** menu instead: their hunts, `Give a treasure map` and `Settings` |
| `/realm:maps_hunts` | Everyone | Your treasure hunt: the clue, the landmark once seen, which clue you're on; buttons for a new copy of the map (when you don't carry one) and to give the hunt up |
| `/realm:maps_give <player>` | Operators | Gives the players picked (`@a` works) a free treasure map, starting where each one stands. Skips players outside the Overworld or already on as many hunts as allowed (default 1, `maxHunts`) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `price` | `50` | Crowns a treasure map costs at a cartographer (0 = free) |
| `npcRole` | `"cartographer"` | The NPC role whose NPCs sell treasure maps |
| `maxHunts` | `1` | Treasure hunts a player can have at once (1 to 3 in game) |
| `minDistance` | `400` | The treasure is at least this many blocks from where the map was bought. Every leg is at least 170 blocks, so a short hunt has fewer legs (2 at 400) |
| `maxDistance` | `1000` | ...and at most this many |
| `legsMin` | `2` | Fewest clues a hunt has |
| `legsMax` | `4` | Most clues a hunt has (each uses a different kind of clue, so 4 at most stay varied) |
| `legRadius` | `30` | Where no marker can stand, coming this close (blocks, ignoring height) to the end of a leg finds the next clue in a bottle |
| `revealDistance` | `96` | Coming this close to where a clue points (once the land is loaded) picks the landmark, builds the marker or buries the chest, and names the landmark (the land 32 blocks around the spot must be loaded, so with a simulation distance of 4 chunks this happens about 50 blocks away) |
| `searchRadius` | `32` | How far from where the last clue points the chest may be buried when no landmark spot works |
| `avoidSpawn` | `64` | Never bury a chest or build a marker closer than this to world spawn |
| `markers` | `true` | Build a marker (cairn, flag or standing stone) at the end of each leg but the last. Disabled: the next clue waits in a bottle, found within `legRadius` |
| `warmth` | `true` | Show Warmer / Colder / Very warm while holding a Treasure Map |
| `warmthRadius` | `64` | Warmer / Colder only works this close to the marker or the chest; farther away the map says faintly warm, cool or cold |
| `showAt` | `"right3"` | Where Warmer / Colder shows for players who haven't chosen: a [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp) box, `right1` to `right4` or `left1` to `left4` (top to bottom) or `middle` (under the crosshair), or `hotbar`. The boxes show at the same time as other packs' boxes. Other add-ons that redraw the line above the hotbar (waypoint and compass add-ons) can cover only `hotbar`. Players pick their own with **Where Warmer / Colder shows for me** in `/realm:prefs` |
| `veryWarm` | `40` | `Very warm` within this many blocks of the marker or the chest |
| `plainHints` | `false` | `/realm:maps` also shows the plain direction and distance from where you stand, like `(W, about 1,000 blocks)` |
| `crownsMin` | `30` | Least Crowns found with a treasure |
| `crownsMax` | `90` | Most Crowns found with a treasure |
| `rivalShare` | `0.5` | The share of the treasure's Crowns paid after losing a race to Rook to that chest (Story Questlines' `realm:map_rival`); the loot is the same |
| `reputation` | `10` | Wayfarers reputation for a treasure |
| `skillXp` | `50` | Exploration skill XP for a treasure |
| `partyShare` | `50` | Party mates ([Parties](#parties--party_bp)) near the finder each get this percent of the treasure's Crowns, on top of the finder's (0–100; 0 = none), plus the Field Journal entry and the Exploration XP |
| `partyRange` | `32` | How near (blocks, same dimension) a party mate must be when the treasure is found to share it (8–128 in game) |
| `relicChance` | `0.1` | Chance (0 to 1) that a treasure also holds a relic |
| `relics` | `compass_echoes`, `wayfarer_boots`, `sun_pendant`, `rain_charm` | The relics a treasure can hold (Relics pack ids) |
| `loot` | 10 lines | What the chest holds: `{ item, min, max, chance }`, each line rolled on its own. Default: gold ingots 2-6 (80%), iron ingots 3-8 (70%), emeralds 1-5 (50%), diamonds 1-2 (25%), a golden apple (20%), ender pearls 1-3 (30%), bottles o' enchanting 3-8 (50%), a name tag (15%), a saddle (10%), a heart of the sea (3%). A chest that rolls nothing gets the first line |

The clue, landmark and marker wording lives in `scripts/clues.js`.

Operators can change `price`, `maxHunts`, `minDistance`, `maxDistance`, `warmth`, `warmthRadius`, `markers`, `showAt`, `plainHints`, `crownsMin`, `crownsMax`, `partyShare`, `partyRange` and `avoidSpawn` in game with `/realm:config` (**Treasure Maps & Riddles**). The rest stays in `config.js`. Each player picks where Warmer / Colder shows with **Where Warmer / Colder shows for me** in `/realm:prefs`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `maps:hunts` | Player | JSON list of the player's hunts: `{ v, id, dim, pts, leg, clue, from, fromName, used, feats, near?, mark?, style?, nomark?, chest?, markUndo?, chestUndo?, rv?, tries, t }`: the planned end of each leg (the last is the treasure), the leg being followed, its clue, where the leg starts and what the clue calls it, the clue kinds and landmark kinds used, the landmark riddle, the marker (its spot and kind) or that there is none, where the chest was buried, failed chest spots and when the map was bought, and the cleanup records of its marker and chest, and when a race against Rook to its chest ends (`rv`, ms). Older hunts without `v` are upgraded when read |
| `maps:undo`, `maps:undo:<id>` | World | Blocks a marker or a buried chest placed, waiting to be put back: `{ id, dim, owner, hunt, what, due, types, blocks }`, each block as x, y, z, the kind placed and the kind (type and states) that was there before; `due` is 0 while the hunt still needs them. Checked every 5 seconds |
| `maps:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `maps:pref` | Player | The player's **Where Warmer / Colder shows for me** choice, when it differs from the realm's |
| `crowns` | Scoreboard | The map's price is taken from, and the treasure's Crowns added to, the shared Crowns balance |

### How it works

- **The route** is planned when the map is bought: a random direction (retried up to 16 times to keep the treasure away from world spawn), a distance, and evenly spaced leg ends with a sideways wander of up to a quarter of a leg. Nothing is placed then: the far land isn't loaded yet. Each clue is written when its leg starts, from the leg's start to its planned end.
- **Following:** once a second the pack checks each player with a hunt (Overworld only) against the end of their leg (the marker once it stands); the Warmer / Colder line runs every 2 seconds for players holding a map. In a box it follows the side boxes protocol (`scripts/side.js`, `realm:side`, see [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)) and shows for 45 ticks. Above the hotbar it is a steady line with rank 35: every 2 seconds it sends `realm:actionbar` `{ player, ticks: 45, from: "maps_bp", steady: 35 }`, then writes unless another pack's note or a higher-ranked line holds the bar. It keeps announcing while it waits, so build mode (30), the Chest Finder arrow (25) and the story tracker (20) wait for it; expedition (40), Relics (45) and Elytra (50) lines take priority.
- **Landmarks** are a search spread over time, like burying: the top block of every 4th column within 32 blocks of the planned end (about 200 reads), sorted into landmarks; then, for up to 4 columns at each landmark, nearest the planned end first, a marker spot check (the ground, room for the marker's blocks, 5 x 5 top blocks) or, on the last leg, a chest spot search within 8 blocks. Level ground is tried after the other landmarks, and landmarks the hunt already used last. Markers are placed with `Block.setType`. The pack listens to the safe zones protocol (`realm:zones`, its own copy of `scripts/zones.js`) and skips spots in or touching a zone.
- **Burying** is a search spread over time: at most 150 block reads every 10 ticks for all players together. It tries the spot, then rings 6, 12, 18, 24 and 30 blocks out (only the first ring at a landmark), and for each candidate reads the ground, the blocks down to the chest, and the 9 x 9 columns around it (surface +4 to -4). The chest is placed with `Block.setType` and filled through its inventory component.
- **The map** is plain paper (no map mechanics) identified by its name and its last lore line, `Map <id>`; its lore is rewritten in the inventory when the clue or landmark changes, and it's taken away when the hunt ends.
- **Cartographers:** on `realm:npc_talk` with the `cartographer` role the pack answers `realm:npc_offer` with **Buy a treasure map** (`order` 20) and, during a hunt, **Your treasure hunt** (21).
- **Legs for other packs:** `realm:map_leg` `{ player, hunt, dim, x, z, leg, legs, final }` goes out when a hunt's current leg changes (a new clue, its marker or the chest placed, the treasure moved further), checked once a second, and for every hunt again after `realm:map_leg_ping`; `{ player, hunt, gone: true }` when the hunt ends (found or given up). `x`, `z` are the chest once buried, else the marker, else the leg's planned end; `final` is the last leg. [Wanderers of the Wilds](#wanderers-of-the-wilds--wander_bp) sends Rook to a player near their own last leg; Story Questlines races to it.
- **Races:** `realm:map_rival` `{ player, hunt, until }` (Story Questlines, when a race to that hunt's chest starts; `until` in ms since 1970) is saved on the hunt. Found after `until`, the treasure's Crowns are cut to `rivalShare`. A second message can only end the race sooner.
- Events sent on finding a treasure: `realm:quest_done` `{ kind: "treasure" }`, `realm:rep_add` `{ guild: "wayfarers" }`, `realm:journal` `{ page: "places", entry: "treasure" }`, `realm:skill_xp` `{ skill: "exploration" }`, and sometimes `realm:relic_give`. Each party mate near the finder (the finder's `realm_party:<code>` tag, `Dimension.getPlayers` within `partyRange`) gets the Crowns share from the `crowns` scoreboard, `realm:journal` and `realm:skill_xp`.
- **Test hook:** the script event `realm:maps_test` `{ action: "found", player }` (a player name) finds the treasure of that player's first hunt right away, for the BDS scenario tests. It only works from the server console.

## Waystones & Inns — `waystone_bp`

Fast travel you build yourself. Put a sign saying `Waystone: <name>` next to a lodestone and tap the lodestone: it becomes a waystone. Everyone who finds it (by tapping it or walking up to it) can later travel there from any other waystone, for a few Crowns per 100 blocks after standing still for 10 seconds. Innkeepers, like Elsie from [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp), rent beds that make the inn your respawn point and leave you Well Rested, and pass on the latest news.

### How to use

1. Make a waystone: place a lodestone, put a sign next to it (on it, beside it or on the block next to it, standing or on a wall) and write `Waystone: River Gate` on the sign. Then tap the lodestone with an empty hand. Chat says `You raised the waystone River Gate!`
2. Discover waystones by tapping them or walking within 4 blocks of one: `Waystone discovered: River Gate.`
3. To travel, tap any waystone with an empty hand. Pick a waystone you've discovered; each button shows how far it is and what it costs (`240m NE, 3 Crowns`).
4. Stand still for 10 seconds while the countdown runs above the hotbar (`Traveling to River Gate in 7...`). Moving more than a block or getting hurt cancels the trip. The screen fades and you arrive next to the other waystone; the trip is paid then.
5. Traveling with your [party](#parties--party_bp)? Mates standing within 6 blocks of you when you start a trip come along: they stand still through the same countdown and each pays their own fare. A mate who walks away stays behind.
6. Run `/realm:waystones` for the waystone menu: **My waystones** (also `/realm:waystones_list`) lists the waystones you've discovered and how far they are.
7. At an inn, tap the innkeeper: **Rent a bed** (10 Crowns) makes the inn your respawn point and gives you Well Rested; **Hear the news** tells what's happened lately (tornadoes, meteors, caravans...).
8. **Operators:** **Remove a waystone** in `/realm:waystones` lists every waystone, nearest first, to pick from; or look at a waystone's lodestone or sign and run `/realm:waystones_remove`. `/realm:config` → **Waystones & Inns** sets who can make waystones, whether travel costs Crowns or XP levels and how much, the wait, travel between dimensions and from anywhere, whether party mates come along (and how near they must stand), and the inn's price and Well Rested time.

### What players see

- **Making a waystone:** an empty-hand tap on a lodestone with a `Waystone:` sign within one block (any of the 26 blocks around it, front or back of the sign) registers it under the name after `Waystone:` (or after `Waystone` on the first line, with the name on the lines below; up to 24 characters; color codes and other symbols are dropped). Any player can (`whoCanCreate`, or operators only). Names are unique: `There's already a waystone named River Gate.` A sign with nothing after `Waystone:` says `Write a name after Waystone: on the sign`, and a lodestone with no such sign says `Put a sign saying Waystone: <name> next to this lodestone, then tap it again to make a waystone.` The realm keeps at most 150 waystones (`maxWaystones`). Changing the sign later doesn't rename the waystone.
- **Discovering:** tapping a waystone or coming within 4 blocks of it (`discoverRadius`) adds it to your list, with a chime, and as a `places` entry in the [Field Journal](#field-journal--journal_bp) (`waystone_river_gate`). The one who makes a waystone discovers it at once.
- **In a land claim:** a lodestone in someone else's [land claim](#land-claims--claims_bp) can't be made into a waystone, or traveled from, by anyone but that claim's players (the tap is refused: `This land is claimed by Sam`). Walking up to it still discovers it, so others can travel there from another waystone.
- **Travel menu** (tap a waystone): `Where to? You have 42 Crowns.` and a button per discovered waystone, nearest first: `River Gate` / `240m NE, 3 Crowns`, or `Nether, 10 Crowns` for one in another dimension.
- **Cost:** 1 Crown per 100 blocks (`costPer100`), rounded up, at least 1 (`minCost`); 10 to another dimension (`crossDimensionCost`, or not offered with `crossDimension` disabled). With `currency` set to `levels`, trips cost XP levels instead. The cost is checked when you choose and taken when you arrive (`Paid 3 Crowns for the trip to River Gate.`).
- **The wait:** 10 seconds (`channelSeconds`, 0 = at once): `Traveling to River Gate in 10 seconds. Stand still.` in chat and a countdown above the hotbar. Moving more than 1 block, changing dimension or taking any damage cancels it: `You moved: the trip to River Gate is canceled.` Half a second before the jump the screen fades to dark blue and back. Tapping a waystone (or `/realm:waystones` with `travelAnywhere`) during the countdown says `You're already traveling to River Gate. Stand still.`
- **Party travel** (`partyTravel`): when a player in a [party](#parties--party_bp) starts a trip, online mates in the same dimension within 6 blocks (`partyRadius`) who aren't traveling already come along. The traveler's line adds who comes (`Traveling to River Gate in 10 seconds. Bob, Dan come along. Stand still.`), and each mate gets `[Party] Ann is traveling to River Gate in 10 seconds: stand still to come along (3 Crowns), or walk away to stay.` Each mate has their own countdown, ending with the traveler's, and pays their own fare, priced from where they stand (with their own Waystone Friend discount), when they arrive.
  - A mate who can't pay is told and stays: `Ann is traveling to River Gate, but you can't come along: the trip costs 3 Crowns. You have 1 Crown.`
  - A mate who moves or gets hurt stays, and the others still go: `You moved, so you stay here: Ann travels to River Gate without you.`
  - When the traveler's own trip is canceled, every mate coming along stays too: `Ann's trip to River Gate is canceled: you stay here.` (`The trip was canceled: you stay here.` when the traveler logs off).
  - When the traveler's own jump fails on arrival (the waystone is gone or walled in, they can't pay, or the teleport fails), the mates stay too and pay nothing: `Ann's trip to River Gate didn't happen: you stay here.`
  - Mates can come along to a waystone they haven't discovered; arriving there discovers it the usual way.
- **Arriving:** you land beside the other waystone's lodestone, facing it, on a free spot with solid floor (or, for a waystone in a cellar, the first open space straight above it); if its surroundings aren't loaded yet you land on top of the lodestone and are moved beside it once they load. If you'd land inside a block, in lava, or over a drop where the lodestone used to be, you're moved to a free spot, and when there's none you're sent back to where you started with the trip paid back (`There's no safe place to stand at River Gate, so the waystone sent you back.`). A waystone that's loaded and walled in on every side isn't traveled to at all, and nothing is paid.
- **A broken waystone:** breaking or blowing up its lodestone removes the waystone (`The waystone River Gate is gone.`). A lodestone that vanished another way (pistons, commands) is noticed when someone is within 96 blocks, or when someone arrives there. Trips on the way to it are canceled.
- **`/realm:waystones`:** a menu saying how many waystones you've discovered, with **My waystones** (**Travel** with `travelAnywhere` enabled) and, for operators, **Remove a waystone** (asks first; the lodestone and sign stay).
- **`/realm:waystones_list`** (the menu's first button): lists your discovered waystones with distance and direction. You can't travel from it unless `travelAnywhere` is enabled; then it opens the travel menu, priced from where you stand (or from the waystone you're standing at).
- **Inns** (tap an NPC with the `innkeeper` role, `npcRole`):
  - **Rent a bed** (10 [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp), `bedPrice`): your respawn point becomes the innkeeper's spot, until you sleep in a bed of your own, and you're Well Rested: Health Boost I (2 extra hearts) for 60 minutes (`wellRestedMinutes`), plus a moment of Saturation and Regeneration to fill them, all without particles. Chat says `-10 Crowns (A bed at the inn)` and `You rest at the inn. Well Rested: 2 extra hearts for 60 minutes.` Beds can only be rented in the Overworld. Dying ends Well Rested, like any effect.
  - **Hear the news:** the latest 6 (`newsKept`) sky events other packs announced, newest first, like `3h ago: A tornado tore across the land (240m NE of here)` or the event's own text: tornadoes, rainbows, meteors, blood and harvest moons, auroras, storms, caravans and fishing tournaments. Nothing yet: `Nothing new lately. Quiet times, and I'm not complaining.`
- **Elsie's friends:** a player who is a Friend of Elsie ([Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)) pays 10% less for a bed (10 to 9 Crowns by default, rounded down), from `realm:affinity`.
- **Waystone Friend:** a Pathfinder with the Waystone Friend talent ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp) Callings, `bonus.waystoneOff` in `realm:calling`) pays 25% less for trips (rounded down, at least 1 when the trip isn't free).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:waystones` | Everyone | The waystone menu: your waystones, and for operators, remove a waystone from a list |
| `/realm:waystones_list` | Everyone | Lists the waystones you've discovered, with distance and direction. With travel from anywhere enabled (default off, `travelAnywhere`), opens the travel menu instead |
| `/realm:waystones_remove` | Operators | Removes the waystone whose lodestone or sign you're looking at (within 8 blocks). The lodestone and sign stay |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `whoCanCreate` | `"everyone"` | Who can make a waystone: `everyone` or `operators` |
| `currency` | `"crowns"` | What travel costs: `crowns` or `levels` (XP levels) |
| `costPer100` | `1` | Cost per 100 blocks, rounded up |
| `minCost` | `1` | The least a trip costs |
| `crossDimension` | `true` | Allow travel between waystones in different dimensions |
| `crossDimensionCost` | `10` | What a trip to another dimension costs (instead of the distance cost) |
| `channelSeconds` | `10` | Seconds to stand still before traveling (0 = at once) |
| `travelAnywhere` | `false` | `/realm:waystones` opens the travel menu anywhere |
| `partyTravel` | `true` | Online party mates ([Parties](#parties--party_bp)) standing within `partyRadius` of a player who starts a trip come along, through the same countdown, each paying their own fare |
| `partyRadius` | `6` | How near (blocks) a party mate must stand to come along (2–16 in game) |
| `discoverRadius` | `4` | Standing this close (blocks) to a waystone discovers it |
| `maxWaystones` | `150` | Most waystones the realm keeps |
| `npcRole` | `"innkeeper"` | The NPC role whose NPCs rent beds and tell the news |
| `bedPrice` | `10` | Crowns a bed at the inn costs (0 = free) |
| `wellRestedMinutes` | `60` | How long Well Rested (Health Boost I) lasts, in minutes; 0 = no Well Rested |
| `newsKept` | `6` | How many of the latest sky events the innkeeper remembers |

Operators can change `whoCanCreate`, `currency`, `costPer100`, `minCost`, `crossDimension`, `crossDimensionCost`, `channelSeconds`, `travelAnywhere`, `partyTravel`, `partyRadius`, `bedPrice` and `wellRestedMinutes` in game with `/realm:config` (**Waystones & Inns**). The rest stays in `config.js`. There are no player preferences.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `waystone:list` | World | JSON list of waystones: `{ i, n, d, x, y, z, by, t }` (id, name, dimension, lodestone position, who made it, when) |
| `waystone:next` | World | The next waystone id |
| `waystone:known` | Player | JSON list of the waystone ids the player discovered |
| `waystone:news` | World | JSON list of the latest sky events: `{ k, t, text?, d?, x?, z? }` (kind, when, text, dimension, place) |
| `waystone:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |
| `crowns` | Scoreboard | Trips (with `currency` `crowns`) and beds are paid from the shared Crowns balance |

### How it works

- **Taps:** `beforeEvents.playerInteractWithBlock` with an empty hand on a lodestone (first event only); the work happens a tick later. The sign is read with the stable `minecraft:sign` block component (`getText`, front then back) on the 26 blocks around the lodestone.
- **Discovery** checks every online player against the waystones in their dimension once a second (distance math only, no block reads).
- **Removal:** `afterEvents.playerBreakBlock` and `afterEvents.blockExplode` on a registered lodestone; every 5 seconds up to 8 waystones within 96 blocks of a player are checked for their lodestone; arriving checks the one you traveled to.
- **The trip** is followed every 5 ticks: distance from where it started (over 1 block cancels) and `afterEvents.entityHurt`. Then `player.camera.fade`, the cost, and `player.teleport` with the destination dimension. The landing spot is checked for free feet and head room and a solid, safe floor (no lava, fire, magma, cactus, powder snow or water) on the 12 blocks around the lodestone at its height, one above and one below, then on top of it and up to 40 blocks straight above it; 10, 40 and 100 ticks after landing the pack checks the player's feet, head and the block under them again in case the area wasn't loaded. The countdown sends `realm:actionbar` first, so the [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) steps aside.
- **Party travel:** starting a trip looks for players with the traveler's `realm_party:<code>` tag within `partyRadius` (`Dimension.getPlayers`) and gives each who can pay a trip of their own to the same waystone, with the same countdown, marked with the traveler as its leader. A follower's trip ends on its own when they move or get hurt; the leader's ending without a jump (canceled, logged off, or a failed arrival) ends every follower's, so the mates pay nothing. Followers needn't have discovered the waystone.
- **Inns:** on `realm:npc_talk` with the `innkeeper` role the pack answers `realm:npc_offer` with **Rent a bed** (`order` 20) and **Hear the news** (21). Renting finds the innkeeper (the nearest `minecraft:npc` with its `realm:npc_id:<id>` tag within 16 blocks) and sets the player's spawn point there with `Player.setSpawnPoint`. The news is every `realm:sky_event` the pack hears (the same kind twice within a minute counts once), kept in the world.
- Events sent: `realm:journal` `{ page: "places", entry: "waystone_<name>" }` on discovery; `realm:waystones_known` `{ player, part, parts, list }` (the waystones that player knows) on discovery, when a known one is removed and on `realm:waystones_known_ping` `{ player? }`, for the [Minimap](#minimap--map_bp).
- **Scenario tests:** `/scriptevent realm:waystone_test {"action":"tap","player":"<name>","x":..,"y":..,"z":..}` taps a waystone for a player without a hand tap (simulated players can't tap with an empty hand), for the test harness. It's only honored from the server console or an operator.

---

## Expeditions — `expedition_bp`

Dungeon runs for you and your [party](#parties--party_bp), in the spirit of Diablo's Nightmare Dungeons. Pick one of eight dungeons (the Crypt, the Drowned Vault, Frost Hollow, the Nether Forge, the Sculk Depths, the Pillager Keep, the Spider Nest or the Ender Spire) and a difficulty: **Easy**, **Normal**, **Hard**, or **Nightmare tiers 1 to 20**, which you unlock one by one by clearing the tier below. A fresh dungeon is built for you deep underground: 6 to 18 rooms joined by corridors, with waves of mobs, elite halls, trap halls, shrines, puzzles (nine kinds), vertical shafts, hidden side caches, a boss and treasure. Rooms come in many shapes (L, T, cross, round, octagon, a ring around a pillar, long halls, halls split by walls, raised ledges, cover) and grow with the difficulty, and the way out is always across the room from the way in. For a longer run, the **Gauntlet** has 14 rooms, harder fights and a sanctuary every 5 rooms where each player picks one of three **boons**, optionally with a **fixed loadout** (your own items are stored safely and you run with a starter kit). Higher tiers have more rooms and waves, tougher and armored mobs, champions, tall rooms you climb, build or fly up, and **affixes** that change the run (Frenzied, Volcanic, Lightning Storm...). The clock runs from the moment you arrive; the fastest clears of each dungeon and difficulty go on a leaderboard. Finishing pays [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp), Warden reputation in [Guilds & Reputation](#guilds--reputation--guilds_bp), a page in the [Field Journal](#field-journal--journal_bp), sometimes a [relic](#relics--relics_bp), and bosses and champions may drop a **Nightmare Sigil** that opens one exact run. No structure files: every dungeon is generated from a random seed, and the ground is filled back in after each run, so the next one is new.

### How to use

1. Run `/realm:expedition` and tap **Start an expedition**. Pick a dungeon, then a difficulty: Easy, Normal and Hard are open to everyone; **Nightmare 1** unlocks when you clear Hard, and each Nightmare tier unlocks the next.
2. The last screen shows what the run is like: rooms, time limit, waves, how strong the mobs are, the **affixes** (Nightmare only) and the rewards. Tap **Start**, or **Reroll affixes** (costs 25 Crowns, `rerollCost`) for a different set. If you're in a party, every party member online is asked, wherever they are (any distance, any dimension; `partyRadius`): a popup on their screen says `Ann is starting an expedition: Crypt (Nightmare 5). ... Join?`, and they have 20 seconds to tap **Join** (`confirmSeconds`).
3. The screen fades and you arrive in the entry room, with the clock running. The bar above the hotbar shows the dungeon, the time, what to do next and the affixes, like `Crypt N5 2:41/24:00 | Room 3/10: defeat the wave (2 left)`.
4. Walk into each room. The bars on the way out rise once the room is done (`The bars rise. Onward!`):
   - **Combat** and **elite** rooms send waves (`Wave 1 of 4!`): kill every mob. Elite halls bring a champion every wave.
   - **Puzzle** rooms explain themselves on signs and in chat: levers, a memory sequence, a safe path of pressure plates, target practice, lights out, a color riddle, a climb, a button rush or a riddle (see below).
   - **Trap halls**: the door out is already open, but it's on the far side and walls make the way wind through the hall. Run for it while flames flicker on the floor along the way (they burst a moment later), arrows fly from the walls across it, and pits cross it (soul sand at the bottom, magma from Nightmare 1): jump them.
   - **Shrines**: press one of three buttons: a **Blessing** for the rest of the run, a **curse** (one more affix, but more treasure and Crowns), or pass by.
   - **Shafts** (Nightmare 3 and up): the way on is high up the wall. There's no ladder: jump up the ledges and stepping stones, pillar up with your own blocks, or fly with an elytra. Fall and you get 3 seconds of Slow Falling and drift gently back to the floor to try again. At the top, drop down the chute into the pool.
   - **Side rooms** (Nightmare): an open doorway off a room leads to a puzzle; solve it for a hidden cache chest.
5. In the boss room the boss appears with its name as a title; on high tiers it calls adds onto the balconies. Defeat it: `Expedition complete` and your time fill the screen, everyone still in the dungeon is paid, and the treasure room opens. You have 90 seconds (`exitSeconds`) to empty the chests; opening a chest when less than 20 seconds are left gives you 20 more (up to 2 minutes more in all). Press the gold button by the treasure room's far wall (or run `/realm:expedition_leave`) to go back sooner. When the time is up you're taken back to where you started, and whatever is still in the chests comes with you (in your inventory, or at your feet when it's full); the last player to leave early takes what's left.
6. **Gauntlet:** run `/realm:expedition_gauntlet` (or **Start a Gauntlet** in `/realm:expedition`), pick a dungeon and a difficulty you've unlocked. The preview has a **Fixed loadout** switch (Disabled by default, `loadoutDefault`): enabled, everyone's own inventory, armor and offhand are stored away when the run starts and they get a starter kit instead; it all comes back exactly when they return. Every 5 rooms (`boonEvery`) is a **sanctuary**: a form shows each player three boons, and the bars rise once everyone has picked (or a minute after the first pick). Closed it by mistake? Press the button on the altar, or open `/realm:expedition` → **Choose your boon**.
7. **Nightmare Sigils** dropped by bosses and champions open one exact run: use the sigil (right-click) or pick it under **Use a Nightmare Sigil** in `/realm:expedition`. It works even before you've unlocked its tier, and it's used up when the run starts (a run called off before anyone goes in, say because the site isn't safe, gives it back).
8. To give up, run `/realm:expedition_leave` (or **Leave the expedition** in `/realm:expedition`, which asks first). If you die you're out of the run, you respawn as usual and are sent back to where you started, and the items you dropped are given back (also if you die in the moment after leaving, before you're sent back).
9. `/realm:expedition` → **Leaderboards** shows the fastest clears of each dungeon at each difficulty, the **Highest tiers** players have cleared, the **Recent runs** and the best **Gauntlets**, each player with their [Skills](#skills--skills_bp) Calling (`Ann (Delver), Bo`); **My progress** shows what you've unlocked, your best and your own recent runs.
10. **Operators:** stand somewhere far from spawn and from anyone's builds and mines, and run `/realm:expedition_site` once (or `/realm:expedition_site <x> <z>`, or **Operator tools** → **Set the site where I stand**). Dungeons are built deep underground around that spot (up to 120 by 120 blocks, y -41 to -8), and the site is refused if it's within 124 blocks of world spawn or if anything that isn't natural rock, ore, dirt, gravel, water, lava or cave plants is in the way. With `slots` above 1, a second or third dungeon that would come within `avoidSpawn` of world spawn is never used, and setting the site says so. Where the ground at the site is below the dungeon (a flat world, a deep valley) you're warned: the dungeon would be built above the ground. Before removing the pack, end every run with `/realm:expedition_reset`, so nobody is left in a sealed dungeon. `/realm:expedition_reset` ends a run in progress and fills the dungeon back in (**Operator tools** → **End every expedition and reset** does the same after asking, with the runs in progress listed). **Operator tools** also has **Create a Nightmare Sigil** (any dungeon, tier and affixes) and **Unlock every tier for me**. `/realm:config` → **Expeditions** sets the party size, the time limit, the time at the treasure, the highest tier, building, the reroll cost, the Gauntlet's length and boons, and more.

### What players see

- **Difficulties and tiers.** Every dungeon can be played at every difficulty you've unlocked. Clearing Hard unlocks Nightmare 1; clearing Nightmare N unlocks N + 1, up to Nightmare 20 (`maxTier`). Progress is per player; the leader's unlocks decide what can be started (party members can join any run). How each level scales (time with the default 20 minutes per 7 rooms; mobs per wave get one more for every two players after the first):

  | Level | Rooms | Time (min) | Waves | Mobs per wave | Monster buffs | Elites / champion chance per wave | Affixes | Boss | Crowns / treasure | Room mix (as room allows) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Easy | 6-8 | 17-23 | 2 | 2-3 | none | 0 / 0% | 0 | x1.0 health | x1.00 / x1.0 | 1 puzzle |
  | Normal | 6-8 | 17-23 | 3 | 2-3 | none | 0 / 0% | 0 | x1.2 health | x1.25 / x1.1 | 1 puzzle, 1 trap |
  | Hard | 7-9 | 20-26 | 4 | 2-3 | Strength 1 | 1 / 0% | 0 | x1.4 health | x1.50 / x1.2 | 1 puzzle, 1 trap, shrine (75%), 1 elite |
  | Nightmare 1 | 7-9 | 20-25 | 4 | 3-4 | +4 health, Strength 1 | 1 / 14% | 1 | x1.6 health | x1.75 / x1.3 | as Hard, 1 side cache |
  | Nightmare 3 | 8-10 | 22-28 | 4 | 3-4 | +8 health, Strength 1, chainmail armor (31%) | 1 / 21% | 1 | x2.0 health | x2.25 / x1.5 | as above, 1 shaft, tall rooms 41% up to 14 high |
  | Nightmare 5 | 9-11 | 24-30 | 4 | 4-5 | +12 health, Strength 1, Speed 1, chainmail (38%) | 1 / 28% | 2 | x2.4 health, 2 adds every 20 s | x2.75 / x1.7 | tall rooms 45% up to 18 high |
  | Nightmare 6 | 9-12 | 24-32 | 5 | 4-5 | +12 health, Resistance 1, Strength 1, Speed 1, chainmail (41%) | 2 / 31% | 2 | x2.6, 2 adds | x3.00 / x1.8 | 2 puzzles, up to 20 high |
  | Nightmare 8 | 10-13 | 26-34 | 5 | 5-6 | +16 health, Resistance 1, Strength 2, Speed 1, iron (48%) | 2 / 38% | 2 | x3.0, 2 adds | x3.50 / x2.0 | 2 elite halls, up to 24 high |
  | Nightmare 10 | 10-13 | 26-33 | 5 | 6-7 | +20 health, Resistance 1, Strength 2, Speed 1, iron (55%) | 2 / 45% | 3 | x3.4, 3 adds | x4.00 / x2.2 | 2 traps, 2 side caches, up to 28 high |
  | Nightmare 12 | 11-14 | 28-35 | 6 | 6-7 | +24 health, Resistance 1, Strength 2, Speed 1, diamond (62%) | 3 / 52% | 3 | x3.8, 3 adds | x4.50 / x2.4 | up to 30 high |
  | Nightmare 15 | 12-16 | 29-39 | 6 | 7-8 | +32 health, Resistance 1, Strength 3, Speed 2, diamond (73%) | 3 / 63% | 4 | x4.4, 4 adds | x5.25 / x2.7 | 3 puzzles, 2 shafts |
  | Nightmare 17 | 13-17 | 31-40 | 7 | 8-9 | +36 health, Resistance 2, Strength 3, Speed 2, netherite (80%) | 3 / 70% | 4 | x4.8, 4 adds | x5.75 / x2.9 | 3 elite halls |
  | Nightmare 20 | 14-18 | 32-41 | 7 | 9-10 | +40 health, Resistance 2, Strength 3, Speed 2, netherite (90%) | 4 / 80% | 4 | x5.4, 5 adds | x6.50 / x3.2 | 3 puzzles, 2 traps, shrine, 3 elite, 2 shafts, 2 side caches, tall rooms 75% |

  Tiers in between follow the same steps. The grid grows from 3 by 3 to 5 by 5 cells for the bigger runs. Elite mobs (`Elite Zombie`) have extra health and Strength; champions (`Champion Skeleton`, or a named champion from the [Champions](#champions--elite_bp) pack) much more. Every dungeon mob has Fire Resistance. At most 18 dungeon mobs (`mobCap`) are alive at once.
- **Affixes** (Nightmare runs: 1 at tiers 1-4, 2 at 5-9, 3 at 10-14, 4 at 15-20, rolled by weight, never twice; plus a 15% chance of the Blessing). They're shown before you start, on a sign in the entry room, in chat and on the bar above the hotbar:

  | Affix | From tier | What it does |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Frenzied` | 1 | Mobs (and the boss) get Speed, one level more |
  | `Bulwark` | 1 | Mobs and the boss get one more level of Resistance |
  | `Swarming` | 1 | Half again as many mobs in every wave |
  | `Shrouded` | 1 | Darkness pulses over everyone in the dungeon every 20 seconds or so |
  | `Frozen` | 1 | Snowflake patches appear at your feet, then slow anyone standing in them for about 6 seconds |
  | `Hunger` | 1 | Hunger while fighting (stronger from tier 12) |
  | `Volcanic` | 3 | Flames flicker on the floor around you for 2 seconds, then fire bursts there (real fire on stone floors, put out after 4 seconds; on wooden floors only the burn) |
  | `Explosive Death` | 3 | A mob hisses when it dies and bursts a second later: damage within 3 blocks, no block damage |
  | `Backup` | 3 | A mob brought below half health calls one more mob, once |
  | `Vampiric` | 5 | Mobs heal half the damage they deal you |
  | `Thorned` | 5 | Hitting a mob in melee hurts you a little (1, 2 from tier 10) |
  | `Champion Packs` | 5 | Every wave brings a champion |
  | `Venomous` | 5 | Mob hits poison you (Wither from tier 15) |
  | `Arcane Beams` | 7 | A line of blue sparks crosses the room through you; 2 seconds later it burns anyone still on it |
  | `Lightning Storm` | 7 | Sparks circle your spot; 2 seconds later lightning strikes there (damage, no fire) |
  | `Blinding` | 10 | Bursts of blindness during fights |
  | `Juggernaut` | 10 | Mobs have far more health, the boss a third more |
  | `Blessing` | 1 (15% chance, extra) | Half again as much treasure and a quarter more Crowns |

- **Dungeons** (from `dungeons`; mobs join the pool from the level shown):

  | Dungeon | Mobs | Flyers in tall rooms | Boss (extra health) | Built of | Crowns |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Crypt | zombies, skeletons; husks (Hard), zombie villagers (N1), wither skeletons (N5), witches (N8) | vexes | `The Crypt Lord` (wither skeleton, +40) | deepslate bricks, soul lanterns, cobwebs | 40 |
  | Drowned Vault | drowned; zombies (Normal), bogged (N2), witches (N7) | none | `The Tide Keeper` (drowned, +60) | prismarine, sea lanterns in the floor | 60 |
  | Frost Hollow | strays, skeletons; zombies (Normal), breezes (N6) | breezes | `The Frost Archer` (stray, +80) | packed ice, snow, blue ice | 90 |
  | Nether Forge | magma cubes, blazes; wither skeletons (Hard), zoglins (N4) | blazes | `The Forge Heart` (blaze, +80) | polished blackstone, basalt, gilded blackstone, magma in the floor | 90 |
  | Sculk Depths | zombies, silverfish; endermites (Normal), husks (N1), bogged (N4) | vexes | `The Listener` (bogged, +90) | deepslate tiles, sculk floor, soul lanterns | 100 |
  | Pillager Keep | pillagers, vindicators; witches (N1), evokers (N3), ravagers (N10) | vexes | `The Warlord's Ravager` (ravager, +60) | stone bricks, spruce planks, dark oak | 70 |
  | Spider Nest | spiders, cave spiders; skeletons (Hard), bogged (N6), witches (N10) | none | `The Brood Mother` (spider, +60) | mossy stone bricks, lots of cobwebs | 50 |
  | Ender Spire | endermen, endermites; skeletons (Hard), shulkers (N2) | vexes | `The Starless Walker` (enderman, +100) | purpur, end stone bricks, end rods | 110 |

  Each dungeon has a line of lore on a sign in its entry room (`Where the town buried what it chose to forget.`). No wardens ever spawn. Cobwebs can be cut.
- **Rooms.** Every run starts with the entry room and ends with the boss room and the treasure room; in between come at least two combat rooms and the rest of the level's room mix, shuffled. Rooms are 15 by 15 to 19 by 19 blocks inside (17 by 17 at most on Easy; the entry and treasure rooms 15, puzzles and shafts 15 or 17, fights and trap halls 17 to 19, the boss room the biggest), 5 high (trap halls 5 or 6, some fights 8 high from Hard), joined by corridors 3 wide that turn to meet each door. The door in and the door out are pushed apart: to opposite ends of the room, or, when they're on walls that meet, each toward the far end of its wall, so you always cross the room (at least the room's half width plus 3 blocks of walking; a trap hall's way through is longer still). Fights, trap halls, shrines, sanctuaries, the entry and the boss room take a shape:

  | Shape | What it is | Rooms |
  |---|---|---|
  | Plain | The open square (fights may get 4 cover pillars or a low ring wall) | Any |
  | L, T | One corner, or two on one side, walled off | Fights, trap halls |
  | Cross | All four corners walled off: arms 5 to 9 wide | Fights, trap halls, entry, shrines, sanctuaries |
  | Octagon, round | Corners cut off diagonally, or a round hall | Fights, boss, entry, shrines, sanctuaries |
  | Ring | A big square or diamond pillar in the middle | Fights (also tall ones), trap halls, boss |
  | Pillars | A grid of pillars, 1 or 2 blocks thick | Fights (also tall ones), boss |
  | Long hall | Walls along two sides leave a hall 7 to 9 wide | Fights |
  | Split hall | 1 or 2 walls (2 or 3 in trap halls) from the sides partway across, so the way winds | Fights, trap halls (most often) |

  Low rooms with a fight may also get cover (low walls and crates) and a **raised ledge** 2 blocks high along a wall without a door, with a step up; mobs spawn on it too. Tall rooms keep their walls clear for the balconies (plain, ring or pillars). Every shape is checked before it's built: each door, chest, button and spawn spot can be walked to; a room that fails gets another shape, and the plain square last.

  | Room | What happens | Done when |
  |---|---|---|
  | Entry | Signs: the dungeon and level, its lore, the affixes | (its door is open) |
  | Combat | Waves of the dungeon's mobs, with elites and maybe a champion; some rooms have cover pillars or a low ring wall; tall rooms have balconies where mobs spawn too, and flyers; higher balconies have ladders, and the lowest is often (about 60% of the time) reached by jumping up ledges instead | Every mob of the last wave is dead |
  | Elite hall | One wave fewer, fewer mobs, one more elite each, and a champion every wave (`Elite guards wake in this hall...`) | Last wave dead |
  | Puzzle | One of nine puzzles (below) | Solved |
  | Trap hall | The exit is open at once, on the far side, usually behind walls that make the way wind; flame patches telegraphed by flickering flames along the way (often just ahead of you), arrow volleys across it from the walls telegraphed by sparks, and 1-block pits across it (soul sand, magma from Nightmare 1; up to 4 at high tiers) | Someone reaches the far door |
  | Shrine | Three buttons: the Blessing (Vigor: extra hearts, Swiftness, Ward: Resistance, Haste: Haste and Strength, or Fortune: a quarter more treasure), a curse (one more affix for the rest of the run; treasure x1.4 and Crowns x1.25), or pass by. The effects last until the run ends or you leave it | Someone presses a button |
  | Shaft (N3+) | 17 to 30 blocks high; the exit is in the wall near the top, over a landing. No ladder: a route of ledges climbs the walls to it, mostly 1 block up over a gap of 1 or 2 blocks, some flat jumps of 2 (3 from tier 8), and some stepping stones 1 block out from the wall; flyers harass you. A member falling fast gets 3 seconds of Slow Falling and drifts back to the floor to try again. Over the exit, a chute drops into a pool, so the fall never hurts | Someone stands on the landing |
  | Side cache (N1+) | An open doorway off a room leads to a puzzle; solving it puts a chest with extra loot in the side room | Optional |
  | Boss | The boss, with its name as a title. From Normal it calls its guards once at half health; from N5 it calls adds every 20 seconds. Tall arenas (N3+) have balconies on several levels | The boss dies |
  | Sanctuary (Gauntlet) | An altar with a button: each player picks one of three boons in a form (the button shows it again) | Everyone has picked, or a minute after the first pick |
| Treasure | The treasure chest (two from N6 or with 12 rooms or more, as in every default Gauntlet; three with both), and a gold button by the far wall under a `Leave now` sign that takes you back at once | (open after the boss) |

- **Puzzles** (each run picks different kinds where it can; signs and chat explain each one, and none can get stuck):

  | Puzzle | From | How it works |
  |---|---|---|
  | Lever logic | Easy | Four levers on red, blue, yellow and green wool; clue signs like `2 levers are on` and `RED and GREEN differ` always fit exactly one setting (at least one lever on). Pulling a lever shows all four above the hotbar |
  | Memory | Easy | The game flashes the four colored pillars in a sequence (3 long on Easy up to 8 at Nightmare 20, never one color twice in a row) with notes; press the buttons on top in the same order. A wrong press replays it; the gold button shows it again |
  | Color riddle | Easy | Four pillars of wool with a button each; each press changes the color (red, blue, yellow, green, white, black). The sign in front of each says `is the color of lapis lazuli`: match them all |
  | Riddle | Easy | A riddle on the signs and in chat, and 3 answer buttons (4 from N4) labeled by signs. A wrong answer locks the buttons for 6 seconds and spawns mobs |
  | Lights out | Easy | A 3 by 3 panel of lamps with a button on each; a button flips its lamp and the ones next to it. Light all nine (every start can be solved) |
  | Safe path | Normal | A 4 by 4 grid of pressure plates (5 by 5 from N6). The safe path flashes plate by plate; step on its plates in order from the near row to the far row. A wrong plate starts you over (and stings a little in Nightmare runs); the gold button shows the path again |
  | Target practice | Normal | 3 to 7 target blocks set in the walls, some high up. Hit each with an arrow, snowball or trident; everyone is given 16 snowballs, and anyone in the room who runs out (or comes in late) gets 16 more within a few seconds |
  | Button rush | Normal | 4 to 8 buttons around the walls: press them all within a time limit from the first press (about 3 seconds per button, a little less at high tiers), or they reset |
  | Climb | Normal | A tall room: jump up ledges and stepping stones along the walls to a button at the top (8 to 24 blocks up). There's no ladder; fall and you get 3 seconds of Slow Falling, drift back to the floor and start again; or pillar up with your own blocks where building is allowed |

- **The Gauntlet** (`gauntletEnabled`): a long run of 14 rooms (`gauntletRooms`, 10 to 20) at the difficulty you pick, with a sanctuary every 5 rooms (`boonEvery`), each behind an elite hall, and one more puzzle, trap hall and shrine than a run at that level. It's harder: one more wave and one more mob per wave, one more elite from Normal, champions 10% more often from Normal, and the boss has 30% more health. It pays more: Crowns times the rooms / 8 and another quarter (x2.2 for 14 rooms), half again as much treasure (and a second chest), and 10% more relic chance. The time limit is the rooms' time plus 15%. Clearing one unlocks the next tier like any run; Gauntlet clears aren't on the fastest-clear boards but on their own **Gauntlets** board (hardest first, then fastest), and the history marks them `Gauntlet`. Sigils always open a normal run.

  Boons (three different ones offered, by rarity: common 10, rare 5, epic 2; ones you have aren't offered again, except gear, food and wolves). Effects last until the run's time is up and are taken away when you leave it; boon gear (marked `Expedition gear: stays in the dungeon`) is taken away when you come back, food, arrows and totems are yours:

  | Boon | Rarity | What it gives |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Vitality` | common | Health Boost 2 (2 extra hearts) |
  | `Swiftness` | common | Speed |
  | `Iron Skin` | common | Resistance |
  | `Might` | common | Strength |
  | `Springheel` | common | Jump Boost 2 |
  | `Fire Ward` | common | Fire Resistance and Night Vision |
  | `Rations` | common | 3 golden apples and 16 steaks |
  | `Quiver` | common | A Power 3 bow (boon gear) and 48 arrows |
  | `Regeneration` | rare | Regeneration |
  | `Champion's Blade` | rare | A Sharpness 4 sword (iron, diamond from N8, netherite from N15; boon gear) |
  | `Guardian Plate` | rare | A Protection 4 chestplate (same metals; boon gear) |
  | `Second Wind` | rare | A totem of undying |
  | `Bloodthirst` | rare | Heal 1.5 hearts for each dungeon monster you kill |
  | `Greed` | rare | Half again as many Crowns when you finish |
  | `Wolf Pack` | rare | Two tame wolves with extra health and Resistance, removed when the run ends |
  | `Vampire's Edge` | epic | Heal a fifth of the melee damage you deal to dungeon monsters |
  | `Giant's Heart` | epic | Health Boost 4 (8 extra hearts) |
  | `Berserker` | epic | Strength 2 and Speed |
  | `Midas Touch` | epic | Twice the Crowns when you finish (with Greed: x3) |
  | `Golden Feast` | epic | An enchanted golden apple and 4 golden apples |

  **Fixed loadout** (the leader's switch in the preview; party members are told when asked to join): as you're taken in, everything you carry (all 36 inventory slots, armor and offhand, with enchantments, names, lore and durability) is stored, then you get the kit (`gauntletKit`): a Sharpness 1 iron sword (Sharpness 2 diamond from N8), a Power 1 bow, 32 arrows, a shield, Protection 1 iron armor (Protection 2 diamond from N8), 16 steaks, 2 golden apples, and 64 cobbled deepslate from Nightmare 1. When you come back (finished, failed, left, died, or after you rejoin or the server restarted) the whole kit (food, arrows and blocks too) and boon gear are taken away, your own items go back into the slots they came from (into the inventory when that slot is taken now, at your feet when it's full: nothing is overwritten), then the items you dropped and the leftover treasure. Everything in the kit is marked `Expedition gear: stays in the dungeon`, so leaving at once leaves you with nothing extra. Treasure and boon food and totems you got on the way are yours to keep. If your items can't be stored, you keep your own gear for the run and are told so.
- **Building** (from Nightmare 1, `buildFromTier`, while `allowBuilding` is on): blocks you place in the dungeon stay, so you can pillar up a shaft, bridge between balconies or wall yourself in, and you can break your own blocks again (also sand or gravel that fell, or a block an enderman moved, as long as it's a kind someone placed this run and not one the dungeon is built of). They're removed when the dungeon is filled in (they're used up). Containers, TNT, beds, respawn anchors and pistons still pop straight back out, so nothing is lost, blown up or pushed through the bars. In every run, lava, powder snow and empty buckets can't be used in a dungeon (`That bucket can't be used in the dungeon.`), so nobody scoops the pool under a shaft's chute; water buckets can. On Easy, Normal and Hard every block you place pops back out (`Blocks placed in the dungeon pop back out.`). The dungeon's own blocks can never be broken (`The dungeon's blocks can't be broken.`), except cobwebs; explosions never break them either. Operators in creative mode can do both.
- **Finishing:** the title `Expedition complete` (`Gauntlet complete`) with `Crypt Nightmare 5 cleared in 6:12`, chat to everyone `Ann, Bob cleared the Crypt (Nightmare 5) in 6:12.`, and `A new record!` or your place when you made that difficulty's leaderboard. Each player still in the dungeon gets the dungeon's Crowns times the level (x1 on Easy up to x6.5 on Nightmare 20; x1.25 more with the Blessing, x1.25 with a shrine curse; a Gauntlet's length bonus and the Greed and Midas Touch boons on top), Warden reputation (`rep`, plus 10% per tier), the Journal page `expedition_<dungeon>` under Places, a relic by chance (`relicChance` plus 1% per tier, at most 50%), counts as a finished quest of kind `expedition` for other packs, and unlocks the next tier (`Nightmare 6 is unlocked!`). The treasure chests hold the dungeon's `loot` plus `tierLoot` from the tier on, scaled by the level (x1 to x3.2), a quarter more per extra player, half again with the Blessing.
- **Nightmare Sigils:** a boss in a Hard or Nightmare run drops one 35% of the time plus 1% per tier (`sigilChanceBoss`), a champion in a Nightmare run 8% of the time (`sigilChanceChampion`). It's an echo shard (`sigilItem`) named `Nightmare Sigil` whose lore lists the dungeon, the tier (usually the run's tier or one above, sometimes one below) and the affixes, then `Opens this run, used up as it starts` and `Hold it in your hand and use it`. Using it (or **Use a Nightmare Sigil**) shows the run's preview with **Start (uses the sigil)**.
- **The time limit:** a run not finished in time fails: `Time's up! The Crypt wasn't cleared within 24 minutes.` Everyone is sent back, and the run is listed as failed in the history. The clock counts game time: on a lagging server it runs as slowly as the game does, so lag never eats your time (and clear times are fair on any server).
- **Leaving:** `/realm:expedition_leave`, dying, leaving the game, or getting out of the dungeon any other way (a teleport, for example; you're out after 5 seconds outside it) all take you out of the run. Nobody can join a run after it starts. When the last player is out, the run fails and the dungeon is filled in. Anyone who leaves the game during a run is sent back to where they started when they next join. Leaving from the menu asks first.
- **When every dungeon is taken:** choose **Wait for a dungeon** in the preview. Up to 8 parties wait in first-come order for at most 30 minutes; a repeated request keeps its place. When a reset really frees a slot, the next eligible request starts automatically and asks the current party to join. Leaving, an operator reset or forget, or a reload clears the relevant request; no sigil or stored gear is taken while waiting.
- **Death:** your items drop in the dungeon as usual, are collected right away (everything within 6 blocks of where you fell; when several of you fall in the same moment, each item goes to whoever fell nearest it) and given back after you respawn (`returnItemsOnDeath`). They're kept in the world (a parcel, like the Fixed loadout stash) until then, so a restart or leaving the game first loses nothing. Experience is lost as usual. Dying just after you leave (before the fade sends you home) counts the same: your items come back and you're sent back to where you started when you respawn.
- **Above the hotbar** every second during a run: the dungeon and level, the clock and limit, the current step, and the affixes on a second line. With the [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) on, the HUD steps aside (the pack sends `realm:actionbar`). The run line waits while a note holds the bar (a puzzle's count, another pack's skill XP or mob health), so notes stay readable. It is a steady line of rank 40 (`steady: 40` in its `realm:actionbar`, see the action bar protocol in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)): the build mode line and the story tracker wait for it, and it waits for the Elytra HUD while you glide and for a Relics readout while you hold one.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:expedition` | Everyone | The Expeditions menu: start an expedition (dungeon, difficulty or Nightmare tier, affix preview and reroll), use a Nightmare Sigil, leaderboards (fastest clears per dungeon and difficulty, highest tiers, recent runs), your progress, go back to where you started. During a run: how it's going, the affixes, and leave it. Operators also get **Operator tools** (set the site, reset, create a sigil, unlock every tier) |
| `/realm:expedition_gauntlet` | Everyone | Start a Gauntlet: pick a dungeon and difficulty, then switch Fixed loadout and start (14 rooms, default `gauntletRooms`; a sanctuary every 5, `boonEvery`). During a run it opens the run menu |
| `/realm:expedition_leave` | Everyone | Leave your expedition and go back to where you started it (also how to leave the treasure room early)  Also leaves your queued request. |
| `/realm:expedition_site [x] [z]` | Operators | Sets where dungeons are built: where you stand, or at x z. Refused within 124 blocks of world spawn (default 64, `avoidSpawn`, plus half the biggest dungeon) or where anything but natural underground blocks is in the way of the biggest dungeon, with what and where. With more than one slot (`slots`), a dungeon that would come within `avoidSpawn` of spawn is left out; where the ground is below the dungeon (a flat world) it warns you |
| `/realm:expedition_reset` | Operators | Ends every expedition in progress (players are sent back) and fills the dungeons back in |

**Queue (when every slot is busy):** a party that tries to start while all `slots` are in use joins a first-come line of up to 8 parties (`QUEUE_MAX`). A queued party is kept for 30 minutes (36000 ticks). A leader's repeated request keeps its place. When a slot frees, the party at the front is asked along at the real start, and its sigil or stash is not debited while it waits. Finishing a reset also waits for the old dungeon loader to close before the next party starts. `/realm:expedition_leave` takes a queued party off the line. `/realm:expedition_reset` clears the line. An operator's forget clears it and blocks new starts and saves until the next reload. A queued stale Nightmare reroll is refused before any Crowns are debited. If the site is unloaded or unsafe, the line waits 60 seconds before retrying. The line is saved: after a script reload every waiting leader keeps their place and is told so (`The realm reloaded and you're still number 1 of 2 in line for a dungeon`), with the time already waited counting toward the 30 minutes. After a restart a leader who joins again within 5 minutes keeps their place and is told so; one who doesn't is dropped from the line. Leaving the game otherwise still takes a party out of the line, 10 seconds later (`QUEUE_GONE`, so a server stopping, which disconnects everyone first, doesn't empty the saved line); a leader who reconnects sooner keeps the place.

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | New expeditions can start. Disabled: the menu only shows the leaderboards; a run in progress still finishes |
| `depth` | `-40` | Floor height of the dungeon; it fills from 1 block below to 2 above its tallest room (y -41 to -33 for a run without tall rooms, up to y -8). Kept between -58 and -20 |
| `avoidSpawn` | `64` | The site's nearest dungeon edge must be at least this far from world spawn (flat distance), so a dungeon is never dug under the spawn town |
| `slots` | `1` | Expeditions that can run at the same time (1 to 3), each in its own dungeon: the first at the site, each next one `slotSpacing` blocks east. One that would come within `avoidSpawn` of world spawn is never used  Overflow parties use the bounded queue; each occupied dungeon uses one of the world's 10 shared ticking areas while gathering, building, running or resetting. |
| `slotSpacing` | `132` | Blocks between those dungeons (at least 132: the biggest dungeon is 120 wide) |
| `maxParty` | `4` | Most players in one expedition, the leader included (1 to 4) |
| `partyRadius` | `0` | `0`: every party member online is asked along, wherever they are. Above 0: only members within this many blocks of the leader, in the same dimension |
| `confirmSeconds` | `20` | Seconds party members have to answer; no answer is a no |
| `timeLimitMinutes` | `20` | Minutes of game time for a 7-room run: each run gets this much per 7 rooms, 1% less per Nightmare tier, at least 5 minutes |
| `exitSeconds` | `90` | Seconds after the boss falls before everyone is sent back, to collect the treasure. Opening a treasure chest when less than 20 seconds are left gives 20 more (up to 2 minutes more in all); what's left in the chests goes home with the players |
| `returnItemsOnDeath` | `true` | Items dropped dying in a dungeon are given back after respawning (otherwise they'd be lost when the dungeon is filled in) |
| `leaderboardSize` | `10` | Fastest clears kept on each leaderboard (one per dungeon and difficulty or tier), and Gauntlet clears on the Gauntlets board |
| `gauntletEnabled` | `true` | Gauntlets can start. Disabled: **Start a Gauntlet** is hidden and `/realm:expedition_gauntlet` says so |
| `gauntletRooms` | `14` | Rooms in a Gauntlet, entry, boss and treasure included (10 to 20) |
| `boonEvery` | `5` | A Gauntlet has a sanctuary (pick one of three boons) every this many rooms (3 to 8); a Gauntlet too short for that still gets one, in the room right before the boss |
| `loadoutDefault` | `false` | The Gauntlet preview starts with **Fixed loadout** enabled; the leader can still switch it |
| `gauntletKit` | the kit above | The Fixed loadout starter kit: `{ item, count, from, to, slot, ench }` (`from`/`to` levels as for `mobs`; `slot` is `head`, `chest`, `legs`, `feet` or `offhand`; `ench` is `{ <enchantment id>: level }`). Everything in the kit (food, arrows and blocks too) is run gear and stays in the dungeon |
| `announceFromLevel` | `0` | Chat line for a clear only from this level up (0: every clear; the menu names each level, 0 to 22 = Easy, Normal, Hard, Nightmare 1 to 20). Only the chat line changes: rewards, XP and progress are the same |
| `tierBoardSize` | `20` | Players kept on the Highest tiers board |
| `historySize` | `20` | Runs kept in the world's run history and in each player's |
| `maxTier` | `20` | Highest Nightmare tier (1 to 20) |
| `tallFromTier` | `3` | From this Nightmare tier, rooms can be tall (14 to 30 blocks) with balconies, and shafts appear |
| `buildFromTier` | `1` | Players may place blocks in a dungeon from this Nightmare tier |
| `allowBuilding` | `true` | Players may place blocks at all (see `buildFromTier`). Disabled: blocks placed in a dungeon always pop back out |
| `useChampionsPack` | `true` | Champions in waves come from the Champions pack when it's installed and knows the mob (zombie, husk, drowned, zombie villager, skeleton, stray, spider, witch); otherwise, or when disabled, the pack makes its own |
| `mobCap` | `18` | Most dungeon mobs alive in one run at a time: waves, adds and reinforcements stop there |
| `rerollCost` | `25` | Crowns to reroll the affixes shown before a Nightmare run (0: free) |
| `sigilItem` | `"minecraft:echo_shard"` | The item a Nightmare Sigil is |
| `sigilChanceBoss` | `0.35` | Chance a boss of a Hard or Nightmare run drops a sigil, plus 1% per tier |
| `sigilChanceChampion` | `0.08` | Chance a champion in a Nightmare run drops a sigil |
| `rep` | `15` | Warden reputation (Guilds) for each player who finishes, plus 10% per Nightmare tier |
| `relicChance` | `0.1` | Chance (0 to 1) that each player who finishes also gets a relic (Relics pack), plus 1% per tier, at most 50% |
| `relics` | `lantern_deep`, `miners_lamp`, `compass_echoes`, `frost_band`, `tide_boots` | The relics a finished run can give, one at random |
| `tierLoot` | diamonds (N1), emeralds (N3), golden apples (N5), netherite scrap (N8), a totem (N10, 20%), an enchanted golden apple (N12, 15%), a netherite ingot (N15, 25%), an elytra (N18, 5%) | Extra treasure from a Nightmare tier on: `{ from, item, min, max, chance }`, added to the dungeon's `loot` (half chance in side caches) |
| `dungeons` | the eight above | The dungeons: `{ id, name, lore, difficulty, mobs, flyers, boss: { mob, name, health, adds }, wall, floor, accent, trim, light, door, decor: { block, count, floor, breakable }, crowns, loot: [{ item, min, max, chance }] }`. `mobs` entries are an id or `{ id, from, weight }` (`from` is the first level: 0 Easy, 1 Normal, 2 Hard, 3 to 22 Nightmare 1 to 20). `difficulty` (1 to 3) is the difficulty the dungeon had before tiers: its old fastest clears were moved there. `health` is extra boss health in points (times the level and party); `adds` are what the boss calls. `accent` is the corner pillars, `trim` the balconies and ledges, `light` the lanterns, `door` the bars, `decor` a block scattered in combat rooms. Keep each `id`: the leaderboards and Journal entries use it |
