Default treasure (`loot`, each with its chance): **Crypt** 4–10 iron ingots, 2–6 gold ingots (80%), 4–12 bones, 1–2 diamonds (40%), a golden apple (40%), 4–10 bottles o' enchanting (80%), a name tag (25%). **Drowned Vault** 8–16 prismarine shards, 4–10 prismarine crystals (80%), 4–10 gold ingots, 1–3 diamonds (60%), 1–2 nautilus shells (50%), a heart of the sea (10%), 6–12 bottles o' enchanting (80%). **Frost Hollow** 2–5 diamonds, 4–12 emeralds, 1–3 golden apples (70%), an enchanted golden apple (5%), 8–16 blue ice (60%), 8–16 bottles o' enchanting. **Nether Forge** 6–14 gold ingots, 2–6 blaze rods (90%), 8–16 quartz (80%), 1–3 diamonds (60%), netherite scrap (15%), 8–14 bottles o' enchanting. **Sculk Depths** 1–3 echo shards (60%), 6–14 amethyst shards, 2–4 diamonds (80%), 1–3 disc fragments (30%), 10–18 bottles o' enchanting. **Pillager Keep** 6–16 emeralds, 6–12 iron ingots, a crossbow (50%), a totem of undying (15%), 1–3 diamonds (50%), 6–12 bottles o' enchanting (80%). **Spider Nest** 8–20 string, 2–6 spider eyes (80%), 4–10 iron ingots, 1–2 diamonds (40%), 1–2 golden apples (40%), 4–10 bottles o' enchanting (80%). **Ender Spire** 4–10 ender pearls, 1–2 shulker shells (40%), 2–4 diamonds (80%), 6–14 chorus fruit (80%), 10–18 bottles o' enchanting.

Operators can change `enabled`, `slots`, `maxParty`, `timeLimitMinutes`, `exitSeconds`, `gauntletEnabled`, `gauntletRooms`, `boonEvery`, `loadoutDefault`, `returnItemsOnDeath`, `relicChance`, `maxTier`, `allowBuilding`, `useChampionsPack`, `mobCap`, `rerollCost`, `sigilChanceBoss` and `sigilChanceChampion` in game with `/realm:config`. The rest stay in `config.js`.

### Saved data

Once a stored-items cart has actually been found, its saved record remembers that fact. If the cart is later broken or goes missing, the pack reports missing items instead of placing the saved structure over a survivor and paying a second copy. The world remembers it too, without the player (`expedition:cart_marks`): from the tick the structure is put down, the pack looks for its carts at once and then every tick for 2 seconds, notes any of them being broken or unloaded in that time, and notes one loading later (after a restart, say). So a player leaving, a cart broken or a restart in the few ticks before the hand-back finds the carts can't put the structure down a second time once its carts were there; only carts that never appeared are put down again. The world also notes how each of those carts left (`expedition:cart_gone`): a cart that went still holding its items (unloaded where nobody is, or taken away by a script, so nothing of it was dropped) is put down again from the structure and handed back; a cart that was broken, emptied or killed (its items fell out) is not, and its part is taken away empty if it turns up again. The player's record is never forgotten while the structure that holds their items is still saved: when nothing may come back, the structure is deleted first, then the player is told their items couldn't be found. A partial hand-back says how many of the expected carts were found. The Nether round-trip scenario is a regression guard, not a claimed fail-before reproduction.

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `expedition:site` | World | JSON `{ x, z, by, at }`: the site an operator set |
| `expedition:run:<slot>` | World | JSON `{ id, slot, dungeon, seed, x, y, z, leader, phase, l, g, c, h, pt }` while a dungeon exists in that slot (`l` level, `g`/`c`/`h` the box's grid, cell size and height, `pt` block types players placed; while the treasure room is open also `to`, the players in the run, and `ch`, the treasure chests), so one cut short by a restart is filled in when the world starts again. Records from before tiers (without `g`, `c`, `h`) are read as the old 48 by 48 by 9 box |
| `expedition:next` | World | The next run's number |
| `expedition:best:<dungeon id>` | World | JSON `{ <level>: [{ t, n, at, a }] }`: the fastest clears per level (`e`, `n`, `h`, `t1` to `t20`): milliseconds of game time (ticks x 50), the players' names, when, the affixes |
| `expedition:best` | World | The fastest clears from before tiers (`{ <dungeon id>: [{ t, n, at }] }`). Copied once into `expedition:best:<id>` at the dungeon's old difficulty, then only kept |
| `expedition:best_v2` | World | `1` once that copy was made |
| `expedition:tiers` | World | JSON `[{ id, n, l, d, at }]`: the highest level each player cleared (the Highest tiers board) |
| `expedition:queue` | World | JSON `[{ i, n, d, L, a, s?, g?, w }]`: the parties waiting for a dungeon, in order (leader id and name, dungeon id, level, affixes, the sigil line, `g: { loadout }` for a Gauntlet, `w`: game ticks waited so far); removed when the line is empty |
| `expedition:history` | World | JSON `[{ d, l, ok, t, n, at, a, g }]`: the latest runs, cleared or failed, newest first (`t`: milliseconds of game time; `g`: a Gauntlet's room count) |
| `expedition:callings` | World | JSON `{ <player name>: <Calling> }` from Skills' `realm:calling`, for the leaderboards (at most 300 names, the oldest dropped first) |
| `expedition:gauntlets` | World | JSON `[{ d, l, t, n, at, r, k }]`: the best Gauntlet clears, hardest then fastest (`r` rooms, `k` 1 with Fixed loadout) |
| `expedition:stash_next` | World | The next stash number |
| `expedition:parcels:<player id>` | World | JSON list `{ id, tag, k, c, placed?, seen?, skip?, at? }` of parcels waiting for that player (`k`: `spoils` treasure left in the chests, `dropped` items dropped dying; `c`: its carts); `placed` once its carts were put down to hand it over, so it's never put down twice; `seen` and `skip` as for `expedition:stash` |
| `expedition:parcel_next` | World | The next parcel number |
| `expedition:cart_marks` | World | JSON `{ <cart tag>: 0 or 1 }`: a stash or parcel whose structure was put down to hand it over (`0`) and whether its carts were in the world since (`1`), kept until that hand-over ends (at most 800: over that, the oldest `0` goes first, and a `1` only when no `0` is left). When the hand-over runs again, a `1` is copied onto its record as `seen` |
| `expedition:cart_gone` | World | JSON `{ <cart tag>: { <part>: 0 or 1 } }`: for a stash or parcel being handed over, how each of its carts left the world: `1` removed still holding its items (nothing dropped), `0` broken, emptied or killed. Only `1` parts are put down again when the record can't find its carts. Goes with the record's `expedition:cart_marks` entry |
| `expedition:parcel_<n>` | Structure (saved in the world) | A parcel: chest minecarts (tagged `realm:exp_parcel`, `realm:exp_parcel_<n>` and, since 2.4.14, `realm:exp_parcel_part_<k>`) holding the items, made in the sealed pocket in the dungeon box's corner. Deleted once handed over |
| `expedition:stash_<n>` | Structure (saved in the world) | A Fixed loadout player's own items while they're on a Gauntlet: two chest minecarts (tagged `realm:exp_stash`, `realm:exp_stash_<n>` and `realm:exp_stash_part_<0 or 1>`) holding slots 0 to 26 and 27 to 40 (inventory, then head, chest, legs, feet, offhand). Deleted once the items are back |
| `expedition:stash` | Player | JSON `{ id, tag, placed?, seen?, skip?, at? }`: which stash holds the player's items (`id` empty: they carried nothing); `placed` once its carts were put down to give the items back, so they're never put down twice; `seen` once they were found; `skip`: parts never to hand back again (their carts were broken after being seen) |
| `expedition:return` | Player | JSON `{ d, x, y, z, run }`: where to send the player back to, while they're on a run (or until they rejoin after one) |
| `expedition:buffs` | Player | JSON list of the effects a run gave the player (shrine blessing, boons), taken away when they leave the run, also after a restart |
| `expedition:prog` | Player | JSON `{ u, b, c, r }`: the highest Nightmare tier unlocked, the highest level cleared, clears, the player's recent runs |
| `expedition:rolls` | Player | JSON `{ <level>: [affix ids] }`: the affixes shown for each Nightmare level, kept until that run starts or they're rerolled (so reopening the menu doesn't reroll) |

| `expedition:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

Forgetting this pack's saved data (`/realm:diag`) deletes its world entries and its parcel structures (orphaned parcels are cleaned up). It keeps the `expedition:stash_<n>` structures: a stash is named on the owner's player data, and offline players can't be listed, so deleting one early would lose the items inside. A stash is removed only when its owner's items are handed back, so a forget can leave stash chests in the world. The cleanup sweep waits for hand-overs still in flight and rechecks every 40 ticks; it isn't a delivery retry. After a forget the pack saves nothing until you run `/reload` or restart the server.
| `realm:exp_mob`, `realm:exp_run:<id>`, `realm:exp_champ`, `realm:exp_called`, `realm:exp_ch_<id>`, `realm:bounty:exp_<id>`, `realm:exp_pet` | Entity tags | On the dungeon's mobs (champions, mobs that called for help, champions asked of the Champions pack; the last one on the boss only) and a Wolf Pack's wolves (`realm:exp_pet`). Leftovers are removed when the world starts |
| `realm_expedition` | Player tag | On every player in a running expedition, from the moment they're taken in until they're out of it (leave, die, leave the game, the run ends; one who was offline loses it when they next spawn, also after a restart). Other packs read it (the Deck of Many Things' The Swap) |
| `realm_exp_<slot>` | Ticking area | Keeps the dungeon loaded while it's built, played and filled in; removed afterward |

Runs themselves are kept in memory: a restart ends a run in progress (its players are sent back when they join, and the dungeon is filled in); after a script reload, players still online are sent back at once. A player is only taken off their return spot once the teleport back worked, so one who can't be moved right then (dead, say) is sent back when they next spawn. Shrine and boon effects are taken away when a player leaves the run, also after a restart (they're saved on the player). Boons and sanctuary choices live with the run, so a restart ends them with it: the boon effects go, boon gear stays in the dungeon and Wolf Pack wolves are removed (boon items that aren't gear, like golden apples, are kept). What players are owed is in the world, so it survives restarts and players leaving the game, and is given back when they're next sent back or spawn: a Fixed loadout stash, items dropped dying, and treasure left in the chests (packed into parcels when a player leaves the treasure room or the run ends; after a restart in the treasure window, what's still in the chests is shared out the same way between the players who were in the run, before the dungeon is filled in). Nothing is given twice: a parcel is marked as put down before its carts appear.

### How it works

- **Never near builds:** the dungeon is a sealed box of 3 by 3 to 5 by 5 cells of 20 to 24 blocks (22 on Easy, 24 from Normal and in Gauntlets; 60 to 120 blocks wide) and 9 to 34 high, deep underground. Where the site is closer to world spawn than `avoidSpawn` plus half that size (a site set when dungeons were at most 100 wide), the cells shrink (down to 20) so the box still keeps its distance. Before every run the box is checked with `Dimension.containsBlock`, a column at a time, for any block that isn't natural (stone, deepslate, tuff, granite, diorite, andesite, ores, raw ore blocks, dirt, gravel, clay, water, lava, obsidian, magma, amethyst geodes, dripstone, lush cave plants, sculk), and the run is called off if there is one (operators are told what and where). `/realm:expedition_site` runs the same check over the biggest possible dungeon where it can. While building, every fill only touches a volume that holds nothing but natural blocks, air and the dungeon's own (such a volume is filled whole; any other is filled through a filter that replaces only natural and dungeon blocks). The site must also be far from world spawn (`avoidSpawn`).
- **Building:** a ticking area keeps the box loaded. Once its chunks can be read and the box is found clean, anyone in it, dropped items and named or tamed animals are moved to the surface (the top of the water over a lake or the sea; the ground under the box where the ground is below it), then the whole box is filled with deepslate (sealing any caves), and the rooms, floors, the shapes' walls, corner pillars, ceiling lanterns, corridors (out of each door, along the gap between the rooms and into the next door; with a chute and pool under a shaft's high exit), closed bars, balconies, ladders, ledges, cover, pits (the floor block goes and the box's bottom layer under it becomes soul sand or magma), puzzles, signs and decor are placed. The work runs as a `system.runJob` job, so the server never stalls (a Nightmare 20 dungeon builds in about a second): every fill (the deepslate columns, a room's walls and its air, and the reset's fills) is split into horizontal slabs of at most 2,048 blocks, one per step (`scripts/slabs.js`), and a room's parts and decor are placed in turns of at most 8 ms; with 40 players on, the slowest step went from 36 ms to about 10. The layout follows from the seed and level alone (`scripts/layout.js` and the shapes in `scripts/rooms.js`, which have no game code, so they're checked in Node across thousands of seeds, every level and Gauntlet lengths: rooms fit their cells, each room's walk reaches every door, chest, button and spawn, the way through is long enough, ledges can be climbed, every puzzle has an answer).
- **Filling in:** after the run (or when it fails or an operator resets it) the chests in the box are emptied, the dungeon's mobs and dropped items are removed, anything else in the box (a pet) is moved to the surface, any player is sent back to where they started their expedition (or to the surface; to the world spawn, on the ground, when there's no surface above the box), and the whole box is filled with deepslate again: the box held only natural blocks before the run and stayed sealed, so everything in it came from the run, including the blocks players placed and whatever came of them (cobblestone where water met lava, concrete, frosted ice). Nothing is left behind that would call off the next run there. The ticking area is removed. If the box can't be loaded (the world has its 10 ticking areas, say), it's tried again every minute, when someone wants to start a run, after a restart and with `/realm:expedition_reset`; operators online are told once, and no new run starts there until then; its blocks still can't be broken meanwhile. A box is only ever filled in after the check before its run found it clean.
- **The run** is checked twice a second: who is in which room, wave mobs left (mobs that leave the dungeon are removed; a wave mob or the boss that ends up somewhere else in it, like an enderman that teleported into a room behind the bars, is brought back once it has been away from the room, and from everyone, for 3 seconds), the boss (an `entityDie` for it finishes the run), goal spots of trap halls and shafts, side rooms, the button rush clock, affix hazards (warned with particles for 1.5 to 2 seconds before they hit), the time limit (in game ticks), and players who left. **Spawning** checks what the game hands back (its type, dimension, place and tags), so a world whose entity ids repeat never turns an existing entity, such as someone's chest minecart or pet, into a dungeon mob or a stash cart. Buttons, pressure plates, target blocks, projectiles and levers are read from `afterEvents.buttonPush`, `pressurePlatePush`, `targetBlockHit`, `projectileHitBlock` and `leverAction`; puzzle buttons pop back up at once so the same one can be pressed again. Vampiric, Venomous, Thorned and Backup work through `entityHurt`. Explosions inside a dungeon are kept from breaking blocks (`beforeEvents.explosion`).
- **Fixed loadout:** as each player is taken in, a 1 by 2 pocket in the box's corner (always solid rock outside every room) is opened, two chest minecarts are spawned in it and filled with the player's 41 slots (copies with every component), and `world.structureManager.createFromWorld` saves the pocket with its entities (no blocks) as a world structure. Only once that structure exists are the player's slots emptied (the same tick, so nothing can change in between); the carts are emptied and removed either way, and the pocket is sealed again. Coming back, the structure is placed (entities only) at the player's feet, the carts' items go back slot by slot, the carts and the structure are removed. A player sent home far away can stand in chunks that aren't loaded yet for a moment, and a structure placed there puts nothing down, so the stash and parcels wait until the spot under the player is loaded (tried every 2 seconds for a minute, then again when they next spawn); carts that were marked as put down but never appeared are put down again from the structure, which is only deleted once everything is handed over. Kit gear is found by its lore line.
- **The `realm_expedition` tag** is on every player while they're in a running expedition, for other packs (the Deck of Many Things' The Swap leaves them out).
- **Party members** are players with the same `realm_party:<code>` tag as the leader ([Parties](#parties--party_bp)), online and not on another run (with `partyRadius` above 0, also in the same dimension and within that many blocks). All of them are asked at once, nearest first; the first to tap **Join** fill the run up to `maxParty`, and anyone who joins after it's full is told so and stays put. Each one is brought back to where they were when the run started, in their own dimension.
- **Messages sent:** `realm:quest_done` `{ player, pack: "expedition_bp", id: "expedition_<dungeon>", label, kind: "expedition", guild: "wardens", dungeon, level, tier, nightmare, gauntlet }` (`tier` is `easy`, `normal`, `hard` or `nightmare`, `nightmare` the Nightmare number or 0, `gauntlet` true for a Gauntlet; [Story Questlines](#story-questlines--saga_bp) reads them), `realm:rep_add` `{ guild: "wardens" }`, `realm:journal` `{ page: "places", entry: "expedition_<dungeon>" }` and, by chance, `realm:relic_give`, for each player who finishes. Champions are asked of the Champions pack with `realm:champion_spawn` `{ dim, x, y, z, mob, tag: "realm:exp_ch_<run>" }`; if none with that tag appears within 3 ticks (the pack isn't installed), the pack makes its own. Crowns go straight into the `crowns` scoreboard.
- **For tests:** the script event `realm:expedition_debug` (`{ room?, skip?, slot? }`) is answered with `realm:expedition_state` (`{ part, parts, data }`): the state of the first run (or the run in `slot`: members, Gauntlet, loadout, boons) and one room's layout, shape, size, doors and puzzle, used by the BDS scenarios that play whole runs; `skip: true` counts the current room (not the boss) as cleared. Script events need operator rights.

---

## Town Projects — `town_bp`

Grow the realm's towns together. Operators add a town and it gets a mayor of its own from [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) (Mayor Bram for the realm's first town, a new mayor such as Mayor Alda for every other), who takes deliveries of materials for the town's projects: a well and a notice board, then lamp posts and a garden plot, a market stall and a dock, and finally a bell tower. When a project has everything it needs, it is built on a spot the town picked by itself (on natural ground near the center, never touching anything players built, leveling the ground gently where the build needs it) or one an operator set, fireworks go up and the top contributors are paid in [Crowns](#crowns--crowns_bp). Finishing every project of a level raises the town: Settlement, Village, Town, City and Capital, and from Village on the town builds houses by itself, one for each family the level brings. Paths lead from its builds to the center, lantern posts light them, and a garden pen with sheep and chickens sits by the garden. This is separate from [Community Goals](#community-goals--goals_bp), which collect one item into a chest: town projects take several items, are delivered through the mayor, and build something.

### How to use

1. Find your town's mayor (they stand in the town; Mayor Bram is the first town's), tap them and pick **Town projects (Riverside)**. You see the town's story so far (`Day 12: The Well was finished, thanks to Ann`), its level, this level's projects with why the town wants each (`Well - Fresh water, so families can move in`) and their progress bars, and what the next level brings.
2. Pick a project to see what it needs (`Oak Planks: 32 / 64 (you carry 20)`) and who has helped, then tap **Deliver what I have**. It takes what you carry of the needed items, up to what's still needed: partial deliveries count. Chat says `You delivered 20 Oak Planks, 4 Iron Ingot for Riverside's Dock. Now 52 percent.`
3. When the last item is in, everyone hears `Riverside finished its Dock! Top contributors: Ann 64, Bob 32. Thank you, everyone!`. Players near its spot see its outline in green for a few seconds (`Riverside's Dock goes up here in 5 seconds.`), then it goes up and fireworks rise over it. The top three contributors get 60, 35 and 20 Crowns, and everyone who helped gets reputation in [Guilds & Reputation](#guilds--reputation--guilds_bp) (if you're offline, it's waiting when you join).
4. When every project of a level is finished, the town levels up: `Riverside is now a Town (level 3)` on everyone's screen, with the new projects. From level 2 the town also builds its houses by itself, nothing to deliver (`Riverside has a new house (House 3) at 130, 64, -12.`). With residents Enabled (`residents`, default Enabled), villagers move in: 2 beside the well once it's built, then a family for each house (`A new family moved into Riverside: Tilly.`). As it grows the town lays grass paths from its builds toward the center, puts up lantern posts beside them and, once the garden is built, a pen next to it with 2 sheep and 2 chickens (`townLife`, default Enabled). The notice board shows the projects done, the resident count and the newest families, and the mayor tells the town's news.
5. Run `/realm:town` anywhere for the town menu: **Town info** (the nearest town's level, projects, progress and contributors; also `/realm:town_stats`), **Projects** (what each still needs) and **Other towns**.
6. **Operators:** stand in the middle of a town, open `/realm:town` and pick **Add a town here** (or run `/realm:town_add Riverside`, quotes for a name with spaces). Its mayor appears where you stand (with Townsfolk; the realm's first town has Mayor Bram instead, wherever he lives). That's all: the town picks a spot for each project by itself, a little at a time while a player is in the town (a minute or two for a level, up to about ten on a steep hillside). To choose one yourself instead, stand where it should be built, facing the way it should face, and pick **Set a project spot** and the project (or run `/realm:town_spot <project>`: `well`, `notice_board`, `lamps`, `garden`, `stall`, `dock`, `bell_tower`). Its outline appears in green particles, with a blue arrow for its front: pick **Set spot here**, **Rotate 90**, **Look around** (10 seconds to walk around it) or **Cancel**. A spot you set is kept and its ground is never leveled. When the town finds no good spot for a project (a dock with no water nearby), the town menu says so and you set it by hand; a project finished without a spot waits, and operators are reminded when they join.
7. **Operators:** **Manage spots** in `/realm:town` removes a spot (a built project is taken away and the ground put back, leveled ground included), rebuilds a damaged build, or relocates it (preview at the new place, then it's taken away from the old one and built at the new one). **Find spots again** looks again for every project up to the town's level that has no spot (after you cleared room, or for those without a good spot). **Mayor** moves the town's mayor to where you stand (facing your way) or renames them; Mayor Bram can only be moved (his name belongs to the stories). **Protect from world events** (Enabled for new towns) keeps meteors, tornadoes and storms from breaking blocks in the town. **Remove town** (or `/realm:town_remove`) removes the town you're in. `/realm:config` → **Town Projects** sets the town radius, announcements and more.

### What players see

- **Levels** (`levelNames`): 1 Settlement, 2 Village, 3 Town, 4 City, 5 Capital. A new town is a Settlement. Only the projects of the town's current level take deliveries.
- **Projects** (from `projects`):

  | Level | Project | Needs | Built |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | Well | 64 cobblestone, 8 oak logs, 1 bucket | A 5 by 5 cobblestone well set into the ground, with water, fence posts and an oak slab roof |
  | 1 | Notice Board | 32 oak planks, 3 oak signs | A planked board between two log posts, with three signs: the town's name and level; projects done and the resident count; the newest families (or, with none yet, the top three contributors). Kept up to date |
  | 2 | Lamp Posts | 16 oak fences, 4 lanterns | Four fence posts with lanterns, 4 blocks apart in a row ahead of the spot |
  | 2 | Garden Plot | 16 oak logs, 16 wheat seeds, 16 bone meal | A 5 by 5 plot edged with logs: farmland planted with wheat, carrots, potatoes and beetroot around a water block with a lily pad |
  | 3 | Market Stall | 32 oak planks, 8 white wool, 8 red wool, 2 barrels | A counter and two barrels under a striped red and white wool roof on fence posts |
  | 3 | Dock | 64 oak planks, 32 oak logs, 16 iron ingots | A plank deck 3 wide reaching 10 blocks out over the water, on log posts down to the bottom, with fence rails and two lanterns at the end |
  | 4 | Bell Tower | 128 stone bricks, 16 gold ingots, 16 iron ingots | A stone brick tower 3 by 3 and 8 high with a bell hanging under its roof and a lightning rod on top |

- **The town's story** (the mayor's page and **Town info**): the newest 12 things that happened in the town, dated with the Realm day when [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) or [Realm Calendar](#realm-calendar--calendar_bp) says it (`Day 3: Founded by Ann`, `Day 12: The Well was finished, thanks to Ann`, `Day 20: It became a Village`). Towns from before this version start their story with the next thing that happens. Below the open projects (each with its `why`) the page says what the next level brings: `Next, as a Village (level 2): new projects (Lamp Posts, Garden Plot).` Levels, needs and rewards are as before.
- **Houses** (`houses`, default Enabled): from level 2 (Village) the town builds a house for each family its level brings (`residentsPerLevel`: 4 at Village, 6 at Town, 8 at City, 10 at Capital; at most `residentCapTown`, 10). They are the town's own works, `house_1` to `house_10`: no deliveries, rewards or quests, and they don't count for leveling. Each goes up at a spot the town picks (as for projects: natural ground, at most 3 blocks of leveling, the outline first, a few blocks a tick) and is a 7 by 7 cottage: oak log corners, oak plank walls with glass panes, a door in the middle of the front wall facing the spot (and the town's center), an oak slab roof, a lantern, a bed and one job-site block, a different one for each house in turn (`houseJobs`: composter, lectern, barrel, smoker, cartography table, brewing stand, fletching table, loom, stonecutter, grindstone). Players in the town (and operators) hear of each new house, and it goes into the town's story. The mayor's page says `Houses: 2 of 4 built`. A town that was already level 2 or more gets its houses after this update. Operators see houses in **Manage spots** (remove, rebuild, relocate) and, once due, in **Set a project spot**. Disabled: no new houses go up (one half built is finished); built ones stay.
- **Residents** (`residents`, default Enabled): ordinary villagers move into the town as it grows, named from `residentNames` (`Tilly`, `Otto`; each name once in the world while there are free ones), each with the look (profession) of its home's job-site block: a composter's family are farmers, a lectern's librarians, a barrel's fishermen, and so on. At a Settlement 2 families live beside the well once it's built (a farmer and a fisherman); from Village on there is a family for each house (`residentsPerLevel`: 4, 6, 8, 10; at most `residentCapTown`, 10, a town), and the well's two move into their own houses once those are built (when no player is within 24 blocks of either place). Players in the town read `A new family moved into Riverside: Tilly.` and the story says so. Residents wander like villagers but stay near home: one more than 32 blocks from its home is brought back by the next census (every 30 seconds) once no player is within 16 blocks of it, and one past the town radius always is. They never claim a bed, a job site or a bell, so a player's bed in the town stays the player's; they never work, so a farmer-looking resident never harvests a player's crops; and they don't trade (`residentsTrade`, default Disabled, since vanilla trading would bypass the Crowns economy: a tap says `Tilly lives in Riverside and doesn't trade.`). When one dies, a new family moves in after `replaceMinutes` (20 in-game minutes, one in-game day). The whole world has at most `residentCapWorld` (20) residents, since each is a mob the server runs: over it, towns with the highest level get theirs first, then the oldest. Lowering a cap never removes anyone; nobody new comes until the count is under it. Disabled: nobody new moves in and nobody is replaced; residents already living stay.
- **Small life** (`townLife`, default Enabled): every build at a spot the town picked gets a path, 1 block wide, from the ground in front of it toward the center (up to 3 blocks from it): only grass at ground level becomes a grass path (a grass tuft, dead bush, bush or leaf litter on it is cleared), each block at most 1 up or down from the last, at most 48 blocks; it stops at anything else (stone, sand, another path, a block players built, a flower, fern or mushroom, which may be someone's flower bed, a two-block plant or a crop), at another build's outline and its 2 blocks around, a land claim, a story place or a natural block a player placed. Builds at spots operators set get no path. At each new level, once that level's builds are up, lantern posts (an oak fence with a lantern on it) go up beside the paths: every 8 blocks along a path, on natural ground right beside it with 2 open blocks above, at least 4 blocks apart, at most 12 in a town. When the garden is built, the town builds a **Garden Pen** next to it (a town work like the houses, at a spot it picks within 30 blocks of the garden: a 5 by 5 oak fence ring with a gate facing the center) and 2 sheep and 2 chickens are put in it (tagged `town:a:<town>`). They are ordinary animals, so they despawn when no player is near, like any animal the game didn't place with the world: one that vanished comes back once a player has stood within 24 blocks of the pen for 30 seconds, but one that died (eaten, a fox) never does. Players in the town read `Riverside has a garden pen at 120, 64, -30.` **Remove spot** turns a build's path back to grass and takes its lantern posts away (parts not loaded then follow when they are); towns from before this version get paths and posts for their picked spots, and their pen once the garden is built. Disabled: no new paths, posts or pen (one half built is finished); those already there stay.
- **Town news:** a new family, a new house and a new level are news the town's own mayor tells ([Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) gossip: `Riverside keeps growing. New roofs, new faces.`), only that mayor (Mayor Bram for his town), at most one piece of this pack's news an in-game hour.
- **Delivering** takes the needed items from anywhere in your inventory, never more than still needed. Locked items stay, and so do items with lore (Storm Glass, Relic Shards, relics and other special items) and items with a custom name (`keepNamedItems`). Items are used up by the project, not stored in a chest.
- **Mayors** (`townMayors`, default Enabled, with [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp)): every town has a mayor of its own. Adding a town makes one at the town's center, named from `mayorNames` (`Mayor Alda`, each name once; then `Mayor <Town>`), shown as `Mayor Alda of Riverside`; the realm's first town has Mayor Bram, the realm's main mayor, wherever he lives (when his town is removed, the next town added is his, once every older town has its mayor). A town's mayor offers **Town projects (Riverside)** for that town wherever the player stands. Any NPC with the `mayor` role (`npcRole`) also offers the town the player is in (within 96 blocks of its center, `townRadius`) when that town's own mayor isn't placed, after its own town (two buttons at most); an NPC with the role that an operator added in Townsfolk's `config.js` offers the town the player is in, as before. A mayor that is missing (removed with `/realm:npc_remove`, or not made yet because Townsfolk wasn't installed) is asked for again, at the town's center, when a player is in the town (at most every 30 seconds per town). **Remove town** removes its mayor too (never Mayor Bram). **Towns from before mayors** (an existing world): once Townsfolk has said where the townsfolk are (5 seconds after the world loads), Mayor Bram keeps his town (the town nearest his post within `townRadius`; with none that close, or Bram not placed, the oldest town), and every other town gets its own mayor the next time a player comes near it. Spots, progress and rewards stay as they are. Without Townsfolk nothing changes until it is installed. Disabled: no new mayors, and every NPC with the `mayor` role offers the town the player is in. With `deliverWithCommand` enabled, `/realm:town` also takes deliveries while you're within a town's radius.
- **Automatic spots** (`autoSpots`, default Enabled): when a town is added or reaches a new level, it picks a spot for each new project, and towns from before this version pick one for their open and finished projects that have none (spots already set stay where they are). It looks in rings around the center, only while a player is within the town radius (the ground there is loaded), and takes, in this order: the spot needing the least leveling, then one that is already level, then one at a different height from the town's other builds (so a hillside town keeps builds at several heights, like a well on a rise or terraced stalls), then the nearest (the well stays nearest the center). Every build faces the center; the dock goes on the shore nearest the center, its deck over water. A spot is never picked where its outline or a 2-block margin around it has anything but natural ground (grass, dirt, sand, gravel, stone, snow and the like), wild plants or natural leaves: planks, glass, cobblestone, terracotta, farmland, paths, crops, saplings, a waystone and any other block players place or build with count as man-made, and so do a tree, a roof or overhang, water and lava. Nor where a land claim ([Land Claims](#land-claims--claims_bp)), another project (builds stay at least 5 blocks apart), a townsfolk's house (6 blocks from their post), the mayor (4 blocks) or a story place (16 blocks) is, or within 4 blocks of the town's edge, or where a player placed a natural block (dirt, sand, stone...) or a plant (a flower, fern, petals...) since this version. Safe zones don't matter (the town is one).
- **Leveling** (automatic spots only): where the ground under a build isn't flat, its natural ground is cut down or filled up to one height, at most `levelDepth` (3) blocks either way, and the 2 blocks around it are graded back to the ground in steps of at most 1 block. Fill is dirt with the surrounding top block (grass, sand...) on top; a cut never opens into a cave or lets water in. Nothing outside the build and those 2 blocks changes, so the town keeps its hills. A finished project at an automatic spot is checked again block by block just before it goes up (anything built there since, or a claim, and another spot is picked once; then it waits for an operator), waits while someone stands on it or on the ground leveled around it (`Step off the spot: Riverside's Well goes up here.`), and is built a few blocks a tick. A server restart in the middle finishes it afterwards.
- **Building:** every build starts at the spot where the operator stood and goes forward the way they faced. Builds only replace air, plants (grass, flowers, ferns, snow layers, bushes, mushrooms, vines), and for the well's water and the garden's farmland the grass or dirt they sit in, and for the dock, water. Anything else in the way (a build, a path, stone) is left alone and that block of the project is skipped; operators are told how many. Water (the well's and the garden's) goes in last and only where blocks or more of its water hold it in on every side and below, so it never spills onto anything nearby; a lily pad only goes on that water. A project is built all at once: while any part of it is in a chunk that isn't loaded, it waits, and it's built as soon as a player comes within 64 blocks of its spot with all of it loaded. Chat says `Riverside's new Dock is built at 120, 63, -45.`
- **Structures instead:** a project with a `structure` id places that structure (saved by an operator with a structure block or `/structure save`) with its corner at the spot, turned to the way the operator faced (saved facing south), instead of the built-in design. It's placed as saved, replacing what's there. Without such a structure in the world, the built-in design is used.
- **Rewards** for each finished project: Crowns for the top contributors (`topCrowns`: 60, 35, 20), shown as `+60 Crowns (Dock, Riverside)`; for every contributor, `repPerProject` (10) reputation to the Growers when the project is mostly wood, crops and wool, or the Miners when it's mostly stone and metal, plus a finished quest of kind `town` for other packs. Contributors who are offline get theirs when they next join (`Town projects you helped with were finished while you were away. Thank you!`).
- **Announcements** (`announce`): finished projects, builds and level-ups go to everyone in chat, with fireworks (`fireworks`) and a title for level-ups. Disabled: only the contributors and the operators hear about it, and only players in the town see the level-up title.
- **The menu:** `/realm:town` says which town you're in (or the nearest one and how far), then has a button for everything you may do: **Town info**, **Projects** (each open project with its percent; pick one for what it needs, and **Deliver what I have** where `deliverWithCommand` allows it) and **Other towns**. Operators also see, inside a town, **Set a project spot**, **Manage spots** (when the town has spots), **Find spots again** (with `autoSpots`), **Mayor** (who it is; **Move here** and **Rename**, or **Move Bram here**), **Protect from world events** with its state, and **Remove town**; outside one, **Add a town here** (a name field).
- **Spot preview** (operators): the project's outline, the exact blocks it covers when built at the spot, is drawn in green particles (only you see them) at where you stood, facing the way you faced to the nearest quarter turn, with a blue arrow on the ground from the spot pointing at the build's front. It's redrawn twice a second for 30 seconds after each answer; with no answer by then it closes and nothing changes (`The spot preview timed out. Nothing was changed.`). The form says the size (`5 by 5 blocks, 6 high`) and how many blocks would be left out because something is in the way. **Rotate 90** turns it a quarter to the right; **Look around** closes the form for 10 seconds so you can walk around the outline, then asks again. The outline comes from the build's own blocks (a saved `structure`'s size for a project with one), so it's always the real size: a well 5 by 5 and 6 high, the lamps 1 by 13, a dock 3 by 10 and 11 deep.
- **Removing, rebuilding and moving** (operators, **Manage spots**): just before a project is first built at a spot, the blocks its outline covers are saved in the world as a structure (at an automatic spot, the 2 blocks around it and the ground below too, so the leveled ground goes back as well). **Remove spot** forgets an unbuilt project's spot, or takes a built one away and puts the saved ground back block by block (blocks added inside its outline since then stay, and a chest keeps its items, unless they are of a kind the build is made of; a barrel, smoker or brewing stand of the build with something in it, or a lectern, is broken the way a player breaks it, so what it holds drops instead of being lost); the project stays finished and waits for a new spot. **Rebuild** puts the saved ground back and builds it again, fresh. **Relocate** previews a new spot where you stand; on **Set spot here** the build is taken away from the old spot and built at the new one. Setting a spot for a built project (from the menu or `/realm:town_spot`) moves it the same way. Each asks first. Projects built before this version have no saved ground: the form warns about it, removing or moving clears only the build's own blocks that are still there (ground blocks become grass, a dock's posts water, the rest air), and **Rebuild** puts back the missing blocks.
- **Protect from world events** (operators, per town, default Enabled): world events (meteors, tornadoes, storms and the like) still happen within the town radius (96 blocks, `townRadius`), but packs that support safe zones don't break or place blocks there. Disabled, they can. It also keeps the Gray Choir's sieges ([Realm Calendar](#realm-calendar--calendar_bp)) away from the town, unless that pack's `spareSafeTowns` is Disabled.
- **Heartened and Shaken** ([Realm Calendar](#realm-calendar--calendar_bp)): a town that held off a Choir siege is **Heartened** for a day: every item delivered counts 1.25 (`You delivered 8 Oak Planks ... Heartened: it counts x1.25!`; never more than still needed). A town that lost one is **Shaken**. The town menu says which.
- **Letters:** contributors who are offline when a project is finished get a letter from the town with [Realm Mail](#realm-mail--mail_bp) (`<Project> is finished`): how much they delivered, and that their Crowns wait for them. At most 10 letters a project, the biggest contributors first. The top contributor is still town gossip (with [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp); at most one piece of news from this pack per in-game hour, see Town news in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:town` | Everyone | The town menu: town info, projects, other towns, and for operators, add a town, set a project spot with a preview, manage spots (remove, rebuild, relocate), find spots again (default Enabled, `autoSpots`), the town's mayor (move here, rename), protect from world events (default Enabled) and remove the town |
| `/realm:town_stats` | Everyone | The nearest town's level, its projects with progress bars, what each still needs and who has helped. Delivering is at the town's mayor (or here, inside a town, with `deliverWithCommand`, default off) |
| `/realm:town_add <name>` | Operators | Adds a town centered where you stand. Towns must be at least 48 blocks apart (half of default 96, `townRadius`) |
| `/realm:town_spot <project>` | Operators | Shows the project's outline where you stand, facing the way you face, in the town you're in (within 96 blocks of its center, default, `townRadius`), and asks to set the spot there, rotate it or cancel. Builds it right away if it's already finished; a built project is moved there (the ground at the old spot is put back) |
| `/realm:town_remove` | Operators | Removes the town you're in and its project progress, after asking, and its own mayor (not Mayor Bram). What's built stays standing |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `announce` | `true` | Finished projects, builds and level-ups are announced to everyone in chat, with a title for a level-up |
| `fireworks` | `true` | Fireworks rise over a project when it's built |
| `deliverWithCommand` | `false` | `/realm:town` also takes deliveries while you're within a town's radius, without the mayor |
| `keepNamedItems` | `true` | Items with a custom name are never delivered |
| `townRadius` | `96` | How close to a town's center (blocks) its mayor answers and `/realm:town_spot`, `/realm:town_remove` and `deliverWithCommand` work. New towns must be at least half this far apart |
| `townMayors` | `true` | A mayor for each town (Townsfolk): made at the center when a town is added, Mayor Bram for the first town; it offers its town wherever the player stands. `false`: no new mayors, and NPCs with `npcRole` offer the town the player is in |
| `autoSpots` | `true` | Towns pick a spot for each project themselves, on natural ground, leveling it gently where needed. Spots operators set are kept and never leveled. `false`: operators set every spot |
| `levelDepth` | `3` | Most blocks an automatic spot's natural ground is cut down or filled up, 0 to 3 (0: only ground that is already level) |
| `outlineSeconds` | `5` | Seconds a build's outline is shown to players within 32 blocks before it goes up at an automatic spot, 0 to 15 |
| `houses` | `true` | From level 2 a town builds a house for each family its level brings, at spots it picks, with nothing to deliver. `false`: no new houses |
| `townLife` | `true` | Paths from the town's builds toward the center (only grass becomes path), lantern posts beside them at each new level (at most 12 a town) and a garden pen with 2 sheep and 2 chickens by the garden. `false`: none of these are added; those there stay |
| `residentsPerLevel` | `[2, 4, 6, 8, 10]` | Families a town has room for at levels 1 to 5; from level 2 it builds a house for each |
| `residentCapTown` | `10` | Most families (residents, and houses) one town has, 0 to 10 |
| `residents` | `true` | Residents move in: villagers that never claim a bed, job site or bell, never work and stay near home (2 at the well, then a family per house). `false`: nobody new moves in and nobody is replaced; residents already living stay |
| `residentCapWorld` | `20` | Most residents in the whole world, 0 to 40. Lowering it removes nobody |
| `residentsTrade` | `false` | Residents trade like vanilla villagers. `false`: a tap on one does nothing (trading would bypass the Crowns economy) |
| `replaceMinutes` | `20` | In-game minutes before a new family moves in for one that died, 5 to 120 (20 is one in-game day) |
| `residentNames` | 40 first names | Residents' names, each used once in the world while there are free ones (plain letters, at most 16) |
| `houseJobs` | 10 job-site blocks | The job-site block of each house a town builds, in turn: `composter`, `lectern`, `barrel`, `smoker`, `cartography_table`, `brewing_stand`, `fletching_table`, `loom`, `stonecutter_block`, `grindstone` |
| `mayorNames` | 20 first names | Names for new towns' mayors (`Mayor Alda`), each used once; when all are taken, `Mayor <Town>` |
| `npcRole` | `"mayor"` | The townsfolk role that offers **Town projects**: for the town the player is in when that town's own mayor isn't placed (and always for one an operator added in Townsfolk's `config.js`) |
| `repPerProject` | `10` | Guild reputation for each contributor when a project is finished (Growers or Miners, by its materials) |
| `topCrowns` | `[60, 35, 20]` | Crowns for the first, second, third... contributor of each finished project |
| `levelNames` | Settlement, Village, Town, City, Capital | What a town is called at levels 1 to 5 |
| `projects` | 7 projects (above) | `{ id, name, level, needs: { <item id>: amount }, build, why?, structure? }`. `why` is what the mayor says the town wants it for (plain text, up to 60 characters: `Fresh water, so families can move in`). `level` 1 to 4 (finishing all of a level raises the town; a level without projects is skipped); `build` is `well`, `lamps`, `stall`, `bell_tower`, `dock`, `garden`, `notice_board` or `house` (a 7 by 7 cottage with a bed and a job-site block); `structure` is an optional saved structure to place instead. Keep each `id` (lowercase letters, digits, `_`): progress and spots are saved by it, and `/realm:town_spot` lists them. `house_1` to `house_10` and `pen` are the town's own works: a project with one of those ids is skipped |

Operators can change `announce`, `fireworks`, `deliverWithCommand`, `keepNamedItems`, `townRadius`, `repPerProject`, `townMayors`, `autoSpots`, `levelDepth`, `outlineSeconds`, `houses`, `townLife`, `residents`, `residentCapWorld`, `residentsTrade` and `replaceMinutes` in game with `/realm:config`. The rest stay in `config.js` (the project list is read when the world starts).

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `town:t:<town>` | World | JSON `{ id, n, dim, x, y, z, lvl, spots, by, at, prot?, v?, m?, mn?, scan?, nos?, rt?, as?, plf?, log?, lp? }`: the town's name, center, level, its story `log` (`[[day, text], ...]`, the newest 12, each at most 60 characters, day 0 when no calendar said it; the oldest go first should the record ever near 30,000 characters), `prot: 0` when **Protect from world events** is Disabled, its mayor `m` (`"bram"`, or `"mayor:<town>"` named `mn`) with `v: 2` (towns saved before mayors have neither and still read), and each project's build spot `{ x, y, z, f, snap?, b?, old?, a?, lv?, lt?, bs?, pt? }` (`f`: 0 south, 1 west, 2 north, 3 east; `snap: 1` once the ground was saved, `b` the box it covers `[x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2]`; `old: 1` for a project built before snapshots, rebuilt in place; `a: 1` for a spot the town picked, with its leveling plan `lv` (one character per column of the outline plus 2 blocks: `.` untouched, `0` to `6` the new ground height from 3 below to 3 above the spot's ground), `lt` the block a fill gets on top, `bs: 1` while its build has started and isn't finished, and `pt: 1` once its path was laid). Automatic spots: `scan` the projects still to get one, `nos` those with no good spot, `rt` those whose spot failed its last check once, `as: 1` once the town's projects were queued (towns from before this version get it on their first check), `plf: 1` once the town's placed-block cells were full (it never levels again), `lp` the level its lantern posts were last put up for (missing: 1) |
| Structure `town:<town>__<project>` | World | The blocks a project's outline covered just before it was built (no entities; at an automatic spot also the 2 blocks around it, from 5 below the spot's ground), put back when it's removed, rebuilt or moved, and deleted after a removal or move or with the town |
| `town:p:<town>:<project>` | World | JSON `{ got, c, done, built }`: items delivered, contributors `{ <player id>: [name, amount] }`, finished and built. Past about 30,000 characters the smallest contributors are dropped. A house (`town:p:<town>:house_<n>`, 1 to 10) has only `{ done, built }`: `done: 1` once the town's level makes it due, and its spot is in the town's `spots` as `house_<n>` like a project's. The garden pen (`town:p:<town>:pen`) is the same, plus `an: 1` once its animals were put in and `k`, the types of those that died (`["minecraft:sheep"]`; never put back) |
| `town:w:<town>` | World | JSON `{ <project or work>: [path, posts] }`: the town's paths and lantern posts by the build they belong to, 6 base-36 characters a block, relative to the town's center (a path at most 48 blocks, at most 12 posts in the town), and `"~<project>"` for what Remove spot couldn't reach yet (not loaded), put back when it is. At most about 16,500 characters (18 builds with full paths and leftovers). Deleted with the town (the paths and posts stay standing) |
| `town:r:<town>` | World | JSON `{ n, r, new }`: the town's residents, one `{ s, i, n, h, e, p, d?, m? }` each (its slot 0 to 9, its resident number, name, home `well` or `house_<n>`, entity id, look, the in-game time a new family replaces it once it died or went missing, censuses it was missing), the next resident number `n`, and the newest 5 names (`new`). Under 2,000 characters. Towns from before this version have none until their first family moves in; it's deleted with the town |
| `town:pl:<town>:0`, `town:pl:<town>:1` | World | Where players placed natural-kind blocks (dirt, sand, stone and the like) or wild plants (flowers, ferns, petals...) in the town since this version, as 4 by 4 by 4 cells (4 base-36 characters each, 2,500 a property, 5,000 in all, the oldest dropped first). Saved at most every 10 seconds. With more than that the town record gets `plf: 1` |
| `town:owed:<player id>`, `town:owed_idx` | World | Each offline contributor's `{ cr, q }` Crowns and latest 10 finished projects, with unknown fields preserved, plus the bounded oldest-first index. Uses the [offline reward storage limits](#offline-reward-storage) |
| `town:owed` | World | Legacy all-player contributor reward map, retained only for unmigrated leftovers |
| `town:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- **The mayor** is an offer in the [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) offer round: the pack answers `realm:npc_talk` with `realm:npc_offer` (key `town:<town id>`, order 30, and 31 for a second town) for the town whose `m` is that NPC, and for the town the player is in from NPCs with the `npcRole` role (see Mayors above), and opens the town's menu on `realm:npc_choose`.
- **Mayors:** the pack asks Townsfolk for a town's mayor with `realm:npc_mayor` `{ op: "set", id: "mayor:<town>", name, town, tn, dim, x, y, z, yaw }` (when a town is added, on **Move here**, and again when a player is in a town whose mayor isn't among the placed townsfolk of `realm:npc_places`, checked every 5 seconds, at most every 30 seconds per town), `{ op: "rename", id, name, tn }` and `{ op: "remove", id }` (with the town); refusals come back as `realm:npc_mayor_ack` `{ id, op, ok: false, error }` and are told to the operator who asked. Five seconds after the world loads it sends `realm:npc_places_ping` and every mayor id as `realm:npc_mayors` `{ part, parts, ids }` (parts under 2,048 characters, `parts: 0` for none), so Townsfolk removes mayors of towns removed meanwhile. Mayor Bram is never created, renamed or removed: **Move Bram here** sends `realm:npc_summon` `{ id: "bram", player }`.
- **Builds** are placed block by block in code (no structure files needed), each block only after checking what's there. Spots that aren't loaded are checked every 5 seconds against where players are, and built when one is within 64 blocks. Fireworks are `minecraft:fireworks_rocket` entities.
- **Automatic spots** (`scripts/sites.js`): a scan reads the ground column by column (`getTopmostBlock`, then down through plants, snow and natural leaves; the water's surface with `getBlockBelow` and liquids included, since `getTopmostBlock` skips water) and keeps the columns until it ends. Candidates sit on rings every 3 blocks from the center (from 6 blocks for the well, 10 for the rest, to 8 blocks inside the edge); a project is decided once it has 6 valid candidates and the next ring is 16 blocks beyond the best, and the best 3 are read again under every cut. Leaves count as natural only when `persistent_bit` is false. Claims come from one `realm:claims_check` `{ id, player: "", dim, x1, z1, x2, z2 }` over the town's square (answered with `realm:claims_check_result`; with 10 claims back, each finalist is asked again; no answer in 1 second means Land Claims isn't installed), townsfolk posts from `realm:npc_places`, story places from `realm:place_ready` (asked with `realm:place_ping` 5 seconds after the world loads). Ground that isn't loaded makes candidates wait (the project stays in `scan`); after 3 such scans in a session the best spot known is taken. One town is scanned at a time.
- **Building at an automatic spot:** the outline for `outlineSeconds`, a block-by-block check of the region (from 5 below the spot's ground to 1 above the build), the snapshot and `bs: 1`, then cuts top down, fills bottom up and the design, 48 block changes a tick. A chunk that unloads pauses it; `bs: 1` resumes it when a player is near again (applying it twice changes nothing). Whether resumed or not, it waits while a player stands in the region ("Step off the spot"), and it never cuts, fills or builds over a block in a cell a player placed blocks in since the check. A resumed build checks for land claims again; a saved structure is placed only when its box holds nothing but air, natural ground and wild plants nobody placed. If either fails, the half-done build stops where it is and operators are told: Remove spot puts the region back, or it tries again after a restart. Remove spot during a build puts the region back too.
- **Houses** are town works (`house_1` to `house_10`), not entries of `projects`: when a town reaches a level (or on the 5-second check, for towns from before this version and after `houses` is Enabled) the ones due are marked done and queued for the scan, then built like a finished project at an automatic spot. Their design is built in code; the bed's two halves and the door's two halves each go in together in one step (or neither does, if something is in the way), with their direction turned to the spot. Removing a house (or any build) breaks a barrel, smoker or brewing stand with something in it, and a lectern, the way a player does, so what it holds drops instead of being lost.
- **Small life** (`scripts/life.js`): on the 5-second check, while a player is in the town, one job at a time asks Land Claims about the area (`realm:claims_check`, 1 second), reads the blocks 32 a tick and then lays the path or the posts at once, each block checked again just before it changes (a path block only while it is still grass with air or its wild plant above, a post only on natural ground with 2 open blocks). A path's start is the block in front of the build (1 block ahead of its spot); a path that meets ground that isn't loaded waits for a later check (3 times in a session, then what was found is laid). The pen's spot is picked by the scan in rings from 9 to 30 blocks around the middle of the garden instead of the center; its animals are spawned with `spawnFresh` (`minecraft:sheep`, `minecraft:chicken`) and tagged once spawned.
- **Residents** are vanilla `minecraft:villager_v2`, spawned with `spawn_from_village` (as Wanderers of the Wilds spawns its villagers, checked with `spawnFresh`), named with the vanilla name tag (a named villager never despawns), given their look's `minecraft:become_<profession>` event and then `realm:become_resident`, and tagged `realm:resident`, `town:r:<town>` and `town:rid:<town>.<n>`. Vanilla villagers claim any free bed, job site and bell in a village, players' too, and the stable script API can't stop it, so this pack carries a copy of the vanilla villager's behavior file (`entities/villager_v2.json`, format 1.26.20: the newest `villager_v2.json` among Bedrock Dedicated Server 1.26.52's vanilla packs, which are packed into archives) with three additions: the property `realm:resident` (bool), the component group `realm:town_resident` (`minecraft:dweller` with `can_find_poi: false` and `can_migrate: false`, so no bed, job site or bell is ever claimed; `minecraft:home` with a 16-block restriction and `minecraft:behavior.move_towards_home_restriction`, so they stay near home without script work), and the event `realm:become_resident`, which first takes off the vanilla work schedules, work goals and love groups (`basic_schedule`, `farmer_schedule`, `fisher_schedule`, `librarian_schedule`, `work_schedule`, `work_schedule_farmer`, `work_schedule_fisher`, `work_schedule_librarian`, `work_schedule_villager`, `job_specific_goals`, `make_and_receive_love`: a farmer's work harvests every ripe crop near it, a player's farm too), then adds the group and the vanilla `jobless_schedule` (a nitwit's day: wander, gather, home) and sets the property. The profession event goes first because a profession's group brings back its own dweller; it keeps the look only. Nothing in the base components changes, so every other villager in the world (village villagers, Wanderers, cured zombie villagers) behaves exactly as before. Only one behavior pack may define `minecraft:villager_v2`: with another add-on that does, the property is missing on the first villager spawned, it is removed again at once, residents stop and operators are told. After a Minecraft update that changes the villager, copy the newest vanilla file into `entities/villager_v2.json` and put the three additions back. A death (`entityDie`, villagers only) marks the family for replacement `replaceMinutes` of in-game time later (`world.getAbsoluteTime()`). Every 30 seconds, only for a town with a player in it and one town per check, a census does one `getEntities` by the town's tag: a resident missing for 2 censuses in a row while its home is loaded is gone (a zombie conversion, `/kill` without the event) and is replaced too; one past the town radius, or more than 32 blocks from its home (`HOME_LEASH` in `residents.js`: vanilla villagers explore the outskirts at dusk, and `minecraft:home`'s restriction doesn't hold them) while no player is within 16 blocks of it, is teleported home (unless a player leads it); a second villager with the same tag or one the record doesn't know (a cured zombie villager, a family replaced meanwhile) loses the tags and stays an ordinary villager, never killed; then at most 2 new families, replacements or moves. A town removed takes the tags off its loaded residents; one far away loses them the first time someone taps it. A tap on a resident is canceled in `world.beforeEvents.playerInteractWithEntity` (it returns at once when another pack canceled the tap already).
- **Cost:** with nothing to do, nothing runs (the job runs only while there is a scan or a build). A scan reads at most 12 columns a tick (3 to 5 block reads each) and stops for the tick sooner once it has looked through 100 columns of what it already read (`SCAN.workTick`; a grading plan counts row by row), so a tick of scanning costs about 1.2 ms on Bedrock Dedicated Server 1.26.52 (October 2026, 10 players; the longest tick 7 ms). Each footprint is looked at and graded once a scan (the houses reuse what the first house found), and a pad whose footprint alone already needs more leveling than a plan found there is never graded; a level's projects take one to two minutes on flat ground and up to about ten on a steep hillside (8.5 minutes for a Village's 6 projects on the test's terraces); a build checks 64 blocks or changes 48 a tick for a few seconds. The 5-second build check adds a loop over the towns. Residents are vanilla mobs, so their AI is the game's own cost; the script side is a death handler and one census per town with a player in it every 30 seconds (one `getEntities`, under 0.01 ms a tick on average). Small life is blocks placed once: a path or the posts take a second or two of 32 reads a tick when a build goes up or a level is reached; the pen's 4 animals are ordinary mobs, counted every 30 seconds only while a player is by the pen. Two towns at Capital have 2 mayors (plus their name labels while a player is near), at most 20 residents and 8 pen animals; with 10 players there and no scan or build running, Town Projects costs 0.013 ms a tick and Townsfolk 0.07 (measured October 2026).
- **Town news** goes to Townsfolk as `realm:gossip` `{ kind: "town_life", place: <town name>, from: <the town's mayor, "bram" or "mayor:<town>"> }` for a new family, a new house and a new level (towns from before mayors send no `from`), each once a session and at most one piece of this pack's news an in-game hour (shared with the project news).
- **Messages sent** to each contributor of a finished project: `realm:quest_done` `{ player, pack: "town_bp", id: "town_<town>_<project>", label, kind: "town", guild }` and `realm:rep_add` `{ player, guild, amount: repPerProject }`, with `guild` `growers` or `miners`. Crowns go straight into the `crowns` scoreboard.
- **Snapshots** use `world.structureManager.createFromWorld` (saved to the world) right before the first build at a spot, and `Structure.getBlockPermutation` to put the ground back block by block, only where the block now is air, liquid, of a kind the build is made of, and not already the saved one. The outline is the min and max of the design's block offsets, turned to the spot's facing (or a saved structure's size, with x and z swapped for a quarter turn).
- **Safe zones:** every town with **Protect from world events** Enabled is sent as `realm:zones` `{ src: "town", part, parts, zones: [{ id, name, dim, x, z, r, shape: "circle" }] }` (`r` = `townRadius`, `part` from 1, split under 2,048 characters; an empty list has `parts: 0`) when a town is added, removed or toggled, when `townRadius` changes, 5 seconds after the world loads, and in reply to `realm:zones_ping`.
- **The Realm day** for the story comes from `realm:calendar` `{ day, ... }` (Townsfolk or Realm Calendar), asked for with `realm:calendar_ping` 5 seconds after the world loads.
- **Realm Calendar:** every town goes out as `realm:town_list` `{ part, parts, towns: [{ id, n, dim, x, y, z, safe }] }` with the zones (and on `realm:town_list_ping`); moods come in as `realm:town_state` `{ town, mood, until }` (kept in memory; asked again with `realm:town_state_ping` at load).
- **Scenario tests:** `/scriptevent realm:town_test {"action": ...}` runs the operator actions without forms (`add`, `spot` with an optional `spot: { x, y, z, f }`, `finish`, `remove`, `rebuild`, `protect`, `zones`, `dump` with the placed townsfolk ids, `mayor_move` with an optional `spot: { x, y, z, yaw }`, `mayor_rename` with `name`, `remove_town`, `v1`: every town as saved before mayors, until the next load, `scan`: **Find spots again** and start the scan now, `build_pause` with `after`: builds at automatic spots stop after that many block changes until the next load, as if the server stopped; `census`: the town's residents census now; `residents_due`: every family waiting to be replaced is due now; `dump` also shows the scan and build in progress, the placed-block cell count, the residents and each slot's home, the paths and posts (`life`, as saved) with the small-life job in progress (`living`), and each spot's region), for the test harness. It's only honored from the server console or an operator.
- **Placed blocks:** natural-kind blocks look like the ground to a script (a block has no owner), so `world.afterEvents.playerPlaceBlock` marks the 4 by 4 by 4 cell of each one, and of each wild plant (a flower bed looks like wild ground), a player places within a town's radius (one type check, then a distance check per town), and packs that place natural blocks by script can send `realm:blocks_placed` `{ dim, box: [x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2] }` (or `x1` to `z2` as fields; a box of more than 5,000 cells marks the town full at once). Every other kind is man-made anyway.
- **Not Community Goals:** [Community Goals](#community-goals--goals_bp) is a realm-wide donation chest for one item; Town Projects belong to a town, need several items, go through the mayor and build something. They don't share data.
