## Easy Building — `build_bp`

Effortless Building v5.0 ported directly into the Realm: build lines, walls, floors, diagonal lines and walls, sloped floors, cubes, circles, semicircles (flat, arch or dome), cylinders, spheres, cones and Bezier splines by clicking two or three anchor points in the world with a live 3D block outline preview. Includes floating 3D in-world UI panels, a hold-right-click radial Quick Switch Wheel, Mirror/Array/Radial modifiers (which also work on single hand-placed and broken blocks), multi-block Palettes with noise/gradient/structural patterns, Air Build and Infinite Reach, Copy/Cut/Paste with a multi-slot Clipboard, Destroy mode with digging tools, Undo/Redo, a 48-page illustrated 3D Tutorial Book, and an interactive Live Coach in 13 languages.

### How to use

1. Hold the **Building Book** (`/realm:build_book`, or craft one from a book and paper or a brick; its last lore line says `Hold it in your hand and use it`):
   - **Right-click (tap):** opens the floating 3D **Mode Menu** (or `/realm:build`). Aim at any tile and click to pick a mode, toggle options (filled/hollow/skeleton, even/uneven, straight/bezier, horizontal/arch/dome), pin favorite modes, or open Tools.
   - **Hold right-click:** opens the floating **Quick Switch Wheel** right in front of you; aim at a slice and release right-click to switch modes on the fly.
   - **Left-click (swing):** opens the **Block Palette** (`/realm:build_palette`).
   - **Sneak + left-click:** opens **Modifiers** (`/realm:build_modifiers`: Mirror, Array, Radial).
   - **Sneak + right-click:** opens **Settings** (`/realm:build_settings`).
   - **Double-sneak while holding the book:** toggles between your active build mode and `Disable`.
2. **Two-click shapes** (Line, Diagonal Line, Wall, Floor, Circle, Semicircle, Sphere): hold any block and right-click to set the **first anchor** (`Anchor set`). As you look around, the live 3D outline preview stretches to your aim and shows the dimensions and block count above the hotbar. Right-click again to place the entire shape. The anchor stays while you hold something else (a sword, food, an empty hand): its outline just isn't drawn until you hold that block again. Right-clicking with a different block or a digging tool starts a new anchor instead; changing the mode or going to another dimension clears it.
3. **Three-click shapes** (Cube, Cylinder, Cone, Diagonal Wall, Slope Floor): right-click to set the first anchor, right-click a second time to lock the horizontal **XZ footprint**, then look up or down to stretch the height and right-click a third time to build.
4. **Bezier curves:** select **Line** or **Diagonal Line** and set **Curve** to `Bezier`. Right-click to add curve waypoints through the world, then **Sneak + right-click** to place the smooth Catmull-Rom spline through all points.
5. **Destroy mode:** while any shape mode is active, hold a **pickaxe, axe or shovel** and right-click a block to set a red **Destroy anchor**. Right-click again (or a third time for 3-step shapes) to mine the entire shape with tool tier checks, Unbreaking wear, Fortune/Silk Touch drops, and spare-tool swapping.
6. **Air Build and Infinite Reach:** choose **Air Build** mode to place single blocks in midair in front of you (`airBuildReach`, default 4 blocks), or enable **Infinite Reach** in `/realm:build_settings` (`allowInfiniteReach`) to set anchors and build shapes at a distance in midair (`maxReachCap`, default 64 blocks).
7. **Modifiers** (`/realm:build_modifiers` or Sneak + left-click with the Building Book): enable **Mirror** (X, Y, Z axes, odd/even center, radius), **Array** (offset X/Y/Z and copy count), and/or **Radial** (2 to 16 slices around a center, optional alternate slice mirroring). Colored guide planes mark your active mirror and radial axes, and modifiers also copy single blocks you place or break by hand when build mode is `Disable`.
8. **Palette** (`/realm:build_palette` or left-click with the Building Book): mix blocks from your **Hotbar**, **Inventory**, or **Both**, weighted by item count, slot count, or unique block types, using Random, Spread, Gradients (X, Y, Z, Radial, Diagonal), Concentric Rings, Checkerboard, Noise (Value/Worley), Bricks, Pillars, or Frame patterns, plus smart Glazed Terracotta pinwheel tiling.
9. **Copy, Cut and Paste:** select **Copy / Paste** mode. Right-click corner 1, corner 2, and height (corner 3) to open the **Copy / Cut** prompt. Once copied or cut, aim to preview the rotated bounding box (or full ghost preview) and right-click to paste; **Sneak + right-click** clears the clipboard to select a new region. Manage saved slots in `/realm:build_clipboard`.
10. **Undo and Redo:** run `/realm:build_undo` and `/realm:build_redo` (or click **Undo** / **Redo** in the Mode Menu Tools row) to step backward or forward up to 10 actions; survival builds refund placed blocks to your inventory on undo.
11. **Tutorial Book and Live Coach:** run `/realm:build_tutorial` for the 48-page illustrated 3D **Effortless Building Tutorial** book (its last lore line: `Works in your main hand`), `/realm:build_guide` to start the interactive **Live Coach** walkthrough, and `/realm:build_language` to switch between 13 languages.
12. **Operators:** `/realm:config` -> **Easy Building** (or the **Admin** tab in `/realm:build_settings`) sets realm-wide limits and permissions. Prefer standard menus instead of 3D floating panels? Switch **Menu Style** to **Plain** under Controls in `/realm:build_settings` (or enable `plainMenusForAll` for everyone).

Beds use Bedrock's `minecraft:bed` and `minecraft:straw_bed`, not Java color-specific ids. A complete bed is two blocks but costs one bed item. Placement, clipboard limits and undo keep both halves together; an unavailable partner rejects the pair. This holds in every shape mode (Line through Cone), with Mirror, Array and Radial, in Air Build, for paste and for Destroy (breaking one half takes the other). Native item data and supported facing states are retained. Preview and modifier loops run only for players holding a building tool (see How it works).

### Modes and options

| Mode | Steps | Options |
|---|---|---|
| **Disable** | - | Normal vanilla block placing and breaking (active Modifiers still mirror/repeat hand-placed and broken blocks) |
| **Air Build** | 1 | Places blocks in midair at your Air Build reach distance (1 to 64 blocks, default 4) |
| **Line** | 2 | `Curve`: `Straight` or `Bezier` (multi-point Catmull-Rom spline; Sneak + click to finish) |
| **Diagonal Line** | 2 | `Curve`: `Straight` or `Bezier` |
| **Wall** | 2 | `Fill`: `Filled` or `Hollow` (vertical wall along the dominant axis) |
| **Diagonal Wall** | 3 | `Fill`: `Filled` or `Hollow` (angled wall between any two XZ points, then height) |
| **Floor** | 2 | `Fill`: `Filled` or `Hollow` (horizontal floor on the anchor's Y plane) |
| **Slope Floor** | 3 | `Fill`: `Filled` or `Hollow` (inclined ramp between two XZ points, then height) |
| **Cube** | 3 | `Fill`: `Filled`, `Hollow` (6 walls), or `Skeleton` (12 wireframe edges) |
| **Circle** | 2 | `Fill`: `Filled` or `Hollow`; `Shape`: `Even` or `Uneven` (ellipses) |
| **Semicircle** | 2 | `Shape`: `Horizontal`, `Arch`, or `Dome`; `Fill`: `Filled` or `Hollow` |
| **Cylinder** | 3 | `Fill`: `Filled` or `Hollow`; `Shape`: `Even` or `Uneven` |
| **Sphere** | 2 | `Fill`: `Filled` or `Hollow` |
| **Cone** | 3 | `Fill`: `Filled` or `Hollow`; `Axis`: `Straight` or `Diagonal` |
| **Copy / Paste** | 3 | Select 3 corners to Copy or Cut, then right-click to Paste (rotates with your facing) |

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:build` | Everyone | Opens the Effortless Building mode menu (3D floating panel or plain menu) |
| `/realm:build_book` | Everyone | Gives you an Effortless Building `Building Book` |
| `/realm:build_tutorial` | Everyone | Gives you the 48-page illustrated `Effortless Building Tutorial` book |
| `/realm:build_guide` | Everyone | Starts or stops the interactive Live Coach tutorial |
| `/realm:build_palette` | Everyone | Opens the Block Palette (source, weighting, distribution patterns, glazed terracotta tiling) |
| `/realm:build_modifiers` | Everyone | Opens Modifiers: Mirror (X/Y/Z), Array, and Radial symmetry |
| `/realm:build_clipboard` | Everyone | Opens the Clipboard Manager (auto-saved copy and named saved slots) |
| `/realm:build_settings` | Everyone | Opens Effortless Building Settings (Setup, Building, Preview, Controls, and Admin for operators) |
| `/realm:build_preview` | Everyone | Opens the Preview Settings tab directly (outline style, refresh quality, defer shape, flick mode) |
| `/realm:build_setup` | Everyone | Opens the device performance preset picker (Low-end, Mid-end, High-end) |
| `/realm:build_language` | Everyone | Opens the 13-language picker for floating panels, coach, and tutorial book |
| `/realm:build_undo` | Everyone | Undoes your last Effortless Building placement (restores blocks and refunds survival items) |
| `/realm:build_redo` | Everyone | Redoes the last undone Effortless Building placement |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Easy Building for the whole realm. Disabled: commands say so and placing blocks builds nothing extra |
| `operatorsOnly` | `false` | Only operators can use the building tools |
| `maxBlocksCap` | `50000` | Maximum blocks per build allowed on the realm (64 to 300000 in game); Woodwrights with Builder's Eye ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp)) get up to 25% more. Lowering it immediately clamps saved personal limits. Raising it does not raise an unset player's default |
| `defaultMaxBlocks` | `50000` | Starting blocks-per-build limit for a player with no saved choice, always clamped to `maxBlocksCap`. Independent of the cap, so increasing the cap does not silently increase everyone's limit |
| `modeComplexity` | `"player"` | Mode list complexity: `"player"` (players choose Simple or All modes), `"simple"` (Force Simple: Disable, Line, Wall, Floor, Cube), or `"advanced"` (Force All 15 modes) |
| `tagRequired` | `false` | Require a player tag (`requiredTag`) to use Effortless Building (operators are always allowed) |
| `requiredTag` | `"admin"` | The tag name required when `tagRequired` is enabled |
| `allowDestroy` | `true` | Allow Destroy mode when right-clicking with a pickaxe, axe or shovel |
| `destroyCreativeOnly` | `false` | Restrict Destroy mode to Creative mode only |
| `allowInfiniteReach` | `true` | Allow players to enable Infinite Reach to place and destroy at a distance in midair (on a public server, consider disabling it: big builds at a distance are a lag tool in the wrong hands) |
| `maxReachCap` | `64` | Longest Infinite Reach distance players may pick, in blocks (0 = no cap, up to 256) |
| `autoGiveBook` | `false` | Automatically give the Building Book and Tutorial Book to new players on their first spawn |
| `configTagRequired` | `false` | Restrict changing Preview Quality to players with `requiredTag` |
| `plainMenusForAll` | `false` | Use standard menus instead of 3D floating panels for all players |
| `inOthersClaims` | `false` | Allow builds and destroy actions to reach into other players' land claims ([Land Claims](#land-claims--claims_bp)) |
| `safeZonesOperatorsOnly` | `true` | Inside a safe zone made with [Safe Zones](#safe-zones--zones_bp) (`/realm:zones`), only operators can build or destroy with the tools |

Operators can change every option in game with `/realm:config` (**Easy Building**) or in the **Admin** tab of `/realm:build_settings`. Each player's own preferences in `/realm:prefs` and `/realm:build_settings` share the same `eb:*` properties.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `build:cfg` | World | World settings changed in `/realm:config` (`enabled`, `operatorsOnly`, `inOthersClaims`, `safeZonesOperatorsOnly`) |
| `eb:adminMaxBlocksCap`, `eb:defaultMaxBlocks`, `eb:adminModeComplexity`, `eb:tagRequired`, `eb:requiredTag`, `eb:allowDestroy`, `eb:destroyCreativeOnly`, `eb:allowInfiniteReach`, `eb:maxReachCap`, `eb:autoGiveBook`, `eb:configTagRequired`, `eb:globalCustomUI` | World | Effortless Building admin settings shared between `/realm:config` and `/realm:build_settings`; the default block limit is separate from the cap |
| `eb:modifiers`, `eb:palette`, `eb:palette_dist`, `eb:palette_weight`, `eb:smartPattern`, `eb:modeOpts`, `eb:pins`, `eb:wheel` | Player | Active mirror/array/radial modifier settings, palette settings, per-mode options, pinned modes, and quick-wheel layout |
| `eb:clip_meta`, `eb:clip_<slot>_<chunk>` | Player | Saved clipboard slots and auto-saved copy/cut data |
| `eb:undo_n`, `eb:undo_<i>`, `eb:redo_n`, `eb:redo_<i>` | Player | Persistent undo and redo snapshots |
| `eb:previewMode`, `eb:destroyPreviewMode`, `eb:previewQuality`, `eb:deferShapeCalc`, `eb:flickPreview`, `eb:simpleModes`, `eb:buildSpeed`, `eb:maxBlocks`, `eb:replaceBlocks`, `eb:infiniteReach`, `eb:infiniteReachDistance`, `eb:airBuildReach`, `eb:destroyDrops`, `eb:undoThreshold`, `eb:floatingUI`, `eb:cursor`, `eb:panelSize`, `eb:coachSide`, `eb:panelSounds`, `eb:swapBookActions`, `eb:fovZoomEnabled`, `eb:hintsEnabled`, `eb:bookLanguage` | Player | Per-player preferences shared between `/realm:prefs` and `/realm:build_settings`. Without `eb:maxBlocks` a player gets `defaultMaxBlocks` (default 50,000), clamped to `maxBlocksCap`. Raising the cap does not raise that default; lowering the cap immediately clamps an existing saved choice. A build speed changed in `/realm:prefs` applies to the next build (before, at the next join). The old menu switch `eb:customUI` moves to `eb:floatingUI` when a player joins, so **Floating 3D panels** in `/realm:prefs` shows and sets what counts. **Preview refresh interval** offers only the speeds the pack has (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20 ticks); preferences that do nothing for a player (Easy Building off, operators only, a missing tag, Destroy mode or Infinite Reach not allowed, plain menus for everyone, a forced mode list) show as locked there |

### How it works

- **Idle players cost nothing per tick:** what each player holds comes from the hotbar and inventory events (a change in the selected slot), not from reading every hand. The preview and modifier loops look only at players holding a building tool: the Building or Tutorial Book, Copy / Paste mode, or a block or digging tool while a build mode or a Mirror, Array or Radial is on. A survival player holding dirt with building off is not one, so a server where nobody builds runs none of that work. The double-sneak toggle and the book's name and lore check look only at Building Book holders, the Tutorial Book only at its holders, and the camera zoom only at players with an anchor. As backstops for a missed event, the hotbar slot of players who are building is compared every tick and everyone else's every half second (a property read, no inventory read), and a fifth of the players' hands are read again every second (each about every 5 seconds).
- **The line above the hotbar** (mode prompts, sizes, the paste countdown) is a steady line of the action bar protocol (rank 30, see [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)): it announces itself with `realm:actionbar` at most every 10 ticks while it shows, and most of its one-off notes (`Built 15 blocks`) send a request first (a few from the Effortless Building port, such as the undo and paste notes, don't yet).

## Easy Building Guides — `build_rp`

The resource pack for [Easy Building](#easy-building--build_bp): 3D floating UI panels, the radial Quick Switch Wheel, the 48-page illustrated 3D Tutorial Book, Live Coach markers, directional block outline and destroy particles (`eb:*`), UI sound definitions (`eb.ui.*`), 13 language files, and the Building Book and Tutorial Book icons. Part of **Realm Resources** (or downloadable on its own).

### How to use

1. Nothing to do as a player: when the realm has **Realm Resources** active, Minecraft downloads it automatically when you join.
2. Hold the **Building Book** and right-click (or hold right-click for the radial wheel) to use the 3D floating panels in the world, or hold the **Effortless Building Tutorial** book (`/realm:build_tutorial`) to flip through its 3D illustrated pages.
3. **Operators:** included in **Realm Resources** under **Resource Packs**.

### What players see

- **3D Floating Panels & Quick Switch Wheel:** interactive in-world panels for the Mode Menu, Quick Switch Ring, Modifiers, Mirror/Array/Radial configuration, Block Palette, Clipboard, Copy/Cut prompt, Onboarding Setup, and Settings, with hover highlights, aiming cursor, and UI sounds.
- **3D Illustrated Tutorial Book & Live Coach:** an animated book entity (`eb:guide_book`) that opens in front of you with 24 spreads (48 pages) in 13 languages, plus ghost previews and markers for the Live Coach.
- **Block Outlines & Modifier Guides:** crisp per-face white build outlines (`eb:top*`, `eb:bottom*`, `eb:x1*`, `eb:x2*`, `eb:z1*`, `eb:z2*`), red destroy outlines (`*_d*`), controller emitters (`eb:controller*`) across 7 refresh quality tiers (`q1` to `q20`), and colored symmetry planes (`eb:mod_x`, `eb:mod_z`, `eb:mod_top`).
- **Book Icons:** icons for `eb:building_book`, `realm:building_book`, and `eb:tutorial_book`.

### Saved data

None. It's a resource pack: no scripts and no commands.

### How it's made

`npm run gen:build` (`tools/gen-build/gen.mjs`) verifies the generated pack icon and base guide textures; the Effortless Building v5.0 models, animations, render controllers, particles, texts, and panel/book textures live alongside them in `packs/build_rp/`.

Geometry/client resources for `realm:npc_name_probe` support a disabled, test-only name-visibility experiment. Production scripts never spawn it; these resources do not establish readable 20-block names or replace the existing legacy-label cleanup resources.

## Safe Zones — `zones_bp`

Mark your base, a town square or a farm as a **safe zone**, and world events leave it alone: meteors don't make craters there, storm lightning doesn't strike (so it can't start fires), tornadoes can be set to calm down or steer around it, and Blood Moon creepers don't spawn in it. The events still happen, and you still see the meteor streak across the sky; they just break no blocks inside. Towns ([Town Projects](#town-projects--town_bp)) and land claims ([Land Claims](#land-claims--claims_bp)) can be safe zones too, and the world-event packs treat them all the same.

### How to use

1. Run `/realm:zones`. The top of the menu says whether the spot you're standing on is protected, and by what (`Where you stand: protected by Home (Safe zone).`).
2. **Safe zones** lists every zone made with this pack, nearest first, with its center, radius and how far it is from you. Pick one and **Show outline**: green sparkles trace its edge around you for 20 seconds (`previewSeconds`), and the bar above the hotbar says whether you're inside and how far the edge is.
3. **Towns and claims** lists the protected areas other packs share (towns with **Protect from world events**, claims while **Protect claims from world events** is on), read only, with their source; **Show outline** works for them too, and operators get **Teleport (operator)** to the center's surface (the top of the water over a lake or the sea). **Show nearby outlines** traces every zone whose edge is within 64 blocks of you.
4. **Operators:** stand in the middle of the place and pick **Add a safe zone here**. Type a name (up to 24 characters) and set the radius with the slider: 8 to 512 blocks in steps of 8 (starting at 64, `defaultRadius`; at most `maxRadius`). Pick **Preview**: white sparkles outline the circle around you, and after a few seconds a menu asks **Create it**, **Look again**, **Change name or size** or **Cancel** (closed it? `/realm:zones` shows **Create Home** at the top until you decide). A zone reaches from the bottom of the world to the top.
5. **Operators:** pick a zone in **Safe zones** to **Edit name or size**, **Move here** (centers it where you stand, with the same preview), **Teleport** to its center, or **Remove** it. Meteor Strikes' **Protect this area from meteors** button opens the same **Add a safe zone here**.
6. **Operators:** to let everyone protect their own base, enable **Players can add safe zones** in `/realm:config` → **Safe Zones** (`playersCreate`). Each player can then add up to 1 zone (`playerMaxZones`) of up to 64 blocks radius (`playerMaxRadius`), and change, move or remove their own.

### What players see

- **Inside a safe zone** (any zone from any provider, in the zone's dimension, top to bottom):
  - [Meteor Strikes](#meteor-strikes--meteor_bp): no meteor is aimed into one, and no crater block is ever placed or removed in one. A meteor that still comes down over a zone lands just outside it, or bursts in the sky above it (the meteor pack's **A meteor over a safe zone** setting).
  - [Storm Chasing](#storm-chasing--storm_bp): no storm cell lightning strikes in or right next to a zone, so it can't start fires there. Lightning rods inside still get struck and charged.
  - [Tornadoes](#tornadoes--tornado_bp): a tornado never breaks blocks anywhere; its **Tornadoes and safe zones** setting picks whether it passes through as usual, moves nothing inside a zone, or steers around zones.
  - [Blood Moon](#blood-moon--harvest-moon--moon_bp): no Blood Moon creeper spawns in a zone (another monster comes instead).
  - [Creeper Guard](#creeper-guard--guard_bp): in its protected zones mode, creeper blasts break nothing in a safe zone either.
- **What it doesn't stop:** vanilla lightning from an ordinary thunderstorm, fire spread, creepers and other mobs that spawn on their own (use Creeper Guard for creeper blasts), and players. A safe zone isn't a land claim.
- **Overlaps** are fine: zones may overlap each other, towns and claims.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:zones` | Everyone | Opens the Safe Zones menu: whether you're in a safe zone, the list of safe zones (nearest first) and of protected towns and claims, with **Show outline** for each and **Show nearby outlines**. Operators also add a zone where they stand (radius 8 to 512, default 64, `defaultRadius`) with a preview, edit, move, teleport to and remove zones. With `playersCreate` enabled (default disabled), players can add their own too (1 each, `playerMaxZones`, radius up to 64, `playerMaxRadius`) |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `defaultRadius` | `64` | Where the radius slider of **Add a safe zone here** starts, in blocks |
| `maxRadius` | `512` | Largest radius a zone can have, in blocks (8 to 512, in steps of 8) |
| `previewSeconds` | `20` | Seconds an outline shows: the preview of a new zone, **Show outline** and **Show nearby outlines** |
| `playersCreate` | `false` | Players who aren't operators can add safe zones, within the two limits below. Operators always can |
| `playerMaxZones` | `1` | Most safe zones one player (not an operator) can have |
| `playerMaxRadius` | `64` | Largest radius a player (not an operator) can give a zone, in blocks |

Operators can change every option but `previewSeconds` in game with `/realm:config` when Realm Settings is installed. The realm has room for 100 zones made with this pack.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `zones:list` | World | JSON list of the zones: `{ id, name, dim, x, y, z, r, o?, on? }`, its id (`z1`, `z2`...), name, dimension, center (and the height it was made at, for **Teleport**), radius, and the id and name of the player who added it when that wasn't an operator |
| `zones:next` | World | The next zone id number |
| `zones:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

Towns and claims aren't saved here: their packs send them again whenever the world starts.

### How it works

- This pack is the `zones` provider of the safe zones protocol (see [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)): it sends its whole list as `realm:zones` whenever a zone changes, 5 seconds after the world loads, and when any pack sends `realm:zones_ping`. It also listens to the other providers, so its lists are complete.
- `realm:zones_open` `{ player, action: "add" }` opens **Add a safe zone here** for that player (Meteor Strikes' **Protect this area from meteors**); any other action opens the menu (Creeper Guard's **Safe zones** button).
- Outlines are `Player.spawnParticle` (`minecraft:villager_happy`, `minecraft:endrod` for a preview) every half second, only along the part of the edge within 40 blocks of you and at your height, so a 512-block zone costs no more than a small one.

## Weather Almanac — `weather_bp`

Plans the overworld weather hours ahead, so the realm has a forecast: clear spells, rain and thunderstorms come and go on a schedule in real time, and anyone can look up what's coming with `/realm:weather` (or ask Sol the Sky-reader). Rain and storms last a realistic while, a clear spell always ends in rain or a storm, and rain can build into a thunderstorm.

### How to use

1. About 10 seconds after you first join each day (UTC), chat gives the day's forecast in one line, for example `Forecast: clear now, rain in about 25 minutes. More with /realm:weather`. Don't want it? Disable **Daily forecast in chat** in `/realm:prefs`.
2. Run `/realm:weather` (or `/realm:weather_forecast`) to see the forecast for the next 3 hours: what the weather is now and how long it lasts, then every spell coming up with its start time (in UTC) and length, and a summary such as `Rain in 25 min, for about 12 min. Thunderstorm likely around 14:40 UTC.`
3. With the [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) pack, tap Sol the Sky-reader (or any townsfolk with the `skymage` role) and pick **Forecast** for the same.
4. Sleeping through rain or a thunderstorm ends it, as in vanilla: the sky clears and the plan carries on from there (the forecast updates).
5. **Operators:** `/realm:weather` opens a menu with **Forecast** and **Set the weather** (pick clear, rain or a thunderstorm and 5 to 240 real minutes). `/realm:weather_set <clear|rain|thunder> <minutes>` does the same from chat: it starts that weather now for that many real minutes, and the plan carries on after it. Everyone else online gets a chat line: `An operator set the weather: Rain for 10 minutes. The forecast is updated.` Vanilla `/weather` doesn't stick while the almanac runs: it's put back within a second. `/realm:config` → **Weather Almanac** sets how long each kind of weather lasts and how likely thunder is, or disables the almanac to give the weather back to the game.

### What players see

- **The weather follows a plan**, 3 hours ahead (`horizonHours`), in real time:
  - **Clear** spells last 30 to 90 minutes (`clear.minMinutes`, `clear.maxMinutes`) and always end in rain, or, one time in ten (`thunderAfterClear`, 0.1), straight in a thunderstorm.
  - **Rain** lasts 8 to 20 minutes (`rain.minMinutes`, `rain.maxMinutes`), then clears, or builds into a thunderstorm 35% of the time (`thunderAfterRain`).
  - **Thunderstorms** last 6 to 12 minutes (`thunder.minMinutes`, `thunder.maxMinutes`), then clear, or ease back into rain half the time (`rainAfterThunder`).
  - Each length is picked at random between its shortest and longest.
- **The forecast** (`/realm:weather`, title `Weather Forecast`) starts with the summary line, then `Now: Rain, for about 12 min more (until 14:40 UTC).` and a `Coming up:` list such as `15:15 UTC  Thunderstorm, about 9 min (in 47 min)`. Times are real time in UTC, so they mean the same for everyone. The plan is saved in the world: after a restart it carries on where it was, skipping whatever the realm missed while it was closed.
- **The daily chat line** reads `Forecast: clear now, rain in about 25 minutes.`, `Forecast: rain now, clearing in about 12 minutes.` or `Forecast: thunderstorm now, easing to rain in about 8 minutes.` (`dailyForecast`; once per player per UTC day).
- **Sleeping:** when a night or a daytime thunderstorm is skipped by sleeping (vanilla's or [AFK + Smart Sleep](#afk--smart-sleep--afk_bp)'s), the rain or storm that was on is over and a new clear spell starts, so the forecast after waking is fresh. This matches vanilla, where sleeping clears the weather.
- **Other weather changes** (vanilla `/weather`, or another pack) are put back to the plan a second later, and operators online are told in chat (at most every 10 minutes): `[Weather] The Weather Almanac put the weather back to Rain (it was changed to Thunderstorm without the almanac, maybe by /weather). Use /realm:weather_set to change the weather.` If something keeps changing it (more than 6 times in a minute), the almanac stops fighting it for the rest of that minute and the content log says so.

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:weather` | Everyone | The forecast (below). Operators get a menu instead: **Forecast** and **Set the weather** (clear, rain or thunder for 5 to 240 real minutes) |
| `/realm:weather_forecast` | Everyone | The forecast for the next 3 hours (`horizonHours`): the weather now and when it changes, every spell coming up, in real time (UTC) |
| `/realm:weather_set <clear\|rain\|thunder> <minutes>` | Operators | Starts that weather now for 1 to 1440 real minutes; the plan carries on after it. With the almanac disabled it just sets the weather, and the game's weather cycle takes over after. Everyone else online is told in chat |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | The almanac runs the overworld weather: it sets the `doWeatherCycle` gamerule to false and plays its plan. Disabled, it puts the gamerule back how it was before and the game's weather takes over |
| `storyEvents` | `true` | Story Questlines can ask for rain or a thunderstorm when a story step needs one (`realm:sky_request` kinds `rain`, `thunder`): it's planned to start within 8 minutes for 6 minutes and shows in the forecast, then the plan carries on. Not when that weather is already here or planned that soon; at most one every 20 minutes |
| `horizonHours` | `3` | How far ahead the plan reaches, in real hours. The forecast shows this far |
| `clear.minMinutes` | `30` | Shortest clear spell, in real minutes |
| `clear.maxMinutes` | `90` | Longest clear spell, in real minutes |
| `rain.minMinutes` | `8` | Shortest rain, in real minutes |
| `rain.maxMinutes` | `20` | Longest rain, in real minutes |
| `thunder.minMinutes` | `6` | Shortest thunderstorm, in real minutes |
| `thunder.maxMinutes` | `12` | Longest thunderstorm, in real minutes |
| `thunderAfterClear` | `0.1` | Chance (0–1) a clear spell ends straight in a thunderstorm instead of rain |
| `thunderAfterRain` | `0.35` | Chance (0–1) rain builds into a thunderstorm instead of clearing |
| `rainAfterThunder` | `0.5` | Chance (0–1) a thunderstorm eases into rain instead of clearing |
| `dailyForecast` | `true` | A one-line forecast in chat the first time each player joins on a UTC day |
| `npcRole` | `skymage` | The [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp) role that offers **Forecast** when tapped. Empty = no offer |

Operators can change `enabled`, `storyEvents`, every `.minMinutes` and `.maxMinutes`, `thunderAfterClear`, `thunderAfterRain`, `rainAfterThunder` and `dailyForecast` in game with `/realm:config` when Realm Settings is installed; length and chance changes apply from the next spell (the one on now keeps its length). Each player can switch the daily chat line for themselves with **Daily forecast in chat** in `/realm:prefs`, which follows `dailyForecast` until they choose. `horizonHours` and `npcRole` stay in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `weather:plan` | World | JSON `{ v: 2, s: [{ w, s, e }] }`: the plan, each spell's weather (`Clear`, `Rain` or `Thunder`) and its start and end (ms since 1970). The first one is now. A plan saved by an older version (`v: 1`, made with the old 20-60 minute clear spells) keeps only the spell on now and is planned again after it |
| `weather:weather` | World | The overworld weather at the last change. The stable Script API can't read the current weather |
| `weather:cycle` | World | The `doWeatherCycle` gamerule as it was before the almanac took over, put back when it's disabled. Not set while the almanac isn't running |
| `weather:day` | Player | The UTC day number of the player's last daily forecast |
| `weather:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's own `dailyForecast` choice from `/realm:prefs` |
| `weather:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- On start (and when enabled), the pack saves the `doWeatherCycle` gamerule and sets it to false, so the game never changes the weather on its own, then plays the plan's current spell with `Dimension.setWeather` (with the spell's remaining length, plus a minute, as the game's own fallback). Once a second it checks whether the current spell has ended; if so it plays the next one and plans further ahead, to `horizonHours`. Every 10 seconds it makes sure `doWeatherCycle` is still false.
- The plan is a chain: each spell's kind is picked from the one before it with the chances above, and its length at random between its shortest and longest. It's saved as `weather:plan` on every change.
- `weatherChange` in the overworld is checked against the plan. A change to clear within 10 seconds of anyone being in bed, or a jump in the time of day right after, is sleeping: the wet spell ends and a clear one starts. Any other mismatch is put back a second later (at most 6 times a minute).
- **Other packs:** whenever the plan changes, the pack sends `realm:weather_plan` `{ now, until, next: [{ weather, at }] }`: `now` is the current weather (`Clear`, `Rain` or `Thunder`), `until` when it ends and `at` when each later spell starts (ms since 1970), up to 24 spells. It sends the same in answer to `realm:weather_ask`, coalescing asks that arrive within 10 ticks into one answer. Rain Extras, Storm Chasing, Regional Weather, Tornadoes, Aurora & Shooting Stars and Blood Moon & Harvest Moon all ask 5 seconds after world load, so they can learn about weather already under way. With the almanac disabled the answer is `{ now, until: 0, next: [], off: true }`, with `now` the last weather seen; these consumers ignore that disabled plan.
- **Townsfolk:** on `realm:npc_talk` with the `skymage` role it offers **Forecast** (`realm:npc_offer`, key `forecast`), and `realm:npc_choose` opens the forecast for that player.

### Known limits

- When the almanac first starts, it doesn't know the weather at that moment, so it starts from clear (or the last weather it saw) and sets that.
- `/weather` and other packs can't change the weather for long while it runs: use `/realm:weather_set`, or disable the almanac.
- The plan runs in real time; `/time` and sleeping don't move it, except that sleeping ends rain or a storm.

## Regional Weather — `climate_bp`

The weather depends on where you stand: when it rains, deserts and badlands get a sandstorm and snowy places a blizzard, and on the morning after rain a fog bank rolls in off lakes, rivers and the sea. Each player gets the condition of the ground around them, with its own fog and blowing sand or snow; sandstorms and blizzards also slow you down.

### How to use

1. **Sandstorm:** when it rains or storms and you're outdoors in a desert or badlands, the air turns tan, sand blows past you on the wind and you get Slowness I. Wear any helmet to keep the sand out of your eyes: no Slowness. Above the hotbar: `Sandstorm! A helmet keeps the sand out of your eyes.`
2. **Blizzard:** when it rains or storms and you're outdoors where snow or ice lies on top, it's a white-out with driving snow and Slowness I. Get under a roof, or within 4 blocks of a lit campfire, and it's gone. Above the hotbar: `Blizzard! Get under a roof or near a lit campfire.`
3. **Fog bank:** for 30 real minutes after rain ends, dawn (from sunrise to mid-morning) brings a low, pale fog when you're by water and below y 80. Above the hotbar: `A fog bank rolls in off the water.`
4. Run `/realm:climate`, or use the same switch in `/realm:prefs`, to disable the fog and particles for yourself (on a slower device, say). Slowness still applies. The choice is remembered.
5. **Operators:** add [Realm Skies](#realm-skies--sky_rp) under **Resource Packs**: the fogs and particles come from it, so without it only the Slowness happens. `/realm:config` → **Regional Weather** enables or disables each condition and the Slowness, sets the campfire distance and the fog bank window.

### What players see

- **Where:** decided once a second for each player in the overworld from the highest block over them and over one random column within 4 blocks: sand, red sand, sandstone, terracotta, cactus or dead bushes mean desert or badlands (cut, smooth and chiseled sandstone, sandstone stairs, slabs and walls, and glazed terracotta are building blocks and don't count); snow, powder snow or ice mean a snowy place. Sand with water within 8 blocks (and no more than 3 below your feet) is a beach or a riverbank, where it really rains, so no sandstorm there. The Script API can't read biomes, so this is a guess from the ground (as [Rain Extras](#rain-extras--rain_bp) does). Outdoors means nothing 2 or more blocks over your head, and not flying more than 16 blocks over the ground.
- **Sandstorm** (rain or thunder, outdoors on desert ground): the `realm:sky_sandstorm` fog (tan, about 6 to 20 blocks of sight) and 2 bursts of blowing sand a second (`particlesPerSecond`) from upwind. The wind (`wind.speed`, 6 blocks a second) slowly turns (`wind.turnDegrees`, 2° a second), so the sand drifts from a different side over a few minutes. Slowness I without a helmet (`slowness`, `sandstorm.helmetProtects`).
- **Blizzard** (rain or thunder, outdoors on snow or ice): the `realm:sky_blizzard` white-out fog, driving snow from upwind, and Slowness I. A lit campfire or soul campfire within 4 blocks (`blizzard.campfireRadius`) or a roof ends it for you.
- **Fog bank** (no rain): from time 23000 (sunrise) to 2500 (mid-morning) (`fogbank.fromTime`, `fogbank.toTime`), within 30 real minutes of the last rain ending (`fogbank.minutesAfterRain`), outdoors, below y 80 (`fogbank.maxY`), with water within 6 blocks to the side (`fogbank.waterRadius`) and no more than 3 below your feet (`fogbank.waterBelow`): the `realm:sky_fogbank` fog and wide, faint sheets of mist lying low around you, a new one each second, that overlap into one layer instead of separate puffs.
- A condition lingers 3 seconds after you step out of it (`lingerSeconds`), so a patch of grass in a desert doesn't make it flicker. The note above the hotbar shows at most once every 2 minutes for each condition.
- **Slowness** is Slowness I for 2 seconds, renewed every second while you're in it, without particles. A stronger or longer Slowness (a potion) is left alone. None in creative or spectator mode.
- The fogs and particles are only for the player they're for. Rain itself still comes from [Realistic Rain](#realistic-rain--rain_rp) and [Rain Extras](#rain-extras--rain_bp), which leave deserts and snowy places alone.
- The first time you're in each condition, the [Journal](#field-journal--journal_bp) records it on its weather page (`sandstorm`, `blizzard`, `fogbank`).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:climate` | Everyone | Enables or disables the sandstorm, blizzard and fog bank fog and particles **for yourself** (enabled by default). Slowness still applies. Remembered between sessions |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Sandstorms, blizzards and fog banks happen. Disabled, the pack does nothing and clears its fogs |
| `slowness` | `true` | Sandstorms (without a helmet) and blizzards give Slowness I |
| `lingerSeconds` | `3` | Seconds a condition lingers after you step out of it |
| `particlesPerSecond` | `2` | Bursts of sand or snow per second around each player (fog bank puffs are half that) |
| `wind.speed` | `6` | Wind speed for the blowing sand and snow, in blocks per second |
| `wind.turnDegrees` | `2` | How fast the wind turns, in degrees per second |
| `sandstorm.enabled` | `true` | Rain or thunder over desert ground blows up a sandstorm for players outdoors |
| `sandstorm.helmetProtects` | `true` | Wearing any helmet keeps sandstorm Slowness away |
| `blizzard.enabled` | `true` | Rain or thunder over snow or ice is a blizzard for players outdoors |
| `blizzard.campfireRadius` | `4` | A lit campfire or soul campfire within this many blocks shelters you from the blizzard (1–8 in game) |
| `fogbank.enabled` | `true` | Low fog by the water at dawn after rain |
| `fogbank.minutesAfterRain` | `30` | Real minutes after the rain ends during which dawn brings a fog bank |
| `fogbank.fromTime` | `23000` | Dawn starts at this time of day (ticks; 23000 is sunrise) |
| `fogbank.toTime` | `2500` | Dawn ends at this time of day |
| `fogbank.maxY` | `80` | Fog banks only below this height |
| `fogbank.waterRadius` | `6` | Water must be within this many blocks to the side |
| `fogbank.waterBelow` | `3` | ... and no more than this many blocks below your feet |

Operators can change `enabled`, `slowness`, `sandstorm.enabled`, `sandstorm.helmetProtects`, `blizzard.enabled`, `blizzard.campfireRadius`, `fogbank.enabled`, `fogbank.minutesAfterRain` and `particlesPerSecond` in game with `/realm:config` when Realm Settings is installed. Each player switches the visuals for themselves with **Sandstorm, blizzard and fog bank visuals** in `/realm:prefs` (the same switch as `/realm:climate`). The other numbers stay in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `climate:weather` | World | Last known overworld weather (`Clear`, `Rain` or `Thunder`), learned from a native change or an enabled Almanac plan |
| `climate:dry` | World | When the last rain ended (ms since 1970), for fog banks |
| `climate:seen` | Player | Conditions already sent to the Journal, such as `sandstorm,blizzard` |
| `climate:pref` | Player | JSON of the player's own visuals choice from `/realm:climate` or `/realm:prefs` |
| `climate:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- `weatherChange` in the overworld keeps the weather (saved as `climate:weather`), and a change to clear after rain saves the time as `climate:dry`. The pack's loop only runs while it rains, during the fog bank window after rain, or while a player still has its fog; it runs twice a second and updates half of the players each time, so each player once a second.
- Five seconds after world load it also asks the Weather Almanac for the current plan, so adding it mid-storm needn't wait for a weather change. Until a real overworld `weatherChange` arrives, it accepts a valid enabled plan's `now` and saves it as weather. Plans for another dimension and unknown weather values are ignored. Without the Almanac it keeps using native changes and its saved weather.
- Each update: one `getTopmostBlock` over the player (outdoors, and the ground) and, in rain, one over a random column within 4 blocks. In a blizzard, a lit campfire is looked for with `Dimension.getBlocks` in the 9 x 9 x 9 blocks around the player (at the default `blizzard.campfireRadius` of 4) every 3 seconds; on sand, water (for a beach) with `Dimension.containsBlock` in the 17 x 17 blocks around and up to 3 below every 5 seconds; for a fog bank, water the same way every 5 seconds. Each is a single native call.
- Fogs use `/fog @s push realm:sky_… climate_sky` and `/fog @s remove climate_sky`, so only this pack's fog entry is ever touched; joining clears it and the next update puts back what's needed. Particles use `Player.spawnParticle` with the wind in `variable.wx` and `variable.wz`, so only that player sees them.
- Slowness uses `addEffect("slowness", 40, { amplifier: 0, showParticles: false })`, skipped while a stronger or longer Slowness is on.
- The first time in each condition sends `realm:journal` `{ player, page: "weather", entry, label }` and the note above the hotbar sends `realm:actionbar` first, so the [Coordinates HUD](#coordinates-hud--hud_bp) steps aside.

### Known limits

- Biomes can't be read, so a plain sandstone or terracotta roof or a snow-covered field counts as desert or snowy ground, and the sand by a desert river or well counts as a riverbank. Rain or thunder anywhere is a sandstorm or blizzard on that ground.
- Fogs stack, and the one pushed last shows. Rain Extras leaves its storm fog off on sand, terracotta, snow and ice, and Blood Moon & Harvest Moon leaves its moon fog off while it rains, so a sandstorm or blizzard fog is never covered by theirs.
- Realm Skies has one fog for each condition, so the fog comes and goes in one step rather than rolling in by stages like the storm fog of Rain Extras.

---

## Storm Chasing — `storm_bp`

Thunderstorms get a storm cell: a heart of the storm that drifts with the wind, throwing lightning as it grows and fades. Chase it with a clock or the Storm Meter relic, and set out lightning rods: a rod lightning strikes becomes charged, and tapping it gives Storm Glass.

### How to use

1. In a thunderstorm, chat soon says `A storm cell is forming to the NE.` The cell forms 200 to 500 blocks from one of the players online, drifts 1 to 3 blocks a second and lasts 4 to 8 minutes.
2. Hold a clock and run `/realm:storm` → **Read the storm** (or `/realm:storm_read`) for a reading: `Cell: 340m NE, strength 7/10`. Holding the Storm Meter relic ([Relics](#relics--relics_bp)) shows the reading all the time.
3. Near the cell, lightning lands every 3 to 8 seconds, more often as it grows. Watch out: it hurts. Getting within 64 blocks of the cell adds **Storm cell** to the Weather page of your [Field Journal](#field-journal--journal_bp).
4. Place lightning rods where the storm goes. When lightning strikes one you placed (the cell's, or ordinary storm lightning), it sparks blue and is charged. Tap a charged rod to collect 1 or 2 **Storm Glass**, and it can be charged again. A rod in someone else's [land claim](#land-claims--claims_bp) is theirs: only the claim's players can collect its glass.
5. Don't want the chat line when a cell forms? Disable **Storm cell notes** in `/realm:prefs`.
6. Storm cell lightning never strikes in or right next to a safe zone ([Safe Zones](#safe-zones--zones_bp), protected towns and claims), so it can't set your base on fire. Lightning rods there still get struck.
7. **Operators:** `/realm:storm` also has **Start a storm cell**, **Start a storm cell anyway** (without a thunderstorm) and **End the storm cell**. `/realm:storm_cell` starts a cell 48 to 96 blocks from you during a thunderstorm; `/realm:storm_cell true` starts one even without a storm. `/realm:config` → **Storm Chasing** enables or disables the cells, their lightning and the chat line, and sets the wait between cells.

### What players see

- **One storm cell at a time**, in the overworld only. A thunderstorm's first cell forms 10 to 40 seconds after it starts, and after a cell passes the next one waits 60 seconds (`gapSeconds`). The cell ends when its time is up or the thunderstorm ends.
- **Strength** goes from 1 up to the cell's peak (5 to 10) halfway through its life, then back down. Strikes come every 8 seconds at strength 1 and every 3 at strength 10 (`strikeSecondsMax`, `strikeSecondsMin`), give or take a second.
- **Wind:** each cell drifts at its own speed (`minSpeed` to `maxSpeed`) in a direction that turns a few degrees a second (`turnPerSecond`), so it wanders.
- **Lightning** lands at a random spot within 30 blocks of the cell (`strikeRadius`), only where the world is loaded (around players). To keep builds from catching fire, a strike is skipped within 64 blocks of world spawn (`avoidSpawn`) and anywhere a check of the 9 x 9 columns around the spot (the surface and 4 blocks under it) finds a player-made block: planks, glass, chests, barrels, signs, beds, torches, lanterns, doors, fences, wool, carpet, concrete, glazed terracotta, polished, cut and chiseled stone, copper blocks, paths, farmland, crafting tables, furnaces, bricks, slabs, stairs, rails, redstone parts and the like.
- **Lightning rods:** the pack remembers rods players place (up to 200, `maxRods`), in any copper stage, waxed or not: a rod that oxidizes or gets waxed stays the same rod. Half the time (`rodChance`) a strike goes to an uncharged rod within the cell's reach instead, even near spawn (a struck rod doesn't start fires). Any lightning within 3 blocks of a remembered rod charges it: a blue spark and a beacon hum, then a spark every 2 seconds while someone is within 48 blocks. Tapping a charged rod (with anything in hand) collects `You collect 2 Storm Glass from the lightning rod.` Tapping an uncharged one with an empty hand says `This lightning rod isn't charged. A lightning strike charges it.` The sparks come from [Realm Skies](#realm-skies--sky_rp); without it, the rods still charge.
- **Storm Glass** is prismarine crystals named `Storm Glass` with the lore `Charged by a lightning strike`. Other packs may buy or use it ([Relics](#relics--relics_bp) ascension takes it).
- **More glass:** a Stormcaller with Rod Reader ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp) Callings, `bonus.rodGlass` in `realm:calling`) and a player carrying the [Relics](#relics--relics_bp) Storm set (`realm:relic_sets`) each get 1 more from every charged rod (`You collect 4 Storm Glass from the lightning rod (2 more from your Calling and relics).`). The pack asks with `realm:calling_ping` and `realm:relic_sets_ping` 7 seconds after the world loads.
- **Read the storm** without a clock in your hand says `Hold a clock to read the storm.`; with no cell (or outside the overworld), `No storm cell.`
- **A rod haul** (Storm Glass collected from a charged rod) is town gossip, each player once per storm cell (with [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp); at most one piece of news from this pack per in-game hour, see Town news in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:storm` | Everyone | Opens the Storm Chasing menu: **Read the storm**; operators also start a storm cell (with or without a thunderstorm) or end it |
| `/realm:storm_read` | Everyone | With a clock in your hand: the storm cell's distance, direction and strength (`Cell: 340m NE, strength 7/10`) |
| `/realm:storm_cell [force]` | Operators | Starts a storm cell 48 to 96 blocks from you now (default, `commandMinDistance` to `commandMaxDistance`), replacing any other. Needs a thunderstorm unless `force` is `true`; a forced cell lasts its full time even if the weather clears |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Thunderstorms in the overworld get a storm cell |
| `lightning` | `true` | The storm cell throws lightning. Disabled, it still drifts and can be read |
| `avoidZones` | `true` | No lightning in or within 4 blocks of a safe zone (Safe Zones, protected towns and claims). Lightning rods there still get struck and charged |
| `formNotes` | `true` | A chat line when a storm cell forms. Each player can choose in `/realm:prefs` |
| `gapSeconds` | `60` | Seconds after a cell passes before the next can form (0–3600 in game) |
| `minDistance` | `200` | A new cell forms at least this far from a random online player (blocks) |
| `maxDistance` | `500` | ...and at most this far |
| `minLifeSeconds` | `240` | Shortest a cell lasts (seconds) |
| `maxLifeSeconds` | `480` | Longest a cell lasts (seconds) |
| `minSpeed` | `1` | Slowest a cell drifts (blocks per second) |
| `maxSpeed` | `3` | Fastest a cell drifts (blocks per second) |
| `turnPerSecond` | `3` | How fast the wind turns, at most (degrees per second) |
| `strikeRadius` | `30` | Lightning lands within this many blocks of the cell |
| `strikeSecondsMin` | `3` | Seconds between strikes at strength 10 |
| `strikeSecondsMax` | `8` | Seconds between strikes at strength 1 |
| `avoidSpawn` | `64` | No lightning within this many blocks of world spawn (rods excepted) |
| `rodChance` | `0.5` | Chance a strike goes to an uncharged lightning rod near the cell, when there is one |
| `maxRods` | `200` | Lightning rods remembered; past this the oldest are forgotten |
| `glassMin` | `1` | Fewest Storm Glass from a charged rod |
| `glassMax` | `2` | Most Storm Glass from a charged rod (before the Rod Reader and Storm set extras) |
| `journalRadius` | `64` | Players this close to the cell get the Field Journal's Storm cell entry |
| `commandMinDistance` | `48` | `/realm:storm_cell` puts the cell at least this far from the operator |
| `commandMaxDistance` | `96` | ...and at most this far |

Operators can change `enabled`, `lightning`, `avoidZones`, `gapSeconds` and `formNotes` in game with `/realm:config`. Each player can switch the chat line for themselves with **Storm cell notes** in `/realm:prefs`, which follows `formNotes` until they choose. The rest stays in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `storm:cell` | World | JSON of the current cell (`x`, `z`, `heading`, `speed`, `age`, `life`, `peak`, `forced`), saved every 10 seconds so it survives a restart during the storm |
| `storm:rods` | World | JSON `[[dimension, x, y, z, charged], ...]`: lightning rods players placed, and which are charged |
| `storm:weather` | World | Last known overworld weather (`Clear`, `Rain` or `Thunder`), learned from a native change or an enabled Almanac plan |
| `storm:pref` | Player | The player's own **Storm cell notes** choice |
| `storm:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

### How it works

- Weather comes from `weatherChange` (saved as `storm:weather`). Once a second the cell moves along its heading and counts down to its next strike; the cell itself is just a point, not an entity.
- Five seconds after world load it asks the Weather Almanac for the current plan, so it can learn about a storm already under way. Until a real overworld `weatherChange` arrives, a valid enabled plan's `now` updates the saved weather; other dimensions and unknown weather are ignored. Without the Almanac the native change and saved-weather paths work as before.
- A strike first checks the spot's column with `getTopmostBlock`: in an unloaded chunk that fails and the strike is skipped. Then the 9 x 9 build check (at most 405 block lookups, only when a strike is due, spread over a few ticks as a job, one strike at a time: a strike due while the last one's check still runs is skipped), then `dimension.spawnEntity("minecraft:lightning_bolt")` on the surface.
- Rods are remembered from `afterEvents.playerPlaceBlock` and forgotten on `playerBreakBlock`, or when found missing (a strike aimed at one, a tap, or the spark check of a charged rod near a player, so a rod blown up or pushed away stops sparking). `afterEvents.entitySpawn` of a `minecraft:lightning_bolt` within 3 blocks of a rod charges it. A tap is `beforeEvents.playerInteractWithBlock`; on a charged rod it's canceled (so no block is placed against it) and the glass is given. A tap another pack already canceled (Land Claims, in someone else's claim) collects nothing.
- Every 2 seconds the pack sends `realm:storm_cell` `{ dim, x, z, strength }` (`{ dim: null }` once the cell is gone), which the [Relics](#relics--relics_bp) Storm Meter shows, and `realm:journal` `{ page: "weather", entry: "storm_cell" }` to players within `journalRadius` (once per cell). A new cell sends `realm:sky_event` `{ kind: "storm_cell", dim, x, z, text: "A storm cell is forming" }` for the packs that listen to sky events (see [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).

## Tornadoes — `tornado_bp`

Some thunderstorms spin up a tornado: a tall, dense, swirling vortex funnel with a churning ground dust skirt and dark upper storm collar that wanders across open country for a couple of minutes. It sucks up nearby players (in any gamemode), spins them rapidly up the funnel for a few seconds, and shoots them high into the sky out the top before cushioning their landing with Slow Falling. It never breaks or places a single block and never touches mobs or dropped items, so builds, pets, villagers and farms are completely untouched, and it leaves a few Storm Glass behind where it dies down. The funnel is drawn with particles from [Realm Skies](#realm-skies--sky_rp): without that resource pack the tornado still pulls, launches and warns, but you can't see it.

### How to use

1. When a thunderstorm starts, there's a chance (`chance`, 0.2) that a tornado touches down during it, 1 to 4 minutes in, somewhere 80 to 160 blocks from one of the players in the Overworld, on open grass, dirt or sand.
2. Anyone within 150 blocks gets a warning in chat, such as `§cTornado! 140m to the SW, moving NE.`, and hears a warning horn every 20 seconds while it lasts. Closer in you hear the wind roar and the storm rumble from its direction.
3. Run `/realm:tornado` → **Where is the tornado?** (or `/realm:tornado_info`) any time to see where it is and which way it's heading, or `No tornado right now.`
4. Want to ride the vortex? Step within `pullRadius` (14 blocks) of the funnel in **any gamemode** (Survival, Creative, Adventure): the wind sucks you into the core, spins you around up the twisting funnel for a few seconds, and shoots you high into the sky out the top, granting Slow Falling near the apex that lasts until you land, so you float down safely. Mobs, NPCs, items and blocks are left completely alone.
5. When it dies down (after 1.5 to 3 minutes), chat says `§7The tornado has died down.` and 2 to 5 **Storm Glass** lie on the ground at the end of its path. Go pick them up.
6. **Operators:** add [Realm Skies](#realm-skies--sky_rp) under **Resource Packs** so players can see the funnel. `/realm:tornado` → **Spawn one** (or `/realm:tornado_spawn`) makes a tornado 40 blocks in front of you right away, in any weather; **End the tornado** stops it. `/realm:config` → **Tornadoes** enables or disables tornadoes in storms and sets the chance, the distance kept from spawn, what a tornado does in safe zones, the funnel's density and view distance, the pull radius and whether players are sucked up and launched.

### What players see

- **The funnel:** a dense, multi-layered swirling vortex stacked 42 blocks (`height`) up from the ground—flaring into a churning dust and debris skirt at the base, tapering through a dark inner condensation core wrapped in silver-gray spiral cloud bands, and spreading into a brooding storm collar with lightning sparks at the top. Each player within `viewDistance` (128) blocks gets their own copy (`rings`, 22 rings, half as many beyond 64 blocks; `density` scales both), so players far away cost nothing.
- **Where it goes:** it drifts 2 to 4 blocks a second (`speed`) on a slowly wandering heading, follows the ground over hills, and turns away rather than come within `avoidSpawn` (64) blocks of the world spawn. It may pass by builds: it never changes a block.
- **Safe zones** ([Safe Zones](#safe-zones--zones_bp), protected towns and claims), by **Tornadoes and safe zones** (`zoneMode`): `pass` (default) goes through them like anywhere else, since it breaks nothing; `calm` leaves players inside a zone alone; `avoid` never forms within `pullRadius` + 16 blocks of a zone and turns away before its pull reaches one (and is calm inside one, if an operator spawns it there).
- **Players only (any gamemode):** mobs, pets, villagers, townsfolk and dropped items are never pulled or harmed. Players within `pullRadius` (14) blocks feel the vortex suck them inward toward the base; once inside the funnel core they spiral rapidly around and up the vortex for ~2.8 seconds before being shot high into the sky out the top (boosted by `liftHeight`, 16) and receiving Slow Falling near the apex of their sky launch, for at least `slowFallingSeconds` (8) and then until they're back on the ground or in water (at most a minute), so the fall never hurts. Works in Survival, Creative, Adventure and Spectator alike. `throwPlayers` disabled leaves players alone.
- **Warnings and sounds:** within `warnDistance` (150) blocks, a chat warning once per tornado with its distance, direction and heading (`§cTornado! 140m to the SW, moving NE.`), and the raid horn every `hornEvery` (20) seconds. Within 100 blocks a deep thunder rumble every 6 s; within 48 blocks the roar of wind every 5 s. Sounds come from the tornado's direction. Wind, rumble and horn volume are set in 8-block bands (`SOUND_BAND`) from each player's distance, measured at the band's midpoint, with a minimum of 0.15. Each player gets their own sound call (it comes from their own direction to the funnel); the wind's restart is one `stopsound` for everyone near the funnel, not one command per player.
- **When it ends:** chat says `§7The tornado has died down.` to everyone who was warned (also when an operator ends it), and 2 to 5 (`stormGlass`) Storm Glass drop along the last part of its path: prismarine crystals named `Storm Glass` with the lore `Charged by a lightning strike`, the same item other packs use. A natural tornado dies down within 10 seconds once the thunderstorm ends.
- **Journal:** players who see it (within `viewDistance`) get the **Tornado** page in their journal (Journal pack), and innkeepers' **Hear the news** ([Waystones & Inns](#waystones--inns--waystone_bp)) passes on `A tornado touched down` (the `realm:sky_event` script event).
- **Riding one out:** the first player shot out of the top of a tornado is town gossip, once per tornado (with [Townsfolk](#townsfolk--npc_bp); at most one piece of news from this pack per in-game hour, see Town news in [How the packs work together](#how-the-packs-work-together)).

### Commands

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/realm:tornado` | Everyone | Opens the Tornadoes menu: **Where is the tornado?**; operators also **Spawn one** (40 blocks in front of you) and **End the tornado** (no Storm Glass; warned players get the all-clear) |
| `/realm:tornado_info` | Everyone | Where the tornado is and where it's heading (`§cTornado! 140m to the SW, moving NE.`), or `No tornado right now.` |
| `/realm:tornado_spawn` | Operators | A tornado forms 40 blocks in front of you now, in any weather (one at a time). It lasts and drifts like a natural one, but doesn't end with the storm |

### Configuration (`scripts/config.js` → `CONFIG`)

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Tornadoes form on their own during thunderstorms (`/realm:tornado_spawn` works either way) |
| `chance` | `0.2` | Chance (0-1) that a thunderstorm brings one tornado, rolled when the thunderstorm starts |
| `formAfter.min` | `60` | Earliest second after the thunderstorm starts that the tornado forms |
| `formAfter.max` | `240` | Latest second after the thunderstorm starts that the tornado forms |
| `lifetime.min` | `90` | Shortest life of a tornado, in seconds |
| `lifetime.max` | `180` | Longest life of a tornado, in seconds |
| `speed.min` | `2` | Slowest drift, blocks per second |
| `speed.max` | `4` | Fastest drift, blocks per second |
| `formDistance.min` | `80` | Closest it forms to the chosen player, in blocks |
| `formDistance.max` | `160` | Farthest it forms from the chosen player, in blocks |
| `avoidSpawn` | `64` | It never forms or travels closer than this many blocks to the world spawn |
| `zoneMode` | `"pass"` | Safe zones: `pass` goes through them as usual (it never breaks blocks anyway), `calm` leaves players inside them alone, `avoid` never forms near one and turns away from them |
| `viewDistance` | `128` | Players within this many blocks see the funnel (and get the journal page) |
| `height` | `42` | Height of the funnel, in blocks |
| `rings` | `22` | Rings of vortex clouds stacked up the funnel for each player near it (half as many beyond 64 blocks) |
| `density` | `1` | Multiplies `rings` and the debris, 0.25 to 1.5: lower it if the funnel slows devices down |
| `pullRadius` | `14` | Players within this many blocks of the funnel are sucked in, spun up the vortex and shot out the top |
| `liftHeight` | `16` | Extra sky launch boost height above the top of the funnel |
| `throwPlayers` | `true` | Players close to the funnel (in any gamemode) are sucked in, spun up the funnel and shot high out the top with Slow Falling |
| `slowFallingSeconds` | `8` | Seconds of Slow Falling at least, after being shot out the top; it then lasts until the player lands |
| `warnDistance` | `150` | Players within this many blocks get the chat warning and the horn |
| `hornEvery` | `20` | Seconds between warning horns; `0` = no horn |
| `stormGlass.min` | `2` | Fewest Storm Glass dropped where it dies down |
| `stormGlass.max` | `5` | Most Storm Glass dropped where it dies down |
| `sounds.wind` | `"elytra.loop"` | The wind roar near the funnel (within 48 blocks) |
| `sounds.rumble` | `"ambient.weather.thunder"` | The rumble within 100 blocks, played low |
| `sounds.horn` | `"raid.horn"` | The warning horn |

Operators can change `enabled`, `chance`, `avoidSpawn`, `zoneMode`, `density`, `pullRadius`, `throwPlayers`, `viewDistance` and `rings` in game with `/realm:config` when Realm Settings is installed. The other numbers stay in `config.js`.

### Saved data

| Key | Scope | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `tornado:weather` | World | Last known overworld weather (`Clear`, `Rain` or `Thunder`), learned from a native change or an enabled Almanac plan |
| `tornado:cfg` | World | Settings changed in `/realm:config` |

A tornado itself isn't saved: if the realm restarts during one, it's gone, and no Storm Glass drops.

### How it works

- `weatherChange` in the overworld: a change to `Thunder` rolls `chance` once and schedules the tornado `formAfter` seconds later. A check every 5 s forms it: it picks a random Overworld player and tries 16 spots `formDistance` away (the last 8 at half the distance, in case the far chunks aren't loaded), keeping spots at least `avoidSpawn` from spawn whose ground (`getTopmostBlock`, looking under low plants, and the water's surface over a lake or the sea, since `getTopmostBlock` skips water) is grass, dirt, coarse dirt, podzol, sand or red sand, so not water, leaves, stone or a build. A failed attempt is retried every 10 s, up to 12 times, while the thunderstorm lasts.
- Five seconds after world load it asks the Weather Almanac for its plan. Until a real overworld change arrives, it saves a valid enabled plan's `now`, ignoring other dimensions and unknown values. Taking a plan mid-storm does not roll a tornado: that happens when a storm starts. Taking a non-thunder plan cancels a pending natural tornado and fades an existing natural one. Without the Almanac native changes and saved weather work as before.
- While a tornado exists one loop runs every 2 ticks: it moves the funnel, draws a slice of the rings (`realm:sky_tornado` with `variable.radius` and `variable.spin`, `realm:sky_debris` with `variable.radius`): with two or more players within 64 blocks once for all of them (`Dimension.spawnParticle`), otherwise for each player near it (`Player.spawnParticle`, half the rings beyond 64 blocks); and pulls players with `applyKnockback` (no other entity is ever moved). A launched player's Slow Falling is topped up every 10 ticks until they land (its own loop runs only while someone is falling). Once a second it wanders, finds the ground under it, warns and plays sounds (`Player.playSound`, from the tornado's direction). The loop stops when the tornado ends.
- Blocks are only ever read, never changed. Safe zones come from the safe zones protocol (`realm:zones`), kept in memory.
- Script events: `realm:sky_event` `{ kind: "tornado", dim, x, z, text }` when it forms, `realm:journal` `{ player, page: "weather", entry: "tornado", label: "Tornado" }` once per player who sees it.
