**The safe zones protocol** (script events with JSON messages; the shared code is `tools/zones-shared.js`, copied into each pack that takes part as `scripts/zones.js` by `node tools/sync-zones.mjs`):

- **Providers** send `realm:zones` `{ src, part, parts, zones: [{ id, name, dim, x, z, r, shape? }] }` with their full list whenever it changes, about 5 seconds after the world loads, and in reply to `realm:zones_ping` `{}`. `src` names the provider: `zones` (Safe Zones), `town` (Town Projects, towns with **Protect from world events**), `claims` (Land Claims, with `protectWorldEvents`). A list longer than one message (2048 characters) is split into parts numbered from 1 (parts numbered from 0 are accepted too); `parts` 0 or an empty list clears that provider's zones. `shape` is `circle` (default: within `r` blocks of `x`, `z`) or `square` (`x - r` to `x + r`, `z - r` to `z + r`); zones reach from the bottom of the world to the top of `dim`.
- **Consumers** (every pack that breaks or places blocks in a world event) keep the latest list from each provider, ping on world load, and skip block changes inside any zone: the event still happens, it just changes no blocks there.
- **`realm:zones_open`** `{ player, action }` asks Safe Zones to open **Add a safe zone here** (`action: "add"`) or its menu for that player.

**The access check** (Quick Stack & Sort and Chest Finder ask; Land Claims and Quick Stack & Sort's chest locks answer; JSON script events, each under 2048 characters):

- **`realm:access_check`** `{ id, player, spots: [[dim, x, y, z], ...] }`: which of these containers (at most 40 a message; `dim` is the full dimension id, like `minecraft:overworld`, and x, y, z are block coordinates) may this player not open? Every protection pack answers, even when nothing is closed, with **`realm:access_check_result`** `{ id, from, closed: [i, ...] }`, the indexes of the closed spots in that message. An asker waits for every pack that has answered before (2 seconds at most), or 5 ticks if none has yet; each asker sends a hello (`id: "hello"`, no spots) 3 seconds after the world loads so it learns who answers. Stash and Land Claims also send **`ours`**: the indexes of the spots the asker owns or is shared on (Land Claims also counts a claim shared through the asker's party; an operator gets no bypass here). Chest Finder lists an `ours` container even if it hasn't indexed it yet. `closed` and `ours` never overlap; a spot in neither list has no rule from that pack, so another pack may still close it.

**The Hearth & Hearsay events** (Townsfolk and the packs around it; JSON script events, each under 2048 characters):

- **`realm:affinity`** (Townsfolk sends) `{ player, npc, level, pts, off }` on every level change (level `0` Stranger, `1` Acquaintance, `2` Friend, `3` Close, `4` Confidant; `off` the percent off at that townsfolk's shop), and `{ player, all: { <npc>: level }, off: { <npc>: percent } }` when a player joins and 5 seconds after the world loads. Consumers keep it in memory.
- **`realm:gossip`** (any pack sends, Townsfolk listens) `{ kind, player?, name?, place?, n?, from? }`: one piece of news about a player (`player` an id or name, `name` the name to say, `place` what or where, `n` a number), or town news about nobody when `player` is left out; `from` (a townsfolk id, `bram` or `mayor:<town id>`) makes it that townsfolk's alone to tell. Each sender sends at most one piece per in-game hour (Town news, below). Kinds with lines: `goal`, `milestone`, `bounty`, `treasure`, `tornado`, `storm_haul`, `caravan`, `news`, `champion`, `fish_legendary`, `expedition`, `act`, `guild_master`, `town_project`, `blood_moon`, `meteor`, `wander_chain` (Story Questlines: a wanderer's chain finished, `place` the wanderer), `siege`, `atlas` (an Atlas milestone, `place` the title), `atlas_site` (a cairn silenced or a watch post held), `calling` (Skills: a new Calling, `place` its name), `relic_starlit` (Relics: a relic at +3, `place` its name), `town_life` (Town Projects: a town's new family, house or level, `place` the town, `from` its mayor); any other lowercase kind gets general lines (`wander_hostile`: an ambush beaten).
- **`realm:npc_flags`** (Story Questlines sends) `{ player, flags }`: the story flags the townsfolk react to, only the set ones, on join and on change; `realm:npc_flags_ping` asks for all of them again.
- **`realm:calendar`** `{ day, doy, year, season, festival?, ends?, from }`: the Realm day (`day`, counted up at every dawn, never back), its day of the 96-day Realm Year (`doy`), the season (`thaw`, `high_sun`, `harvest`, `long_dark`), the festival while one runs (`hatchling_tide`, `midsummer_regatta`, `lantern_fair`, `long_night`) and its last day (`ends`). [Realm Calendar](#realm-calendar--calendar_bp) sends it at every dawn, when a player joins, on `realm:calendar_ping` and every 5 minutes (`from: "calendar_bp"`; no `festival` while its festivals are switched off). Without it Townsfolk sends it; while Realm Calendar does, Townsfolk only listens (its first day is Townsfolk's, asked with `realm:calendar_ping` `{ own: true }`).
- **`realm:npc_gift`** (Townsfolk sends) `{ player, npc, tier }`: a gift given to a townsfolk (`tier` `loved`, `liked`, `neutral` or `disliked`).
- **`realm:mail_send`** (any pack sends, Realm Mail listens) `{ to, from, subject, body }`: a letter to a player (id or name from the roster) from any sender name, without the send wait; subject up to 40 and body up to 600 characters. Senders: Townsfolk, Story Questlines, Wanderers of the Wilds, Community Goals (thank-you letters to a reached goal's top contributors) and Town Projects (to offline contributors of a finished project, at most 10).

**The Wanderers events** (Wanderers of the Wilds and Story Questlines; JSON script events, each under 2048 characters):

- **`realm:wander_spawn`** (wanderer pack sends) `{ player, wid, archetype, name, hostile?, dim, x, y, z }`: someone appeared for a player. `wid` is a Recurring Wanderer's id (`pell`) or a Stranger's (`s` + base 36); their NPC id for stories is `w_<wid>`; `archetype` one of `miner`, `ghost`, `pilgrim`, `rival`, `hermit`, `storm`, `exile`, `traveler`; `hostile` one of `spy`, `toll`, `sailor`, `hermit`.
- **`realm:wander_turn`** (wanderer pack sends) `{ player, wid, kind, dim, x, y, z, accused? }`: a disguise dropped (its time came after the first talk, or the player accused it) where it stood: the fight starts there.
- **`realm:wander_gone`** (wanderer pack sends) `{ player, wid, why }`: a wanderer left the road (`timeout`, `far`, `gone` for unloaded or removed, `accused` for a friendly one wrongly accused).
- **`realm:wander_done`** (Story Questlines sends) `{ player, wid, how }`: `accepted` (a Stranger stays 30 minutes), `left` (paid, toll paid, given up: they go), `turn` (the fight started: the disguise goes), `camp` (a Recurring Wanderer's camp is up: the one on the road goes).
- **`realm:wander_state`** (Story Questlines sends) `{ player, ch: { <wanderer>: "n" | "o" | "a" | "d" }, h: [hostile kinds], s, q }`: per Recurring Wanderer, their chain can start (`n`), something waits at them (`o`), the player is on it (`a`) or done (`d`); the hostile kinds this player may meet; `s` 1 = **Something's off...**; `q` 1 = a request or fight is going on (no Strangers). Sent on join and on change (checked every 5 seconds), and again on `realm:wander_ping`.
- **`realm:wander_hide`** (Story Questlines sends) `{ wid, player, seconds }`: a camp's wanderer walks with someone (an escort): the camp's own copy hides that long (sent again every 10 seconds).
- **`realm:wander_tether`** (wanderer pack sends, test hook) `{ camp: { snaps, steers, steering }, road: { ... } }`: the answer to `realm:wander_debug` `{"action":"tether"}`, the counters of the walkers' tethers since the world loaded.
- **`realm:place_ready`** (Story Questlines sends) `{ name, state, dim, x, y?, z, wid? }`: where a story place or camp is: `picked`, `built`, `set`, `moved`, `removed`; a built camp's x, y, z is where its wanderer stands. On every change, 5 seconds after the world loads and on `realm:place_ping`.
- **`realm:poi`** `{ kind, dim, x, z, name }` ([Atlas of the Realm](#atlas-of-the-realm--atlas_bp) sends): a built site (hermit hut, shrine, tablet, cairn, watch post, camp), when built and after every world load; the wanderer pack counts each like a story place (anchors for ghosts and the site bonus).
- **`realm:saga_progress`** `{ player, act }` (Story Questlines sends): the main acts a player has finished in order (0 to 5), on join, on change and on `realm:saga_progress_ping`. Atlas of the Realm reads it for the Starwright tablets.

**The race events** (Rook's races: [Bounty Board](#bounty-board--bounty_bp), [Treasure Maps](#treasure-maps--riddles--maps_bp), [Wanderers of the Wilds](#wanderers-of-the-wilds--wander_bp) and Story Questlines; JSON script events, each under 2048 characters):

- **`realm:bounty_targets`** (Bounty Board sends) `{ targets: [{ id, name, dim, x, z }], part, parts }`: today's unclaimed champion targets, where they were last seen, 8 to a message (`part` of `parts`; `targets: []` when there are none). When the list changes (a new day, a claim, a target that moved more than 16 blocks; checked every 2 seconds) and within 2 seconds of **`realm:bounty_targets_ping`** `{}` (the wanderer pack and Story Questlines send it after the world loads).
- **`realm:map_leg`** (Treasure Maps sends) `{ player, hunt, dim, x, z, leg, legs, final }`: a hunt's current leg (the chest once buried, else the marker, else the planned spot; `final` on the last leg), when it changes (checked every second) and for every hunt after **`realm:map_leg_ping`** `{}`; `{ player, hunt, gone: true }` when the hunt is over.
- **`realm:bounty_rival`** (Story Questlines sends) `{ id, player, until }`: a race against Rook on bounty `id` started for that player and ends at `until` (ms since 1970). Bounty Board pays that player `rewards.rivalShare` of the reward if they defeat it later. A second message can only end it sooner.
- **`realm:map_rival`** (Story Questlines sends) `{ player, hunt, until }`: the same for a race to that hunt's chest; found later, Treasure Maps pays `rivalShare` of its Crowns.

**The Callings and relic events** ([Skills](#skills--skills_bp), [Relics](#relics--relics_bp) and the packs around them; JSON script events, each under 2048 characters):

- **`realm:calling`** (Skills sends) `{ player, name, calling, label, talents, bonus, ready, from: "skills_bp" }`: a player's Calling id (`""` none) and name, talent ranks by id, the numbers other packs use (`bonus`: `waystoneOff`, `mapReveal`, `dishPct`, `luckyLine`, `buildEye`, `rodGlass`; only the player's own) and whether their total skill level reaches the Calling level. Sent on join, on any change and for everyone on **`realm:calling_ping`** `{}` (answered at most once a second). Consumers keep it in memory.
- **`realm:relic_sets`** (Relics sends) `{ player, sets, from: "relics_bp" }`: the relic sets a player carries whole (`storm`, `tide`, `deep`, `sun`), on change and once on join; **`realm:relic_sets_ping`** `{}` sends everyone's again.

**The Realm Calendar events** ([Realm Calendar](#realm-calendar--calendar_bp) and the packs around it; JSON script events, each under 2048 characters):

- **`realm:town_list`** (Town Projects sends) `{ part, parts, towns: [{ id, n, dim, x, y, z, safe }] }`: every town, `safe` while **Protect from world events** is Enabled; on every change, 5 seconds after the world loads and on `realm:town_list_ping`. Split into parts like `realm:zones`; `parts: 0` means no towns.
- **`realm:town_state`** (Realm Calendar sends) `{ town, name, mood, until }`: a town's mood after a siege, `heartened` or `shaken`, until a time in ms; again after every load and on `realm:town_state_ping` (Town Projects asks at load).
- **`realm:siege`** (Realm Calendar sends) `{ state, town, id, result? }`: `warn` (the 3 minutes start), `on` (the circles rose), `end` with `result` `held`, `failed` or `scattered`.
- **`realm:siege_marks`** (Realm Calendar sends, the Minimap listens) `{ dim, town: { n, x, z }, circles: [{ x, z }] }`: where a siege is, with the circles still singing (none during the warning); `{}` when none runs. Sent at the warning, when the circles rise, at each silenced bell and at the end, and in answer to `realm:siege_ping`.

**The minimap events** (JSON script events, each under 2048 characters; long lists in parts `{ part, parts }`, `parts: 0` for an empty list): every pack sends its own data when it changes and again on its ping, which the Minimap sends when the world loads (everything) and 2 seconds after a player joins (`{ player }`).

- `realm:npc_places` `{ part, parts, folk: [{ id, n, dim, x, z }] }` from Townsfolk: where each townsfolk is placed (their post), when the list changes; `realm:npc_places_ping` `{}`. Welcome Message reads it too (who to name in the story start line) and sends the ping with its installed-packs ping.
- `realm:waystones_known` `{ player, part, parts, list: [{ i, n, dim, x, z }] }` from Waystones & Inns: the waystones that player discovered, on a discovery and when one they know is removed; `realm:waystones_known_ping` `{ player? }`.
- `realm:atlas_region` `{ player, name }` from Atlas of the Realm, when the player enters a region; `realm:atlas_sites` `{ player, part, parts, sites: [[label, x, z, region]] }`, every site they found; `realm:atlas_site` `{ player, site }`, one more; `realm:atlas_ping` `{ player? }` sends both again.
- `realm:death_point` `{ player, dim, x, z }` (or `{ player }`: none) from Death Point, after a death; `realm:death_point_ping` `{ player? }`.
- `realm:track` `{ player, label, dim?, x?, z?, npc? }` (or `{ player }`: nothing to point at) from Story Questlines: where the tracker points (`npc` when it's a townsfolk or wanderer to talk to), whether the player shows the tracker or not, when it changed (checked every 2 seconds); `realm:track_ping` `{ player? }`.
- `realm:place_ready` (Story Questlines' places, above) now carries `label` for camps (`Pell's Camp`); the Minimap uses only camps (with `wid`), states other than `picked` and `removed`.
- `realm:town_list` (Town Projects, above): the Minimap shows the nearest town; it sends `realm:town_list_ping` `{}` when the world loads.
- `realm:rainbow_pot` `{ dim, x, z }` (or `{}`: no unfound pot) from Rainbows & the Pot of Gold: where the pot of gold is while nobody has found it, when it appears, moves onto its chest, is found or expires; `realm:rainbow_ping` `{}`.

**The action bar protocol** (one bar above the hotbar, many packs):

- **Every write** to a player's action bar is preceded by `realm:actionbar` `{ player, ticks, from?, background?, steady? }`: "my text is on this player's bar, leave it for `ticks` ticks" (at most 200). `from` is the sending pack's folder, so a pack can ignore its own requests. `steady` (a number) marks a steady line's own redraw and gives its rank; notes leave it out.
- **Steady lines** that redraw every second or two wait while someone else's request lasts, then redraw: the Coordinates HUD, the stats ticker (without the HUD), Story Questlines' tracker, the Party HUD, an expedition's run line, Treasure Maps' Warmer / Colder line, the Chest Finder arrow line, Easy Building's build mode line (it announces itself at most every 10 ticks while it shows), the [Relics](#relics--relics_bp) Storm Meter and Lantern Shard readouts and the [Elytra HUD](#elytra-hud--elytra_bp) above the hotbar. So a note (a durability warning, skill XP, mob health, a sort result) stays readable instead of being drawn over within a second.
- **Between steady lines:** those that listen and send `steady` with each redraw take turns by rank, higher first: the Elytra HUD while you glide (`steady: 50`), the Relics readouts while you hold that relic (45), an expedition's run line (40), Treasure Maps while a map is held (35), the build mode line (30), the Chest Finder arrow (25), the story tracker (20). A steady line waits for a request without `steady` (a note, or a pack from before ranks) and for a higher rank (a tie goes to the `from` that sorts first); it draws over a lower rank, which waits for it in turn. When the higher line stops, its last request runs out (30 to 50 ticks) and the lower one comes back. Their notes (`Built 15 blocks`, a puzzle's count, a story's progress note) leave `steady` out, so every steady line waits for them. The Elytra HUD keeps sending its request while a note holds it, so when the note ends it gets the bar back before a lower line does.
- **`background: true`** marks a steady line that the ranked steady lines above needn't wait for (the Coordinates HUD and the stats ticker still do). The Party HUD sends it, so an expedition's run line takes the bar during a party run; the Party HUD itself waits for the ranked lines and for every note.
- Packs that only show a short note now and then just send the request and write; they don't listen. Without any listener nothing happens.
- **The one exception:** the Coordinates HUD and the stats ticker are the bottom lines. They write without a request (a request from them would hold every other line, the Party HUD's too) and wait for everyone else's. `npm run check` (`tools/check-actionbar.mjs`) finds any other `setActionBar` with no request before it; the known exceptions are listed in `tools/check-actionbar.allow.json`.

**The title protocol** (one title and subtitle on screen, shared with the side boxes):

- **Every real title** (`onScreenDisplay.setTitle` with text, `updateSubtitle`, a `/title` through `runCommand`) is preceded by `realm:title` `{ player, ticks, from }`: "my title is on this player's screen for `ticks` ticks" (its fade in + stay + fade out; at most 600). `from` is the sending pack's folder. A second request from the same pack replaces its first (`ticks: 0` ends it early, as a story scene does when it's skipped); requests from different packs add up. The Deck of Many Things, Expeditions, Skills, Story Questlines, Blood Moon & Harvest Moon, Slot Machine, Silly Enchants, Town Projects, Welcome Message and Realm Configuration (`/realm:admin_title` and its **Show a Title** quick action, `from: "admin_bp"`) send it.
- **The side box packs** (every copy of `scripts/side.js`) listen: while any request lasts for a player they keep updating their picture of the boxes but don't draw, so the title stays readable. When the last request ends (checked every 4 ticks), each pack with a readout for that player draws the boxes again. A pack with a copy of `side.js` sends the request with its `holdTitle(player, ticks)`, which also takes effect in that pack at once.
- **Not covered:** `/title` typed by an operator or run by a command block or another add-on (nothing tells the packs: operators use `/realm:admin_title` instead), and the side box marker titles themselves (`§s§2§r`, `§s§0§r`), which never send it. Script events arrive in the same tick (checked on a dedicated server), so a box drawn in the same tick before the title is replaced by it.

**The side boxes protocol** (nine boxes and the Minimap's two slots, from [Side HUD](#side-hud--hud_rp)): every pack that shows a readout in a box keeps a copy of `tools/side-shared.js` as `scripts/side.js` (`node tools/sync-side.mjs` keeps them the same; `--check` is part of `npm run check`) and calls `show(player, slot, text, ticks)` or `clear(player)`. Slots are `right1`-`right4`, `left1`-`left4` and `middle`; a pack holds one slot per player, and two packs in the same slot take turns (the newest wins). Each copy keeps the same picture of every player's slots: a pack that changes its slot sends `realm:side` `{ player, from, slot, text, ticks, tick }` (`text` up to 159 bytes, `""` when its readout ended; `ticks` up to 1200; `tick` when it was sent), then draws the whole title with every slot that hasn't run out (`setTitle("§s§2§r", { subtitle })`, no fade, staying until the last one runs out). The other copies update their picture, and draw again only if they drew in the last 2 ticks or later (their title may have crossed this one on the way). A copy skips its own messages without reading them (by their `from`) and cleans another pack's text only when it draws, so a busy box costs the other packs little. When a readout runs out (checked every 4 ticks), the pack that wrote it draws again without it, or clears the title (`§s§0§r`) when nothing is left. Mob Health, the Elytra HUD, Treasure Maps, the Realm Calendar and the Coordinates HUD (when a player puts it in a box) use it. Story Questlines writes the slot `quest` (up to 511 bytes): Side HUD's bigger quest box, which shows right under the place its text starts with, `questCode(slot)` (`§s§q§1` for Right 1 ... `§s§q§9` for Middle, color codes only), so it never takes turns with a small box there. The Minimap writes two slots players can't pick, `top` (the compass strip) and `radar`; a pack that shows two readouts writes the second as a part (`from` `map/radar`), which holds its own slot, and draws once after both (`show(..., part, false)`, then `redraw`). While another pack's real title shows (the title protocol, above), no copy draws; the boxes come back when it ends. **The compositor claim:** the Minimap redraws a player's title many times a second with a 1.3 KB radar, so it doesn't broadcast its parts (every message wakes every pack's listener). A copy made with `sideBoxes(from, { compositor: true })` (only the Minimap's) claims the players it shows something to with `realm:side_comp` `{ from, ticks, players, part, parts }` (renewed every 40 ticks for 100, at most 60 ids a message; `ticks` 0 ends it) and draws their titles with every pack's slots. While another pack's live claim covers a player, a copy still sends `realm:side` for its own slot changes but doesn't draw that player's title: the compositor draws it the next tick (a resend of the same text draws nothing). When the compositor has nothing left to show for a player, it draws once more (the other boxes stay) and ends the claim; a claim that runs out without being renewed lets the packs with a readout draw again, so every pack still works alone. Another pack's message is kept as it came and parsed only when a copy draws that player.

**Town news** (gossip, titles and letters from progress): when something worth telling happens (a community goal reached, a milestone's top tier, a bounty claimed, a treasure found, a caravan arriving, a town project finished, a tornado ridden out, a storm rod's haul, a Blood Moon survived, an Atlas milestone or site), the pack that saw it sends `realm:gossip` to Townsfolk, and where it's a personal reward also `realm:title_unlock` (Titles & Trails) or `realm:mail_send` (Realm Mail). So that a big server's news doesn't flood the town, each of these packs sends **at most one piece of gossip per in-game hour** (1,000 ticks, about 50 seconds) and **each event once** (one goal, one player's milestone, one bounty a day, one hunt, one site, one caravan visit, one project, one tornado, one player per storm cell, one Blood Moon); news inside the gap is dropped, not queued. The limit is kept in memory and starts again after a restart (the events themselves are saved as done, so nothing repeats). Titles and letters are never limited: each is a one-off reward. On the listening side, Townsfolk keeps at most 24 pieces (`gossipMax`), 4 of one kind, for 48 hours (`gossipHours`). Champions, Realm Calendar (siege, carve-off and regatta; a siege nobody joined sends none), Fishing 2.0 (legendary catches), Meteor Strikes (first finder), Expeditions (a Nightmare 5 or more clear), Guilds (a new Master), Relics (Starlit) and Skills (a new Calling) now follow the same rule: at most one piece of gossip per sender per 1,000 game ticks, and the same event (a champion, a siege, a meteor, an expedition run, a guild or relic or Calling for one player, a legendary catch for one player and species) is not told twice while it is in the sender's 64-event memory (the oldest is forgotten first, so an old event can be told again after an hour). News inside the gap is dropped, not queued, and rewards (drops, Crowns, titles, journal entries, quest credit) are unaffected. A siege held a moment after another piece of calendar news can therefore skip its `siege_lost` line. Expeditions tell one piece for the first online member. Community Goals' thank-you letters keep their limit of 10. Story Questlines' act completions, wanderer chains and hostile-wanderer endings now use the same 1,000-game-tick, 64-key gate; rewards and story progress still run outside it. Nobody-in-particular news no longer leaves an empty name.

**The diagnostics protocol** (every behavior pack; JSON script events, each under 2048 characters): each pack has `scripts/diag.js`, a copy of `tools/diag-shared.js` with the pack's folder, name and version filled in by `node tools/sync-diag.mjs` and imported first by `scripts/main.js`. It times the pack's own callbacks (intervals, timeouts, jobs, event subscriptions and commands; one plain call while nobody measures) and knows which saved entries are the pack's. It has no listener of its own: it answers on the first `realm:` listener its pack subscribes. [Realm Configuration](#realm-configuration--admin_bp)'s Pack diagnostics (`/realm:diag`) uses it.

- **`realm:diag_ping`** `{ id, ticks? }`: every pack answers **`realm:diag_pong`** `{ id, pack, name, version, bytes, props, big, bigKey, forgotten?, shared?, total?, unowned?, unownedProps? }`: its saved entries (`props`), their size in bytes, the biggest entry and its key; in a bundle, `shared` is how many packs share the add-on, `total` the add-on's whole saved data and `unowned` entries no pack claimed. With `ticks` (1 to 1200) the answer comes when that measuring window ends and adds `{ ticks, ms, calls, mpt, top: [{ k, ms, n }] }` (ms per tick `mpt`, the two costliest callbacks). Overlapping windows are measured once and each request is answered at its own end.
- **`realm:diag_forget`** `{ id, pack, confirm: "FORGET <pack>" }`: only the named pack answers, **`realm:diag_forgot`** `{ id, pack, ok, removed, bytes }` or `{ id, pack, ok: false, error }`. A pack alone in its add-on clears all its saved data (`world.clearDynamicProperties()`); **in the Realm Bundle every pack shares one saved-data store, so only that pack's own entries are deleted** (a key belongs to the pack that declares its prefix, the text before the first `:` (read from the pack's `settings.js` `PREFIX`, plus Easy Building's legacy `eb`), even if no pack touched it since the reload; an undeclared prefix goes to the first pack that read or wrote it, else the pack being evaluated; a prefix two packs declare or use is ambiguous, so its keys stay unowned and are not forgotten, even when one of those packs reads or writes them; no two packs share a prefix), and the other packs keep theirs. Afterwards the pack's writes are blocked until `/reload` or a restart, so what it still holds in memory can't bring the data back. Scoreboards, tags, structures and data saved on players are not touched. The `confirm` token guards against typos, not misuse: anyone who can run `/scriptevent` (operators, command blocks) can send it, the same trust as `realm:cfg_set`.

**One script event listener per pack:** `scripts/script-events.js` (copied from `tools/events-shared.js` by `node tools/sync-events.mjs`, checked by `npm run check`) holds the pack's single native listener for the `realm` namespace. Pack code registers with `onScriptEvent("realm:id", handler)` or an array of ids; `"*"` listens to every `realm:` event while the setup wizard waits. `offScriptEvent(handler)` removes a handler; removing the last drops the native listener, and a later registration restores it. Handlers run in registration order, with copy-on-write lists so a handler can safely register or remove one during delivery. A throwing handler doesn't stop the rest: its error is rethrown after delivery, and further errors are logged. Console-only hooks still check `event.sourceType` themselves. The old tree had 237 direct subscription sites; now each of the 67 packs holds one native listener rather than waking one per handler. Diagnostics ride that listener and attribute the whole dispatch to its pack, not separate timing rows for individual handlers.

Rain Extras needs Realistic Rain and the sky packs need Realm Skies to be seen, both in Realm Resources; and the adventure packs are best together, but any combination works. Translucent Tools only changes how held items are drawn; its one link is Translucent Tools Switch, which tells it per player whether to draw tools solid.

---

## Troubleshooting
<!-- on the site -->

| Problem | Check |
|---|---|
| A command doesn't show up | Run `/realm:help` to see the features this realm has, or type `/realm` to list the commands (e.g. `/realm:stats`). Is the pack **Active**, not just Available? Minecraft 1.21.100+? Rejoin after activating. Ops-only commands are hidden from regular members |
| Commands missing after adding a bundle | The individual packs and the bundle are both active, so duplicates fail. Keep only one |
| Popup never appears | Close chat/inventory. The welcome popup retries for 30 s, news for about 90 s. Check the content log |
| Changes to `config.js` don't show up | Increase `header.version` in `manifest.json`, rebuild, and re-apply. In-game edits override `config.js` defaults: `/realm:config` → **Reset a pack to defaults** clears that pack's settings, `/realm:welcome_reset` clears welcome edits; news, tips and tip settings saved in game always win over `config.js`. A player's own choice in `/realm:prefs` wins over both for that player |
| A pack is missing from `/realm:config` or `/realm:prefs` | It isn't installed or active, or it has nothing to change there (`/realm:prefs` only lists packs with preferences of their own). If a pack answers too slowly on a busy realm, raise Realm Settings' `answerTicks` |
| Settings reset after switching to or from a bundle | Expected: Bedrock keeps each pack's saved data separately, so in-game settings (welcome text, news, tips, `/realm:config` settings, per-player toggles and preferences, first-joined dates, Creeper Guard zones, the Farm Loader list, what Chest Finder remembers) start fresh. Scoreboard stats are kept |
| Night doesn't skip | Is `sleep.enabled` on? The `Zzz x/y sleeping` status shows how many are asleep (x) and how many are needed (y). Players in other dimensions only count if `sleep.countOtherDimensions` is on |
| The server lags (low TPS) with many players | Operators: `/realm:diag` lists every pack's script time, slowest first (red over 0.5 ms a tick). Turn the costly one's feature down or off in `/realm:config`, or pick **Large server** in Operator Tools > **Server size** |
| Script errors | **Settings → Creator → Enable Content Log GUI**, then rejoin. Errors start with the pack's name in brackets, such as `[welcome]`, `[stats]` or `[chairs]` |
| No tornado, aurora, shooting stars, meteor streak, sandstorm, blizzard, moon fog or trail to see | Is Realm Skies (`sky_rp`) active under **Resource Packs**? Those packs draw only with its particles and fogs; without it the events still happen (chat warnings, the pot of gold, the crater) but nothing shows. Players must accept the resource pack download when they join |
| An NPC's buttons are missing (no Market, Guild hall, Forecast...) | Each button comes from its own pack, answering for the NPC's roles: is that pack in the bundle? On a very busy realm an answer can miss the 4-tick window: tap the NPC again |
| Rain looks and sounds like vanilla | Is Realistic Rain active under **Resource Packs**, at the top of the list? A resource pack above it that changes rain wins. Players must accept the resource pack download when they join |
| No storm fog, haze, mist, drips, wind or roof sound | Is Rain Extras active under **Behavior Packs**, and Realistic Rain under **Resource Packs**? Run `/realm:rain` in case they're off for you, and check `/realm:config` → Rain Extras. If the pack was added during rain, they start at the next weather change. Nothing shows in deserts, badlands or snowy places, or deep underground. The haze only shows on Vibrant Visuals |
| Storm fog or haze stays after a storm | Rejoin: Rain Extras clears its fogs when you join. Running `/realm:rain` twice also resets them |
| Wind, thunderstorm or rain on the roof too loud or too quiet | Operators: `/realm:config` → Rain Extras → **Storm wind volume**, **Rain breeze volume**, **Thunderstorm sound volume**, **Rain on the roof volume** (also the muffled rain indoors). Everyone: the game's **Weather** volume slider covers them too |
| Rain as loud indoors as outdoors | Is **Muffled rain indoors** enabled (`/realm:config` → Rain Extras), and are the extras on for you (`/realm:rain`)? It needs Realistic Rain, whose rain clips fade in slowly enough to be stopped quietly. Leaves don't count as a roof |
| Tools still look solid in your hand | Is Translucent Tools active under **Resource Packs**, above other packs that change held items? Did you accept the resource pack download when you joined? Inventory icons stay solid; only the item in your hand is see-through |
| The pack shows a pink and black placeholder icon | Harmless: single behavior packs have no icon. Both bundles carry Realm Skies' icon (`--icon`) |

## Keeping this file current

`npm run check` runs these, in order, and stops at the first that fails:

- `tsc -p .`: the type check.
- `tools/check-pipeline.mjs`: every check tool (each `tools/check-*.mjs` and every tool with a `--check`) and the unit tests are in this chain, and each test scenario's header runs its own file.
- `tools/check-ascii.mjs`: every pack's script code (comments aside) and English lang file (`texts/en_US.lang`) is plain ASCII plus `§`, since Bedrock draws a line with `…`, `–`, `•` or an emoji in a smaller fallback font (Easy Building Guides' known lines are held as they are: more fail, fewer warn).
- `tools/check-docs.mjs`: this file has
  - a `##` section whose heading contains `` `<folder>` `` for **every pack** in `packs/`
  - a `### How to use` section in every pack section: short numbered steps for players, operators last
  - **every command** a pack registers, e.g. `` `/realm:stats` ``
  - **every option** in a pack's `config.js`, as `` `option` ``, or `` `parent.option` `` for nested options like `` `sleep.percent` ``
- `tools/check-commands.mjs`: every command and enum a pack registers uses the `realm:` namespace (a second namespace in one add-on throws `NamespaceMismatch`, so a bundle would lose those commands), and no two packs register the same command.
- `tools/check-stories.mjs`: Story Questlines' story content (`packs/saga_bp/scripts/stories/`) uses known objective types and fields, places, NPC ids, unique ids, champion tags and requirements. It also flags partial block families, reused cast names and wanderer ids, ungated pack items, unknown champion traits, out-of-scale rewards and once-built resources without a renewable/replacement signpost. Exact unresolved content findings need individual reasons in `tools/check-stories.allow.json`; only four owner-pending reward decisions are currently allowed. Flags read that nothing sets remain warnings.
- `tools/check-ids.mjs`: ids in typed uses (`spawnEntity`, `ItemStack`, block writes and filters, particles, sounds and commands) must exist in the matching kind, not merely somewhere in the vanilla id list. Blocks, items and entities use pinned `@minecraft/vanilla-data`; particles and sounds also use the pinned, attributed identifiers in `tools/vanilla-ids/` and our resource packs. Checks are offline; `tools/update-vanilla-ids.mjs` updates the pin from a local matching samples checkout. Known exceptions are in `tools/check-ids.allow.json`.
- `tools/check-events.mjs`: every script event a pack sends is `realm:`, and a payload built from a list or player text is split or capped under 2048 characters (`tools/check-events.allow.json` lists the exceptions).
- `tools/check-actionbar.mjs`: every `setActionBar` has a `realm:actionbar` request before it in the code that runs it (its function, or the function handing over an inline callback), directly or through a helper it actually calls. Helpers resolve by file and import, not a matching name elsewhere; aliases of `setActionBar` are reported. Known exceptions such as the Coordinates HUD and stats ticker are in `tools/check-actionbar.allow.json`.
- `npm run test`: the unit tests (`tools/**/*.test.mjs`: the Realm Configuration item, Side HUD's layout, the Minimap's terrain, the name labels, Expansive Inventory pages, Easy Building Guides, the diagnostics copies, the test server tools).
  The three `check-*` tools above take `--list` to print every case, ignoring their allow lists. Fix a listed case together with removing its line (a stale line only warns).
- `tools/sync-events.mjs --check`: every behavior pack has the same `scripts/script-events.js` as `tools/events-shared.js`, and no pack subscribes directly to `scriptEventReceive`. Change the canonical helper and run `node tools/sync-events.mjs`, never edit the generated copies.
- `tools/sync-settings.mjs --check`: fails if a behavior pack (other than Realm Settings) has no `scripts/settings.js`, or its copy of the shared Realm Settings helper differs from `tools/settings-shared.js`. Change the helper there, then run `node tools/sync-settings.mjs` and bump the version of every pack it updates.
- `tools/sync-zones.mjs --check`: the same for the safe zones protocol: every pack with a `scripts/zones.js` has the same copy as `tools/zones-shared.js`. Change it there, then run `node tools/sync-zones.mjs` (with pack folders to add the file to new ones) and bump the version of every pack it updates.
- `tools/sync-side.mjs --check` and `tools/sync-labels.mjs --check`: the same for the side boxes (`tools/side-shared.js`, each pack's `scripts/side.js`) and the townsfolk name labels (`tools/name-labels-shared.js`, the `scripts/name-labels.js` of Townsfolk, Merchant Caravan, Wanderers of the Wilds and Story Questlines). Change the shared file, never a copy, then run `node tools/sync-side.mjs` or `node tools/sync-labels.mjs`.
- `tools/sync-diag.mjs --check`: every behavior pack has `scripts/diag.js` (the diagnostics protocol), a copy of `tools/diag-shared.js` with that pack's folder, `header.name` and `header.version` filled in, and `import "./diag.js";` as the first import of its `scripts/main.js`. After changing the shared file, a manifest's name or **any version bump**, run `node tools/sync-diag.mjs` (it also adds the copy and the import to a new pack); `help-catalog.mjs` and `gen-news.mjs` do it for Realm Help and Realm News after they bump.
- `tools/help-catalog.mjs --check`: the in-game `/realm:help` text (`packs/help_bp/scripts/catalog.js`) is generated from each pack's summary, `### How to use` and Commands table here, so after changing those, run `node tools/help-catalog.mjs` (it bumps `help_bp`'s patch version). It also fails if a behavior pack doesn't answer `/realm:help`'s `realm:help_ping` script event. Resource packs have no scripts, so they're left out of the help.
- `tools/admin-catalog.mjs --check`: the Realm Configuration menu's list of commands (`packs/admin_bp/scripts/catalog.js`) matches what the packs register. After adding or changing a command or its parameters, run `node tools/admin-catalog.mjs` and bump `admin_bp`'s version.
- `tools/gen-news.mjs --check`: Realm News' update popup (`packs/news_bp/scripts/release.js`) is the newest entry of `docs/NEWS.md`. After adding an entry, run `node tools/gen-news.mjs` (it bumps `news_bp`'s patch version; `npm run bundle` runs it too).
- `tools/gen-rain/textures.mjs --check` and `tools/gen-rain/fogs.mjs --check`: Realistic Rain's textures, fogs and client biomes are what `npm run gen:rain` generates.
- `tools/gen-sky/gen.mjs --check`: every file in Realm Skies is what `npm run gen:sky` generates, none missing or left over.
- `tools/gen-translucent/generate.mjs --check`: Translucent Tools (all but its `manifest.json`) is what `npm run gen:translucent` generates.
- The other generators' `--check`s, the same way: `tools/gen-rain/sounds.mjs`, `tools/gen-platypus/gen.mjs`, `tools/gen-build/gen.mjs`, `tools/gen-silly/gen.mjs` and `tools/gen-glyphs/gen.mjs`.
- `tools/check-versions.mjs`, last: every pack whose files changed since `origin/master` (tracked or not) has a higher `header.version` in its `manifest.json` than there. Without `origin/master` it is skipped.

When adding or changing a pack: update its section here, and the pack table in `README.md`, in the same commit.

## Publishing to mc.nish.software

The [Our realm](https://mc.nish.software/realm/) page shows this file to players. It is generated, never hand-written, so the site and this repo can't drift:

| | |
|---|---|
| What goes on the site | Every pack section (one collapsible card per pack, `### How to use` first; behavior packs under the Realm Bundle, resource packs under **Realm Resources**), plus every section marked `<!-- on the site -->` |
| What stays behind "For operators" | A pack's `### Configuration…`, `### Saved data` and `### Resetting…` subsections, collapsed |
| What goes in "How it works in detail" | A pack's other subsections (`### What players see`, `### How it works`, `### Known limits`…), collapsed |
| Commands page | Every pack's Commands rows also go into the searchable commands table on mc.nish.software (`site/commands/index.html`) |
| Pictures and sound clips | A pack's `### See and hear it` subsection becomes a gallery at the top of its card: each `[label](media/….mp3)` link as a listening clip at the top (with a **Listen** button in the card's header, so it plays without opening the card), each `![caption](media/…)` image (`.webp`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`) with its caption, two images on one line (`![Before label](media/…) ![After label](media/…) caption`) as a before/after comparison you drag across, and any other paragraph as a note. The files live in `docs/media/` here, and `pack-docs.mjs` copies the ones the page uses to `site/realm/media/` |
| How | In a checkout of `nishant/hosting`: `cd minecraft && node tools/pack-docs.mjs --from <path to this repo>` (default `../../mc-packs`, or `MC_PACKS`), then `node tools/check-site.mjs realm` (only the realm page changes) and a PR to `master` there, which you merge (the merge is the deploy); `node tools/check-live.mjs` then checks the live pages. `--check` fails if the page is out of date |
| Downloads | `node tools/publish-packs.mjs --from <path to this repo> --notes "what changed" --pack-notes <folder>="what changed"` there builds the Realm Bundle, Realm Resources and every single pack from this repo and publishes each new version (see `minecraft/docs/OPERATIONS.md`, "Publishing a pack version"; `--resource-notes` gives Realm Resources its own notes, `--dry-run` writes nothing). A single pack is only published when its `header.version` goes up, and then needs its `--pack-notes` (a first version gets `First version hosted here.`); the same version with different files is an error, since a published version is never replaced. A bundle is published whenever anything in it changed, and needs `--notes`. The realm page leads with the two bundles, and every pack can still be downloaded on its own from its card |
| When | After every change to this file that players should see, and with every new bundle or pack version published on the site |

Links in this file to its own sections (`#…`) are dropped on the site; links to web pages are kept.
